title: Fusing Vessel Behavior and Weather Context for Real-time Attribution of AIS Dropouts.
abstract: The Automatic Identification System (AIS) provides real-time vessel identity and kinematics, but abrupt signal dropouts leave operators uncertain whether the cause is a benign equipment failure or deliberate evasion. The majority of existing works detect anomalous maneuvers while transmission is active, overlooking cause attribution at the moment of disappearance and ignoring meteorological context. We propose a three-stage framework that attributes AIS dropouts in real-time by fusing vessel behavior with environmental signals. Stage 1 summarizes the preceding two minutes of motion into maneuver probabilities using a bidirectional LSTM. Stage 2 applies a transparent policy that integrates these probabilities with sustained wind, gusts, traffic density, and channel membership to assign context aware attribution outcomes. Stage 3 compiles this policy into a lightweight Random Forest, producing calibrated risk scores and interpretable decision paths in 0.38 s, well within the 30 s AIS heartbeat. On a held out dataset from the Port of Houston, the system achieves AUROC of 0.834 and accuracy of 0.84. By incorporating weather alongside kinematics, our approach delivers deployable, auditable, and recall oriented attribution precisely when Vessel Traffic Services require actionable intelligence.

title: SIM-Aided Near-Field Channel and Localization Estimation With Dimensionality Reduction: A Multiport Network Theory Approach.
abstract: The deployment of Extremely Large-Scale Antenna Arrays for 6G enables radiative near-field sensing but poses significant challenges in terms of hardware complexity and interference. Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces (SIMs) address these limitations by enabling wave-domain dimensionality reduction. This paper proposes a rigorous SIM-aided framework for near-field channel and localization estimation based on Multiport Network Theory, which provides an electromagnetically consistent characterization accounting for mutual coupling and non-unilateral inter-layer propagation effects. An indirect estimation approach is adopted, where the SIM is optimized to perform analog spatial filtering by projecting the received signal onto a relevant subspace identified through coarse prior location information. Within this realistic setting, we analytically characterize the impact of SIM approximation errors on channel estimation and quantify the resulting effects on localization performance. The results show that the proposed architecture preserves the essential wavefront curvature information required for accurate near-field localization, achieving performance comparable to fully digital solutions while drastically reducing the number of radio-frequency chains.

title: Contrastive Deep Reinforcement Learning for Resource Management in Coexisting Satellite and Terrestrial Networks.
abstract: The coexistence of terrestrial (TN) and non-terrestrial networks (NTN) in the Frequency Range 3 (FR3) spectrum enables wide-area connectivity but also introduces cross-layer interference and dynamic spectrum contention, requiring efficient carrier allocation and beamforming. These challenges stem from mixed discrete–continuous variables, strong interference, and stringent quality-of-service (QoS) constraints. Conventional convex optimization is computationally prohibitive, whereas standard deep reinforcement learning (DRL) struggles with hybrid action spaces and fast channel variations. We propose a contrastive-based generative primal-dual proximal policy optimization (CG-PD-PPO) framework that reformulates resource allocation as a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP). A primal-dual PPO backbone enforces QoS guarantees, while a diffusion-based generative module and contrastive learning enhance exploration and stability. The system is modeled under 3GPP and ITU NTN specifications, incorporating Earth station in motion (ESIM) mobility, Loo fading, and Doppler effects, with simulations centered on the Ku-band downlink around 12 GHz. Results show that CG-PD-PPO outperforms successive convex approximation (SCA-MA) and PD-PPO in throughput, QoS satisfaction, and interference robustness, while maintaining lower complexity, making it a practical and scalable solution for TN–NTN coexistence in FR3 scenarios.

title: Exploring Small Language Models for Efficient HTTP Traffic Generation.
abstract: Realistic HTTP traces are essential for benchmarking intrusion detection, performance analysis, and traffic engineering in modern communication networks. However, privacy regulations and limited access to real data restrict their availability. Synthetic generation has therefore emerged as a practical alternative. Recent work employs Large Language Models (LLMs) to synthesize protocol-level traffic, but such models are computationally expensive, prone to protocol violations, and exhibit limited portability.This paper presents a lightweight framework for HTTP request generation using a domain-adapted Small Language Model (SLM) based on DistilGPT-2 (82M parameters). The model is fine-tuned on a blended corpus combining CSIC 2010 and CIC-IDS-2018 HTTP samples using a causal language modeling objective with controlled decoding. The generated traffic is evaluated across fidelity, utility, indistinguishability, and privacy.The SLM achieves a Jensen–Shannon Divergence of 0.015, adversarial AUC ≈ 0.5, and Train-on-Synthetic-Test-on-Real accuracy of 0.59—all while running on commodity hardware with an order-of-magnitude lower memory and energy footprint than LLM baselines. The results confirm that compact, protocol-aware SLMs can reliably synthesize high-fidelity HTTP traces, offering a scalable and energy-efficient alternative for privacy-preserving traffic generation and network evaluation in mobile and wireless communication systems.

title: Design and Validation of a Flexible Satellite IoT Testbed.
abstract: Non-terrestrial networks (NTN) are a key enabler for extending massive Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity beyond the coverage of terrestrial infrastructure. Supporting a large number of low-power and sporadically active devices over satellite links requires scalable and energy-efficient access mechanisms. Investigating and optimizing such mechanisms, as well as evaluating new architectures and protocol designs, requires flexible and realistic experimental environments. In this paper, we present SIMON, a satellite IoT testbed designed to support the evaluation of different scenarios and optimization techniques for NTN IoT systems. Among various IoT technologies, LoRaWAN is selected and implemented as a representative low-power wide-area solution, while the testbed architecture is designed to be extensible to other IoT technologies. SIMON integrates two complementary emulation environments for the satellite backhaul link: a hardware-based emulator and a software-based emulator, enabling controlled experimentation under diverse network, channel, and weather conditions. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed testbed, we implement and evaluate two methods proposed in our prior work: SALSA, a satellite-aware transmission scheduling mechanism that assigns collision-free uplink timeslots based on predicted satellite visibility, and REACT, a lightweight application-layer time-synchronization method providing a time reference for devices. Experimental results show that SIMON provides a reliable and efficient platform for validating access optimization and synchronization mechanisms in NTN-IoT systems, and can serve as a flexible experimental framework for future satellite IoT technologies.

title: Performance Analysis of Sub-band Full-duplex Cell-free Massive MIMO ISAC Systems.
abstract: This paper presents sub-band full-duplex (SBFD) as an alternative to in-band full-duplex (IBFD) for enabling simultaneous wireless communication and sensing in cell-free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) systems. Unlike IBFD integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems that require self-interference cancellation and the decoupling of mutual interference between uplink communication and radar signals, SBFD employs non-overlapping frequency resources for uplink and downlink or radar transmissions within a predefined SBFD timeslot. In the proposed SBFD CF-mMIMO ISAC system, we demonstrate a multi-target position tracking scheme, where range and angle-of-arrival (AoA) measurements are fused with an extended Kalman filter. We further characterize the joint impact of residual self-interference (SI), access point (AP)-to-AP cross-link interference (CLI), uplink communication interference, and AP-user equipment association on the Cramér-Rao lower bounds (CRLBs) of range and AoA estimation. Results indicate that, in the high residual SI/CLI power regime, SBFD experiences less degradation in range and AoA CRLBs compared to IBFD due to its inherent frequency isolation. Specifically, increasing residual SI/CLI power from 30 dBm to 50 dBm increases the CRLBs by 3.01 m2 and 0.09 rad2 for SBFD compared to an increase of 12.94 m2 and 0.34 rad2 for IBFD at a residual UL communication interference of -10 dBm. Further, performance analysis reveals a performance dependence on power allocation and the ratio of radar to communication sub-band allocation.

title: Distributed Learning for Scalable and Efficient UAV-RIS-Enabled IoT Networks.
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle-assisted reconfigurable intelligent surface (UAV-RIS) systems are developing as a key technology for next-generation Internet of Things (IoTs), presenting adaptable coverage, improved connectivity, and intelligent beamforming. Typically, the beamforming decisions are executed in a centralized manner at the base station (BS) using machine learning-based algorithms. Conventional centralized learning is constrained by low processing efficiency, sequential computation, and limited scalability, hindering effective coordination and real-time adaptation in multiple UAV-RIS-assisted IoT deployments. To address this, we propose a novel distributed learning technique that supports parallel local model training on UAV-RIS, asynchronous aggregation across edge and cloud servers, and accessible high-dimensional policy learning. The proposal effectively distributes computation across multiple UAV-RISs to assist IoT devices, achieving faster convergence, improved scalability, and higher training throughput than state-of-the-art decentralized and centralized techniques. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposal, which significantly improves task completion efficiency and throughput for UAV-RIS-assisted IoT networks.

title: Edge Implementation of a Fault-Tolerant Wireless Sensor Network for Environmental Monitoring.
abstract: Environmental sensor networks face significant systemic challenges to sustained long-term operation. These systems must satisfy stringent and often competing design requirements to withstand environmental exposure, node failures, limited energy resources, and prolonged deployment durations. Moreover, the geophysical hazards they monitor can disrupt the communication infrastructure required for continuous operation, while many remote regions may lack such infrastructure altogether. In this paper, we present an edge implementation of a fault-tolerant wireless sensor network. The network is governed by an energy management policy formulated within the Model Predictive Control framework. We implement the proposed system and demonstrate its capability for autonomous, real-time control of sensor nodes during two heavy rainfall events. Our results show that predictive control strategies enable sensor nodes to sustain long-term hazard monitoring and early warning operations under uncertain energy availability, even in the absence of communication infrastructure.

title: Performance Analysis of Cell-Free Massive MIMO under Imperfect LoS Phase Tracking.
abstract: We study the impact of imperfect line-of-sight (LoS) phase tracking on the uplink performance of cell-free massive MIMO networks. Unlike prior works that assume perfectly known or completely unknown phases, we consider a realistic regime where LoS phases are estimated with residual uncertainty due to hardware impairments, mobility, and synchronization errors. To this end, we propose a Rician fading model where LoS components are rotated by imperfect phase estimates and attenuated by a deterministic \textit{phase-error penalty factor}. We derive a linear MMSE channel estimator that accounts for statistical phase errors and unifies prior results, reducing to the Bayesian MMSE estimator when phase is perfectly known and to a zero-mean model when no phase information is available. To address the non-Gaussian setting, we introduce a virtual uplink model that preserves second-order statistics of channel estimation, enabling the derivation of tractable virtual centralized and distributed MMSE beamformers. To ensure fair assessment of network performance, we apply these virtual beamformers to the operational uplink model that reflects the actual physical channel and compute the spectral efficiency bounds available in the literature. Numerical results show that our framework bridges idealized assumptions and practical tracking limitations, providing rigorous performance benchmarks and design insights for 6G cell-free networks.

title: Secrecy analysis of indoor optical wireless communication for health monitoring.
abstract: We evaluate the physical-layer security of uplink infrared optical wireless communication for indoor health-monitoring applications, with a focus on the impact of user body-induced blockage and environment characteristics on secrecy performance. The scenario considers sensitive data upload from wearable sensors to a ceiling-mounted gateway while a passive eavesdropper occupies a fixed location. Using ray-tracing technique associated to Monte-Carlo method to generate a large dataset of channel realizations, we perform a statistical analysis on the legitimate and eavesdropper optical channel gains. Secrecy is assessed through practically attainable metrics under on-off keying (OOK) modulation, including the achievable secrecy rate and the secrecy area, accounting for target bit error rate (BER) and data rate requirements of representative health sensors. Results show that body presence has a strong influence on secrecy, improving it when the eavesdropper is shadowed, but potentially reducing it when the legitimate link is obstructed. Reducing ceiling reflectivity further improves secrecy by degrading eavesdroppers’ channels more than the legitimate link. These findings highlight the importance of realistic body modeling and environment conscious design in enabling secure uplink infrared (IR) communication, providing a practical baseline for further enhancement through more complex techniques.

title: DRL-based AoI Optimization for Energy Harvesting Human Body Communication ECG Networks.
abstract: In energy harvesting (EH) Internet of Bodies (IoB) networks, maintaining information freshness is critical for time-sensitive applications such as electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring. Timely transmissions are essential for reliable ECG analysis, which requires complete and synchronous data from all sensors, as each ECG lead is derived from potential differences between paired sensors. To this end, we leverage model-free deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to learn adaptive scheduling policies that minimize the age of information (AoI) in dynamic and intermittent energy arrival conditions. Specifically, in a human body communication (HBC)-enabled EH-ECG network, wearable ECG sensors transmit data to a central wearable hub acting as the scheduler. The hub implements the DRL scheduling algorithm that selects sensor transmissions based on their battery and AoI levels. Furthermore, we propose an ECG synthesis framework for a 3-lead ECG that mitigates the impact of EH scarcity by reconstructing missing leads from data transmitted by active sensors, thereby ensuring complete signal availability at the hub. Simulation results show that the proposed solution reduces AoI by up to 57% compared to the greedy myopic policy and up to 96% relative to a baseline learning policy.

title: Robust Generative-Augmented DRL for Multi-Beam Jamming of Drone Swarms.
abstract: The increasing deployment of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms introduces critical security risks through adversarial surveillance and attacks on infrastructure. Traditional counter-UAV (C-UAV) systems relying on kinetic interceptors or omnidirectional electronic warfare face limitations in scalability, precision, and energy efficiency. While phased-array beamforming enables targeted RF jamming, challenges persist in early detection, spectrum interference, and adaptive responses to evolving swarm tactics. To address these challenges, we propose a generative-augmented adaptive jamming framework grounded in deep reinforcement learning (DRL) and generative AI. Our system model incorporates drone mobility, multi-beam phased-array jamming, and a probabilistic jamming success metric based on the Jamming-to-Signal-plus-Noise Ratio (JSNR). We formulate the problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) optimized via Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and integrate three generative modules: a variational autoencoder (VAE) for scenario diversification, a diffusion model for predictive swarm tracking, and a GAN-based adversarial perturbation module. Simulations demonstrate that our method outperforms conventional DRL baselines, achieving 30% higher jamming accuracy, 2x lower latency, 80% less power consumption, and over 4× higher success rates in high-noise environments.

title: RCS modeling for ISAC-Enabled 6G Robotic Sensing Using Gaussian Process Regression.
abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) is a key enabling technology for 6G networks, supporting emerging robotic and autonomous systems that require joint high-accuracy sensing and reliable wireless communication. A fundamental challenge in ISAC channel modeling is the accurate characterization of radar cross section (RCS), which directly impacts detection, localization, and classification performance. This paper presents a calibrated RCS measurement and modeling framework tailored for ISAC operation at 28 GHz. Using a controlled quasi-monostatic experimental setup, we measure the RCS of a rectangular metallic target across a wide range of incident angles to simulate a sparse, multistatic ISAC deployment. To reconstruct full 360° RCS profiles from limited data points, Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) is employed, providing both predictive mean estimates and uncertainty-aware bounds. The methodology is experimentally validated through comparison with theoretical RCS expressions for rectangular plates, achieving an accuracy within 0.9 dB. Hyperparameters such as kernel length-scale and signal variance are systematically tuned to ensure high-fidelity interpolation while preserving physical scattering characteristics, with independent testing demonstrating that all predictions fall within the 68–99% confidence bounds of the GPR posterior. Finally, the framework is applied to a security-centric scenario involving the detection of metallic objects concealed beneath fabric. Measurements confirm that while attenuation occurs, the fundamental RCS pattern remains preserved, enabling target identification in obscured conditions and highlighting the potential for 6G-enabled robotics to perform automated object identification in complex, visually degraded environments.

title: A POF-PDMS Matrix Wearable for Multi-Angle Joint Tracking in eHealth Systems.
abstract: Current rehabilitation monitoring devices often rely on electronic strain gauges, inertial measurement units (IMUs), or conductive textiles, which are bulky, power-dependent, and subject to electromagnetic interference (EMI), while offering limited multi-angle tracking. To address these challenges, this paper presents a novel 30 × 30 mm matrix-based sensor consisting of six jacketed plastic optical fibers (POFs) embedded in a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) substrate. The system employs LEDs and photodiodes for light transmission, with Arduino-based acquisition and MATLAB analysis. Baseline characterization confirmed stable and repeatable signals with minimal noise. Controlled multiangle bending examined the fibers within the deformation, resulting in voltage reductions of up to 32.5%, while unaffected fibers remained stable, validating selective sensitivity. Heatmap visualization further demonstrated directional resolution and spatial mapping capability. These results highlight the proposed POF– PDMS matrix as the first demonstration of a matrix-based wearable optical sensor for physical rehabilitation, offering a lightweight, low-cost, and flexible platform for multi-angle joint monitoring and integration in eHealth architectures.

title: Keyed Compressive Sensing for Efficient and Privacy-aware Distributed ISAC.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables communication nodes to jointly perform sensing and data exchange, allowing radio sensing information to be collected and shared across the network. In OFDM-based systems, this capability allows sensing information to be extracted and distributed using the communication waveform itself, transforming sensing from a single-device capability into an inherently distributed function of the communication infrastructure. To fully realize its potential, however, ISAC must address three key challenges: (i) achieving high-resolution radio sensing under limited radio resources, (ii) enabling efficient data fusion with constrained communication capacity, and (iii) protecting sensing data from unauthorized receivers. In this paper, we show that compressive sensing provides a powerful framework to jointly address these challenges. We propose a keyed variant that simultaneously enables compression, supports efficient fusion, and offers inherent secrecy. Our results show that legitimate receivers can reliably reconstruct the sensed scene even under strong dimensionality reduction, while eavesdroppers are unable to recover meaningful information without knowledge of the secret key.

title: LWM-Temporal: Sparse Spatio-Temporal Attention for Wireless Channel Representation Learning.
abstract: LWM-Temporal is a new member of the Large Wireless Models (LWM) family that targets the spatiotemporal nature of wireless channels. Designed as a task-agnostic foundation model, LWM-Temporal learns universal channel embeddings that capture mobility-induced evolution and are reusable across various downstream tasks. To achieve this objective, LWM-Temporal operates in the angle-delay-time domain and introduces Sparse Spatio-Temporal Attention (SSTA), a propagation-aligned attention mechanism that restricts interactions to physically plausible neighborhoods, reducing attention complexity by an order of magnitude while preserving geometry-consistent dependencies. LWM-Temporal is pretrained in a self-supervised manner using a physics-informed masking curriculum that emulates realistic occlusions, pilot sparsity, and measurement impairments. Experimental results on channel prediction across multiple mobility regimes show consistent improvements over strong baselines, particularly under long horizons and limited fine-tuning data, highlighting the importance of geometry-aware architectures and geometry-consistent pretraining for learning transferable spatiotemporal wireless representations.

title: Coordinated Multipoint Transmission in Pinching Antenna Systems.
abstract: We study a coordinated multi-point (CoMP) transmission where two base stations (BSs), each supported by a pinching antenna system (PASS), are deployed to jointly serve communication users under spatial division multiple access (SDMA) technology. Pinching Antenna technology was introduced as a promising solution to overcome the large-scale fading that has been shown to be an impediment in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. To realize the advantages of this technology in CoMP systems, which suffer from an upper-bound rate limitation when traditional uniform linear arrays (ULAs) are adopted, we formulate an optimization problem with the aim of maximizing the achievable sum rate by jointly determining the transmit beamforming vectors and pinching locations on the waveguides while respecting the quality of service (QoS) requirements of users. This problem is inherently non-convex due to the strong coupling among its decision parameters, making it challenging to solve using traditional optimization methods. Thus, we utilize a gradient-based meta-learning (GML) strategy specifically designed for large-scale optimization tasks. Finally, numerical analysis demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed GML approach, achieving 92% of the optimal solution, and the superiority of the solution presented compared to other benchmarks. In addition, it achieves a higher upper bound on the achievable rate compared to conventional CoMP systems.

title: Modeling and Optimizing Release Patterns of Cytotoxic T Cells for Rapid Target Killing.
abstract: In this paper, we present a mathematical framework to quantify the apoptotic effect of cytotoxic T cells on a given target cell. As the key molecule which triggers apoptosis, we focus on granzyme B and discuss the role of perforin in enabling its entry into the target cell. Furthermore, we model the most relevant intracellular signaling pathway. Based on the obtained model, we discuss different molecule release strategies and the corresponding target-cell killing speed. We found that synthetic strategies might improve the killing speed compared to bio-inspired approaches.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning Aided Scheduling Design for Pipelined Layered QC-LDPC Decoder.
abstract: Due to the widespread use of Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) codes in modern wireless communication and broadcasting standards, the architectures of their decoders have been extensively discussed in the literature. In this paper, we propose a unified decoding framework for pipelined layered quasi-cyclic LDPC decoders, which encompasses various decoder architectures as special cases, each corresponding to a specific parameter setting within a three-dimensional parallel architecture. Based on this framework, we derive an optimal grid re-scheduling method to mitigate memory conflicts between layers under a fixed decoding order. We also explore the impact of both adjacent check nodes and previously processed check nodes on the number of inserted NOPs, which leads to a reformulation of the scheduling problem as an episodic Markov decision process. To solve this problem, we apply classical heuristic algorithms, such as genetic programming and Beam Search, and propose a Deep Reinforcement Learning aided approach to further enhance the performance. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms traditional approaches in terms of memory conflict resolution.

title: Task-Oriented Wireless Communications with Distributed Inference and Semantic Compression.
abstract: Autonomous wireless systems increasingly rely on distributed inference to support latency-critical sensing and control. Existing split-DNN approaches for such distributed inference have analyzed the impact of neural compression on inference accuracy in isolation. However, the combined effects of wireless network congestion and heterogeneous compute resources on end-to-end task success remain insufficiently characterized. This paper proposes an analytical framework that couples compression-driven task utility, traffic dynamics, and compute latency on the system level. We quantify trade-offs between compute resources, user density, model split choice, and the probability of meeting task-level requirements, by comparing a representative split-DNN architecture for computer-vision tasks with systems based on conventional codecs. The proposed framework provides a general tool for evaluating task-oriented wireless systems with distributed inference and compression across diverse application types.

title: spkLLR: A Spiking Neural Network-Based Energy-Efficient Soft Demodulation Scheme for 6G.
abstract: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) achieve significantly lower energy consumption than traditional artificial neural networks (ANNs) through event-driven and sparse computation. This property is highly desirable in wireless systems with growing demands for energy-efficient intelligence, particularly on power-constrained user equipments. Therefore, this paper investigates the feasibility of SNN-based signal processing by examining an SNN-based soft demodulation architecture, termed spkLLR. We introduce two neuron activity regularized architectures; IM-spkLLR maximizes the information and RR-spkLLR regularizes the spiking rate. These models are simulated under an additive white Gaussian noise channel, and simulation results demonstrate that spkLLR achieves comparable bit error rate performance to ANN-based approach while reducing energy consumption by more than two times. The RR-spkLLR model consistently provides the highest energy efficiency by constraining spiking rates and minimizing synaptic operations. Analysis across 16-quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM), 64-QAM, and 256-QAM schemes further shows that spiking demappers maintain favorable scalability. Overall, the proposed spkLLR framework highlights the potential of SNN-based demapping for low-power, high-efficiency communication systems and establishes a foundation for future neuromorphic receiver designs.

title: Hybrid Active-Passive Massive Access in Symbiotic Backscatter: Joint Activity Detection and Channel Estimation via Deep Learning.
abstract: Ambient backscatter communication (AmBC) enables ultra-low-power connectivity by reusing ambient radio signals, but scalable random access remains challenging when multiple radio-frequency (RF) sources and backscatter devices (BDs) coexist. This paper studies joint activity detection and channel estimation (JADCE) for hybrid active–passive massive access in multi-device symbiotic radio (SR) backscatter systems. By exploiting the inherent element-wise sparsity and cluster-induced block sparsity of the equivalent channels, we develop a deep-unfolding approach termed the Learned Sparse-Group Iterative Shrinkage–Thresholding Algorithm (LSGISTA). Moreover, an autoencoder is introduced to jointly learn the pilot pools of user equipments (UEs) and BDs together with the LSGISTA network, thereby suppressing inter-device interference under non-orthogonal pilots. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed scheme improves activity detection and channel reconstruction accuracy, enabling reliable access for more UEs and BDs under the same pilot resources.

title: Simulation of Distributed Quantum Computing based on Teleportation.
abstract: Distributed quantum computing (DQC) uses quantum communication to pool the computational power of multiple quantum processors (QPU). Since qubits in a DQC system are not necessarily co-located, interactions between non-co-located qubits require quantum teleportation, which relies on entanglement to transfer qubit states between distant nodes. As DQC typically requires many teleportations, quantum networks must efficiently generate and distribute high-fidelity entanglement to enable these teleportations. However, since large-scale quantum networks are not yet available, simulations are essential to understand their impact on DQC performance. This paper presents a simulation-based evaluation of teleportation-based DQC under varying real-world network conditions and two distribution schemes. Network parameters such as maximum connection length, entanglement fidelity, and quantum memory coherence time are evaluated using two small-scale Grover circuits to show the impact on computational fidelity and execution delay. The results show that computation fidelity drops sharply below practical thresholds when entanglement fidelity falls below 0.95 or memory coherence is under 1s. Additionally, a runtime analysis shows a 32 times increase in simulation time when both circuit width and circuit depth are increased.

title: 3GPP-Compliant Noise-Robust Denoising Encoder for Deep Learning-based CSI Feedback.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based channel state information (CSI) feedback has emerged as a promising alternative to conventional codebook-based methods in multiple-input multiple-output system. However, its performance deteriorates under practical channel estimation errors caused by interference, noise, and hardware impairments, resulting in inaccurate eigenvector reconstruction and degraded digital beamforming. To address this issue, we propose a novel 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP)-compliant noise-robust denoising encoder (D-Enc) framework that trains the encoder using paired noisy and ideal data (eigenvectors and latent representations) to learn a denoising mapping while maintaining compatibility with inter-vendor training collaboration options agreed in 3GPP Release 19 without modifying the network-side decoder. System-level evaluations demonstrate that D-Enc significantly improves robustness, eigenvector reconstruction accuracy and 5th percentile downlink user throughput over legacy AI methods.

title: New Sphere-Packing Bounds for Finite Blocklengths.
abstract: This paper investigates the maximal channel coding rate, denoted by R, with a given decoding error probability ϵ and a finite blocklength n. The existing bounds for this problem are tight for moderate-to-large blocklengths (n ≥ 1000), however, significant disparities persist for n ≤ 100. In this paper, a new achievable bound is derived by employing the sphere-packing tool. Specifically, with an additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel at a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) P, a concise and explicit asymptotic bound is obtained as ϵ≈ exp {−n[E0(P ) − R + O(n−0.5)]}, where E0is a simple explicit function of only P, whose form bears similarity to Gallager’s error exponent. Numerical results show that the proposed bounds are much tighter compared to existing bounds when n ≤ 100.

title: Quantum Capacity Analysis of the DNA-to-Protein Channel via Extreme Channel Decomposition.
abstract: Quantum information theory has recently been employed to model biological processes, shedding light on how nature may exploit quantum effects for efficient information transfer. This work explores the potential of quantum channels derived from biological models to advance next-generation communication systems. Focusing on the transfer of genetic information between DNA and proteins, we propose a model that incorporates quantum coherence between synonymous codons, namely, codons encoding the same amino acid. This quantum feature leads to an increase in mutual information compared to classical models. To characterize the resulting communication process, we generalize Birkhoff’s theorem for doubly stochastic matrices, expressing the quantum channel as a convex combination of ten extreme maps, each represented by a sub-permutation matrix. By linking quantum coherence in DNA-to-protein information transfer to channel structure and capacity, this work establishes a theoretical foundation for biologically inspired quantum communication models.

title: Denoising Diffusion Decoding with U-Shaped Error Correction Code Transformers.
abstract: Recent neural decoders substantially improve error correction for short block codes but remain computationally intensive and lack adaptive refinement. This work introduces enhanced U-shaped transformer architectures with two key innovations: (i) double-masked attention from complementary parity-check matrices for improved structural diversity, and (ii) cross-attention message-passing that bridges neural and classical decoding principles. To enable adaptive iterative refinement, we extend these single-shot U-shaped decoders into the denoising diffusion paradigm, where channel corruption is modeled as a forward diffusion process and iteratively reversed based on continuous soft syndrome conditioning. Our key finding demonstrates that U-shaped backbones provide disproportionately larger performance gains under diffusion compared to shallow or deep alternatives, nearly matching deep architectures while utilizing half the parameters. Extensive experiments on LDPC(49,24) and Polar(64,32) codes show that the proposed diffusion-enhanced U-shaped transformers achieve state-of-the-art bit-error-rate performance while achieving superior computational efficiency.

title: Energy-Efficient Dynamic Spectrum Allocation for Massive THz IoT Networks Using Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm.
abstract: The exponential growth of IoT devices in 6G networks poses unprecedented challenges for spectrum allocation in energy-constrained THz communications. We present the first application of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) to energy-efficient spectrum allocation in massive THz IoT networks. Our approach formulates the multi-objective optimization problem as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem, jointly optimizing spectrum assignment, interference mitigation, and energy consumption. Through comprehensive evaluation with up to 36 qubits (representing 9 IoT devices across 4 THz bands), QAOA demonstrates consistent improvements of 7.1-18.9% over classical methods, including greedy allocation, genetic algorithms, and simulated annealing. Statistical validation with 95% confidence intervals confirms quantum advantage across all performance metrics. The favorable scaling behavior and 15.3% average energy reduction establish QAOA as a viable solution for next-generation 6G networks, positioning quantum computing as an essential enabler for massive IoT deployments.

title: Physics-Informed Score-Based Diffusion Model for Bio-Nano Communication Channels.
abstract: Probabilistic diffusion models effectively capture complex, multimodal stochastic processes in communications, signal restoration, and physics-informed flow modeling. Bio-nano communication channels remain underexplored despite their stochastic diffusion–advection–reaction dynamics and discrete ligand–receptor interactions, which hinder analytical characterization and simulation. This work introduces a physics-informed probabilistic diffusion framework that learns the conditional distribution of receptor counts given molecular releases and environmental parameters. By combining score-based generative modeling, variance stabilized residualization, and transformer-based conditioning on physical priors, the approach represents both deterministic transport behavior and stochastic fluctuations across diverse channel conditions. The framework enables efficient reconstruction of temporal receptor dynamics without directly solving the governing PDEs. Experiments on synthetic microfluidic datasets show close agreement with numerical simulations in peak amplitude, timing, and cross-correlation structure, which establishes a scalable and interpretable foundation for data driven bio-nano communication system design.

title: Discriminative Siamese Learning for Pilot Spoofing Attack Detection in MIMO Uplink Systems.
abstract: Pilot Spoofing Attacks (PSAs) represent a critical vulnerability in Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) networks. An adversary transmits spoofed pilot signals to disrupt the channel estimation process at the base station, compromising both system performance and data confidentiality. Recent studies have explored deep learning-based detection methods to address this critical problem. However, existing approaches primarily employ conventional Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), which face challenges in generalizing under varying channel conditions, require large labeled datasets, and often fail to detect subtle attacks, particularly when the eavesdropper transmits at low power. In this paper, we propose the first application of Siamese Neural Networks (SNNs) for PSA detection in MIMO uplink systems. Our data-driven approach learns a discriminative embedding space that enables effective differentiation between legitimate and spoofed pilot signals without relying on fixed thresholds or prior channel knowledge. The proposed framework also provides unified detection of both synchronous and asynchronous spoofing attacks. Extensive simulations reveal that our SNN-based framework outperforms state-of-the-art detection techniques, achieving 17% higher accuracy and 2.2 times less inference latency for a base station with 300 antennas and 20 frames per signal, even under low-power PSAs.

title: OTFS-IDMA: An Unsourced Multiple Access Scheme for Doubly-Dispersive Channels.
abstract: We present an unsourced multiple access (UMAC) scheme tailored to high-mobility wireless channels. The proposed construction is based on orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation and sparse interleaver division multiple access (IDMA) in the delay-Doppler (DD) domain. The receiver runs a compressive-sensing joint activity-detection and channel estimation process followed by a single-user decoder which harnesses multipath diversity via the maximal-ratio combining (MRC) principle. Numerical results show the potential of DD-based uncoordinated schemes in the presence of double selectivity, while remarking the design tradeoffs and remaining challenges introduced by the proposed design.

title: Adaptive Position-Guided Multi-Armed Bandit for Beam Refinement in mmWave RIS.
abstract: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RISs) are envisioned as key enablers for future Millimeter Wave (mmWave) networks by providing programmable radio environments with low-cost and energy-efficient beamforming. Fast and accurate beam alignment remains challenging due to the huge training overhead of exhaustive codebook search and the sensitivity of Position Information (PI)-based approaches to localization errors. An adaptive PI-guided multi-level Multi-Armed Bandit (MAB) approach is proposed for RIS-assisted mmWave communication. The algorithm refines beam selection by combining PI-based initialization with online MAB learning and hierarchical codebook updates, ensuring robustness against position errors. Simulation results show that the proposed method achieves near-optimal SNR and energy efficiency while significantly reducing training overhead. It outperforms conventional PI- and MAB-based baselines and surpasses a dense PI-based sweeping method that uses 450 codewords, achieving similar performance with only 30 codewords. This corresponds to a 15× reduction in beam evaluations. The approach is well aligned with digital twin frameworks for RIS-assisted beam management, where virtual models provide priors and online adaptation enables efficient real-time operation.

title: HyperNQ: A Hypergraph Neural Network Decoder for Quantum LDPC Codes.
abstract: Quantum computing requires effective error correction strategies to mitigate noise and decoherence. Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check (QLDPC) codes have emerged as a promising solution for scalable Quantum Error Correction (QEC) applications by supporting constant-rate encoding and a sparse parity-check structure. However, decoding QLDPC codes via traditional approaches such as Belief Propagation (BP) suffers from poor convergence in the presence of short cycles. Machine learning techniques like Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) utilize learned message passing over their node features; however, they are restricted to pairwise interactions on Tanner graphs, which limits their ability to capture higher-order correlations. In this work, we propose HyperNQ, the first Hypergraph Neural Network (HGNN)- based QLDPC decoder that captures higher-order stabilizer constraints by utilizing hyperedges-thus enabling highly expressive and compact decoding. We use a two-stage message passing scheme and evaluate the decoder over the pseudo-threshold region. Below the pseudo-threshold mark, HyperNQ improves the Logical Error Rate (LER) up to 84% over BP and 50% over GNN-based strategies, demonstrating enhanced performance over the existing state-of-the-art decoders.

title: CRC-Assisted Channel Codes for Integrated Sensing and Communications.
abstract: We propose a novel integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, where the base station (BS) passively senses the channel parameters using the information carrying signals from a user. To simultaneously guarantee decoding and sensing performance, the user adopts cyclic redundancy check (CRC)-assisted sparse regression codes (SPARCs) to transmit its information bits. The BS generates an initial coarse channel estimation of the parameters after receiving the pilot signal. Then, a novel iterative decoding and parameter sensing algorithm is proposed, where the correctly decoded codewords indicated by the CRC bits are utilized to improve the sensing and channel estimation performance at the BS. In turn, the improved estimate of the channel parameters lead to a better decoding performance. Simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed iterative decoding and sensing algorithm, where both the sensing and the communication performance are significantly improved with a few iterations. Extensive ablation studies concerning different channel estimation methods and number of CRC bits are carried out for a comprehensive evaluation of the proposed scheme.

title: Reservoir Computing-Based Detection for Molecular Communications.
abstract: Diffusion-based Molecular Communication (MC) is inherently challenged by severe inter-symbol interference (ISI). This is significantly amplified in mobile scenarios, where the channel impulse response (CIR) becomes time-varying and stochastic. Obtaining accurate Channel State Information (CSI) for traditional model-based detection is intractable in such dynamic environments. While deep learning (DL) offers adaptability, its complexity is unsuitable for resource-constrained micro/nanodevices. This paper proposes a low-complexity Reservoir Computing (RC) based detector. The RC architecture utilizes a fixed, recurrent non-linear reservoir to project the time-varying received signal into a high-dimensional state space. This effectively transforms the complex temporal detection problem into a simple linear classification task, capturing ISI dynamics without explicit channel modeling or complex retraining. Evaluated in a realistic 3D mobile MC simulation environment (Smoldyn), our RC detector significantly outperforms classical detectors and achieves superior performance compared to complex ML methods (LSTM, CNN, MLP) under severe ISI. Importantly, RC achieves this with significantly fewer trainable parameters (e.g., 300 vs. up to 264k for MLP) and ultra-low latency inference (approx. 1 $μ$s per symbol).

title: Dynamic Interference Management for TN-NTN Coexistence in the Upper Mid-Band.
abstract: The coexistence of terrestrial networks (TN) and non-terrestrial networks (NTN) in the frequency range 3 (FR3) upper mid-band presents considerable interference concerns, as dense TN deployments can severely degrade NTN downlink performance. Existing studies rely on interference-nulling beamforming, precoding, or exclusion zones that require accurate channel state information (CSI) and static coordination, making them unsuitable for dynamic NTN scenarios. To overcome these limitations, we develop an optimization framework that jointly controls TN downlink power, uplink power, and antenna downtilt to protect NTN links while preserving terrestrial performance. The resultant non-convex coupling between TN and NTN parameters is addressed by a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)–based reinforcement learning method that develops adaptive power and tilt control strategies. Simulation results demonstrate a reduction up to 8 dB in the median interference-to-noise ratio (INR) while maintaining over 87% TN basestation activity, outperforming conventional baseline methods and validating the feasibility of the proposed strategy for FR3 coexistence.

title: Optimized Resource Orchestration for LoRa Networks in CS-enabled SHM.
abstract: The growing complexity of infrastructure systems and the demand for sustainable monitoring solutions have positioned Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) and Low-Power Wide Area Networks (LPWANs) as critical enablers for Structural Health Monitoring (SHM). In this work, we propose a centralized optimization framework for LoRa-based IoT systems that jointly tunes the spreading factor, coding rate, and compression factor to balance energy efficiency and data reconstruction quality. Leveraging the principles of Software-Defined Networking (SDN), a centralized controller dynamically adjusts communication parameters based on environmental conditions and application constraints. Using a MATLAB-based simulation platform, we evaluate system performance under AWGN, Rayleigh, and Rician fading channels. Results highlight the trade-offs between energy consumption and signal fidelity, demonstrating the effectiveness of centralized orchestration in adapting to channel variability while minimizing the computational burden on edge nodes. This approach lays the foundation for intelligent, context-aware transmission strategies in scalable and sustainable IoT deployments. Future directions include AI-driven parameter prediction, real-time scheduling, and hardware validation to further enhance the practicality and adaptability of the proposed system.

title: Online Active Learning for Adaptive Channel Estimation in Fluid Antenna Systems.
abstract: This paper presents a practical online active learning solution for adaptive channel estimation in fluid antenna systems. We model channel state information (CSI) as a spatiotemporal Gaussian process (GP) and approximate it using a deep dropout neural network (DDNN), transforming the challenge into a deep learning task. By leveraging the expressive power of neural networks, our GP model effectively captures the spatiotemporal characteristics of CSI, thereby reducing the number of ports required for accurate estimation. The DDNN, characterized by its low complexity and ease of training, employs a least-squares loss function based solely on port information and pilot measurements, eliminating the need for true CSI. This facilitates dynamic updates and allows for effective adaptation to environmental changes. Additionally, our solution incorporates a port selection method that maximizes mutual information, focusing on prediction uncertainty to optimize port usage. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed online active learning method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art solutions in CSI estimation accuracy and exhibits robust adaptability in dynamic environments.

title: Experimental Validation of Reflective Near-Field Beamfocusing using a b-bit RIS.
abstract: This paper presents the first experimental validation of reflective near-field beamfocusing using a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). While beamfocusing has been theoretically established as a key feature of large-aperture RISs, its practical realization has remained unexplored. We derive new analytical expressions for the array gain achieved with a $b$-bit RIS in near-field line-of-sight scenarios, characterizing both the finite depth and angular width of the focal region. The theoretical results are validated through a series of measurements in an indoor office environment at 28 GHz using a one-bit 1024-element RIS. The experiments confirm that beamfocusing can be dynamically achieved and accurately predicted by the proposed simplified analytical model, despite the presence of hardware imperfections and multipath propagation. These findings demonstrate that near-field beamfocusing is a robust and practically viable feature of RIS-assisted wireless communications.

title: Secrecy-Driven Beamforming for Multi-User Integrated Sensing and Communication.
abstract: This paper proposes a secure integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) framework for multi-user systems with multiple communication users (CUs) and adversarial targets, where the design problem is formulated to maximize secrecy rate under joint sensing and communication constraints. An efficient solution is presented based on an accelerated fractional programming (FP) method using a non-homogeneous complex quadratic transform (QT), which decomposes the problem into tractable subproblems for beamforming and artificial noise (AN) optimization. Unlike conventional artificial noise strategies, the proposed approach also exploits AN to enhance sensing while avoiding interference with legitimate users. Simulation results show significant gains in secrecy rate, communication reliability, and sensing accuracy, confirming the effectiveness and scalability of the proposed framework.

title: { farm-twin }: an Open Farm-Scale Digital Twin.
abstract: Digital Twin (DT) technology has emerged as a critical paradigm for the real-time synchronisation and proactive management of complex cyber-physical systems. This paper explores the design, implementation, and evaluation of a digital twin architecture for precision agriculture, grounded in the practical case of the open-source { farm-twin } project. We demonstrate how continuous data streams from in-field sensors, animals, machinery, and drones, processed via edge-fog computing infrastructure, can create a dynamic virtual model of an agricultural farm. A three-layer architecture, centred on data standardisation, a performant API-driven core, and a service layer, effectively addresses the historical problem of agricultural and livestock data silos. A performance evaluation confirms that the implementation meets the key latency and throughput requirements for near-real-time monitoring and management, providing a solid technical foundation upon which more specialised AI and simulation modules can be integrated, accelerating innovation in data-driven farming.

title: Deep Unfolded Fractional Optimization for Maximizing Robust Throughput in 6G Networks.
abstract: The sixth-generation (6G) of wireless communication networks aims to leverage artificial intelligence tools for efficient and robust network optimization. This is especially the case since traditional optimization methods often face high computational complexity, motivating the use of deep learning (DL)-based optimization frameworks. In this context, this paper considers a multi-antenna base station (BS) serving multiple users simultaneously through transmit beamforming in downlink mode. To account for robustness, this work proposes an uncertainty-injected deep unfolded fractional programming (UIDUFP) framework for weighted sum rate (WSR) maximization under imperfect channel conditions. The proposed method unfolds fractional programming (FP) iterations into trainable neural network layers refined by projected gradient descent (PGD) steps, while robustness is introduced by injecting sampled channel uncertainties during training and optimizing a quantile-based objective. Simulation results show that the proposed UIDUFP achieves higher WSR and improved robustness compared to classical weighted minimum mean square error, FP, and DL baselines, while maintaining low inference time and good scalability. These findings highlight the potential of deep unfolding combined with uncertainty-aware training as a powerful approach for robust optimization in 6G networks.

title: Joint Activity Detection and Channel Estimation for Massive Connectivity: Where Message Passing Meets Score-Based Diffusion Priors.
abstract: Message passing stands as a powerful Bayesian inference framework for joint activity detection and channel estimation (JADCE) in massive connectivity. The existing message-passing algorithms, however, typically rely on some hand-crafted and oversimplified priors for the wireless channel, which can result in significant errors in channel estimation and also degrade the accuracy of activity detection. In this paper, we propose to incorporate a more accurate channel prior learned by score-based generative models (a.k.a. diffusion models) into message passing, so as to push towards the performance limit of JADCE. Specifically, we develop a novel turbo message passing (TMP) framework that models the entire channel matrix as a super node, enabling the seamless integration of score-based generative models as a minimum mean-squared error (MMSE) denoiser. Our approach, termed score-based TMP for JADCE (STMP-JADCE), takes full advantages of the powerful generative prior and, meanwhile, benefits from the fast convergence speed of message passing. Numerical simulations show that STMP-JADCE substantially enhances the activity detection and channel estimation performance over baseline algorithms.

title: QoS-Constrained Scheduling in Multi-Cell Multi-User MIMO Networks.
abstract: In 5G and beyond networks, efficient scheduling is essential to exploit the gains of multi-user MIMO (MU-MIMO) equipped with carrier aggregation and joint transmission (JT). However, cross-cell and cross-carrier scheduling under QoS constraints is challenging due to the strong coupling across users, base stations, and carriers. In this work, we address this problem in multi-cell MU-MIMO networks to maximize system throughput for both JT and non-JT users under rate constraints. The optimization is highly complex as scheduling variables and beamforming (BF) vectors are intertwined. To tackle it, we propose an approximate but tractable surrogate by leveraging the eigen-based zero-forcing BF and massive MIMO asymptotics. The reformulated problem has a separable structure and is amenable to efficient solutions by a penalty-based block coordinate descent method. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed scheduler not only meets the QoS requirements well but also achieves remarkable throughput gains over existing schemes.

title: Helios: Context-, Energy-, and Periodicity-Aware Orchestration for LEO Compute Clouds.
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations have evolved from connectivity providers into a global, in-orbit compute cloud, but orchestrating applications in this environment, where servers move at over 27,000 km/h and power is a finite, harvested resource, presents challenges that existing systems do not address. This paper introduces Helios, a physics-aware LEO cloud orchestrator that co-designs the control plane with the realities of satellite operation through three contributions: (1) a task-aware policy framework via a Domain-Specific Language (DSL) that enables differentiated handover decisions based on application requirements; (2) a physics-based energy model that tracks solar power generation, eclipse cycles, and battery state to ensure constellation sustainability; and (3) a warm-caching mechanism that exploits the predictable, periodic nature of satellite orbits to reduce data transfer and latency for application handovers. Trace-driven evaluation shows that Helios achieves low scheduling latency scaling to thousands of satellites, significantly reduces data transfer through warm caching, and maintains safe battery levels with zero emergency shutdowns.

title: EP-based Spatio-Temporal Channel Estimation for Multi-Frame LEO Satellite MIMO-OTFS Systems.
abstract: Orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation is promising for low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite systems to combat mobility-induced channel variations. However, existing researches are confined to single-frame, single-antenna architectures, overlooking the spatio-temporal correlations inherent in the equivalent delay-Doppler (DD) domain channel in multi-frame LEO satellite multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO)-OTFS systems. Therefore, in this paper, we first establish a multi-frame LEO satellite MIMO-OTFS system with transmitter-windowed under fractional Doppler, derive the input-output relationship, and formulate a structured sparse signal recovery problem. Then, we propose an expectation propagation-based spatio-temporal channel estimation algorithm (EP-ST), which employs a spike-and-slab prior embedded in a hierarchical Gaussian process to exploit the spatio-temporal correlations of the channel, while efficiently tackling high-dimensional posterior intractability via the EP framework. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively captures channel characteristics and substantially improves estimation accuracy.

title: NetAoD: An Energy Efficient AoD-based Network for Large-Scale Items Tracking.
abstract: Angle-of-Arrival (AoA) tracking is widely adopted in warehouse and industrial applications because of its simplicity design on the tag side. However, it requires complex ceiling-deployed locators with wired power and data connections, leading to high installation and maintenance costs, especially at scale. Angle-of-Departure (AoD) approach shifts complexity to mobile tags, which simplifies the infrastructure and reduces its cost. But AoD’s high tag power consumption of continuous listening limits its industrial adoption. This paper presents NETAOD, an energy-efficient AoD-based network for large-scale tracking. To mitigate the tag energy burden, NETAOD establishes a synchronized network between locators and tags. By leveraging scheduled direction-finding packets, tags optimize radio usage and duty cycling. This design preserves locator simplicity for portability while enabling system scalability. Experimental results show that with a 0.5-second update interval and a 2000 mAh AA battery, the system supports up to 0.6 years of locator operation and 0.8 years for tags, while maintaining an angular estimation error within ±5°.

title: Tensor-Based Joint Subarray Channel Estimation for Terahertz Ultra-Massive MIMO Systems.
abstract: Channel estimation in ultra-massive MIMO (UM-MIMO) systems with an array-of-subarrays (AoSA) architecture is challenged by high-dimensional channels and spherical-wave propagation caused by terahertz propagation. To address these issues, we propose a novel tensor-based joint subarray (SA) channel estimation method for UM-MIMO systems. Specifically, we model the received signal of each SA as a third-order low-rank tensor under the hybrid spherical-planar wave model (HSPM). Building on this representation, we develop a joint SA processing scheme that leverages inter-SA spatial correlations. The proposed method applies canonical polyadic decomposition to extract path parameters, resolves permutation ambiguities through path matching, and jointly recovers global channel parameters, thereby enabling accurate reconstruction of the full channel. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms baseline methods in estimation accuracy, paving the way for reliable and scalable terahertz UM-MIMO communications in future 6G networks.

title: A QoE-Aware Asynchronous Coded Caching Approach with Economic Incentive.
abstract: Coded caching, which enables coded-multicast transmission, is an emerging technology to reduce the traffic load for content delivery systems. However, in practice, the asynchronous nature of user requests poses significant challenges. To address this, existing work proposes delivery waiting-based asynchronous coded caching (DWACC), which allows delayed delivery. While DWACC can alleviate the traffic load, the introduction of the delivery delay (DD) degrades the quality of experience (QoE) of users. To overcome this trade-off, the economic incentive (i.e., preferential service price) is introduced to improve the QoE of users in this paper. Inspired by the economic incentive (i.e. preferential service price of users), a joint DD and price aware QoE model (JDP-QoE) is proposed in this paper. To balance the profit of the base station (BS) (i.e., operator benefit) and the JDP-QoE, an optimization problem for economic incentive-based ACC (EIACC) is formulated, aiming to maximize the profit with the JDP-QoE constraint. To solve EIACC, the DD candidates satisfying the JDP-QoE constraint are first obtained via threshold based DD candidate set formulation (T-DCSF), then a dynamic programming (DP) based DD candidate optimization (DP-DCO) algorithm is proposed to obtain the optimal DD candidate. Simulations are carried out to evaluate the performance of the proposed EIACC. It is shown that EIACC can improve the profit by 24.6% and 40.6% on average, compared to delivery waiting-based ACC (DWACC) and uncoded caching, respectively. Moreover, EIACC can increase the number of satisfied users by 20.7% compared to DWACC.

title: Generative Learning-Enabled Delay Distribution Prediction and Delay-Bounded User Scheduling.
abstract: Satisfying stringent delay requirements while sustaining acceptable throughput remains a critical challenge for wireless communication systems. To address this issue, this paper proposes a generative learning–enabled delay–bounded scheduling (GLDBS) framework that integrates a conditional variational autoencoder–generalized pareto distribution (CVAE–GPD) model with parameterized resource scheduling. The CVAE–GPD component captures both the main and tail behaviors of packet delay distributions, enabling precise characterization of stochastic delay dynamics. The predicted statistical parameters are subsequently incorporated into a reinforcement learning–based scheduler that adaptively adjusts interpretable control parameters for proactive and risk–aware resource allocation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed GLDBS framework effectively reduces delay violation probability while maintaining system throughput, offering a promising solution for wireless services.

title: RIS-assisted Cell-Free MIMO with Dynamic Arrivals and Departures of Users: A Novel Network Stability Approach.
abstract: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) have recently emerged as a hot research topic, being widely advocated as a candidate technology for next generation wireless communications. These surfaces passively alter the behavior of propagation environments enhancing the performance of wireless communication systems. In this paper, we study the use of RIS in cell-free multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) setting where distributed service antennas, called Access Points (APs), simultaneously serve the users in the network. While most existing works focus on the physical layer improvements RIS carry, less attention has been paid to the impact of dynamic arrivals and departures of the users on the system performance. In such a case, ensuring the stability of the network is the main goal. For that, we propose an optimization framework of the phase shifts, for which we derive a low-complexity solution. We rigorously prove that our low complexity solution stabilizes a guaranteed fraction (higher than 78.5%) of the stability region, and all this stability region can be achieved by the optimal solution of our framework. We also provide numerical results that corroborate the theoretical claims.

title: Statistics-Aware Low-Overhead Training and Rate Implications for RIS-Aided Systems.
abstract: Channel estimation is essential for a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided system to configure the RIS and achieve a large beamforming gain. We propose a novel scheme that exploits channel correlation statistics to accurately estimate the instantaneous channel gains between the access point, the RIS elements, and the user with a low training overhead. We propose a two-step optimization scheme to jointly optimize the pilot powers and the RIS configurations during training. We also derive a lower bound on the achievable uplink rate that accounts for the training overhead and the channel estimation errors. This leads us to the optimal number of pilots and the pilot and data power allocation that maximize the rate. Our numerical results demonstrate the higher rate achieved by the proposed scheme over several benchmarking schemes. The results show that fewer pilots than the number of RIS elements and even the effective rank of the channel are sufficient.

title: Graph Neural Network-Based Beamforming and User Association for Mixed Near- and Far-Field RIS-Aided mmWave Systems.
abstract: Extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) is expected to enhance spectral efficiency in sixth-generation wireless systems but also introduce near-field effects, where far-field transmissions can interfere with near-field users due to energy spread effects (ESEs). This paper considers a multi-base station (BS) XL-MIMO system with mixed near-and far-field users, aided by a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). We propose a graph neural network (GNN)-based approach to jointly optimize user association, BS beamforming, and RIS phase shifts for sum-rate maximization, incorporating correlation-based attention and near-field array alignment enhanced training to mitigate energy spread. Simulations show that the proposed method outperforms model-based and codebook-based benchmarks by effectively handling ESEs.

title: Attack Path Inferences for Quantum-Safe FutureG Network Security.
abstract: The looming advent of "Q-Day" is urging standardization agencies to overhaul current cryptographic methods like RSA and Diffie-Hellman in favor of two quantum-safe solutions: post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and quantum key distribution (QKD). FutureG will utilize a hybrid PQC-QKD approach to safeguard data as well as provide quantum computing as a cloud-based service (QCaaS) in this new era of computing. To address the limited literature on quantum-safe FutureG network penetration testing, this paper presents a systematic cybersecurity analysis framework. First, we extend MulVAL, an open source framework for generating logical attack graphs, to include vulnerabilities related to PQC, QKD, and QCaaS within a FutureG context. Next, using the extended MulVAL, we construct an attack graph for a quantum-safe FutureG network, convert it into a Markov Decision Process (MDP), and implement multiple reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms on the resulting MDP model, including Q-Learning, SARSA, DQN, PPO, A2C, and TRPO. Lastly, we evaluate and compare these RL algorithms based on the rolling average reward and cumulative reward metrics, and analyze the inferred attack paths in relation to the shortest attack trace and the RL algorithms.

title: Optimal Beam Shape for Resilient FMF-Coupled FSO over Impaired Free-Space Channels.
abstract: Considering the high flexibility of free-space transmission combined with the compatibility of mature fiber-optic devices, fiber-coupled free-space optical (FSO) systems are a promising solution for next-generation communications. Moreover, few-mode fiber (FMF) incorporated with spatial mode multiplexing (SMM) and diversity (SMD) can enhance spectral efficiency and robustness, but atmospheric turbulence introduces modal power degradation and inter-modal crosstalk that substantially limit performance. To address this challenge, we present an end-to-end theoretical framework for FMF-coupled FSO links that jointly accounts for turbulent propagation and fiber coupling. Furthermore, an eigenmode decomposition method is proposed to design the transmission fields aligned with the channel eigenstructure, enabling the optimal power transfer and interference-free spatial channels. To assess communication performance, multiplexing gain is quantified using aggregated data rate, while diversity gain is characterized by outage probability. Simulation results for terrestrial scenarios confirm the effectiveness of the proposed framework, demonstrating substantial improvements in both data rate and reliability under turbulent conditions.

title: Deep Learning-Optimized RIS-Assisted 5G for Underground Mining: Deployment and Performance Insights.
abstract: Underground mining operations face severe wireless communication challenges due to confined geometries, modal propagation effects, and harsh environmental conditions. This paper presents a comprehensive framework for enhancing underground 5G communications through strategic deployment of reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) optimized via deep reinforcement learning (DRL). A new framework using DRL helps to adjust RIS settings, beam directions, and resource distribution all at once, even when there is uncertainty about the Channel State Information (CSI). Our deployment strategy analysis addresses critical challenges including hardware specifications, safety compliance, installation procedures, and maintenance protocols. Extensive simulations demonstrate a 120% improvement in sum rate, a 256% enhancement in energy efficiency, and a 53% reduction in outage probability. The suggested framework has a straightforward calculation process O(N), allowing it to quickly adjust in changing underground settings while keeping communication reliable for people, self-driving vehicles, and sensor networks.

title: Analysis of Joint EMF Exposure and Sensing in Large-scale ISAC Network.
abstract: The densification of 6G networks for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) demands a comprehensive framework to jointly evaluate sensing performance and electromagnetic field (EMF) exposure. In this paper, we introduce a novel analytical model for downlink ISAC. Specifically, we first derive a closed-form expression for the beamforming gain under sensing beam misalignment at a maximal ratio combiner (MRC) receiver. Building on this result, we then characterize both the marginal and joint distributions of the sensing signal-to-interference plus noise ratio (SINR) and the associated EMF exposure. Our numerical results validate the analytical findings and shed light on the fundamental trade-offs inherent in ISAC network design, providing three key insights: (i) there exists an optimal base station (BS) density, approximately λb= 3×10−5BS/m2, that maximizes joint performance, cautioning against uncontrolled densification; (ii) the sensing-communication power allocation provides a flexible control mechanism to navigate the trade-off; and (iii) the advantages of large antenna arrays are highly sensitive to beam alignment, as misalignment losses can offset potential gains and increase EMF exposure. The provided statistical characterizations and design guidelines offer essential tools for the sustainable design of EMF-aware ISAC networks.

title: Semantic-Guided Generative AI Models for Overcoming Satellite Uplink Limitations in Video Transmissions.
abstract: Satellite communication systems are pivotal for global connectivity by ensuring information exchange when terrestrial connection fails. Traditional satellite uplink transmission suffers from low data rates (e.g., tens of Kbps) due to limited user terminal (UT) power, thus hindering high-quality and data-intensive video transmission. To tackle this problem, in this paper, we introduce semantic communication, which focuses on transmitting semantic information (SI) rather than conventional bits. It can be further empowered by large-scale generative models (LGMs) with powerful generative priors, enabling diverse perceptually high-quality video recovery. However, the limited uplink condition, where traditional video codec schemes fail, makes the effective SI extraction and reliable transmission non-trivial for videos. Besides, inherent random nature of LGMs brings challenge of uncontrollable hallucinations in high-fidelity video recovery. To address these two issues, we propose a semantic satellite communication system featuring a tailored semantic encoder/decoder for effective and reliable SI extraction-transmission, as well as an on-orbit semantic-guided LGM with rich priors. Specifically, the UT transmitter strategically selects key frames, which are mapped into compact continuous semantic space, and then encoded into redundancy-augmented symbols for reliable transmission. On the satellite, the received key SI acts as an explicit semantic guidance that continually anchors the LGM’s generation space toward the target sub-space, thus suppressing generative hallucinations while preserving its creative generation. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme outperforms the state-of-the-art ones in terms of video quality and transmission efficiency in case of low uplink rate.

title: Concentration Field Sensing-Based Long-Range Underwater Target Detection and Search.
abstract: Long-range underwater target search plays a crucial role in applications such as aircraft black box recovery, marine resource exploration, and environmental monitoring. Inspired by biological olfactory navigation mechanisms, we propose a divide-and-conquer concentration-gradient adaptive trace (DC-CGAT) algorithm for autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs). DC-CGAT enables efficient underwater target detection by adaptively tracking concentration gradients. Unlike conventional chemical source positioning methods that overlook the spatial heterogeneity of ocean environments, DC-CGAT explicitly incorporates the depth-dependent variation of the ocean diffusion coefficient within the search process. Through a three-dimensional (3D) spatial decomposition strategy, the algorithm transforms the complex 3D search problem into three independent 1D sub-problems. In the vertical direction, a variable step-size strategy accelerates convergence and mitigates oscillations, whereas in the horizontal plane, Gaussian fitting of concentration profiles enhances both positioning accuracy and search efficiency. Simulation results demonstrate that DC-CGAT achieves high precision and efficiency, outperforming existing approaches in long-range underwater target detection scenarios.
