title: Federated Mutual Learning for Detection of Diverse-Frequency DDoS Attacks in Social Internet of Things.
abstract: With the increase in Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks effective and early detection has become critical to service providers and users. One of the services being targeted is Internet of Things (IoT), which results in reduced availability for both interaction paradigms-human to human (H2H) and thing to thing (T2T), or worse, potential security risks due to overwhelmed resources. To combat DDoS, conventional Machine Learning (ML) methods were developed which showed promising results, however they raise privacy concerns due to centralized training implementations and were not developed with IoT application in mind. Privacy concerns increase with the extension of IoT called Social Internet of Things (SIoT), which applies social networking concepts to create social networks of interconnected smart objects. SIoT introduces additional interaction paradigm, called human to thing (H2T) which is designed to mimic social behavior of human in everyday life. Federated Learning (FL) has started gaining interest as a mutual model training solution with focus on privacy issues, that can be applied to SIoT applications. However, FL applications often face the Non-Independent and Identically Distributed (non-IID) data problem, which significantly impacts overall performance of finalized model, resulting in worse performance than the centralized approaches. In this paper a framework of Personalized Federated Learning (PFL) is proposed to detect DDoS attacks in SIoT applications that addresses the privacy issues and the FL non-IID problem, while achieving high accuracy and stability across heterogeneous clients with the addition of optimizing for mutual learning, which reduces communication overhead and training time.

title: A Deep Neural Network Codebook Approach for Near-Field Nulling Control Beam Focusing.
abstract: This paper proposes a deep neural network (DNN) codebook approach for multi-user interference (MUI) mitigation in extremely large multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) systems operating in the near-field region. Unlike existing DNN-based nulling control beamforming (NCBF) methods that face scalability and complexity challenges, the proposed framework partitions the Fresnel region using correlation-based sampling and assigns a lightweight fully connected DNN model to each subsection. Each model is trained on beamforming weights generated using the linearly constrained minimum variance (LCMV) method, enabling accurate prediction of nulling control beam-focusing weights that simultaneously optimize the desired signal strength and suppress potential interference for both collinear and non-collinear user configurations. Simulation results show that the trained models achieve average phase and magnitude prediction errors of 0.085 radians and 0.52 dB, respectively, across 75 sample subsections. Full-wave simulations in Ansys HFSS further demonstrate that the proposed DNN codebook achieves interference suppression better than 31.64 dB, with a performance gap within 2 dB of the LCMV method, thereby validating its effectiveness in mitigating MUI while reducing computational complexity.

title: A Digital Twin Framework with Field Calibrated Propagation Modeling for Vehicular Network Applications.
abstract: Digital Twin (DT) networks for connected vehicles depend critically on accurate wireless communication models that reflect real-world propagation conditions. This paper presents a field-calibrated DT framework that integrates three-dimensional topography, physical vehicle telemetry, and standardized wireless propagation models to estimate path loss in vehicular network environments. The framework is validated through a case study at the Indian Institute of Information Technology, Sri City (IIITS), where a personal mobility vehicle equipped with sensors and a 4G LTE modem serves as the physical twin. Path loss estimation is performed using the 3GPP Urban Macro propagation model with log-normal shadowing, implemented within a Unity-based virtual environment constructed from OpenStreetMap data. Real-world drive tests along an identical campus route provide ground-truth measurements for calibration and validation. The calibrated model achieves a correlation coefficient of 0.756 and a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 10.95 dB when compared against measured data. The validated framework demonstrates that integrating calibrated propagation models with cyber-physical DT architectures enables reliable radio coverage estimation for infrastructure planning in emerging vehicular and micro-mobility applications.

title: Reinforcement Learning-based Resource Allocation in Secure BDRIS-Aided Fluid Antenna Systems.
abstract: The proliferation of network devices has exacerbated the challenge of secure communication in wireless systems. To this end, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) have gained attention for their ability to enhance physical layer security through passive, controllable beamforming that manipulates signal propagation to suppress unauthorized access. Traditional RISs offer limited beamforming gains due to the independent operation of their elements. In contrast, beyond-diagonal RISs promise enhanced resource utilization, which positions them as a key 6G technology. In this paper, we propose a secure design for a novel beyond-diagonal RIS (BDRIS) aided fluid antenna system with multiple communication users and eavesdroppers. We jointly design the antenna position vector and beamforming vectors at the base-station, and the reconfiguration matrix at the BDRIS to enhance secrecy rate performance while meeting the power budget. The formulated problem is non-convex and is solved using proximal policy optimization to obtain a fast-converging solution. Our results demonstrate a 2.5 bps/Hz mean secrecy rate improvement as compared to conventional RIS-aided fluid antenna systems.

title: ISAC meets O-RAN: a RIC service to ensure sensing delay requirements.
abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) is a key enabler for 6G technology, expected to drive new services and enhance the quality and efficiency of wireless communications. To this end, this paper showcases the integration of sensing information into the Open RAN (O-RAN) architecture by extending the E2 Service Models (E2SMs) through the FlexRIC implementation. The proposed E2SM aggregates the capability of monitoring both the physical environment and the statistics derived from the sensing data, while also enabling control over the sensing-Radio Unit (sRU). Moreover, since the traffic generated by the sRU may vary depending on the use of the sensing data, it must meet strict latency and freshness requirements defined by each use case. For this aim, we propose the use of a Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller to dynamically adjust the capacity assigned to the sensing slice, ensuring that the transmitted information remains timely and up to date.

title: On Beamforming for Transmitter Location Privacy in MIMO Systems.
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a beamforming framework to ensure transmitter location privacy against sensing-capable MIMO receivers. We propose a novel privacy metric called the direction-of-arrival obfuscation power ratio (DoA-OPR) to design the transmit beamformer. The design approach reshapes the angular power distribution observed at the receiver so that a false direction appears dominant without nulling the line-of-sight (LoS) component. We derive closed-form bounds on the feasible range of DoA-OPR via generalized eigenvalue analysis and formulate an achievable rate-maximization problem under the DoA-OPR constraint. The resulting problem is non-convex but can be efficiently solved using semidefinite relaxation, eigenmode selection, and optimal power allocation. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed DoA-OPR-based beamformer achieves a trade-off between location privacy and communication rate. The proposed design attains higher achievable rates than existing LoS-nulling approaches while maintaining comparable location privacy. A suboptimal design strategy is also proposed with reduced complexity. It achieves a near-optimal communication rate with a reduction of nearly 85% in computation time at a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 10 dB.

title: Optical RIS-Enabled Mixed FSO/UOWC in Space-Air-Ocean Integrated Network.
abstract: Space–air–ocean integrated networks (SAOINs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for achieving seamless global connectivity, particularly in remote maritime and underwater regions. This paper presents an optical reconfigurable intelligent surface (ORIS)-assisted mixed free space optical/underwater optical wireless communication (FSO/UOWC) framework for reliable transmission across multi-domain SAOIN environments. The proposed multi-layer system comprises a satellite source, an ORIS-equipped high-altitude platform station (HAPS), a maritime relay, and a submarine destination, jointly enabling end-to-end optical connectivity from space to the ocean. Closed-form analytical expressions are derived for key performance metrics, including outage probability, asymptotic outage probability, and average symbol error rate, accounting for the combined effects of atmospheric turbulence, pointing errors, and underwater attenuation. Simulation results validate the analytical derivations and demonstrate that integrating ORIS with mixed FSO/UOWC links significantly enhances link reliability and communication efficiency in SAOINs.

title: Joint Beamforming and Space-Time Filtering for Cell-Free LEO Satellite ISAC Networks with Non-Uniform ISAC Demands.
abstract: The low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite system has emerged as a key enabler for supporting global ubiquitous integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) service in 6G. However, prior works have primarily focused on single-satellite ISAC systems, which faces technical limitations such as short service duration caused by satellite mobility and an inability to effectively accommodate non-uniform ISAC demands across the satellite broadband coverage. Motivated by this, we introduce a cell-free LEO satellite ISAC network, where multiple LEO satellites cooperatively transmit ISAC signals, and a dedicated sensing satellite receives echo signals in a bistatic setup. This architecture alleviates the strict dependence of ISAC performance on the geometric positions of satellites and users. In addition, to enhance target detection performance, a space-time (ST) filter is applied at the sensing satellite receiver. To efficiently handle non-uniform ISAC demands, we propose an ISAC demand matching (IsacDM) framework that jointly optimizes the transmit beamforming (BF) and the ST filter to minimize the gap between ISAC demand and achievable performance. Simulation results show that the proposed framework more efficiently manages nonuniform ISAC demands than benchmarks, improving resource utilization and service quality.

title: A Robust and Lightweight Neural Network Design for OFDM Channel Estimation in the Low-SNR Regime.
abstract: This paper proposes a robust and lightweight channel estimation framework for uplink orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) systems operating in the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) regime. The proposed framework, called the denoising transposed attention network (DnTANet), integrates a denoising and downsampling (DDS) block to suppress high-frequency noise and a transposed attention mechanism to efficiently capture joint frequency-antenna correlations. Numerical simulations demonstrate that DnTANet achieves robust performance across various Doppler frequencies and delay spreads, achieving superior normalized mean squared error (NMSE) and required SNR to attain a 10% block error rate (BLER) performance compared with existing attention-based channel estimation methods. Moreover, DnTANet achieves comparable performance while requiring only 14.6 27.3% of the floating-point operations (FLOPs) of conventional−AI-based solutions, demonstrating its suitability for practical low-complexity deployment.

title: Polarization-Multiplexed Massive Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface for LEO Satellite Networks.
abstract: This paper introduces a polarization-multiplexed massive reconfigurable intelligent surface (PM-mRIS) designed to mitigate link degradation in Ka-band low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite downlinks. While LEO networks are essential for global connectivity, their performance is frequently compromised by polarization mismatch, driven by dynamic factors such as ionospheric Faraday rotation, rapid platform motion, and complex multipath scattering. To address this, we propose a dual-layer liquid crystal (LC) architecture that enables independent phase control for orthogonal linear polarizations, allowing for adaptive polarization conversion to the channel's instantaneous optimum. The proposed 45×50-element PM-mRIS achieves a wide phase-tuning range of over 260° at 27 GHz with high isolation between polarization channels. We experimentally validate the system-level impact of the PM-mRIS in a non-line-of-sight (NLOS) environment, demonstrating successful recovery of high-order modulation signals up to 1024-QAM. Our results confirm that the PM-mRIS significantly enhances the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and spectral efficiency by precisely re-matching distorted polarization states, providing a hardware-efficient solution for robust LEO-to-ground communication.

title: Liquid Crystal Based Optical STAR-RIS for Enhancing VLC Connectivity in Indoor Workspaces.
abstract: Visible light communication (VLC) presents a promising solution for high-speed indoor connectivity. However, its reliance on line-of-sight (LoS) links makes it susceptible to blockages, which limits its practical deployment. In this paper, we address this issue by utilizing a fully liquid crystal (LC) based optical simultaneous transmission and reflection (OSTAR) reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) that can act as both reflecting and refracting elements, enhancing coverage within the indoor workspaces. Specifically, we formulate a problem to maximize the total system spectral efficiency by jointly optimizing the LED power allocation, user-LED association, and the control voltages of the individual LC elements. Due to the non-convex and non-deterministic polynomial (NP)-hard nature of this problem, we consider an iterative alternating optimization (AO) framework that decouples the problem into three sub-problems, which are solved sequentially using techniques including element-wise search, the majorization-minimization (MM) algorithm, and projected gradient descent (PGD). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed system and optimization framework significantly enhance spectral efficiency and effectively overcome LoS limitations, providing robust coverage across indoor workspaces.

title: Duplexity Paradigms in Separated Deployment Cell-Free mMIMO ISAC Systems: A Kullback-Leibler Divergence Analysis.
abstract: This paper presents a unified framework for comparing half-duplex (HD) and full-duplex (FD) operation in separated-deployment cell-free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. Using Kullback–Leibler divergence (KLD) as a common performance measure, closed-form expressions are derived for downlink (DL) and uplink (UL) communication and for radar detection under both duplexing modes. The analysis explicitly incorporates practical impairments—imperfect channel estimation and imperfect interference cancellation (IC)—and makes the dependence of residual interference on the Tx–Rx coupling coefficients, DL precoder energy, radar waveform energy, and UL power explicit. Monte Carlo evaluations over realistic CF layouts validate the derivations and reveal clear trends: (i) DL performance under FD outperforms the HD; (ii) FD provides a pronounced UL gain when IC error is small and the coupling coefficients are small; (iii) radar KLD (and thus detection probability) remains close to HD under accurate IC and small coupling, but degrades as either the coupling or IC error increases. Power-allocation sweeps further quantify the sensing–communication trade-off: communication symbol-error rate decreases as KLD increases, while radar detection probability increases with KLD. Overall, when effective IC is available, FD is recommended as it delivers a higher end-to-end ISAC utility without time-division overhead.

title: Experimental Verification of Doppler Shift Correction in the Sub-6 GHz 5G for 500 km/h Train.
abstract: A Sub-6 GHz 5G communication method applicable to ultra-high-speed trains such as Superconducting Maglev has been prototyped and verified. The most significant challenge, Doppler shift correction, has been addressed by detecting phase rotation of the synchronization signals. This eliminates the need for additional reference signals and minimizes any increase in overhead, thereby enabling efficient communication. In prototype experiments on the Yamanashi Maglev Line, 5G downlink communication was successfully achieved on an actual train traveling at 500 km/h. The block error rate (BLER) was confirmed to be less than 0.3% over 5 km using QPSK modulation.

title: A Robust Structured-Pruning Based Multimodal Semantic Communication Framework in Wireless IoT Networks.
abstract: Semantic communication is an emerging paradigm for efficient information transmission that prioritizes the accurate understanding of data’s meaning over the bit-perfect replication of the data stream. However, existing semantic communication systems, which typically rely on complex deep neural networks, face significant challenges in deployment on computationally constrained wireless Internet of Things (IoT) devices. Furthermore, the distortion and noise induced by wireless channels pose a serious threat to communication reliability. To address these issues, we propose a novel low-complexity and robust semantic communication framework over wireless IoT networks. Specifically, we design a dynamic pruning strategy at the encoders on devices to reduce redundant neurons based on their contribution, adapting the encoder to the task requirements and significantly improving computation efficiency. Then, to address the semantic degradation caused by pruning and channel noise, we introduce a reconstructive feature enhancement module into the decoder at the base station (BS), leveraging multi-scale fusion to restore lost semantic details and counteract channel noise. Extensive experiments on image, text, and speech tasks demonstrate that our method significantly reduces computation costs while maintaining high task quality, highlighting its effectiveness for resource-constrained and multimodal semantic communication systems.

title: Secure and Privacy-Preserving ISAC in RIS-Aided IAB Networks with Delay Alignment Modulation.
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) can significantly enhance integrated access and backhaul (IAB) networks, yet their reprogrammable nature and broadcast backhaul also create new security vulnerabilities. To address these challenges, we propose a secure integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) framework for RIS-aided IAB systems. The framework employs delay alignment modulation (DAM) to synchronize symbol arrivals, thereby mitigating inter-symbol interference under time-selective fading without requiring complex equalization. A dual-function radar–communication base station coordinates with the RIS to enable adaptive beamforming, while a joint optimization of base station precoding, RIS coefficients, and radar receive filters is formulated to maximize secrecy rate. This high-dimensional, non-convex problem is tackled using a deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm with a hybrid multilayer perceptron (MLP)-large language model (LLM)-actor design. Results were compared against benchmark schemes that used DDPG with a standard MLP actor and an LLM-enhanced actor. Simulation results demonstrate secrecy rate gains of up to 45% when RIS is integrated compared to non-RIS systems, while within the learning framework, the hybrid actor achieves 35% improvement over the MLP baseline and 28% over the LLM-only approach.

title: Multi-Hop IoT Network Fault Detection Using Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Network.
abstract: Large-scale multi-hop wireless IoT networks are increasingly being deployed to support critical applications with stringent QoS requirements. Robust fault detection in such networks is vital for ensuring normal network operations and enabling proactive maintenance especially in adversarial environments. However, the existing researches primarily focus on data-driven attack detection, leaving natural network fault detection largely unexplored. Due to the absence of dedicated routers, multi-hop IoT networks require network nodes to transmit their own data and also relay data for others, which introduces inherent and cascaded anomalies, making it difficult to locate anomaly sources. Furthermore, the underlying CSMA/CA based communication protocols adopted in IoT networks incur unpredictable delays in transmissions, thereby complicating timely anomaly detection and accurate diagnosis. This paper proposes innovative network fault detection technologies tailored for large-scale multi-hop IoT networks. We introduce a spatio-temporal graph neural network (STGNN) model capable of accurately detecting both node-level and edge-level faults. Our model takes both temporal data and metadata for context-aware forecasting and reconstruction. To address the lack of labeled data, we adopt an unsupervised learning paradigm. We evaluated our model on various large-scale network topologies and transaction log datasets, and results demonstrate that our model consistently outperforms baseline models across most cases.

title: Signature-Aided Early Termination for Ordered Blind Decoding in 6G Control Channels.
abstract: Blind decoding (BD) of the physical downlink control channel is a major barrier to reducing latency and energy use in user equipment, with 6G exacerbating these issues due to larger search spaces. Current methods to reduce BD depend on channel estimation or partial decoding, which restrict early termination. This paper proposes a signature-aided framework for early BD termination through lightweight pre-demodulation filtering, bypassing the need for channel estimation or polar decoding. Two signature types are introduced: signatures using phase rotation patterns for likelihood filtering and signatures in demodulation reference signals for neural network filtering. Both methods are compatible with existing NR receivers. Simulations show over 90% fewer BD attempts at a 1% block error rate. Furthermore, blocking probability decreases by 46–70%, enabling flexible scheduling without added complexity. This framework offers a scalable base for designing energy-efficient 6G control channels.

title: Advanced Bayesian Channel Estimation for Semi-Passive RIS-Empowered mmWave Systems.
abstract: This paper proposes a channel estimation technique using a Bayesian framework for reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-empowered millimeter-wave (mmWave) multi-user equipment systems, where a few semi-passive RIS elements with baseband processing capability are integrated into the RIS. Here, low-resolution analog-to-digital converters are considered to minimize the power consumption of the RIS. Based on additional information sampled from the RIS semi-passive elements, we propose a separate RIS channel estimation technique using the sparse Bayesian learning (SBL) framework, where we use a complex adaptive Laplace prior to effectively capture the angular domain sparsity normally present in mmWave channels. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed technique provides superior estimation performance to baselines, particularly an approach using a Student’s-t prior.

title: ADPS-Sat: Adaptive Distributed Patch-Sequence Scheduling for Satellite-Edge Vision Transformers.
abstract: Low-Earth-Orbit (LEO) constellations provide global coverage and low latency, but individual satellites have limited compute and offloading to ground adds hundreds of milliseconds of delay. Inter-Satellite Links (ISLs) enable collaborative inference to overcome these limits. Existing inter-satellite schemes focus on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), but Vision Transformers (ViT) excel at high-resolution remote sensing through global self-attention, supporting small-object detection, fine-grained change monitoring, and robust occlusion handling. Deploying ViTs across a constellation is challenging due to large parameters and repeated key/value exchanges, imposing heavy bandwidth, synchronization, and scheduling demands. To tackle this issue, we propose ADPS-Sat (Adaptive Distributed Patch-Sequence Scheduling for Satellite-Edge ViT), the first practical system for collaborative ViT inference in LEO constellations. By decoupling NP-hard scheduling into patch enumeration-and-pruning and Particle Swarm Optimization(PSO)-driven sequence-parallel allocation within an alternating-optimization loop, ADPS-Sat adapts to dynamic task arrivals and link topologies. In a 4-satellite simulation using ViT-Base fine-tuned on the MillionAID dataset, ADPS improves average performance over the two state-of-the-art baselines by roughly 31.8%.

title: Joint Mechanism Selection and Photon Generation Rate Optimization for QKD Military Wireless Networks.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a hybrid quantum key distribution (QKD) scheme to improve the performance and adaptability of QKD applications in dynamic environmental scenarios of military communication systems. Specifically, our proposed hybrid scheme dynamically selects the prepare-and-measure (PM) and entanglement-based mechanisms in QKD to counteract the increase in the quantum bit error rate (QBER) caused by atmospheric loss and turbulence. To efficiently address this issue, we jointly optimize the control of QKD mechanism selection and photon generation rate using a mathematically formulated non-convex mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) problem. This optimization problem is then solved using advanced techniques, including first-order Taylor approximation and Difference of Convex (DC) programming. To enable fast decision-making for optimal solutions, we design and propose an algorithm based on the deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method. Our numerical results show that the performance of the proposed DRL algorithm is close to that of the classical optimal method, while its time complexity is significantly better. Thus, the DRL algorithm is more applicable in practical tactical scenarios.

title: Adaptive DTN Routing Using Spiking Neural Networks for Services over NTNs.
abstract: Delay-Tolerant Networking (DTN) was developed to address long latency and intermittent connectivity in space communications. The Bundle Protocol (BP) employs a store-carry-forward paradigm, making DTN a viable framework for extending 5G services via Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN). NTN links exhibit intermittent visibility, variable capacity, and weather-induced fading, which invalidate conventional end-to-end assumptions. Contact Space Gateway (CSG) enhances DTN routing by combining path performance prediction with machine learning based on spiking neural networks (SNNs) for adaptive next-hop selection. This approach addresses limitations of Contact Graph Routing (CGR) under congestion and rapidly changing conditions. For critical applications, AI-driven adaptability is essential, as demand spikes, interference, contact plan deviations, and abrupt link degradation can occur unpredictably. Learning from delivery outcomes and evolving telemetry enables CSG to align forwarding decisions with observed network behavior rather than nominal schedules. This work introduces two enhancements to improve robustness and responsiveness: (1) periodic reporting, in which nodes disseminate network state at fixed intervals and fuse local and peer metrics to approximate a global network view despite intermittent connectivity; and (2) loop avoidance integrated into SNN training, which penalizes predecessor selection to reduce routing loops while preserving beneficial path reversals. Experimental results obtained using a prototype CSG implementation within NASA’s High-Rate DTN (HDTN) framework demonstrate significantly reduced response times without loss of delivery success, supporting NTN service extension under uncertainty.

title: Collaborative Multistatic Integrated Sensing and Communications-Part I: Radar Sensing = Communication Channel Estimation?
Collaborative Multistatic Integrated Sensing and Communications-Part II: Autofocus via Message Passing in Tanner Graphs.
abstract: The technology of integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) improves the efficiency of spectrum and power by sharing the same waveform and harvesting reflected electromagnetic (EM) waves. In ISAC networks, different nodes can collaborate in sensing by exchanging information related to their measurements, while communications and sensing can collaborate due to the similarity between communication channel estimation and radar sensing. However, the collaboration for sensing is challenged by the imperfection in time and frequency synchronizations among the nodes. In the second part of this paper, an autofocus algorithm is proposed to mitigate the time/frequency synchronization errors based on common targets, similarly to parity check nodes in error correction codes. The inference of sensing information is accomplished by message passing in Tanner graphs, which is similar to the decoding of low density parity check (LDPC) codes. The validity of the proposed collaborative ISAC scheme is demonstrated by numerical simulations.

title: ASTSC: An Asymmetric Swin Transformer-Based Efficient Semantic Communication System for Remote Sensing Images.
abstract: With the advancement of remote sensing (RS) imaging, high-resolution images are increasingly available. However, efficient transmission under resource-constrained on-orbit conditions remains a challenge. Existing neural networks (NN), mostly designed with symmetric architectures, fail to fully exploit the computational resources at ground stations, thereby limiting semantic extraction and image reconstruction performance. To address this, we propose an asymmetric Swin Transformer-based semantic communication system (ASTSC) for RS images, enabling orbit–ground collaborative transmission. Specifically, the satellite encoder is kept shallow to reduce on-orbit computation, while the ground decoder is deeper, incorporating multi-level feature fusion and a generative adversarial network (GAN) for semantic and fine-detail reconstruction. Experimental results show that ASTSC outperforms three representative categories of methods in both compression efficiency and image reconstruction quality: conventional schemes (JPEG + LDPC), an advanced CNN-based model, and an advanced symmetric Transformer-based model. Ablation studies indicate that the asymmetric architecture achieves approximately 0.8 dB PSNR gain over its symmetric counterpart. Furthermore, the "universal model + fine-tuning" strategy further enhances system performance and facilitates model updates in air–ground integrated networks.

title: Pilot-Free Channel Inference via Multimodal Flow Matching.
abstract: Accurate channel state information (CSI) is fundamental to reliable and efficient wireless communication. However, traditional pilot-based channel estimation introduces considerable overhead, particularly in massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. This paper investigates pilot-free channel inference to estimate complete CSI directly from multimodal sensing observations, including camera images, LiDAR point clouds, and GPS coordinates. Specifically, we propose a multimodal flow matching framework that fuses heterogeneous sensing modalities into a latent distribution in the channel space, and learns a velocity field that continuously transports samples from the source latent distribution toward the target channel distribution. To shorten and straighten the transport trajectory, we introduce a modality alignment loss that not only regularizes the encoded source distribution but also encourages it to align with the target channel distribution. During inference, the learned flow is efficiently approximated using a second-order numerical integrator. For evaluation, we construct a multimodal simulation dataset with Sionna and Blender, enabling realistic modeling of sensing scenes and wireless propagation. System-level experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms both pilot-based and sensing-aided baselines in channel estimation accuracy under dynamic environments.

title: DoA Estimation Based on Deep Learning-MUSIC Hybrid Algorithm with Fluid Antenna for Closely Spaced Signals.
abstract: Fluid antenna (FA) has emerged as a highly promising candidate in wireless communications, attributed to its exceptional design flexibility and enhanced degrees of freedom (DoFs). This paper addresses the challenge of direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation for closely spaced signals under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and limited snapshot conditions. To tackle this issue, a dual-driven FA system is proposed, which synergistically integrates data-driven and model-driven paradigms. Drawing inspiration from the Toeplitz algorithm, a deep neural network (DNN)-based multi-layer perceptron (MLP) architecture is developed to learn the mapping relationship between input covariance matrices and labeled covariance matrices. To ensure the output covariance matrices are compatible with subsequent subspace-based search procedures, a constrained forward computation function is designed. Furthermore, a dual-constrained loss function is formulated to balance the numerical precision and structural consistency of the output covariance matrices. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves significant performance improvements over conventional DoA estimation algorithms in terms of estimation accuracy.

title: Coordination of Physical AI in a Wireless-Connected Smart Factory.
abstract: Smart factories represent a typical use case of Physical AI, where collaborative transportation multi-robot systems execute just-in-time material pickup and delivery based on real-time multi-robot task allocation from the edge server, enabling flexible production flows. However, dynamic task patterns and partial observability suggest a challenge in coordinating such distributed AI. This paper studies how wireless communication can fundamentally enhance collaborative Physical AI systems. Instead of optimizing existing communication for AI, we disruptively investigate how wireless communication improves AI execution. We identify two key pieces of information for AI decision-making, namely belief maps and predictive reward maps, to periodically exchange and fuse them via robot-to-infrastructure-to-robot communication. The fused belief maps are fed into the event-triggered planner and Q-learning, while the fused reward maps provide predictive guidance to assist Q-learning. Together, they enable a wireless-connected coordination scheme that integrates learning-based decision-making and dynamic event-triggered planning. Extensive simulations demonstrate that communication significantly improves scalability and efficiency, reducing task completion time and alleviating the computational burden. The results further reveal that timely information sharing can effectively compensate for limited local computation, highlighting the importance of integrated communication and computing for Physical AI and 6G communications.

title: Rethinking Mutual Coupling in Movable Antenna MIMO Systems.
abstract: Movable antenna (MA) systems have emerged as a promising technology for future wireless communication systems. The movement of antennas gives rise to mutual coupling (MC) effects, which have been previously ignored and can be exploited to enhance the capacity of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. To this end, we first model an MA-enabled point-to-point MIMO communication system with MC effects using a circuit-theoretic framework. The capacity maximization problem is then formulated as a non-concave optimization problem and solved via a block coordinate ascent (BCA)-based algorithm. The subproblem of optimizing MA positions is challenging due to the presence of the analytically intractable MC matrices. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a trust region method (TRM)-based algorithm to optimize MA positions, wherein Sylvester equations are employed to compute the derivatives of the inverse square roots of the MC matrices. Simulation results show significant capacity gains from leveraging MC effects, primarily due to customizable MC matrices and superdirectivity.

title: LAB: Integrating Deep Reinforcement Learning and Bayesian Optimization for Task-Oriented Computation Offloading.
abstract: In this paper, we consider an edge inference (EI) system where multiple edge devices (EDs) transmit visual data to an edge server (ES) for object detection. While degrading data (e.g., reducing video resolution from 4K to 720p or 480p) before transmission can reduce transmission delay, it often compromises inference accuracy. To balance the accuracy-latency tradeoff, we formulate a black-box mixed-integer nonlinear program (MINLP) which maximizes long-term accuracy of all EDs while minimizing inference latency. The problem is challenging due to its implicit objective and combinatorial degradation action space. To address this problem, we propose LAB, a novel learning framework that effectively integrates deep reinforcement learning (DRL) and Bayesian optimization (BO). Within LAB, a DRL actor maps the input system state to discrete degradation actions directly, tackling the combinatorial complexity. In parallel, a BO critic employs a Gaussian process surrogate for model-based action evaluation. For each selected action, optimal bandwidth allocation is then efficiently solved via convex optimization. Experiments on real-world datasets show that LAB achieves near-optimal accuracy-latency tradeoff, exhibiting only 1.22% accuracy degradation and 0.07s latency increase compared to exhaustive search. It also outperforms conventional DRL with 3.29% higher accuracy and 42.60% lower latency, demonstrating its effectiveness for complex black-box optimization in EI systems.

title: Secure Cell-free ISAC Systems with Limited Fronthaul Capacity: Centralized versus Distributed Processing.
abstract: This paper investigates secure cell-free integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems with limited-capacity fronthaul. To address the multi-static sensing challenges under fronthaul constraints, two processing architectures, namely centralized and distributed, are proposed and analyzed. For both architectures, the maximum a-posteriori ratio test (MAPRT) detection statistics and their distributions are derived, where the sensing signals are also served as artificial noise (AN) for interfering with potential eavesdroppers. In the centralized case, the central processing unit (CPU) jointly designs beamforming to maximize the detection probability under security constraints; however, since the sensing echoes must be transmitted to CPU via fronthaul links, the performance is limited by the fronthaul capacity. In contrast, the distributed approach performs local target detection and secure beamforming design at each AP, which avoids fronthaul limitations. Simulation results reveal the respective operating regions of the centralized and distributed approaches, providing insights into future design of secure cell-free ISAC systems under fronthaul limitations.

title: Joint Compression and Resource Allocation for Semantic Communication Based Image Transmission.
abstract: In industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) environments, high-resolution images captured by cameras are frequently transmitted to edge servers for analysis. However, constrained wireless bandwidth and real-time requirements pose challenges for raw image delivery. To address this, we propose a three-stage framework comprising local compression, wireless transmission, and edge reconstruction. Specifically, each device locally compresses the image data using lightweight neural networks and then transmits the compressed data to the edge server for semantic reconstruction. A joint compression and resource allocation problem is formulated to minimize the total energy consumption of devices, subject to the constraints of bandwidth, delay tolerance, computing and power capacities, and reconstruction quality. An alternating optimization algorithm is developed for effectively solving the formulated mixed-integer non-convex problem. The simulation results demonstrate our proposed scheme can reduce total energy consumption by up to 17.1% compared to the benchmarks, while maintaining recovery fidelity and satisfying delay requirements.

title: Latency-aware Human-in-the-Loop Reinforcement Learning for Semantic Communications.
abstract: Semantic communication promises task-aligned transmission but must reconcile semantic fidelity with stringent latency guarantees in immersive and safety-critical services. This paper introduces a time-constrained human-in-the-loop reinforcement learning (TC-HITL-RL) framework that embeds human feedback, semantic utility, and latency control within a semantic-aware Open radio access network (RAN) architecture. We formulate semantic adaptation driven by human feedback as a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP) whose state captures semantic quality, human preferences, queue slack, and channel dynamics, and solve it via a primal–dual proximal policy optimization algorithm with action shielding and latency-aware reward shaping. The resulting policy preserves PPO-level semantic rewards while tightening the variability of both air-interface and near-real-time RAN intelligent controller processing budgets. Simulations over point-to-multipoint links with heterogeneous deadlines show that TC-HITL-RL consistently meets per-user timing constraints, outperforms baseline schedulers in reward, and stabilizes resource consumption, providing a practical blueprint for latency-aware semantic adaptation.

title: MCKD: A Modality Compression Knowledge Distillation Model for Efficient Beam Prediction in V2X Communications.
abstract: Beam prediction plays a pivotal role in enabling reliable and low latency communication for Vehicle-to-Everything systems. It typically requires high capacity models trained on multimodal data to achieve accurate and robust performance. However, roadside units face strict computational limits and often have access to only a single sensing modality. These constraints hinder the deployment of heavy multimodal fusion models. To address these challenges, we propose MCKD, a modality compression knowledge distillation model that transfers multimodal representations to a single student model for efficient beam prediction. Specifically, MCKD maintains performance comparable to multimodal models while significantly reducing parameter complexity. Extensive experiments across various weather conditions demonstrate that MCKD achieves high accuracy and adapts robustly to environmental variations.
