title: MMSense: Adapting Vision-based Foundation Model for Multi-task Multi-modal Wireless Sensing.
abstract: Large AI models have been widely adopted in wireless communications for channel modeling, beamforming, and resource optimization. However, most existing efforts remain limited to single-modality inputs and channel-specific objec- tives, overlooking the broader potential of large foundation models for unified wireless sensing. To bridge this gap, we propose MMSense, a multi-modal, multi-task foundation model that jointly addresses channel-centric, environment-aware, and human-centered sensing. Our framework integrates image, radar, LiDAR, and textual data by transforming them into vision- compatible representations, enabling effective cross-modal align- ment within a unified feature space. A modality gating mecha- nism adaptively fuses these representations, while a vision-based large language model backbone enables unified feature align- ment and instruction-driven task adaptation. Furthermore, task- specific sequential attention and uncertainty-based loss weighting mechanisms enhance cross-task generalization. Experiments on real wireless scenario datasets show that our approach outper- forms both task-specific and large-model baselines, confirming its strong generalization across heterogeneous sensing tasks.

title: Performance Analysis of Self-Interference Cancellation for Transmit Beamforming with Quantization Errors in FD Phased Array Systems.
abstract: When transmit beamforming (TxBF) is implemented for self-interference (SI) cancellation (SIC) in simultaneous transmit and receive (STAR) phased array systems, the finite-resolution attenuators and phase shifters (FRAP) will introduce quantization errors, leading to a loss in SIC capability and beam gain. In this paper, we build an orthogonal error perturbation model to demonstrate the effects of quantization errors. Further, we derive the closed-form expression of the performance degradation bounds for the TxBF with the FRAP, in terms of the equivalent isotropically radiated power (EIRP), the SI power and the isolation. In addition, an angle search algorithm is proposed to improve the isolation with the FRAP. Theoretical and test results results validate the effectiveness and accuracy of the derived bounds and show that the isolation with the FRAP under the proposed angle search algorithm is close to that with the ideal infinite-resolution attenuators and phase shifters.

title: UrMap: UAV-assisted Spatio-Temporal Radio Mapping using Sparse Cellular Samples.
abstract: The rapid development of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and wireless communication technologies has fueled the rise of the low-altitude economy, supporting applications such as logistics delivery, precision agriculture, and disaster response. Reliable UAV communication and navigation rely on accurate radio maps that characterize the spatial distribution of signal strength and channel quality. However, constructing such radio maps is challenging, as extensive data collection in complex 3D environments is constrained by flight regulations and energy limits. In addition, pre-constructed radio maps may degrade over time due to environmental dynamics. To address these challenges, this work presents UrMap, a radio map estimation system based on multi-task spatio-temporal modeling. In UrMap, a Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) model is developed to jointly model spatial and temporal correlations, enabling the generation of complete radio maps that remain robust under time-varying environmental conditions. Furthermore, the proposed GPR model generates diverse connectivity maps by exploiting their cross-modality correlations, thereby providing a comprehensive understanding of the radio environment. Extensive experiments show that UrMap outperforms baseline methods, achieving a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 1.1 dB in the best case and maintaining 4.2 dB even in the worst case for radio map estimation.

title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Wireless CSI Feedback.
abstract: Channel state information (CSI) feedback is critical for high-performance transmission in modern wireless systems, but the massive dimensionality of CSI creates prohibitive feedback overhead. Existing deep learning-based methods address this by treating CSI as an image for compression. Such a data-driven "black-box" approach is agnostic to the underlying physical structure, fundamentally limiting its efficiency and interpretability. To address this issue, we propose PINN-CFnet, a Physics-Informed Neural Network for CSI Feedback that departs from the vision-inspired paradigm. By embedding a differentiable signal propagation model into the network architecture, we reframe the high-dimensional CSI "image" reconstruction task into a low-dimensional physical parameter estimation problem. PINN-CFnet features a multi-layer convolutional encoder for multi-path feature extraction, and a hetero-architecture decoder tailored to recover distinct physical parameters of each path (e.g., gain, angle). Moreover, a two-step training strategy is proposed to guide and fine-tune the network’s physical model learning process. Experiments show that PINN-CFnet outperforms the state-of-the-art method, while requiring only 9.9% of its computational complexity.

title: Optimal input distribution of M-PAM over IM-DD optical channel with non-linear capacitive LED.
abstract: In channels with a wide available bandwidth, M-ary pulse amplitude modulation (M-PAM) with a small number of signal levels is a popular modulation method. The capacity of such optical channels has been investigated before as a function of the energy per bit and a limitation in average or peak optical power. However, in practice, the transmit energy consumption can be a complicated function of the signal waveform. In this work, we study a channel in which, firstly, the power associated with radiating a signal level is not a quadratic function of the signal amplitude, because the emitter may not act as a linear ohmic resistor. Secondly, level transitions consume additional power, for instance, because an intrinsic capacitance in the emitter diode junction needs to be charged up quickly. Light-emitting diodes (LED)s or lasers used in optical wireless communications are prime examples. We optimize their source entropy for a limited power budget. This not only leads to asymmetric probabilities for signal levels, as known from previous theory, but also introduces a dependency on previous signal probabilities. For example, our results show that in an energy-constrained system that employs on-off keying (OOK), the conditional probability of transmitting a logical 1 following a logical 0 should be lower than that of transmitting a second 1 after an initial 1.

title: Unleashing Uplink Potential: AI-Driven Channel Selectivity Matching via Compressed Channel State Information.
abstract: The uplink (UL) throughput stands as a critical KPI for wireless communication network. Various technologies have emerged to improve the UL throughput, such as high-order modulation and high-layer transmission. Additionally, sub-band precoding has gained recognition as a crucial enabling technology for UL Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) transmission due to its potential to achieve substantial throughput gains. This work introduces an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven UL high-resolution precoding scheme featured by neural network-powered engine. Our aim is to leverage the performance benefits of sub-band precoding and non-codebook precoding while minimizing the signaling overhead associated with UL precoding control. Furthermore, the proposed precoding scheme addresses the practical implementation challenge, power balancing across antenna ports. The link-level simulations demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves 2dB and 5dB SNR gains at 70% of maximum throughput over the legacy schemes with acceptable control overhead in 4Tx and 8Tx cases, respectively. Field-measurement-based evaluation further proves the effectiveness of proposed scheme

title: Channel Estimation using 5G Sounding Reference Signals: A Delay-Doppler Domain Approach.
abstract: Delay-Doppler multicarrier modulation (DDMC) techniques have been among the central topics of research for high-Doppler channels. However, a complete transition to DDMC-based waveforms is not yet practically feasible. This is because 5G NR based waveforms, orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) and discrete Fourier transform-spread OFDM (DFT-s-OFDM), remain as the modulation schemes for the sixth-generation radio (6GR). Hence, in this paper, we demonstrate how we can still benefit from DD-domain processing in high-mobility scenarios using 5G NR sounding reference signals (SRSs). By considering a DFT-s-OFDM receiver, we transform each received OFDM symbol into the delay-Doppler (DD) domain, where the channel is then estimated. With this approach, we estimate the DD channel parameters, allowing us to predict the aged channel over OFDM symbols without pilots. To improve channel prediction, we propose a linear joint channel estimation and equalization technique, where we use the detected data in each OFDM symbol to sequentially update our channel estimates. Our simulation results show that the proposed technique significantly outperforms the conventional frequency-domain estimation technique in terms of bit error rate (BER) and normalized mean squared error (NMSE). Furthermore, we show that using only two slots with SRS for initial channel estimation, our method supports pilot-free detection for more than 25 subsequent OFDM symbols.

title: Uplink Performance of Fluid Antenna-Aided Cell-Free Massive MIMO With Imperfect CSI.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the uplink spectral efficiency (SE) of FA-aided cell-free massive MIMO (FA-CF) systems with imperfect channel state information (CSI). We design a minimum mean-square error (MMSE)-based channel estimation scheme to estimate the aggregated channels between access points (APs) and user equipments (UEs). We further derive achievable SE expressions for both large-scale fading decoding (LSFD) and equal-gain decoding processing (EGDP) schemes. Moreover, we formulate a mean-square error (MSE) minimization problem based on the signal transmission model. To solve this problem, we develop an efficient algorithm that combines orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) with binary search to jointly optimize FA positions and the combining matrix. Numerical results demonstrate that FA-CF significantly outperforms conventional cell-free systems in terms of SE, even with a limited number of antennas, and maintains strong robustness under imperfect CSI or heavy UE loads by adaptively adjusting antenna positions.

title: Flexible-Sector 6DMA: Joint Sector Rotation and Antenna Allocation Optimization.
abstract: This paper proposes a novel cost-effective six-dimensional movable antenna (6DMA)-enhanced base station (BS) architecture, termed the flexible-sector BS, which allows the deployed antennas to flexibly rotate and move along a circular track, thus enabling common sector rotation and flexible antenna allocation across sectors to adapt to the spatial user distribution efficiently. In particular, we focus on the uplink transmission in a single-cell system, where the flexible-sector BS receives independent messages from multiple users. We introduce an angular-domain user distribution model, which captures the users’ spatial clustering or hot-spot distribution effectively. Assuming the zero-forcing (ZF) based receiver applied at the BS to decode the multiuser signals, we derive the average sum rate achievable for the users as a function of the common rotation of sectors and the antenna allocation over sectors. Moreover, we develop a two-step algorithm to jointly optimize the common sector rotation and antenna allocation to maximize the average sum rate of all users. It is shown that the optimal antenna number in each sector linearly increases with the number of users in it. Numerical results also show that the proposed flexible-sector BS outperforms other benchmark schemes, such as the traditional fixed-sector BS as well as the BS with sector rotation or antenna allocation optimization only.

title: Statistically Robust Energy Efficient Transmit Beamforming for Block-Fading URLLC Systems.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the energy efficiency maximization based statistically robust beamforming design for a multiuser ultra reliable and low-latency communication (URLLC) system under block fading channels, where the random channel uncertainty is explicitly taken into account. To tackle the difficult problem, we first obtain a problem reformulation via the sample average approximation (SAA) method. Then, we decouple the beamforming vector of each user into a normalized transmit beamformer and a transmit power, and develop a minorization-maximization (MM)-based algorithm to find an efficient solution. Specifically, by performing a careful investigation, we achieve a closed-form solution to the normalized transmit beamformer and a semi-closed-form solution to the transmit power in each MM iteration. Simulation results validate the superiorities of the proposed solutions compared with the existing benchmarks.

title: Near-Field Channel Estimation for XL-RIS-Assisted Terahertz OFDM Systems.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the problem of near-field channel estimation in extremely large reconfigurable intelligent surface (XL-RIS)-assisted terahertz (THz) orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems. By utilizing the sparsity of multi-user channels, we design a training protocol and formulate channel estimation as a low-rank tensor recovery problem. A canonical polyadic decomposition (CPD)-based method is then developed to estimate the channel parameters across different tensor dimensions. Moreover, based on the second-order Fresnel approximation of the near-field array response, we propose a two-stage residual fitting (TSRF) algorithm for the angular parameter estimation at the RIS side, which effectively reduces the computational complexity. Simulation results indicate that the proposed tensor-based algorithm significantly enhances estimation accuracy, while the TSRF algorithm is superior to traditional algorithms in both accuracy and complexity.

title: CRA-Enabled Secure ISAC Systems with Joint EM-BB Precoding.
abstract: In integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, dual-functional signaling may leak confidential messages during sensing, especially when the sensing target acts as an eavesdropper. Existing physical-layer security solutions mainly operate in the baseband (BB) via directional beamforming or artificial noise, but their effectiveness is limited by finite spatial resolution and correlated channels. To address this, we propose a secure ISAC framework enabled by compound reconfigurable antenna (CRA) arrays that jointly reconfigure radiation patterns and polarization in the electromagnetic (EM) domain. We develop a unified channel model capturing virtual angular-domain features, spatial propagation, and depolarization, and formulate a mixed-binary optimization problem to jointly design EM- and BB-domain precoders. We derive an efficient iterative algorithm leveraging majorization–minimization (MM), second-order cone programming (SOCP), and penalty methods. Simulations show that the proposed CRA-enabled joint EM– and BB-domain design substantially enhances sensing performance while preserving communication secrecy, achieving up to 11 dB sensing gain over conventional BB-only beamforming.

title: Causal Graph Transformer for Microservices Anomaly Detection.
abstract: As next-generation networked systems increasingly adopt microservice architectures to support scalable, intelligent, and cloud-native applications, the need for next-generation anomaly detection mechanisms becomes critical. However, the complexity of microservice architectures and the dependencies among services pose significant challenges for anomaly detection tasks. Anomalies such as high CPU usage, memory leaks, and unexpected network latency can severely impact system performance. Existing statistical-based methods often fail to accurately capture the dependency relationships between microservice modules, leading to low detection accuracy. To tackle this issue, we propose a Causal Graph Transformer (CGT) model for microservice anomaly detection, which transforms the anomaly detection problem into a graph classification task by representing microservice modules as nodes and service interactions as edges based on the system architecture. The model integrates Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), Transformer, and Causal Attention Learning (CAL). Specifically, GNNs are employed to extract local features, Transformer is utilized to model global relationships, and CAL serves to filter out shortcut features while retaining causal features pertinent to anomaly propagation. Experiments on three popular benchmark microservice system datasets show that the CGT model outperforms other methods and achieves higher anomaly detection accuracy. The average anomaly detection accuracy of the CGT model reaches 95.87%, which is at least 2.87% higher than that of the baseline models.

title: Flag-Preamble-Based Delay-Doppler Channel Estimation for Next-Evolution Waveforms.
abstract: Accurate delay-Doppler channel estimation is critical for next-evolution waveforms (NEWs) to enable reliable signal detection. This paper proposes a robust channel estimation algorithm that integrates Flag sequences optimized via an adaptive accelerated parallel majorization-minimization (AP-MM) algorithm with a proposed channel estimation algorithm. To enable efficient, low-complexity parameter extraction and further overcome the robustness issues of conventional greedy estimation, we introduce two key enhancements, i.e., a candidate selection strategy to mitigate spurious sidelobe peaks, and a global least squares (LS) refinement stage to eliminate error propagation caused by sidelobe masking effects. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed scheme significantly outperforms traditional existing algorithms, achieving the desired estimation accuracy.

title: Toward Resilient Channel Estimation in Wideband High-Mobility Scenarios: A Non-Uniform Pilot Pattern Design.
abstract: In wideband high-mobility scenarios, reliable channel estimation is challenged by strong Doppler effects and frequency-dependent channel variations. Conventional pilot designs based on uniform frequency-domain patterns become increasingly inefficient, as they fail to adapt to heterogeneous channel statistics, such as coherence bandwidth and Doppler spread, across the spectrum. In this paper, exploiting the sparsity of delay–Doppler channel representation, we first establish an explicit analytical relationship between frequency-domain pilot spacing and the mutual coherence of the sensing matrix in compressed sensing (CS), revealing the fundamental subband-dependent coherence constraints on channel estimation performance. Then, we derive the closed-form of the upper bound of mean squared error (MSE) performance, as a function of the mutual coherence and delay-Doppler paths. Finally, we formulate a pilot pattern optimization problem under coherence and frequency domain sampling constraints, and develop a low-complexity Adaptive Subband Pilot Allocation (ASPA) algorithm. Simulation results confirm that the proposed non-uniform pilot design achieves significantly lower MSE than conventional uniform schemes under the same pilot overhead in wideband high-mobility scenarios.

title: Transformer-Based Integrated Sensing and Semantic Communication for Low-Altitude Wireless Networks.
abstract: Emerging low-altitude wireless networks (LAWNs) provide a promising aerial platform for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) due to the high mobility and flexible deployment. Nevertheless, dynamic environment and limited infrastructure support pose significant challenges for achieving high-accuracy ISAC services. To address these issues, we propose a Transformer-based integrated sensing and semantic communication (T-ISSC) framework that transmits task-relevant semantic tokens in distributed sensing networks. In particular, inspired by recent advances in generative large models, the proposed T-ISSC framework integrates the Transformer-empowered joint source-channel coding architecture with a task head for target state estimation. Moreover, transfer learning is leveraged to enhance the framework’s adaptability to diverse communication environments in LAWNs. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed T-ISSC framework achieves a 52.35%-73.66% reduction in root mean square error compared with benchmark schemes.

title: Mitigating Inter-user Interference in Mixed Near-field and Far-field Communications.
abstract: In mixed near-field and far-field systems, the non-orthogonality between near-field and far-field channels may lead to severe inter-user interference and hence degraded rate performance, when the analog beamforming is designed based on full-array maximum ratio transmission (MRT). To tackle this issue, we propose a new scheme that employs the antenna selection technique to effectively suppress mixed-field interference. Specifically, we first consider a typical two-user mixed-field case and show that the strong mixed-field interference can be greatly reduced by deactivating a small portion of antennas only, yet without compromising array gains too much. Then, a sum-rate maximization problem is formulated for the general case, where the antenna selection and power allocation are jointly optimized based on MRT beams in analog beamforming. Although this problem is non-convex and difficult to solve, we propose an efficient penalty dual decomposition (PDD)-based double-layer framework to obtain its high-quality solution by using the block coordinate descent (BCD) and successive convex approximation (SCA) techniques. Last, numerical results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves a favorable trade-off between interference suppression and array gain loss, hence achieving significant performance gains over various benchmark schemes.

title: Robust Spatial Anti-Jamming Based on Steering Vector Estimation and Orthogonal Projection.
abstract: In this paper, a robust spatial anti-jamming algorithm capable of jamming suppression in mismatch scenarios is proposed. Firstly, the Capon spectral peak search is performed in the jamming angular sector and the directions-of-arrival (DOAs) of the jamming signals are initially filtered out. Then, the power spectrum is integrated in the neighboring range of each estimated jamming signal DOA to construct matrices, and the principal eigenvectors of these matrices are utilized to estimate the steering vectors (SVs) of jamming signals. Similarly, Capon spectrum integration is performed in the intended signal angular region, and the expected signal SV is approximate through principal eigenvector extraction. Finally, the proposed beamforming weight is obtained through orthogonal projection and the estimated SVs of jamming signals and desired signal. Numerical results confirm that the presented algorithm exhibits better jamming suppression performance and lower sensitivity to mismatch environments than the comparison algorithms. In addition, the presented beamforming weight is capable of keeping the peak of the beampattern main lobe aligned with the practical incoming direction of the intended signal and the beampattern notches aligned with the practical DOAs of jamming signals.

title: Spatial-Temporal Dual-Branch Learning for Anomaly Detection in Software-Defined Networks.
abstract: The unique architecture of Software-Defined Networking (SDN) offers enhanced management flexibility but also introduces new security threats, especially as 6G networks further expand the scale and complexity of network environments, making traditional intrusion detection methods difficult to apply directly. Although existing research has attempted to solve these problems by combining spatial and temporal features, there remains considerable room for improvement in detection accuracy and generalization capability, especially in practical scenarios with limited labeled data. To address these limitations, this paper proposes the Spatial-Temporal Dual-Network (STD-Net), a small-sample anomaly detection framework designed for SDN environments. The framework begins by dynamically grouping raw flow data into a hierarchical "user–time point" structure through adaptive user identification and temporal aggregation, followed by automated feature selection using Information Value (IV) analysis. Architecturally, STD-Net employs a dual-branch design, a temporal branch using a Transformer encoder to capture long-term dependencies, and a spatial branch leveraging a Graph Attention Network (GAT) to model structural relationships among time points. These two branches are integrated through an adaptive gated fusion module. By explicitly modeling spatiotemporal characteristics and incorporating built-in inductive biases, the design significantly improves performance under conditions of incomplete data and scarce annotations. Experimental results demonstrate that STD-Net outperforms other baseline methods in both detection accuracy and robustness in low-resource settings.

title: Transmit Beamforming Design for Integrated Sensing and Multicast Communication based on Distribution Information.
abstract: In this paper, we study an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, where a multi-antenna base station (BS) simultaneously estimates the unknown angle parameter of a point target using the echo signals received at the BS with prior distribution information, and serves a group of single-antenna communication users in the downlink via multicast transmission. We aim to minimize the posterior Cramér-Rao bound (PCRB) of the target angle parameter by optimizing the multicast beamformer and potential dedicated sensing beamformers, subject to a multicast rate constraint. We propose a successive convex approximation (SCA) based algorithm to effectively solve the non-convex problem, and obtain a stationary solution that satisfies Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions. Through analysis, we derive a specific structure of the proposed KKT solution across different rate regimes, and characterize the number of dedicated sensing beams needed in a multicast ISAC system for the first time. Our analytical results hold for any KKT point solution, including the optimal one. Numerical results are provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed design and the theoretical analysis.

title: Gradient-Aware High-Resolution Pathways for Tiny UAV Object Detection.
abstract: Detecting ultra-small targets in UAV imagery is hindered by (i) gradient washout on fine details, (ii) resolution loss from downsampling, (iii) dilution during cross-scale fusion, and (iv) the cost/misfocus of global attention. We present Gradient-Aware High-Resolution Pathways (GA-Pathways), which tackles these issues with three cooperating parts: a GHRP block that maintains well-conditioned gradient routes along high-resolution paths, an HR-PentaPath (HRPP) fusion pathway with lightweight content-aware merging, and localized CGA applied only at shallow levels for targeted enhancement. Under a single-scale, no-TTA FP32 protocol at 6402, GA-Pathways-s delivers 56.2% Precision, 40.3% Recall, 44.5% AP50, and 27.1% AP0.5:0.95on VisDrone2019-DET with 5.24M parameters and 25.7 GFLOPs; on AI-TOD it attains 36.8% AP50and 17.5% AP0.5:0.95at the same complexity. A nano variant reaches 36.7%/22.8% (AP50/AP0.5:0.95) with 1.94M parameters and 7.83 GFLOPs. On VisDrone, GA-Pathways-s improves over YOLOv12s/13s by +4.2∼+4.6 (AP50) and +2.7∼+3.3 (AP0.5:0.95) while using ∼42% fewer parameters; GA-Pathways-n exceeds YOLOv13n by +2.3/+2.8 with ∼20% fewer parameters. Ablations indicate that safeguarding shallow gradients and favoring high-resolution fusion, complemented by localized attention, yields a strong accuracy–efficiency balance and reliably localizes targets down to 4×4 pixels.

title: Sensing-assisted Predictive Hybrid Beamforming for Low-Altitude Communication Networks.
abstract: This paper proposes a sensing-assisted predictive hybrid beamforming scheme for low-altitude communication networks (LACN). Specifically, we consider that a base station transmits data to multiple unmanned aerial vehicles. Without the estimation of historical state parameters, i.e., angle-of-arrival, channel state information (CSI), we establish a direct mapping between reflected echo signals and hybrid beamforming (HBF) matrices through an end-to-end framework. To enhance the communication quality of service, the predictive HBF design problem is formulated by maximizing communication sum-rate subject to power and hardware constraints. A novel sensing-assisted network architecture is proposed to predict HBF for LACN. This architecture combines Transformer and convolutional modules to jointly extract rich spatio-temporal features from the reflected echoes. We compare our proposed PHBFNN with existing deep learning-based methods and the extended Kalman filtering approach. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed PHBFNN scheme achieves a higher sum-rate, validating its feasibility for realizing LACN without CSI.

title: Deep Learning Enabled Direct Multiuser Hybrid Beamforming for XL-MIMO Communications.
abstract: This paper presents a pilot-efficient direct hybrid beamforming framework for multiuser near-and far-field XL-MIMO systems that operates without downlink channel state information. We design a fully complex-valued end-to-end architecture comprising a grouped complex-convolution sensing frontend, a shared complex multilayer perceptron, and a constant-modulus normalization head that outputs the analog precoder directly from a small set of uplink measurements. A variant minimum mean-squared error surrogate eliminates the digital precoder in closed form during training, providing stable gradients while respecting hybrid hardware constraints. At inference, the learned analog combiner is reused to estimate the equivalent channel from a few additional pilots, enabling a regularized zero-forcing digital precoder computed via Cholesky-based linear solves. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed method delivers up to 3 bps/Hz sum-rate gains over sparse-recovery pipelines and strong deep learning baselines under identical pilot budgets, while approaching ideal hybrid beamforming performance with an order-of-magnitude lower complexity than iterative schemes. The framework remains robust across wide SNR ranges, various multipath levels, and mixed near-/far-field deployments, highlighting its suitability for scalable XL-MIMO implementations.

title: Proactive Channel-Semantic Adaptive JSCC for Robust Image Transmission in High-Mobility OFDM System.
abstract: Semantic communication (SemCom) has demonstrated strong potential to enhance spectral efficiency and communication robustness by transmitting task-relevant meaning rather than bit-level representations. However, in high-mobility multi-carrier systems, Doppler-induced inter-carrier interference (ICI) and rapidly outdated channel state information (CSI) cause severe degradation in semantic fidelity and reconstruction accuracy. To overcome these challenges, we propose channel–semantic joint adaptive JSCC (CSJA-JSCC), an end-to-end predictive framework that adaptively aligns semantic feature transmission with time-varying channel conditions. The proposed design jointly optimizes a transmitter with semantic-to-subcarrier and power allocation guided by predicted CSI, and a receiver that performs integrated channel estimation and semantic decoding. These modules are jointly trained through a differentiable prediction feedback mechanism, allowing the entire system to co-adapt to channel dynamics and prediction uncertainty. Extensive simulations over high-Doppler channels show that CSJA-JSCC consistently achieves higher peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and semantic similarity than baselines, which demonstrates its effectiveness and robustness in dynamic wireless environments.

title: Hyperbolic Pattern-Based Beam Training in Near-Field Communications.
abstract: Extremely large-scale arrays (XL-arrays) are a promising technology for significantly enhancing spectral efficiency and spatial resolution for future 6G mobile networks. However, XL-arrays considerably extend the near-field region, which is characterized by spherical-wave propagation and may span hundreds of meters. Such a spherical-wave nature of the near field leads to substantially higher beam training overhead compared with conventional far-field methods, as the training complexity scales with the spatial dimensionality. To address this challenge, in this paper, we exploit the geometric structure of the near-field beam pattern and observe that its high-energy region follows a hyperbolic trajectory, along which the optimal codeword resides. Motivated by this geometric insight, we propose a novel three-stage hyperbolic beam training method to effectively reduce beam training overhead. Specifically, in the first stage, the curvature parameter is searched to determine the hyperbolic trajectory that contains the optimal codeword. Then, in the second stage, a constrained search is performed along this hyperbolic path to identify the codeword corresponding to the highest received signal strength. Finally, in the third stage, a localized rectangular fine search is conducted around the selected codeword to compensate for residual deviation and further refine the beam alignment. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method approaches the performance of perfect channel state information-based beamforming while drastically reducing the training overhead.

title: Applying Fiber-to-the-Room (FTTR) with RFID for Next-Generation Smart Warehouse Networking.
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid network architecture that integrates Fiber-to-the-Room (FTTR) with Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) for next-generation smart warehouse networking. FTTR provides deep fiber penetration to enable precise synchronization of time, phase, and frequency across distributed Sub Fiber Units (SFUs). Based on this capability, we propose a scheme that applies distributed transmit beamforming (DTB) among SFUs for cooperative RFID transmission. The synchronization inherent in FTTR allows cooperative beamforming to improve signal quality, addressing a longstanding limitation of conventional RFID deployments. A field trial was conducted jointly by a leading system vendor and a top service provider. It demonstrated the benefits of the proposed architecture. Results confirm that automated inventory can be achieved with a 100% success rate, and that SFU cooperation significantly enhances coverage and inventory time. These findings indicate that the integration of FTTR and RFID provides a viable pathway toward high-performance networking in digitalized warehouse environments. The network architecture is promising for the industrial Internet-of-Things (IoT) applications.

title: Blind Channel Estimation Based Positioning Enhancement for ACO-OFDM Integrated Visible Light Communication and Positioning.
abstract: The integrated visible light communication and positioning (VLCP) allows simultaneous communications and the received signal strength (RSS)-based positioning, using identical signals. However, light emitting diode (LED)’s limited bandwidth and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) channels cause inter-symbol interference (ISI), having significant impact on the RSS-based positioning for VLCP systems. Therefore, we propose a blind symmetry-based channel estimation (BSCE) approach to realize high-performance communications and high-accuracy positioning, requiring no pilot. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this is the first work to investigate blind channel estimation to enhance the RSS-based positioning for asymmetrically clipped optical-orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (ACO-OFDM) VLCP systems. The symmetry structure of ACO-OFDM signals in time domain is utilized to estimate LED’s limited bandwidth, line-of-sight (LoS) and NLoS channels, separately. This is different from the previous channel estimation methods that only realize the purpose of communications, estimating LED’s limited bandwidth, LoS and NLoS channels together. Thus, the proposed BSCE approach enhances the RSS-based positioning accuracy much higher than the previous channel estimation works, as the RSS variation caused by LED’s limited bandwidth and NLoS is mitigated. Simulation results show that the proposed BSCE approach can effectively mitigate the impact of LED’s limited bandwidth and NLoS channels on positioning, and provide positioning performance higher than existing channel estimation methods.

title: Robust Edge Inference with Graph Neural Networks under Channel Aging.
abstract: One of the key missions of sixth-generation (6G) networks is to deploy artificial intelligence (AI) at the network edge. The widely recognized paradigm, edge inference, is envisioned to enable diverse IoT applications such as autonomous driving, industrial automation, and human activity recognition. However, its efficient deployment is hindered by two major challenges: 1) the communication bottleneck from uploading high-dimensional features under limited resources, and 2) performance degradation due to outdated channel estimation, known as channel aging. This work addresses these challenges to enable robust edge inference via efficient resource allocation. In particular, we theoretically characterize the effects of channel aging on end-to-end (E2E) performance by linking inference accuracy to a surrogate metric, termed effective discriminant gain. An efficient resource allocation strategy adaptive to channel aging is realized by leveraging the permutation invariance of a graph neural network (GNN) to maximize the proposed surrogate metric. Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed framework over benchmarks that either assume perfect CSI or employ uniform resource allocation.

title: SGCNet: Scenario-Generalizable CSI Feedback Compression via Residual Vector Quantization.
abstract: The rapidly increasing number of antennas in massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems has significantly raised the feedback burden of channel state information (CSI), highlighting the need for efficient CSI compression. While recent learning-based methods outperform classical approaches such as compressive sensing in both accuracy and efficiency, they typically require dedicated models for different channel scenarios, substantially increasing training complexity and deployment cost. This paper introduces SGCNet (Scenario-Generalizable CSI Compression Network), a neural network designed for scenario-generalizable CSI feedback compression. SGCNet employs multi-stage residual vector quantization (RVQ) to learn stage-wise codebooks, which are shared between the user equipment (UE) and the base station (BS). By composing multiple codewords as building blocks, the latent representation is reconstructed in a coarse-to-fine manner from the sum of stage-specific codewords. This approach produces a regularized representation that demonstrates increased robustness to scenario shifts. Extensive simulations indicate that SGCNet attains superior reconstruction fidelity with low computational complexity. In particular, under cross-scenario evaluation at η = 1/16, SGCNet trained exclusively on the COST2100 Indoor and Outdoor scenarios sustains a worst-case NMSE of −8.83 dB on ten unseen DeepMIMO scenarios, whereas state-of-the-art baselines such as AiANet and TransNet degrade to −0.94 dB and −0.98 dB, respectively.

title: Enabling Flying MIMO System with Low-Altitude UAV Swarm for Near-Field Communication.
abstract: By leveraging the intrinsic three-dimensional (3D) mobility and swarm cooperation, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarm serves as an ideal platform for implementing flying multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system. Compared to existing terrestrial MIMO and massive MIMO systems, flying MIMO system facilitates an extremely large-scale array aperture, and thus the conventional far-field uniform plane wave (UPW) model may no longer be valid for aerial-to-ground links. This paper considers the near-field communication enabled by flying MIMO under the non-uniform spherical wave (NUSW) model, with a focus on the dual impact of UAV swarm trajectory on channel amplitude and phase. Subject to practical constraints on UAVs, we formulate a general optimization problem to maximize the minimum average communication rate over user equipments (UEs), by jointly optimizing the receive beamforming for all UEs and the 3D UAV swarm trajectory. Subsequently, an alternating optimization algorithm is proposed to efficiently tackle the highly non-convex optimization problem. Simulation results demonstrate the significant performance gains of the proposed scheme compared with the benchmark schemes.

title: Cooperative Distributed Memory AMP Detection for Oversampled Random Multiplexing Systems.
abstract: Doubly-selective fading continues to challenge wireless communication in high-mobility scenarios. Random multiplexing (RM) with approximate message passing (AMP)-type detectors address it while achieving maximum a posteriori bit-error rate performance. In this paper, we consider oversampled RM systems to further improve the performance. To overcome the limitations of conventional oversampling detectors, including their centralized processing of high-dimensional data and need for noise whitening, we propose a cooperative distributed memory AMP (CD-MAMP) algorithm. We derive the input-output relationship for the distributed oversampled RM and analyze the correlation induced by the shared random transform matrix and the oversampling noise. By leveraging the correlation, we design the CD-MAMP that consists of an inner-iteration cross-domain memory AMP (MAMP) and an outer-iteration optimal fusion strategy. Simulation results show that RM outperforms other modulation schemes. CD-MAMP outperforms both the centralized MAMP and the Nyquist-sampling detectors. After sufficient inner iterations, only one outer iteration is needed to achieve nearly identical gains, reducing communication overhead.

title: Low-Complexity Digital Twin for CSI Acquisition in MIMO Communications.
abstract: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications will continue to be a cornerstone of modern wireless networks, thanks to the spatial multiplexing and beamforming gains enabled by large antenna arrays. However, acquiring precise downlink channel state information (CSI)—essential for effective precoding for large-scale antenna systems—involves substantial signaling overhead. In this paper, we propose a CSI acquisition framework that leverages digital twin to generate user-specific channel prior at the base-station, and reduces the CSI acquisition overhead. To achieve a low-complexity operation, we propose a multi-tiered digital twin architecture and complexity reduction methods, which reduce the ray-tracing runtime with minimal performance loss. Through comprehensive evaluations in an urban scenario, we demonstrate that the proposed framework can effectively reduce CSI acquisition overhead, and decrease the digital twin compute requirement by 56% while maintaining healthy cell coverage and spectral efficiency at the user.

title: Joint Beamforming for Active RIS-Aided Integrated Sensing, Communication, and Power Transfer.
abstract: This paper proposes a promising framework of multi-functional service incorporating single sensing target (ST), multiple information receivers (IRs), and multiple energy receivers (ERs) in an active reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided integrated sensing, communication, and power transfer (ISCPT) system. In the proposed system, we aim to maximize the received radar signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) by jointly optimizing the transmit beamforming at the multi-functional base station (MFBS), the coefficients of active RIS, and the radar receive filter coefficients, while meet the requirements of signal-to-interference-plus-noise-ratio (SINR) for IRs and energy harvesting (EH) for ERs. The formulated problem is tackled by developing an efficient alternating optimization (AO) algorithm combined with Schur complement and majorization-minimization (MM) techniques. Finally, the numerical results reveal that active RIS is remarkably superior to passive RIS for ISCPT systems by over 40 dB, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning Based Beamforming Design in UAV-enabled NOMA ISAC System.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) enabled non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) empowered integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, where the UAV is introduced as the ISAC base station providing services to multiple users employing NOMA, while communication signals is simultaneously exploited for target sensing. To maximum the communication sum-rate while satisfying the maximum Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB) requirement, a beamforming design problem is formulated. The optimization problem is inherently non-convex, which makes it challenging to find the optimal solution through traditional optimization algorithms. To address this challenge, we adopt an online decision-making framework based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to solve the problem. Numerical results indicate that the proposed NOMA-ISAC outperforms conventional ISAC in terms of sum-rate.

title: Stacked Flexible Intelligent Metasurface Design for Multi-User Wireless Communications.
abstract: Stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIMs) have recently emerged as an effective solution for next-generation wireless networks. A SIM comprises multiple metasurface layers that enable signal processing directly in the wave domain. Moreover, recent advances in flexible metamaterials have highlighted the potential of flexible intelligent metasurfaces (FIMs), which can be physically morphed to enhance communication performance. In this paper, we propose a stacked flexible intelligent metasurface (SFIM)-based communication system for the first time, where each metasurface layer is deformable to improve the system's performance. We first present the system model, including the transmit and receive signal models as well as the channel model, and then formulate an optimization problem to maximize the system sum rate under constraints on the transmit power budget, morphing distance, and the unit-modulus condition of the meta-atom responses. To solve this problem, we develop an alternating optimization framework based on the gradient projection method. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed SFIM-based system achieves significant performance gains compared to its rigid SIM counterpart.

title: Neural Network-Based Dynamic Antenna Weight Optimization Scheme for Robust Coverage Fixation in Multi-Cell HAPS Systems.
abstract: High-altitude platform stations (HAPSs) are widely recognized as key enablers of seamless global coverage across space–air–ground networks. Although a single HAPS can offer a coverage radius of up to 100 km, accommodating large numbers of users requires increasing its service-link capacity, which in turn motivates the development of multi-cell architectures with universal frequency reuse. In multi-cell systems, the service-link capacity is highly sensitive to the cell configuration, and the aircraft’s motion and attitude variations shift the cell shapes projected onto the ground (footprints), causing frequent handovers. To address this issue, we propose a neural network (NN)-based beamforming method that explicitly accounts for the implemented array antenna architecture rather than relying on beam-pattern models and directly optimizes the antenna weights to jointly configure the cells, allocate inter-cell power, and maintain fixed footprints. Simulation results show that the proposed method achieves a higher footprint-fixation rate than conventional beamforming methods and improves the median spectral efficiency by at least 21% in representative HAPS operating environments.

title: Mutual Coupling-Aware 3D Non-Stationary Channel Modeling for TRIS Transceiver Systems.
abstract: Transmissive reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (TRIS) are regarded as a promising solution for energy-efficient multi-stream transceivers in next-generation wireless communication systems, yet accurate channel modeling remains a significant challenge. Recent studies have shown that large arraybased communication channels exhibit near-field propagation characteristics and non-stationary behavior in both spatial and temporal domains. Moreover, the mutual coupling (MC) effect among array elements has a significant impact on channel characteristics. In this paper, an MC-aware three-dimensional (3D) non-stationary channel modeling framework is proposed for TRIS transceiver systems in the near-field regime. A visible-region-based clustering evolution approach is developed to capture spatiotemporal non-stationarity, while multiport network theory is employed to characterize the MC effects in TRIS arrays. Results of the spatial cross-correlation function (SCCF) and temporal autocorrelation function (TACF) demonstrate spatiotemporal consistency and reveal that MC enhances subchannel correlations. Furthermore, simulations of the root mean square (RMS) delay spread incorporating the MC effect demonstrate excellent agreement with empirical channel measurements, validating the effectiveness of the proposed channel model.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Interference Suppression in RIS-Aided Space-Air-Ground Integrated Networks.
abstract: Future 6G networks envision ubiquitous connectivity through space-air-ground integrated networks (SAGINs), where high-altitude platform stations (HAPSs) and satellites complement terrestrial systems to provide wide-area, low-latency coverage. However, the rapid growth of terrestrial devices intensifies spectrum sharing between terrestrial and non-terrestrial segments, resulting in severe cross-tier interference. In particular, frequency sharing between the HAPS satellite uplink and HAPS ground downlink improves spectrum efficiency but suffers from interference caused by the HAPS antenna back-lobe. Existing approaches relying on zero-forcing (ZF) codebooks have limited performance under highly dynamic channel conditions. To overcome this limitation, we employ a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided HAPS-based SAGIN framework with a deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm. The proposed DDPG framework optimizes the HAPS beamforming weights to form spatial nulls toward interference sources while maintaining robust links to the desired signals. Simulation results demonstrate that the DDPG framework consistently outperforms conventional ZF beamforming among different RIS configurations, achieving up to \(11.3\%\) throughput improvement for a \(4\times4\) RIS configuration, validating its adaptive capability to enhance spectral efficiency in dynamic HAPS-based SAGINs.

title: Multimodal-Wireless: A Large-Scale Dataset for Sensing and Communication.
abstract: This paper presents Multimodal-Wireless, a large-scale open-source dataset for multimodal sensing and communication research. The dataset is generated through an integrated and customizable data pipeline built upon the CARLA simulator and Sionna framework, and features high-resolution communication channel state information (CSI) fully synchronized with five other sensor modalities, namely LiDAR, RGB and depth camera, inertial measurement unit (IMU) and radar, all sampled at 100 Hz. It contains approximately 160,000 frames collected across four virtual towns, sixteen communication scenarios, and three weather conditions. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the dataset, outlining its key features, overall framework, and technical implementation details. In addition, it explores potential research applications concerning communication and collaborative perception, exemplified by beam prediction using a multimodal large language model. The dataset is open in https://le-liang.github.io/mmw/.

title: Learning-Based Resource Management and Bitrate Adaptation for UAV Video Streaming over Low-Altitude Wireless Networks.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) video streaming scheme to enhance video quality in low-altitude wireless networks. Unlike the existing fifth-generation (5G) scheduling algorithm, which relies on a fixed priority level, we propose a dynamic priority scheme that enhances video quality by adaptively adjusting the priority level based on real-time UAVs’ channel conditions and bitrate feedback. Furthermore, we formulate a long-term video quality maximization problem, which jointly optimizes resource block (RB) allocation, modulation and channel coding scheme (MCS) selection, and bitrate adaptation. Due to the coupled decision variables and nonconvexity, we design a learning-based two-layer scheduling algorithm. In the outer layer, the long-term optimization problem is reformulated as a Markov decision process, and then a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithm is proposed to determine the priority level in each time slot. In the inner layer, given the determined priority level, the optimal RB allocation, MCS selection, and bitrate adaptation decisions are derived in closed forms, thereby reducing computational complexity. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm averagely improves the video quality by 15.67% as compared to the existing 5G scheduling benchmarks.

title: FairEnergy: Contribution-Based Fairness meets Energy Efficiency in Federated Learning.
abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across distributed devices while preserving data privacy. However, balancing energy efficiency and fair participation while ensuring high model accuracy remains challenging in wireless edge systems due to heterogeneous resources, unequal client contributions, and limited communication capacity. To address these challenges, we propose FairEnergy, a fairness-aware energy minimization framework that integrates a contribution score capturing both the magnitude of updates and their compression ratio into the joint optimization of device selection, bandwidth allocation, and compression level. The resulting mixed-integer non-convex problem is solved by relaxing binary selection variables and applying Lagrangian decomposition to handle global bandwidth coupling, followed by per-device subproblem optimization. Experiments on non-IID data show that FairEnergy achieves higher accuracy while reducing energy consumption by up to 79% compared to baseline strategies.

title: Joint Beamforming and Channel Assignment via Complex-Valued Graph Neural Networks in MU-MISO Systems.
abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) have demonstrated promise for resource allocation in wireless networks by taking into account the topological structure of the network. However, a common approach processes channel state information (CSI) as real-valued features, thus discarding critical phase relationships governing interference patterns in multi-user systems. We propose Complex-Valued Graph Neural Networks (CV-GNN) for joint beamforming and channel allocation in MU-MISO systems, which preserve complete complex CSI throughout the optimization process. Our approach introduces complex-valued message passing through native complex graph convolutions, uses modReLU activation to maintain phase structure while providing non-linearity, and leverages Wirtinger calculus for efficient gradient computation in the complex domain. By embedding channels as complex-valued graph features and jointly optimizing beamforming vectors and channel assignments in the complex domain, CV-GNN naturally captures interference relationships that real-valued methods cannot represent. The joint optimization framework enables CV-GNN to learn coordinated resource allocation strategies where channel assignment decisions are informed by complex interference patterns, while beamforming design accounts for multi-channel interference coupling. The results of our simulations on MU-MISO systems with multiple resource blocks demonstrate that CV-GNN achieves superior performance as compared to other optimization approaches and real-valued baselines.

title: Collective Grid: Privacy-Preserved Multi-Operator Energy Sharing Optimization via Federated Energy Prediction.
abstract: Electricity consumption in mobile networks is increasing with the continued 5G expansion, rising data traffic, and more complex infrastructures. However, energy management is often handled independently by each mobile network operator (MNO), leading to limited coordination and missed opportunities for collective efficiency gains. To address this gap, we propose a privacy-preserving framework for automated energy infrastructure sharing among co-located MNOs. Our framework consists of three modules: (i) a federated learning-based privacy-preserving site energy consumption forecasting module, (ii) an orchestration module in which a mixed-integer linear program is solved to schedule energy purchases from the grid, utilization of renewable sources, and shared battery charging or discharging, based on real-time prices, forecasts, and battery state, and (iii) an energy source selection module which handles the selection of cost-effective power sources and storage actions based on predicted demand across MNOs for the next control window. Using data from operational networks, our experiments confirm that the proposed solution substantially reduces operational costs and outperforms non-sharing baselines, with gains that increase as network density rises in 5G-and-beyond deployments.

title: On Channel Correlation-Based Jamming Detection.
abstract: As we increasingly rely on wireless infrastructure for enabling critical applications, e.g., from Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) or healthcare, we must ensure resilience, which includes robustness against both accidental and intentional jamming attacks. Hence, awareness of the potential jamming attack information is crucial to the resilience of a fully automated system. However, channel estimation within modern communications remains highly vulnerable to such attacks. The jamming signal is considered to be projected onto the captured channels, which enables the jamming detection through channel analysis. In this work, we consider the detection of a jamming source within an indoor environment. Narrowband white Gaussian noise (WGN) is employed to jam the communications. The impact of the jamming signal on the channel measurements is analyzed by examining the correlation between the jammed and unjammed channels. Based on the correlation pattern, the presence of interference is detected through a comparative suite of statistical thresholding and machine learning algorithms. An overall detection accuracy of 99.31% is achieved, demonstrating the feasibility of jamming detection through the proposed framework.

title: An Ambiguity-Function-Assisted Newtonized Channel Estimation Method for Pulse-Shaped AFDM Under Fractional Delay and Doppler.
abstract: Accurate channel estimation for pulse-shaped AFDM systems over doubly selective channels with fractional normalized delay and Doppler remains challenging. This paper proposes a low-complexity ambiguity-function-assisted newtonized channel (AFNC) estimation method. Specifically, we first present a closed-form input-output relation for pulse-shaped affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) under fractional normalized delay and Doppler. As a further step, we demonstrate that the input-output relation admits a low-complexity representation by offline precomputing and storing the discretized ambiguity function of the shaping pulse, followed by tailored cyclic-shift and stacking operations. Building on this representation, AFNC performs fractional delay-Doppler channel estimation through Newtonized refinement, where the required Jacobian and Hessian updates are computed efficiently using the low-complexity input-output representation. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: Energy Profiling of Secure MQTT over WiFi on ESP32-Based IoT Devices.
abstract: This paper investigates the energy impact of Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol on an ESP32-based IoT system for ambient intelligence applications. The prototype integrates inertial and electrocardiogram (ECG) sensors and transmits data over WiFi using MQTT, with and without TLS. Current consumption is profiled using an INA219 sensor under varying payload sizes (158 to 4096 bytes) and transmission intervals (1 to 600 seconds). Results show that TLS introduces negligible overhead (below 2%) on average current consumption, even under frequent transmissions and large payloads. Transmission interval remains the dominant factor shaping energy consumption. Deep Sleep mode significantly extends battery life, yielding up to 75% reduction in average current for low-duty-cycle settings. The findings provide guidance for designing secure, energy-efficient IoT systems in constrained environments.

title: Comparison of OTFS and OFDM for RIS-aided Systems in the Presence of Phase Noise.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the performance of RIS-aided orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) and orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems in the presence of oscillator phase noise. OFDM is known to be sensitive to phase noise, which could limit the potential gains promised by RIS systems. OTFS, on the other hand, is a compelling potential waveform for RIS-aided systems in the presence of phase noise due to it’s resilience to time-varying channels. However, the effect of phase noise on OTFS has not been fully analyzed in the literature as of yet. Additionally, no existing works in the literature consider the effect of phase noise on an RIS-aided OTFS system. Hence, we propose a joint RIS channel and phase noise estimation technique using a Wiener filtering approach. Our proposed method exploits the statistical nature of both the phase noise and the Doppler spread channel in a setup with RIS. Our numerical analysis demonstrates the significant gain of RIS-aided OTFS offers compared to RIS-aided OFDM in the presence in the presence of phase noise. Additionally, our results demonstrate the superiority of our proposed estimation technique, with gains of up to 3 dB in terms of bit error rate (BER), over existing methods in the literature.

title: Efficient Clustered Channel Estimation via Channel Knowledge Map Constructed with Tensor Decomposition.
abstract: To address the complexity and accuracy challenges in channel estimation for massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems, conventional channel knowledge map (CKM) approaches that store multipath parameters are prone to model mismatch under clustered multipath propagation. Moreover, their reliance on fine-grained geographical grids results in high construction and storage overhead. To mitigate these issues, we propose a low-complexity CKM construction and utilization framework that leverages historical channel estimates acquired over a relatively large geographical area. A two-layer hierarchical structure is learned via tensor decomposition to characterize both the spatial and frequency subspace structures of the channel and the power distribution in the shared subspaces within this area. We further design a two-stage channel estimation scheme, which utilizes the low-rank subspaces and preprocessed correlation characteristics provided by the CKM. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves significantly improved estimation accuracy while reducing computational complexity across various conditions, offering an efficient solution for high-performance wireless communications.

title: A Digital Twin Framework for Multi-Hazard Risk Assessment in Telecommunication Infrastructure.
abstract: Digital Twin (DT) technology offers a practical and intuitive way to represent complex physical infrastructures in a continuously evolving digital form. In this study, a Digital Twin–based simulation framework is presented to jointly model and analyze the multi-hazard risk conditions of a telecommunication company’s mobile base stations and fixed domain stations within a unified Digital Twin environment. The proposed framework brings together risk information related to earthquakes, hydrological and geotechnical hazards, meteorological conditions, wildfires, planned power outages, and road accessibility. For each risk type, real-time data provided by relevant authorities at predefined update intervals are processed and spatially linked to infrastructure assets using their geographic locations. These periodically refreshed inputs are coherently integrated within the Digital Twin to describe how risk levels evolve at both site and network scales, using a weighted multi-criteria aggregation approach. Rather than relying on continuous data streams, the proposed model adopts a time-stepped update structure that reflects realistic operational practices and data availability. The resulting Digital Twin provides a coherent and scalable representation of infrastructure risk dynamics and illustrates how real-world Digital Twin simulations can support systematic risk mapping, resilience assessment, and informed decision-making for large-scale telecommunication networks operating under diverse natural and operational risk conditions.

title: Secrecy-Driven ISAC Optimization in mmWave via Twin Delayed DDPG and RIS-Assisted Beamforming.
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of secure and efficient joint beamforming and reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) phase shift optimization in an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system. We consider a downlink scenario where a multi-antenna base station (BS) serves multiple single-antenna legitimate users and simultaneously senses a target in the presence of an eavesdropper, assisted by a passive RIS. The optimization objective is to maximize the secrecy sum rate of legitimate users while ensuring sufficient power delivery to the sensing target and adhering to the BS power budget and RIS constraints. Due to the non-convex nature of the problem, we reformulate it as a Markov decision process (MDP) and propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) solution based on the Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed TD3-based approach significantly outperforms conventional DRL (DDPG) and heuristic optimization methods, achieving faster convergence and higher secrecy sum rates across varying system configurations. The proposed framework provides valuable insights for designing secure and efficient RIS-assisted ISAC systems.

title: Deep Multi-Task Learning for Joint Estimation of Impulsive Noise Parameters.
abstract: Impulsive noise poses a significant challenge to the reliability of wireless communication systems, necessitating accurate estimation of its statistical parameters for effective mitigation. This paper introduces a multitask learning (MTL) framework based on a CNN–LSTM architecture enhanced with an attention mechanism for the joint estimation of impulsive noise parameters. The proposed model leverages a unified weighted-loss function to enable simultaneous learning of multiple parameters within a shared representation space, improving learning efficiency and generalization across related tasks. Experimental results show that the proposed MTL framework achieves stable convergence, faster training, and enhanced scalability with modest computational overhead. Benchmarking against conventional single-task learning (STL) models confirms its favorable complexity–performance trade-off and significant memory savings, indicating the effectiveness of the MTL approach for real-time impulsive noise parameter estimation in wireless systems.

title: Transformer-Based Sparse CSI Estimation for Non-Stationary Channels.
abstract: Accurate and efficient estimation of Channel State Information (CSI) is critical for next-generation wireless systems operating under non-stationary conditions, where user mobility, Doppler spread, and multipath dynamics rapidly alter channel statistics. Conventional pilot aided estimators incur substantial overhead, while deep learning approaches degrade under dynamic pilot patterns and time varying fading. This paper presents a pilot-aided Flash-Attention Transformer framework that unifies model-driven pilot acquisition with data driven CSI reconstruction through patch-wise self-attention and a physics aware composite loss function enforcing phase alignment, correlation consistency, and time frequency smoothness. Under a standardized 3GPP NR configuration, the proposed framework outperforms LMMSE and LSTM baselines by approximately 13 dB in phase invariant normalized mean-square error (NMSE) with markedly lower bit-error rate (BER), while reducing pilot overhead by 16 times. These results demonstrate that attention based architectures enable reliable CSI recovery and enhanced spectral efficiency without compromising link quality, addressing a fundamental bottleneck in adaptive, low-overhead channel estimation for non-stationary 5G and beyond-5G networks.

title: Active RIS-Aided Mixed FSO-THz NOMA Network: Performance and Statistical Analysis.
abstract: We analyze the performance of a dual-hop mixed free-space optical (FSO)–Terahertz (THz) downlink system employing non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA), where the THz transmission is assisted by a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). The FSO link follows the Fisher–Snedecor $\mathcal{F}$ distribution to model moderate-to-strong turbulence, while the THz link is characterized by the α − µ distribution to capture severe fading. The probability density function of the individual THz channel with pointing errors and its generalized moments are derived. Subsequently, the cascaded THz channel via the RIS is approximated by a Gamma distribution, from which the end-to-end outage probability is obtained. The impacts of atmospheric turbulence, pointing errors, imperfect channel state information (CSI), and imperfect successive interference cancellation (SIC) are examined. Moreover, an asymptotic outage expression is derived to reveal the influence of key parameters on the outage slope. The analytical results are validated through Monte Carlo simulations.
