title: Sequential BP-based Decoding of QLDPC Codes.
abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes are a leading approach to quantum error correction, yet conventional belief propagation (BP) decoders often perform poorly, primarily due to non-convergence exacerbated by stabilizer constraints, which induce short cycles and degeneracy. We propose two scheduling variants, sequential check node scheduling (SCNS) and sequential variable node scheduling (SVNS), that improve BP’s error-correction ability by processing check nodes (CNs) or variable nodes (VNs), respectively, in a fixed order, stabilizing message updates and reducing stalls. We also employ this technique to an improved BP-variant called BP guided decimation (BPGD), where symbols are progressively fixed during decoding iterations. Here, we demonstrate that the sequential BPGD (SBPGD) decoder can further improve the convergence properties and performance of the decoder. On standard QLDPC benchmarks under a Pauli-X noise model, our sequential schedules are shown to lower the block error rate relative to conventional BP, and SBPGD outperforms BPGD while using significantly fewer decimation rounds, translating to lower computational cost. These results demonstrate that changing the update schedule, without altering the code, can improve both the reliability and efficiency of BP-based decoding for QLDPC codes. For the [[1922, 50, 16]] C2 hypergraph-product code with independent X errors, SVNS-BP surpasses BP–OSD–0 in error correction at roughly the same complexity as standard BP.

title: Distributed Continuous Aperture Arrays for Multiuser SWIPT.
abstract: This paper proposes a distributed continuous aperture array (D CAPA) to support simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) to multiple information users (IUs) and energy users (EUs). Each metasurface supports continuous surface currents that radiate electromagnetic (EM) waves for information and energy transmission to the users. These waves propagate through continuous EM channels characterized by the dyadic Green function. We formulate a system power consumption (PC) minimization problem subject to spectral efficiency and energy harvesting quality of service (QoS) requirements, where the QoS requirements are derived under the equal power allocation (EPA) scheme. An efficient two layer optimization algorithm is developed to solve this problem by optimizing the power allocation subject to the QoS violation penalties using augmented Lagrangian transformation. Our numerical results show that well optimized current distributions over each metasurface in the proposed D CAPA achieve up to 65% and 61% reductions in overall system PC compared to the EPA and colocated CAPA (C CAPA) cases, while maintaining the same total aperture size and transmission power.

title: Distributed Multi-Agent Teacher-Student DDPG for Autonomous RIS-Assisted HSR mmWave Communication.
abstract: This paper presents the novel distributed multi-agent teacher-student deep deterministic policy gradient (MATS-DDPG) framework for autonomous transmissive reconfigurable intelligent surface (ATRIS) phaseshift optimization to maximize the weighted sum-rate of users in high-speed railway (HSR) millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication systems. The frame-work features a teacher agent at the base station (BS) with MBSantennas performing beamforming optimization for C carriages each containing Kcusers, while distributed student agents located at each carriage autonomously control NcATRIS elements phaseshift through a feedback system using only a fraction of the BS-to-ATRIS channel power locally measured. The teacher shares minimal global knowledge of the environment with each student: beamforming vector and weighted sum-rate of all Kcusers per carriage. This shared information generates a $\mathcal{O}\left( {2{M_{BS}} + 1} \right)$ communication overhead for every iteration per student agent, instead of $\mathcal{O}\left( {{N_c}} \right)$ direct control signals received at each ATRIS carriage for the centralized approach. The proposed distributed MATS-DDPG with information sharing architecture achieves an optimization complexity scaling of $\mathcal{O}\left( {{{\left( {{M_{BS}}C} \right)}^2}} \right) + C \cdot \mathcal{O}\left( {{{\left( {{N_c}} \right)}^2}} \right)$ compared to centralized complexity scaling of $\mathcal{O}\left( {{{\left( {{M_{BS}}C + {N_c}C} \right)}^2}} \right)$. Extensive simulations demonstrates that MATS-DDPG achieves performance within 98% of centralized benchmarks while outperforming no information sharing variants by up to 15% in global reward, validating its effectiveness for scalable ATRIS deployment in dynamic HSR environments.

title: Semantic Communication with Hopfield Memories.
abstract: Traditional joint source-channel coding employs static learned semantic representations that cannot dynamically adapt to evolving source distributions. Shared semantic memories between transmitter and receiver can potentially enable bandwidth savings by reusing previously transmitted concepts as context to reconstruct data, but require effective mechanisms to determine when current content is similar enough to stored patterns. However, existing hard quantization approaches based on variational autoencoders are limited by frequent memory updates even under small changes in data dynamics, which leads to inefficient usage of bandwidth.To address this challenge, in this paper, a memory-augmented semantic communication framework is proposed where both transmitter and receiver maintain a shared memory of semantic concepts using modern Hopfield networks (MHNs). The proposed framework employs soft attention-based retrieval that smoothly adjusts stored semantic prototype weights as data evolves that enables stable matching decisions under gradual data dynamics. A joint optimization of encoder, decoder, and memory retrieval mechanism is performed with the objective of maximizing a reasoning capacity metric that quantifies semantic efficiency as the product of memory reuse rate and compression ratio. Theoretical analysis establishes the fundamental rate-distortion-reuse tradeoff and proves that soft retrieval reduces unnecessary transmissions compared to hard quantization under bounded semantic drift. Extensive simulations over diverse video scenarios demonstrate that the proposed MHN-based approach achieves substantial bit reductions around 14% on average and up to 70% in scenarios with gradual content changes compared to baseline.

title: Encoders, Roll Out! A Digital-Twin Enabled Multi-Modal Sensor Transfusion for Proactive I2V Beam Prediction.
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication is a key enabler of high-capacity wireless networks, particularly in infrastructure-to-vehicle (I2V) scenarios. However, mmWave links are highly susceptible to blockages, rapid channel variations, and beam misalignment, making fast and reliable beam selection essential. Conventional beam alignment based on channel estimation and exhaustive beam sweeping incurs prohibitive overhead in dynamic vehicular environments. We propose a transformer-fusion (TransFusion) architecture that functions as a Digital Twin–enabled intelligence module for proactive beam prediction in I2V mmWave networks. In utilizing synchronized multi-modal sensing, the Digital Twin maintains a virtual representation of the physical communication environment, enabling candidate beam configurations to be evaluated in the digital domain before physical actuation. TransFusion integrates camera frames, LiDAR and radar point clouds, and GPS data using modality-specific encoders and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, followed by early fusion and transformer-based refinement. Self-attention mechanisms capture long-range spatiotemporal dependencies and cross-modal interactions, enabling accurate and latency-aware beam selection in dynamic urban settings. Evaluation on real-world multi-sensor data demonstrates that Digital Twin–assisted multi-modal fusion substantially improves beam prediction performance, with the camera-GPS-lidar configuration achieving a top-3 accuracy of 90.0% and-0.009552 average actual power loss (APL). These results highlight trade-offs among predictive accuracy, computational cost, and sensing complexity, and showcase the importance of selective modality fusion for real-time, Digital Twin–enabled wireless operation.

title: Mobility-Aware Power Control for VCSEL-Based Indoor OWC.
abstract: Optical wireless communication (OWC) is a promising technology for supporting data-intensive services in indoor environments due to its large unregulated spectrum, high spatial reuse, and potential for multi-gigabit data rates. In particular, vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL) based systems enable highly directional transmission, allowing efficient spatial separation of users and improved link performance. However, the use of narrow optical beams also makes system performance highly sensitive to user mobility and device orientation, as movement directly affects beam alignment and optical channel gain. Consequently, power allocation strategies that ignore mobility dynamics often provision excess optical power to maintain reliable connectivity, resulting in inefficient energy use. In this work, a power control framework for dynamic indoor OWC networks that explicitly accounts for mobility-driven channel variation is developed. It uses a hybrid Gauss–Markov and learning-based approach that captures both user movement continuity and behaviour-driven orientation changes. The mobility states are then used to guide power allocation decisions. Simulation results show that incorporating mobility-aware channel prediction enables more accurate power allocation, and improves energy efficiency compared with conventional power control schemes in dynamic indoor environments.

title: Robust Beam Codebooks for mmWave/THz Systems: Toward a Stochastic RL Approach.
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) and terahertz (THz) massive MIMO systems often rely on predefined beamforming codebooks, which are usually suboptimal in Non-Line-of-Sight (NLoS) conditions and for hardware-limited transceivers. Reinforcement Learning (RL) enables adaptive, data-driven codebook design without explicit Channel State Information (CSI), but the robustness of such algorithms in practical conditions is underexplored. This paper introduces a robust multi-agent RL framework that learns beam codebooks directly from environmental feedback, eliminating the need for prior channel knowledge. Our method is well-suited for real-world deployments facing unpredictable propagation and hardware constraints. We conduct a comprehensive analysis of three off-policy algorithms, Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG), Twin Delayed DDPG (TD3), and Soft Actor-Critic (SAC), evaluating their resilience to hardware impairments and feedback noise. Simulations show that SAC consistently outperforms deterministic methods, achieving superior beamforming gains and stability in NLoS scenarios, even under severe impairments. These results demonstrate the promise of RL-based codebook design for robust mmWave/THz massive MIMO systems.

title: NOMA-based Joint Mode Selection and Time Allocation for Wireless Powered D2D Social Users Networks Scenarios.
abstract: Device-to-Device (D2D) social communication represents a technique having potential to tackle the challenge of the doubly-near-far scenario in wireless powered social networks (WPCN) through the utilization of social communication techniques. A framework is presented in this paper for a wireless powered communication system in which cell center users (CCUs) initially harvest energy from the radio frequency signals of the hybrid access point (HAP) before communication with cell edge social users (CEUs) through either cellular connections or D2D communication. To boost the overall throughput of the network, CCUs make use of the innovative non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) approach for interactions with CEUs. The issue is mathematically formulated as a mixed integer nonlinear programming challenge and is subsequently split into two distinct sub-problems. The primary sub-problem sets forth an optimal strategy for selecting the mode to enable effective communication between CCUs and CEUs based on the energy harvested from the HAP. Following this, the ideal allocation of time for energy harvesting and data transmission in either cellular or D2D mode is determined using the Hessian and Lagrangian techniques to enhance the performance of CCUs and CEUs, respectively. The results of the numerical analysis demonstrate that the proposed technique produces superior results in comparison to conventional NOMA and orthogonal multiple access (OMA) approaches.

title: An Energy-Efficient Resource Allocation in UAV STAR-RIS Aided Vehicular Cooperative Road Systems.
abstract: The rapid evolution of Vehicle Road Cooperative Systems (VRCS) demands high energy-efficiency to support seamless and immersive vehicular experiences to the end users. However, the emergence of Simultaneously Transmitting and Reflecting Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (STAR-RIS) offers a transformative approach to enhancing wireless communication by intelligently controlling the propagation environment. Motivated from this, in this paper, we present a framework which integrates UAV-mounted STAR-RIS with VRCS and employs Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) to optimize energy-efficient resource allocation. Specifically, a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm is designed to dynamically allocate beamforming vectors and phase-shift coefficients, thereby, maximizing system energy-efficiency while ensuring reliable quality of service. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed DRL driven STAR-RIS assisted VRCS achieves up to 38% improvement in energy-efficiency compared to baseline systems without STAR-RIS and approximately 18% improvement over conventional RIS-based approaches. These findings emphasize the potential of intelligent surface technologies combined with adaptive learning algorithms to enable sustainable, energy-efficient resource allocation in next-generation vehicular communication systems.

title: Tertiary-Mode STAR-RIS for Secure NOMA: Integrating Transmission, Reflection, and Jamming.
abstract: This paper investigates the physical layer security of a non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) system assisted by a tertiary-mode simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS), which can perform transmission, reflection, and jamming simultaneously. The system comprises a base station (BS) serving two users located on opposite sides of the STAR-RIS, assuming perfect channel state information (CSI) at the transmitter. To enhance secrecy performance, a subset of STAR-RIS elements is adaptively configured for jamming. A penalty-based alternating optimization algorithm is developed to jointly optimize the BS's active beamforming and the STAR-RIS's passive beamforming and mode selection. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed design substantially improves the achievable sum rate and secrecy performance compared to conventional RIS-assisted and no-RIS benchmarks, highlighting the potential of tertiary-mode STAR-RIS for secure and efficient next-generation wireless communications.

title: Transformer-Based CSI Prediction for FDD Wireless Backhaul Links Under Antenna Vibration.
abstract: In frequency-division duplex wireless backhaul links, feedback and processing latency can cause severe CSI mismatch under weather-induced antenna vibration (AV), where rapid antenna gain fluctuations render commonly used least-squares (LS) estimation unreliable. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a vibration-robust transformer-based CSI predictor (VRTP) that forecasts future CSI using only the transmit–receive training samples within a single frame. The key insight is that, although AV corrupts delayed CSI, the fine-grained temporal structure embedded in the training sequence itself remains informative and can be exploited for prediction. VRTP captures this structure through time-major Transformer encoding and incorporates explicit delay awareness via feature-wise linear modulation, enabling a single model to operate reliably across a wide range of prediction horizons without retraining. To further improve the estimation of low-power channel components, a lightweight mixture-of-experts (MoE) regression head with tap-dependent routing is introduced. Numerical results for a realistic mmWave backhaul scenario demonstrate that VRTP substantially reduces the CSI prediction mean-squared error compared with LS using outdated CSI, achieving gains exceeding 15 dB at long delays and maintaining strong performance advantages even at low SNR. The MoE-enhanced model provides additional improvements of nearly 2 dB at modest computational cost.

title: Microsecond Federated SVD on Grassmann Manifold for Real-time IoT Intrusion Detection.
abstract: This paper introduces FedSVD, a novel unsupervised federated learning framework for real-time anomaly detection in IoT networks. By leveraging Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) and optimization on the Grassmann manifolds, FedSVD enables accurate detection of both known and unknown intrusions without relying on labeled data or centralized data sharing. Tailored for deployment on low-power devices like the NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, the proposed method significantly reduces communication overhead and computational cost. Experimental results show that FedSVD achieves performance comparable to deep learning baselines while reducing inference latency by over 10x, making it suitable for latency-sensitive IoT applications.

title: Efficient Quantum Soft Actor-Critic Model for Dynamic Spectrum Sharing in Intelligent O-RAN.
abstract: The Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) architecture enables intelligent Dynamic Spectrum Sharing (DSS), although state-of-the-art deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods have demonstrated remarkable practical results, their integration with quantum computing brings greater potential for enhancements in performance. In this study, we present Quantum Soft Actor-Critic (QSAC), a novel hybrid quantum-classical methodology aimed at tackling barren plateaus and demonstrating enhanced performance compared to conventional DRL benchmarks, including Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) and Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3), achieving a higher demand satisfaction ratio and markedly improved ϵ-band compliance rates under demanding conditions. Additionally, we present a comprehensive architectural design for the effective integration of our framework into the O-RAN non-real-time and near-real-time RICs. Our quantum-enhanced actor significantly reduces the number of trainable actor parameters by over 99% compared to its conventional SAC equivalent (from around 73,000 to merely 377), indicating an important improvement in model efficiency. To promote repeatability and facilitate future research, we offer the open-source implementation of our study.

title: A Joint JSCC-Resource Allocation Framework for QoS-Aware Semantic Communication in LEO Satellite-based EO Missions.
abstract: In Earth observation (EO) missions with Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites, high-resolution image acquisition generates a massive data volume that poses a significant challenge for transmission under the limited satellite power budget, while LEO movement introduces dynamic systems. To enable efficient image transmission, this paper employs semantic communication (SemCom) with joint source-channel coding (JSCC), which focuses on transmitting meaningful information to reduce power consumption. Under a quality-of-service (QoS) requirement defined by image reconstruction quality, this work aims to minimize the total transmit power by jointly optimizing the JSCC encoder-decoder parameters and resource allocation. However, the implicit relationship among JSCC parameters, link quality, and image quality, coupled with the presence of mixed integer-continuous variables, makes the problem difficult to solve directly. To address this, a curve-fitting model is proposed to approximate the JSCC compression-SNR-quality relationship. Then, the joint compression ratio-resource allocation (JCRRA) algorithm is proposed to address the underlying problem. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves substantial power savings compared to both greedy algorithms and conventional transmission paradigms.

title: Quantum-Channel Matrix Optimization for Holevo Bound Enhancement.
abstract: Quantum communication holds the potential to revolutionize information transmission by enabling secure data exchange that exceeds the limits of classical systems. One of the key performance metrics in quantum information theory, namely the Holevo bound, quantifies the amount of classical information that can be transmitted reliably over a quantum channel. However, computing and optimizing the Holevo bound remains a challenging task due to its dependence on both the quantum input ensemble and the quantum channel. In order to maximize the Holevo bound, we propose a unified projected gradient ascent algorithm to optimize the quantum channel given a fixed input ensemble. We provide a detailed complexity analysis for the proposed algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed quantum channel optimization yields higher Holevo bounds than input ensemble optimization.

title: SOCP-Embedded DRL for Low-Energy Hybrid Beamforming in Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems with Imperfect CSI.
abstract: As a key technology for future 6G networks, the dense deployment of access points (APs) with digital beamforming (DBF) architecture in cell-free massive MIMO systems significantly enhances user throughput but also leads to substantial energy consumption. Hybrid beamforming (HBF) provides an effective trade-off between performance and energy consumption by reducing the number of RF chains. In practical applications, it is challenging to acquire accurate channel state information (CSI) for HBF, especially due to the large antenna arrays. Moreover, the precoder dimension of HBF becomes strongly coupled with the number of active RF chains. In this paper, the total system energy consumption is reduced in cell-free massive MIMO systems with a partially connected HBF architecture, while simultaneously satisfying user QoS requirements. Specifically, a closed-form expression for the downlink user capacity is derived based on the estimated CSI, decoupling the precoder dimension from the RF-chain configuration. Using the derived capacity expression, a low-energy optimization problem is developed, where the number of activated RF chains and the transmit power are jointly optimized. To efficiently solve the resulting mixed-integer nonlinear programming problem, a second-order cone programming–embedded DRL framework is proposed, which integrates the stability of traditional optimization and the fast decision-making of DRL, achieving faster convergence and superior performance compared with conventional DRL. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm achieves 27.2% faster convergence and 75% higher performance than conventional DRL, and further saves 85.4% and 90.4% energy compared with the full RF-chain activation and DBF schemes, respectively.

title: Improving Key Randomness in Physical-Layer Wireless Security via Semi-Synchronized RSSI and Cubic Spline Projection.
abstract: Robust security methods are crucial in wireless networks to protect sensitive data transmission and physical-layer key generation provides a novel solution for short-term session key encryption in wireless communication systems. This paper presents a new approach to key generation at the wireless physical layer using Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI). We propose a semi-synchronized algorithm to make the synchronization process less dependent on time. To enhance the randomness of generated keys, particularly in low mobility or low entropy scenarios, we introduce the Cubic Spline Projection (CSP) technique to increase the inherent randomness and range of RSSI measurements. Finally, to tackle reconciliation challenges in key generation, we employ an extended version of the Jules Sudan algorithm for error code correction. With the increased randomness from cubic spline projection, we effectively eliminate the need for a high degree of motion in physical layer-based key generation. Numerical results demonstrate that our scheme achieves high bit entropy, low bit disagreement, and reliable key generation even in environments with minimal inherent randomness.

title: On-Device AI/ML Codebook Self-Learning for Enhanced Beamforming of Network-Controlled Repeaters.
abstract: We propose a standards-compliant, artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML)-enabled codebook self-learning method for network-controlled repeaters (NCRs) that preserves the 3GPP Release-18 signalling chain while updating the NCR beam codebook entirely on-device. Our machine-learning pipeline converts discrete precoding matrix indicator (PMI) histories into a high-resolution spatial probability mass function (PMF) via kernel density estimation (KDE), then applies spherical k-means++ to extract representative directions and synthesize a new uniform planar array (UPA) codebook. Because learning runs inside the NCR, no new messages or gNodeB (gNB)–NCR codebook synchronization are required. Using a Hongdae 3D urban digital twin with ray-tracing channels, we quantify gains over a conventional discrete fourier transform (DFT) codebook: the ML-updated codebook produces beams that consistently improve beamforming gain and throughput across codebook sizes, with pronounced sum-rate increases when indoor users dominate. These results show that PMI-driven, ML-based NCR adaptation can significantly enhance the indoor coverage and system sum-rate without any air-interface changes, offering a practical building block for next-generation repeater-assisted deployments.

title: Proof of Concept of QCSP Frames in Earth-to-LEO Satellite Transmission.
abstract: In this paper, we report on a multi-site experiment involving the transmission of a new type of frame for IoT, called Quasi-Cyclic Short Packet (QCSP). QCSP frames are characterized by the combination of a q-ary modulation using Cyclic Code Shift Keying (CCSK) and a q-ary non-binary Error Correction Code (ECC). A QCSP frame does not contain a preamble, making it energy-optimal since no resources are wasted for signaling. However, this absence poses a significant challenge for detection and synchronization, particularly in the case of a LEO satellite, which is subject to strong and fast-varying Doppler shifts. Our experiment demonstrates that such transmission can be successfully recovered.

title: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning with Local-Reconstruction Error-Feedback-Based Rescaled 1-Bit Compressive Sensing.
abstract: Federated learning (FL) is well-suited for the next-generation networks, but it is often constrained by the communication cost of repeatedly transmitting high-dimensional updates. Compressive sensing (CS) alleviates this limitation by utilizing a short measurement vector; however, low-dimensional projection and coarse quantization, especially the 1-bit CS (1BCS), can lead to reconstruction errors that slow down convergence. Therefore, we propose local reconstruction error feedback (LREF), where each device performs 1BCS reconstruction locally to feed back not only the sparsification residual but also the reconstruction discrepancy, and introduce the rescaled 1BCS (R1BCS), which uses a magnitude scalar to rescale the unit sparse gradient estimated from the 1-bit measurement vector. We provide upper bounds on the convergence rate, along with the required constraints to ensure the performance of the proposed design. In experiments, R1BCS-LREF approaches the ideal case (i.e., no reconstruction error) while significantly reducing the cost, confirming that the proposed design effectively counters the reconstruction error.

title: A Federated and Self-Adaptive Generative Adversarial-Based Framework for Real-Time Sensor Anomaly Detection in Human Digital Twins.
abstract: This paper introduces a new federated and self-adaptive generative adversarial network (GAN)-enabled framework, called FedSAGE, for real-time anomaly detection in human digital twin (HDT) networks. Designed for sensor anomaly detection within such distributed environments, FedSAGE adopts federated multi-task learning (FML) to facilitate a self-adaptive GAN, necessary to support local representation learning, data generation and robust anomaly detection. The framework operates in two phases: a collaborative federated adversarial training phase, where local autoencoders and GANs learn from decentralized sensor data without raw data exchange; and an anomaly detection operation phase, where real-time anomaly detection is performed using enhanced local models. Extensive performance evaluations conducted on multivariate sensor data demonstrate FedSAGE’s superiority over commonly adopted traditional methods. Results show significant improvements, including better accuracy, high sample quality and communication efficiency. Overall, FedSAGE is shown to be capable of supporting real-time decision-making in dynamic HDT environments while ensuring low overhead and enhanced privacy. The proposed framework proves highly effective for scalable and decentralized anomaly detection in this emerging cyber-physical system.

title: Experimental Analysis of a Bidirectional Air-to-Ground Optical Communication Link.
abstract: Under the German QuNET initiative, Key Exper iment 3 investigates the integration of dynamic mobile nodes into future quantum networks using airborne optical links as an intermediate step to satellite-based scenarios. The experiment aims to demonstrate the applicability of different quantum key distribution (QKD) technologies over long-distance mobile links. The German Aerospace Center (DLR) contributes with the Free-Space Experimental Laser Terminal 2 (FELT-II) and a bidirectional classical optical link, which is essential for both data transmission and tracking operations. This paper presents a preliminary experimental analysis of the classical communication channel during the flight campaign conducted in Erlangen in September and October of 2025. Performance metrics at both the physical layer (received signal strength indicator (RSSI), signal to-noise ratio (SNR)) and data layer (raw and coded bit error rate (BER), round trip times (RTT)) are evaluated under varying day-time and night-time conditions. The results are in line with the expected performance for scientific data transmission and these are subject to limitations arising from the pointing, turbulence and ambient light. These factors particularly affect the stability required for reliable bidirectional communication in air-to-ground link scenarios.

title: AFDM-guided Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding for Satellite Communication.
abstract: As a key technology for next generation networks, satellite communication faces challenges due to constrained spectrum and interference. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding framework guided by Affine Frequency Division Multiplexing (AFDM-JSCC). To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to seamlessly integrate the AFDM waveform into an end-to-end JSCC architecture. This integration leverages JSCC to improve transmission efficiency while specifically mitigating the performance degradation observed in conventional OFDM-based semantic systems over time-frequency robustness against such channel effects, we further design a channel state information encoder and a novel deep learning-based channel compensation module. We conduct extensive simulations in satellite channels. Results demonstrate that the proposed AFDM-JSCC maintains superior performance compared with benchmarks and demonstrating significant resilience under high Doppler conditions.

title: Energy-Efficient UAV Trajectory and Beamforming Optimizations for mURLLC-Driven AirComp Over ISAC-Enabled Networks.
abstract: To meet the stringent latency and reliability demands of future 6G networks, this paper presents a communication-efficient and energy-aware optimization framework for UAV-assisted over-the-air federated learning (Air-FL) systems under massive ultra-reliable and low-latency communication (mURLLC) constraints. The proposed system enables distributed AI/ML at the edge by integrating UAV-enabled cellfree MIMO access with ISAC-based channel estimation and model aggregation via over-the-air computation (AirComp). We formulate a joint resource management problem involving UAV trajectory control, mobile users (MUs) transmit power allocation, and UAV access points (APs) receive beamforming design, aiming to minimize a weighted sum of AirComp aggregation error and UAV energy consumption, while satisfying mURLLC delay and reliability constraints. To tackle the resulting non-convexity, an alternating optimization strategy is adopted: closed-form solutions are derived for power control and beamforming, while UAV trajectories are predicted using a lightweight Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) model. Simulation results show that the proposed framework significantly improves accuracy of FL task and energy efficiency over benchmark methods, demonstrating its potential for scalable and communication-efficient edge intelligence in time-critical wireless learning scenarios.

title: Importance-Driven Resource Management for MIMO-OFDM Semantic Communications.
abstract: This paper proposes a novel importance-aware quantization, subcarrier mapping, and power allocation (IA-QSMPA) framework for semantic communication in multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) systems, powered by a pretrained Vision Transformer (ViT). The proposed framework leverages attention-based importance extracted from a pretrained ViT to jointly optimize quantization levels, subcarrier mapping, and power allocation. To this end, an optimization problem is formulated which maps semantically important features to high-quality subchannels, while allocating resources according to their contribution to task performance and transmission latency. To solve the resulting nonconvex optimization problem, a block coordinate descent algorithm is developed. Simulation results on multi-view image classification demonstrate that IA-QSMPA consistently outperforms conventional baselines in ideal transmission settings, offering superior task performance and reduced communication latency.

title: A Unified AI-Native 6G Architecture for 3GPP AI Use Cases: Systematic Categorization and Identification of Gaps in Specifications.
abstract: Sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks require a fundamental transformation of the traditional connectivity-oriented design into an intelligence-centric blueprint, in anticipation of a plethora of upcoming artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities and applications to be offered, such as those described in the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) Technical Report (TR) 22.870. This paper performs a systematic categorization of the 61 AI use cases in 3GPP TR 22.870 (v1.0.1) into 10 functional domains based on their primary AI function, deployment characteristics, and network requirements. The analysis gives rise to a unified AI-native architecture for 6G networks, for which the following seven architectural components are considered to be essential for the studied use cases: Service Hosting Environment (SHE) for distributed AI execution, Network Data Analytics Function (NWDAF) for predictive analytics, Network Knowledge Exposure Function (NKEF) for third-party AI integration, Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) function for network-native processing of sensing information, AI agent framework (AAF) for autonomous service orchestration, federated learning infrastructure for privacy-preserving collaboration, and semantic communication protocol implementation for bandwidth efficiency. Finally, with respect to the future standardization activities deemed imperative for fully realizing this architecture, we identify four critical gaps in the current specifications: (1) lack of a standardized agent authentication framework affecting 15 use cases, (2) undefined privacy guarantees for federated learning affecting 10 use cases, (3) missing semantic communication protocols limiting cooperative perception, (4) incomplete explainability requirements vital for safety-critical systems.

title: Volumetric Near-Field Beamfocusing via Zernike Phase Tapering.
abstract: This paper develops the foundational framework for three-dimensional (3D) near-field beamfocusing, termed as volumetric near-field beamfocusing, using uniform rectangular arrays (URAs). We first analyze matched filter (MF) beam-forming, and derive closed-form expressions for the lateral and axial resolutions around a target focal point. The analysis reveals that MF achieves strong lateral intensity but inherently produces an axially elongated focal region, which limits its compact volumetric energy concentration. This demonstrates that existing beamfocusing techniques in literature are primarily two-dimensional (2D) beamfocusing or spot beams, not truly 3D focused beams. To overcome this, we introduce a novel Zernike-based phase tapering approach, inspired by optical aberration correction. By incorporating fourth-order Zernike modes, the extended axial structure is reshaped into a sharper volumetric focus. Both analytical derivations and numerical simulations with URAs of practical dimensions confirm that Zernike-based tapering enhances volumetric focusing and reduces focal depth (approximately up to 73 times) and incurs only a moderate reduction in peak intensity (approximately 1.5 dB) compared to conventional MF. These findings establish phase-domain tapering via Zernike polynomials as a foundational tool for compact volumetric beamfocusing. It also opens up a plethora of promising applications for near-field wireless communications, sensing, and localization systems that require precise energy confinement in three dimensions.

title: Joint Beamforming and Telescopic STAR-RIS Design for NOMA-ISAC: A WMMSE Approach.
abstract: We study an integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) system assisted by a novel telescopic simultaneous transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface (TSTAR-RIS). This surface features per-element height control, providing an additional physical degree of freedom to jointly tune the effective aperture and phase response across its transmit and reflect halves. We consider a RIS-only (no direct BS-UE link) scenario using downlink power-domain NOMA and passive echo-based sensing. We formulate a constrained utility maximization to jointly optimize the communication sum-rate and a sensing-SINR-based utility, subject to hardware constraints including finite-bit quantization, passive energy splitting, and mechanical height limits. To tackle the nonconvex couplings, we propose a three-block alternating optimization (AO) algorithm: (i) the downlink data precoder is updated via the weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE) method to maximize sum-rate; (ii) the dedicated sensing beamformer is updated via projected gradient (PG) to maximize the sensing utility; and (iii) the TSTAR-RIS coefficients and element heights are jointly optimized via PG with Armijo backtracking to maximize the total ISAC utility. Simulations are conducted for a fair comparison where both TSTAR and a conventional non-telescopic (NTSTAR) baseline use the same random, uneven user distributions and channel realizations. Results demonstrate that the proposed TSTAR-RIS consistently outperforms the NTSTAR baseline.

title: Adaptive Feature Selection for Efficient Task-Oriented Semantic Communications.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate point-to-point (P2P) task-oriented semantic communication (SemCom) for image classification using joint source-channel coding (JSCC) with deep neural networks (DNNs). Unlike existing methods, our joint source-channel encoder at the transmitter employs a novel feature map selector enabled by attention mechanism-based learnable pruning functions, allowing for dynamic pruning of feature maps according to both their semantic importance and the channel signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). The proposed approach not only efficiently reduces the overall transmitted data volume without degrading classification accuracy but also supports flexibly adjustable feature pruning under varying channel conditions. Simulation results of an ablation study on two public datasets verify the advantages of the learnable pruning function over its non-learnable counterpart in selecting semantically important features. In addition, our proposed approach consistently outperforms several baseline schemes in terms of classification accuracy, adaptability to channel variations, generalizability of the model, and data transmission efficiency.

title: Robust Multimodal Semantic Communications with Semantic Fusion and Compensation.
abstract: Semantic communication has demonstrated significant potential to improve communication network performance. However, ensuring robustness in multimodal semantic communication remains challenging due to both physical and semantic impairments, with the latter largely underexplored. In this paper, we investigate multimodal semantic impairments and propose a novel framework for robust multimodal semantic communications. We introduce a performance metric to quantify semantic impairments and construct a corresponding dataset for validation. Moreover, we design DeepSC-RM, a deep learning enabled semantic communication system, which integrates an adaptive multimodal semantic fusion module to dynamically combine information across modalities, a multimodal joint semantic–channel codec for symbol-level transmission, and a cross-modal semantic compensation module at the receiver to enhance accurate semantic interpretation. Experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed DeepSC-RM, confirming its effectiveness in mitigating semantic impairments and achieving robust multimodal transmission.

title: Error-Aware Super-Resolution Channel Estimation for RIS-Aided Multi-User mmWave Systems.
abstract: In this paper, we propose an effective two-stage error-aware super-resolution channel estimation method for reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided multi-user (MU) millimeter wave (mmWave) systems based on the ambiguity and correlation of the cascaded channel matrices. From the estimation framework perspective, in Stage I, the method estimates the ambiguous RIS-base station channel by exploiting the MU diversity gain, while in Stage II, it not only estimates the ambiguous user-RIS channels with reduced pilots, but more importantly, explicitly and adaptively estimates and compensates for the estimation errors propagated from Stage I, thereby improving the estimation accuracy of channel parameters in Stage I and consequently enhancing the overall estimation performance. Accordingly, to achieve error-aware super-resolution estimation within the framework, the proposed method introduces the smooth approximation of the lpnorm and dynamic grids to formulate the channel parameter estimation in Stage II as tractable joint sparse recovery and perturbed dictionary adaptation problems, which are iteratively solved using a developed majorization-minimization-based alternating minimization algorithm. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Self-Supervised Deep Learning Design for MU-SIMO Beyond-Diagonal RIS.
abstract: Beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (BD-RISs) have emerged as a promising technology for wireless communications. BD-RIS enhances the capabilities of conventional RIS architectures by enabling full coupling among surface elements connected by adjustable reactances. However, leveraging such extended flexibility requires effectively addressing the added complexity in optimization tasks. In this paper, we propose a self-supervised (SS) deep learning (DL) approach for BD-RIS optimization in multi-user (MU) single-input multiple-output (SIMO) uplink systems. Unlike supervised methods that require expensive optimization solvers for training labels, the learning process of our approach is guided by a loss function derived from the optimization objective function. The proposed neural network (NN) model learns to map the channel state information (CSI) to the BD-RIS scattering matrices that maximize the system sum-rate, while guaranteeing the matrices’ structural constraints. Simulation results show that our approach outperforms traditional optimization-based methods in realistic 3GPP channels, while exhibiting lower computational complexity and maintaining comparable user fairness to state-of-the-art baselines.

title: Joint Time Allocation, Beamforming, and Antenna Location for Pinching Antenna-assisted Downlink Multiuser Systems.
abstract: In this paper, we jointly optimize the time allocation, beamforming, and antenna's locations to maximize the total throughput of all users in pinching antenna (PA)-assisted downlink multiuser systems. The problem is constrained by the limited power budget at the base station, the minimal distances between the PAs, and the minimum throughput of each user. The considered problem is inherently nonconvex due to the complex channel structure and the couplings of variables in the user throughput expressions. To address this, we propose an alternating optimization method to separate the problem into three subproblems that utterly depend on the fractional-time allocation, beamforming, and PA locations, respectively. These subproblems are then tackled by direct solutions, successive convex algorithm, and Armijo backtracking in augmented Lagrangian expression. Simulation results validate the superior performance of our proposed algorithm compared to the baseline methods and highlight its potential for practical implementation.

title: Distributed Semantic Alignment over Interference Channels: A Game-Theoretic Approach.
abstract: Semantic communication acts as a key enabler for effective task execution in AI-driven systems, prioritizing the extraction of the underlying meaning before transmission. However, when devices rely on different logic and internal representations, semantic mismatches may arise, potentially hindering mutual understanding and effectiveness of communication. Furthermore, in interference channel environments, the coexistence of multiple devices introduce a significant degradation due to the presence of multi-user-interference. To address these challenges, in this paper we formulate the joint optimization of linear Multiple-Input-Multiple-Output (MIMO) transceivers as a distributed non-cooperative game, enabling a closed-form solution that effectively addresses semantic coexistence and latent space misalignment. We derive sufficient conditions for the existence of a Nash Equilibrium (NE), considering multiple point-to-point MIMO channels, with corresponding users modeled as selfish players optimizing their transmission and semantic alignment strategies. Numerical results substantiate the proposed approach in goal-oriented semantic communication by highlighting crucial trade-offs between information compression, interference mitigation, semantic alignment, and task performance.

title: Dynamic-Attention Networks for Robust Channel Estimation in Mobility Scenarios.
abstract: In sixth-generation (6G) wireless communication networks, high mobility and Doppler effects pose significant challenges to reliable channel estimation, particularly in time-varying conditions. To overcome this limitation, we propose a Dynamic-Attention Channel Estimator (DyACE), which leverages mobility information to adaptively enhance channel estimation in dynamic environments. DyACE consists of a main network for channel estimation and an auxiliary mobility feature encoder (MFE) that extracts mobility-related features. By leveraging input-related attention scores predicted from the MFE, the DyACE pipeline achieves adaptive parameter adjustment, which facilitates accurate tracking of rapidly time-varying channels. Simulation results show that DyACE achieves consistently superior estimation accuracy compared with both traditional and learning-based baselines. Moreover, extensive generalization experiments demonstrate that DyACE maintains robust performance across diverse velocity profiles and unseen channel scenarios, confirming its effectiveness as a scalable solution for next-generation mobility wireless systems.

title: Indoor and Outdoor Continuous-Space Channel Measurements and Characterization for 6G Wireless Communication Systems.
abstract: Conventional wireless communication channel measurements and modeling typically study channels via discrete spatial sampling. As the sixth-generation (6G) wireless communication places higher demands on the accuracy of channel state information (CSI), this discrete approximation becomes insufficient and motivates research on continuous-space channels. In this work, indoor and outdoor continuous-space channel measurements are conducted at 28 GHz and 10GHz, respectively. Channel characteristics such as multipath components (MPCs) birth-death process, delay spread (DS), and sum-capacity are further analyzed. Based on the analysis, the necessity of continuous-space channel research is confirmed, and the key role of accurate channel knowledge in 6G systems is demonstrated.

title: Impulse-Pilot-Aided OMP Channel Estimation for SEFDM-Based OTFS Systems.
abstract: Orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation offers robust performance over doubly selective channels, yet its spectral efficiency is constrained by the conventional orthogonal subcarrier spacing. To address this limitation, spectrally efficient frequency division multiplexing (SEFDM)-based OTFS intentionally compresses the subcarrier spacing in time-frequency domain to enhance spectral efficiency while retaining the delay-Doppler characteristics of OTFS, at the cost of inherent inter-carrier interference. In this paper, we propose an OMP-based sparse channel estimation framework for SEFDM-based OTFS using an impulse-pilot block at the transmitter. We obtain the corresponding dictionary by deriving the delay-Doppler (DD) domain input-output relationship of the SEFDM-based OTFS system, and address the colored-noise issue induced by subcarrier compression by adopting generalized least squares. Moreover, we derive both the Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB) with unknown support and the oracle CRLB with known support as theoretical performance benchmarks for the proposed channel estimation algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm closely approaches the oracle CRLB and exhibits negligible performance variation across different packing factors.

title: Lending a Hand: Cooperative Active-Passive Uplink Offloading for Low-Power MEC Networks.
abstract: This paper proposes a decode-and-forward (DF) cooperative relaying architecture for uplink task offloading in hybrid active–passive access mobile edge computing (HAPA-MEC) networks. In conventional HAPA systems, the active device (AD) mainly serves as a controllable radio-frequency exciter for the passive backscatter device (BD), leaving the BD reliant on a single backscatter link with limited reliability and throughput. To overcome this limitation, we allow the AD to play a dual role as both an exciter and an information-level cooperative relay for the BD’s offloaded data. In addition, a hybrid active–passive mode-switching protocol is introduced at the BD to provide more flexible offloading opportunities under varying energy conditions. Based on this architecture, we formulate a joint optimization problem to maximize the BD throughput by jointly designing the transmit power, time allocation, reflection coefficients, and receive beamforming, subject to energy-harvesting, peak-power, and quality-of-service constraints. To handle the resulting non-convex coupled problem, we develop an efficient iterative algorithm with closed-form updates for key decision variables. Simulation results verify that the proposed cooperative relaying design significantly improves the BD throughput over benchmark schemes while satisfying system constraints.

title: The Explicit Capacity Region of Deterministic Broadcast Channels: A Bipartite Graph Approach.
abstract: The general broadcast channel (BC) has attracted considerable attention because it is a central problem in network information theory. The deterministic BC (det-BC), in which both output symbols are functions of the input symbol, plays a vital role in studying general BCs. Although the capacity region of det-BCs was revealed independently by Marton and Pinsker in the 1970s, it is expressed as functions of the entropy of output symbols. Based on their result, one must optimize the probability distribution of input symbols numerically to determine the capacity region for general det-BCs. The explicit capacity region remains unknown, except for special cases such as the Blackwell channel. In this paper, we present the explicit capacity region of general det-BCs using a bipartite graph approach. We show that each det-BC can be uniquely and completely characterized by a bipartite graph. Each point on the capacity region boundary is expressed as an explicit function of the degree sequences of the two parts, with boundary coordinates parameterized by the tangent slope. Numerical results validate the explicit capacity region.

title: Secure Transmission via Sub-Symbol Precoding and Port Switching in Fluid Antenna System.
abstract: The fluid antenna (FA) has emerged as a promising technology for enhancing wireless network performance due to its ability to dynamically adjust antenna positions and mitigate poor channel conditions. In this paper, we propose an FA-aided secure transmission scheme where the transmitter, equipped with an FA, intends to send confidential information to a legitimate receiver under the eavesdropping of multiple illegitimate receivers. To overcome the limited beamforming dimensionality, each symbol duration is divided into several sub-symbol periods, during which the FA activates different ports corresponding to varying legitimate and eavesdropping channel conditions. This dynamic switching enhances spatial degrees of freedom (DoF). During each sub-symbol period, the FA transmits a superposition of useful sig- nal and random noise with fine-tuned precoding factors, ensuring that the noise degrades eavesdropping channels while minimally affecting the legitimate channel. We consider a practical scenario where imperfect eavesdropping channel state information (ECSI) is available. A worst-case secrecy rate maximization problem is formulated via jointly optimizing the precoding factors, power allocation, and the receive beamforming vector. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed scheme significantly improves secrecy performance compared to traditional secure schemes.

title: Polarization MIMO Tradeoffs for Commercial Millimeter Wave Systems.
abstract: Commercial deployments of millimeter wave user equipments (UEs) use dual-polarized antenna arrays/modules that are carefully placed on the UE to enhance spherical coverage performance. Spherical coverage is a popular design metric that captures the effective isotropic radiated power (EIRP) distribution over a sphere around the UE. However, it is a diversity (or rank-1) metric as it only captures the cumulated energy across polarizations. Peak spectral efficiencies with these UEs are realized with rank-2 polarization multi-input multi-output (MIMO) schemes. In this work, we first theoretically illustrate the structure of optimal beamforming vectors for peak spectral efficiency performance. From this structure, we establish how the correlation between co- and cross-polarization steering vectors at different angles of departure (AoD) and angles of arrival (AoA) relative to the arrays’ boresight directions impact polarization MIMO performance. Then, we study the impact of two typically realized antenna module placements in practical UE designs on the spectral efficiency with polarization MIMO. From this study, we show that antenna module placements in commercial UE designs lead to good polarization MIMO performance.

title: Measurement Strategies and Estimation Precision in Quantum Network Tomography.
abstract: This work investigates measurement strategies for link parameter estimation in Quantum Network Tomography (QNT), where network links are modeled as depolarizing quantum channels distributing Werner states. Three distinct measurement schemes are analyzed: local Z-basis measurements (LZM), joint Bell-state measurements (JBM), and pre-shared entanglement-assisted measurements (PEM). For each scheme, we derive the probability distributions of measurement outcomes and examine how noise in the distributed states influences estimation precision. Closed-form expressions for the Quantum Fisher Information Matrix (QFIM) are obtained, and the estimation precision is evaluated through the Quantum Cramer-Rao Bound (QCRB). Numerical analysis reveals that the PEM scheme achieves the lowest QCRB, offering the highest estimation accuracy, while JBM provides a favorable balance between precision and implementation complexity. The LZM method, although experimentally simpler, exhibits higher estimation error relative to the other schemes; however, it outperforms JBM in high-noise regimes for single-link estimation. We further evaluate the estimation performance on a four-node star network by comparing a JBM-only configuration with a hybrid configuration that combines JBM and LZM. When two monitors are used, the JBM-only strategy outperforms the hybrid approach across all noise regimes. However, with three monitors, it achieves a lower QCRB only in low-noise regimes with heterogeneous links. The results establish a practical basis for selecting measurement strategies in experimental quantum networks, enabling more accurate and scalable link parameter estimation under realistic noise conditions.

title: Reliable IoT Communications in 6G Non-Terrestrial Networks with Dual RIS.
abstract: The increasing demand for Internet of Things (IoT) applications has accelerated the need for robust resource allocation in sixth-generation (6G) networks. In this paper, we propose a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted upper mid-band communication framework. To ensure robust connectivity under severe line-of-sight (LoS) blockages, we use a two-tier RIS structure comprising terrestrial RISs (TRISs) and high-altitude platform station (HAPS)-mounted RISs (HRISs). To maximize network sum rate, we formulate a joint beamforming, power allocation, and IoT device association (JBPDA) problem as a mixed-integer nonlinear program (MINLP). The formulated MINLP problem is challenging to solve directly; therefore, we tackle it via a decomposition approach. The zero-forcing (ZF) technique is used to optimize the beamforming matrix, a closed-form expression for power allocation is derived, and a stable matching-based algorithm is proposed for device-RIS association based on achievable data rates. Comprehensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed scheme approaches the performance of exhaustive search (ES) while exhibiting substantially lower complexity, and it consistently outperforms greedy search (GS) and random search (RS) baselines. Moreover, the proposed scheme converges much faster than the ES scheme.

title: Dual-Tier IRS-Assisted Mid-Band 6G Mobile Networks: Robust Beamforming and User Association.
abstract: The rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) applications necessitates robust resource allocation in future sixth-generation (6G) networks, particularly at the upper mid-band (7-15 GHz, FR3). This paper presents a novel intelligent reconfigurable surface (IRS)-assisted framework combining terrestrial IRS (TIRS) and aerial IRS (AIRS) mounted on low-altitude platform stations, to ensure reliable connectivity under severe line-of-sight (LoS) blockages. Distinguishing itself from prior work restricted to terrestrial IRS and mmWave/THz bands, this work targets the FR3 spectrum, the so-called "Golden Band" for 6G. The joint beamforming and user association (JBUA) problem is formulated as a mixed-integer nonlinear program (MINLP), solved through problem decomposition, zero-forcing beamforming, and a stable matching algorithm. Comprehensive simulations show our method approaches exhaustive search performance with significantly lower complexity, outperforming existing greedy and random baselines. These results provide a scalable blueprint for real-world 6G deployments, supporting massive IoT connectivity in challenging environments.

title: Performance Analysis of ORIS-Assisted UOWC System over Turbulence with Pointing Errors.
abstract: This paper investigates performance of an optical reconfigurable intelligent surface (ORIS)-assisted underwater optical wireless communication (UOWC) system under Gamma-Gamma oceanic turbulence and pointing errors. Exact closed-form expressions for outage probability and ergodic capacity are derived and validated through extensive Monte Carlo simulations with 107channel realizations. Subsequently, the ORIS-assisted system and a conventional decode-and-forward (DF) relay-assisted UOWC system are compared across different turbulence levels, pointing error severities, and numbers of reflecting elements. The results reveal that the ORIS-assisted system consistently outperforms the DF relay approach, offering notable improvements in both outage probability and ergodic capacity, particularly under harsh oceanic conditions. The outage results are also consistent with asymptotic predictions at high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and ORIS effectively enhances ergodic capacity by mitigating impairments passively without introducing additional noise. The close agreement between analytical and simulation results confirms the accuracy of the developed models and the predicted diversity order.

title: An Enhanced Authentication Scheme for Cellular Communications based on PHY History.
abstract: Security of data transmitted over wireless links is typically dependent on bit-level encryption performed by higher layers of the network stack. This typically involves encryption keys exchanged between the communicating entities as part of an authentication process. The authentication process in a cellular network starts with the transmission of the international mobile subscriber identity (IMSI), which is not encrypted. This is followed by an authentication request and authentication response based on a mutually known secret code associated with the IMSI. An advancement in 5G NR is that the IMSI is replaced with SUCI (Subscriber concealed Identity) which is the encrypted version of the IMSI. With recent advancements in computing power and resources, the probabilities of breaching the authentication process and the consequent vulnerabilities to interception, denial of service and breach of data security have increased multi-fold. Proliferation of IMSI/SUCI catchers and man-in-the-middle interceptors devices enable spoofing and denial of service capabilities to even novice hackers. One of the ways to enhance the security of data over in the presence of adverse nodes is to tighten the authentication process based on logs of past events in encrypted formats, similar to multi-factor authentication used by financial institutions. One of the aspects in wireless communications that cannot be cloned with ease is the physical air interface, whose parameters are exchanged between the network and the user equipment. In this paper, we propose a novel enhancement to the authentication scheme by complementing the exchange of existing authentication parameters with cryptographic hashes of PHY parameters from previous connections. The exchange of hashes does not expose the hidden history owing to their irreversibility but verifies the authenticity of the peer node hereby increasing resilience to spoofing and man-in-the-middle interception.

title: A Multi-Class Autoencoder Framework for Wiretap Code Design.
abstract: In modern wireless communications, an increasing number of devices operate under simultaneous reliability and confidentiality constraints. In information theory, there exists an intrinsic block error rate (BLER)–information leakage (IL) trade-off for finite-blocklength wiretap coding; our goal is to optimize performance on this frontier. Prior neural approaches typically adopt a multi-label bit-reconstruction formulation. We instead introduce a multi-class autoencoder that treats each message as a single class, optimizing reliability with categorical cross-entropy and constraining secrecy via an analytical upper bound on information leakage. We also present a normalization-based variant that improves overall performance and robustness to SNR mismatch. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme consistently advances the BLER–IL Pareto boundary, outperforming state-of-the-art multi-label formulations.

title: On the Minimum Distances of Finite-Length Lifted Product Quantum LDPC Codes.
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is critical for the practical realization of fault-tolerant quantum computing and quantum communication systems. Recently proposed families of quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes are prime candidates for advanced QEC hardware architectures. This paper focuses on finite-length QLDPC code design criteria, specifically aimed at constructing degenerate quasi-cyclic symmetric lifted-product (LP-QLDPC) codes with high minimum distances. We describe necessary conditions to ensure that the designed LP-QLDPC codes have a minimum distance strictly greater than the minimum weight stabilizer generators, thus ensuring superior error correction performance. The focus of the paper is on LP-QLDPC codes built from quasi-cyclic base codes belonging to the class of type-1 protographs, and the necessary constraints are efficiently expressed in terms of row and column indices of the base parity check matrix. This gives us combinatorial constraints - termed as Row-Column Partition Constraints (RCPC) - on classical quasi-cyclic base matrices to construct degenerate LP-QLDPC codes. For type-1 protographs, RCPC constraints provide an efficient certification approach to designing good codes, and we also give exhaustive search evidence on small base matrices. Simulations with BP+OSD decoding demonstrate significant logical error-rate gains when RCPC is avoided. We discuss extensions to circuit-level noise and outline sufficient conditions and research directions for exact distance preservation.

title: Quantum Graph Neural Network for Joint Optimization of Pinching and Fluid Antenna Systems.
abstract: This work optimizes a flexible antenna environment, that incorporates both pinching antenna systems (PASS) and fluid antenna systems (FAS) at the transmitter and the user sides. Optimizing PASS and FAS presents a non-trivial challenge, as the wireless network exhibits a highly dynamic topology and an extensive solution search space. To address this, this work proposes a quantum graph neural network (QGNN)based solution workflow designed to optimize the user’s quality of service by learning the spatial and structural dependencies between the pinching antenna elements and user ports as a quantum state. The QGNN approach encodes the wireless network topology, encompassing both edge and vertex relationships, into the quantum state space, and performs optimization through a tunable single-qubit rotation gate. Overall, the QGNN-based solution shows a faster loss reduction, especially during the early learning episodes, compared to the benchmark model. The QGNN achieves an average training loss approximately 3.4× lower than that of the typical parameter quantum circuit model during model training. In summary, this work points out the feasibility of applying graph-based, data-driven learning, realized through the quantum graph neural network workflow, to the problem of flexible antenna optimization.

title: BER Analysis of Zak-OTFS Using Zero-Forcing Equalization Under Perfect and Imperfect CSI.
abstract: The bit error rate (BER) of Zak orthogonal time-frequency space (Zak-OTFS) modulation using zero-forcing (ZF) equalization over doubly dispersive wireless channels is analyzed. A closed-form BER expression is derived by exploiting the block-circulant structure of the Zak-OTFS channel matrix in the delay-Doppler (DD) domain, enabling an eigenvalue-based representation through discrete Fourier transform diagonalization. To assess its robustness under practical conditions, the analysis is further extended to account for imperfect channel state information (CSI) using an estimation error model. Increasing the number of paths enhances the diversity gain and strengthens effective eigenvalues, hence improving BER performance. In the crystalline regime, the eigenvalue spread narrows, yielding stable and predictable BER. The results demonstrate that Zak-OTFS outperforms the multicarrier OTFS (MC-OTFS) and maintains consistent BER in high-mobility scenarios. However, the channel estimation errors reduce the effective SNR and distort the DD-domain eigenvalues, hence causing higher error floors at high SNR.

title: Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning for Low-Carbon P2P Energy Trading among Self-Interested Microgrids.
abstract: Uncertainties in renewable generation and demand dynamics challenge day-ahead scheduling. To enhance renewable penetration and maintain intra-day balance, we develop a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for self-interested microgrids participating in peer-to-peer (P2P) electricity trading. Each microgrid independently bids both price and quantity while optimizing its own profit via storage arbitrage under time-varying main-grid prices. A market-clearing mechanism coordinating trades and promoting incentive compatibility is proposed. Simulation results show that the learned bidding policy improves renewable utilization and reduces reliance on high-carbon electricity, while increasing community-level economic welfare, delivering a win–win situation in emission reduction and local prosperity.

title: Enhancing User Fairness in Pinching-Antenna Systems-Enabled Multi-User Communications.
abstract: Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) facilitate flexible and strong line-of-sight communication links by reconfiguring the positions of pinching antennas (PAs) along waveguides. A PASS-enabled multi-user communication system is considered by exploiting the newly introduced waveguide division multiple access (WDMA). A resource allocation problem is formulated to maximize the rate fairness via the joint optimization of pinching beamforming and power allocation. The problem is decomposed within a majorization-minimization (MM)-based alternating optimization (AO) framework, where a MM surrogate function is constructed, and an element-wise update is derived for the pinching beamforming. The transmit power allocation is then obtained through MM-based optimization. Numerical results demonstrate that: 1) PASS significantly improve communication rate performance over conventional fixed antenna systems; 2) WDMA scheme efficiently exploits spatial decoupling between users in the waveguide domain enabled by pinching beamforming to support multi-user communications.

title: D2SC: A Personalized Semantic Communications Framework for IoT via Federated Learning.
abstract: By integrating advanced semantic communications (SC) into Internet of things (IoT) devices, we can greatly enhance task execution efficiency and deliver high-quality services to users. However, with the widespread adoption of personalized services, providing customized intelligent communications presents a new challenge. In this paper, we introduce a two-stage SC framework for image transmission. In the first stage, SC is innovatively integrated into a federated learning (FL) framework, which enables the extraction of personalized knowledge while preserving privacy. Furthermore, to accommodate edge IoT devices, knowledge distillation is employed to obtain a small student model with strong semantic understanding capabilities. In addition, the intrinsic value of unlabeled data, which is often overlooked, is fully exploited through the self-supervised scheme in this phase. In the second stage, the global model in FL is deployed in wireless communications to activate specific SC functions. To mitigate channel interference, a signal-to-noise ratio modulation module is designed to achieve adaptive channel coding for semantic representation. We denote the proposed framework as distillation-to-SC (D2SC) and demonstrate its superior performance across diverse tasks through extensive simulation experiments.

title: Spectrum-Weighted Instantaneous Frequency Estimation Empowering Real-Time Drone Detection.
abstract: Existing radio frequency (RF)-based drone detection methods usually rely on time-frequency spectrum (TFS) because drones adopt frequency-hopping spread spectrum (FHSS) communication. However, the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) to obtain TFS and the detection based on TFS bring high computational complexity. On the other hand, instantaneous frequency (IF) is a feature available for drone detection, but IF estimation methods suitable for drone signals also rely on STFT, limiting their real-time capability. To address this challenge, we propose a drone signal detection algorithm based on spectrum-weighted IF (SWIF) estimation. Specifically, the algorithm estimates the amplitude-weighted average frequency of multi-tone signals by constructing the trajectory of the differential I/Q signals. Beyond the existing TFS-based feature extraction methods, the proposed method achieves linear computational complexity. Using the SWIF estimation results as input, the temporal detection network achieves only 2% of the parameters of the TFS network while maintaining detection accuracy, making real-time drone detection possible. Finally, we validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm using simulations and real Radio Frequency data with drone signals.

title: Molecular Communication in Multi-Layered Parallel Channels with an Ocean Surface Case Study.
abstract: Molecular transport through heterogeneous layered structures is fundamental to biological, environmental, and engineered systems, yet molecular communication models typically assume uniform diffusivity or apply averaging approximations that mask interlayer effects. We present an analytical frame-work for multi-layered Cartesian channels that preserves layer-specific diffusion coefficients while accommodating arbitrary source positioning and diverse interface conditions. Application to oceanic stratified systems demonstrates how sea surface microlayer properties and air-water interface permeability control molecular transport behavior. Particle-based simulations validate these analytical findings.
