title: The Role of Excitation Schemes in the Functionality of Metasurface-based Antennas.
abstract: Using metasurface (MTS) antennas in wireless communication networks offers a promising way to achieve both high-quality connections and low power usage. In this paper, we study a setup where a transmissive MTS is integrated into the basestation antenna. We explore how the type of electromagnetic wave used to illuminate the MTS affects communication performance, assuming all other system parameters remain fixed. Our results show that using a cylindrical wave improves downlink performance compared to a plane wave. Although a plane wave might seem ideal due to its uniform illumination, our findings highlight the benefit of a richer set of wavevectors in the illuminating field.

title: Electromagnetically Consistent Modeling of Near-Field Channels With Metasurface Antennas.
abstract: Reliable and energy-efficient indoor wireless communication is increasingly important as user demand and device density continue to grow. Transmissive metasurface-based (TMTS) antennas have emerged as a promising solution for meeting these demands. In indoor environments, users often operate in close proximity to the basestation (BS), placing them within the near-field region of the antenna. In this work, we employ an electromagnetic integral-equation (IE) formulation to deterministically model the wireless channel in such scenarios, capturing the interactions among all objects in the environment and the TMTS antenna deployed at the BS. Our study shows that, beyond the expected spherical wavefronts and reactive fields that characterize the near-field, the electromagnetic interaction between the BS antenna and the users’ antennas plays a critical role in accurately estimating system performance. These interactions must therefore be explicitly incorporated into near-field channel models, and the IE framework offers a rigorous and effective way to achieve this goal.

title: ALIGN: 1 Gbps Optical Inter-Satellite Link Demonstration on 6U CubeSats with the FOCUS Terminal.
abstract: Free-space optical (FSO) inter-satellite links (OISLs) offer dramatically higher data throughput than traditional radio-frequency (RF) systems for satellite constellations. This paper presents the Free-space Optical Communications Unit for Satellites (FOCUS), a compact 2U payload for 6U CubeSats—the 6U form factor referring to a ∼10×10×30cm nanosatellite platform—demonstrating autonomous >1Gbps optical links at ranges up to 1000km in Low Earth Orbit (LEO). The terminal employs non-return-to-zero on-off keying (NRZ-OOK) modulation at 1.25Gbps. Component-level characterisation using an arbitrary waveform generator (AWG) test setup demonstrates receiver sensitivity below −37dBm, measured bit error rate (BER) as low as 10−8under laboratory conditions, closed-loop pointing accuracy below 50μrad using a fast-steering mirror (FSM), and AWG-based end-to-end throughput characterisation at 1.25Gbps. Compared with prior CubeSat-class OISL demonstrations, FOCUS achieves the highest reported ISL data rate at equivalent or better receiver sensitivity within a 2U payload volume. Two 6U CubeSats are planned to launch, subject to funding confirmation, as part of the Autonomous Laser InterSatellite Gigabit Network (ALIGN) mission, funded by the UK Space Agency, to validate optical ISL performance at orbital ranges from 100km to 1000km.

title: RIS-Assisted Near-Field ISAC for Multi-Target Indication in NLOS Scenarios.
abstract: Enabling multi-target sensing in near-field integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems is a key challenge, particularly when line-of-sight paths are blocked. This paper proposes a beamforming framework that leverages a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) to achieve multi-target indication. Our contribution is the extension of classic beampattern gain and inter-target cross-correlation metrics to the near-field, leveraging both angle and distance information to discriminate between multiple users and targets. We formulate a problem to maximize the worst-case sensing performance by jointly designing the beamforming at the base station and the phase shifts at the RIS, while guaranteeing communication rates. The non-convex problem is solved via an efficient alternating optimization (AO) algorithm that utilizes semidefinite relaxation (SDR). Simulations demonstrate that our RIS-assisted framework enables high-resolution sensing of co-angle targets in blocked scenarios.

title: Serial Polar Automorphism Ensemble Decoders for Physical Unclonable Functions.
abstract: Physical unclonable functions (PUFs) involve challenging practical applications of error-correcting codes (ECCs), requiring extremely low failure rates on the order of $10^{-6}$ and below despite raw input bit error rates as high as 22%. These requirements call for an efficient ultra-low rate code design. In this work, we propose a novel coding scheme tailored for PUFs based on Polar codes and a low-complexity version of automorphism ensemble decoding (AED). Notably, our serial AED scheme reuses a single successive cancellation (SC) decoder across multiple decoding attempts. By introducing cascaded and recursive interleavers, we efficiently scale the number of AED candidates without requiring expensive large multiplexers. An aggressive quantization strategy of only 3 bits per message further reduces the area requirements of the underlying SC decoder. The resulting coding scheme achieves the same block error rate of $10^{-6}$ as our baseline based on Bose-Ray-Chaudhuri-Hocquenghem (BCH) codes while requiring 1.75x fewer codeword bits to encode the same K = 312 payload bits. This reduction translates directly into 1.75x less helper data storage and, consequently, a smaller overall chip area.

title: Q-Learning for 3D Coverage in VCSEL-based Optical Wireless Systems.
abstract: Beam divergence control is a key factor in maintaining reliable coverage in indoor optical wireless communication (OWC) systems as receiver height varies. Conventional systems employ fixed divergence angles, which result in significant coverage degradation due to the non-convex trade-off between optical power concentration and spatial spread. In this paper, we introduce a reinforcement learning (RL)–based framework for dynamic divergence adaptation in vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL)–based OWC networks. By continuously interacting with the environment, the RL agent autonomously learns a near-optimal mapping between receiver height and beam divergence, thereby eliminating the need for analytical modeling or computationally intensive exhaustive search. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves up to 92% coverage at low receiver heights and maintains robust performance under challenging conditions, enabling scalable, real-time, and energy-efficient beam control for dense VCSEL array deployments in next-generation OWC systems.

title: A Novel CSI-RS Reporting Scheme for RIS Optimization in O-RAN-based NextG Networks.
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) technology is a promising enabler for next-generation (NextG) wireless systems, capable of dynamically shaping the propagation environment. Integrating RIS within the open radio access network (O-RAN) architecture enables flexible and intelligent control of wireless links. However, practical RIS-assisted operation requires efficient acquisition and reporting of channel state information (CSI) to support real-time control from the base station side. This paper proposes a CSI reference signal (CSI-RS)-based reporting scheme for downlink complex channel information (CCI) to facilitate RIS optimization in an O-RAN-compliant environment. The proposed framework establishing CCI extraction and CSI-RS reporting procedures is experimentally validated on a real-world testbed integrating an open-source O-RAN system with an RIS prototype operating in the n78 frequency band. Existing channel estimation-based RIS optimization algorithms, including Hadamard and orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP), are tailored for integration into the O-RAN architecture. Experimental results demonstrate notable improvements in received signal power for both near and far users, highlighting the effectiveness and practical viability of the proposed scheme.

title: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Sub-Array Design for D2D Interference Channel.
abstract: This paper investigates the utility of reconfigurable intelligent surface-sub-array (RIS-SA) design to optimize the power-domain array factor (PDAF) of device-to-device (D2D) interference channel. We exploit an additional design degree of freedom–namely sub-array element selection– provided by RISSA to enhance the desired PDAF and suppress interfering PDAFs so as to maximize the sum-rate of D2D networks. To achieve this goal, we generate directional beamwidth PDAFs that exhibit significant power towards intended users while minimizing PDAF towards unintended users. To this end, the joint optimization of the RIS-SA element selection and phase shifts is formulated, subject to the interfering PDAFs ratio constraints of users, as a non-convex mixed integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) problem. To address the non-convex optimization problem, we propose solving it using binary differential evolution (BDE) that creates notches at the interference angles and directional beamwidth PDAFs where the intended receiving users might reside. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed joint optimization using BDE enabled D2D interference network outperforms its conventional counterparts, which enhances the performance and reduces the complexity of the beamforming design.

title: AAV-Assisted SWIPT in MU-mMIMO IoT Networks: A Joint Optimization Framework.
abstract: Autonomous aerial vehicles (AAVs) equipped with simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) offer a promising solution to sustain energy-limited and data-driven Internet-of-Things (IoT) networks. This paper presents J-HBF-PSOLPA, a particle swarm optimization (PSO)-based framework for jointly optimizing AAV location, power allocation (PA), and hybrid beamforming (HBF) in a decode-and-forward (DF) multi-user massive MIMO (MU-mMIMO) system over geometry-based millimeter-wave (mmWave) channels. The goal is to maximize the total harvested power (HP) for ground IoT devices while ensuring a minimum user-wise rate threshold for information decoding (ID). Further, we investigate two SWIPT protocols, power splitting (PS) and time switching (TS), for distributing received radio frequency (RF) signals between HP and ID. To evaluate the proposed J-HBF-PSOLPA algorithm for AAV-assisted SWIPT, we benchmark it against a fixed-location, equal-PA scheme (J-HBF-FL-EQPA). Simulation results show that J-HBF-PSOLPA significantly outperforms the benchmark, improving both total HP and achievable rate (AR), and PS yields superior energy–rate trade-offs. By enforcing the rate constraint, user-wise AR is further improved with negligible effect on HP, emphasizing the importance of dynamic resource allocation in emerging AAV-assisted IoT applications.

title: Error Resilient Rate-Scalable Image Compression Using Semantic Communications.
abstract: Scalable image compression and transmission is a capability that underpins a wide range of consumer technologies, ranging from large-format displays to remote sensing cameras. A major challenge in it is that current scalable image compression techniques are inadequately equipped to handle very small bandwidths and very noisy communication channels, which are increasingly common in many consumer electronic applications. A solution for this is proposed using the concept of semantic communications, where an autoencoder-based codec augmented with a residual coding system is used to improve the compression ratio and noise resilience of image transmission over error-prone communication channels. The system is tested with residual coders based on widely accepted and state-of-the-art image codecs, and its performance is evaluated under equal error protection and unequal error protection scenarios. Experimental results show that the proposed systems demonstrate up to 27 dB improvement in the peak signal-to-noise ratio and up to 0.90 improvement in the structural similarity index measure for a given image quality compared to conventional scalable image codecs, in addition to demonstrating superior error resilience against noise distortions for a given level of compression.

title: Physics-Informed Compressed Sensing: Incorporating Rotor Dynamic Equations for High-Fidelity State Estimation from Sub-Nyquist Samples.
abstract: This paper introduces a Physics-Informed Compressed Sensing (PICS) framework for high-fidelity condition monitoring of rotating machinery in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) environments. Classical compressed sensing methods rely solely on generic signal priors like sparsity, often producing reconstructions that are mathematically plausible but physically in-consistent, especially in low-measurement or high-noise regimes. Our proposed method fundamentally enhances the reconstruction process by embedding the governing differential equations of rotor dynamics directly into the optimization problem as a regularizer. This is achieved by introducing a "physics-residual" penalty term that forces the reconstructed signal to conform to the system’s known Lagrangian dynamics. We validate our framework using simulated data from a Jeffcott rotor model under various fault conditions, including mass unbalance and stiffness asymmetry. Experimental results demonstrate that our PICS approach significantly outperforms standard compressed sensing in both reconstruction accuracy (up to a 10 dB SNR improvement) and downstream fault diagnosis, especially at compression ratios below 30%. This work paves the way for more robust and data-efficient monitoring systems that reduce communication overhead in critical IIoT applications.

title: Sign of the Times: Ultra-Low-Power Rotor Fault Diagnosis using 1-Bit Compressed Sensing.
abstract: The proliferation of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) requires the deployment of massive-scale wireless sensor networks for real-time condition monitoring of critical machinery. However, the operational lifetime of these sensors is severely limited by power consumption, with the analog-to-digital converter (ADC) and wireless transmitter being the primary bottlenecks. This paper challenges the conventional high-resolution sensing paradigm by proposing an ultra-low-power framework for rotor fault diagnosis based on 1-bit compressed sensing. In our approach, high-frequency vibration signals are projected into a low-dimensional space and severely quantized to a single bit per measurement, effectively replacing the power-hungry ADC with a simple comparator. We then develop a deep neural network that performs fault classification directly on these binary measurements, bypassing the ill-posed and computationally expensive signal reconstruction step. Through extensive simulations on a high-fidelity rotor dynamics model, we demonstrate that complex gyroscopic fault signatures can be accurately identified from these minimalist data streams. Our proposed method achieves classification accuracy comparable to systems using unquantized data, while requiring only a fraction of the measurements and enabling an order-of-magnitude reduction in sensing power. This work paves the way for a new generation of long-lifetime, cost-effective sensors, making pervasive and truly autonomous predictive maintenance a feasible reality.

title: CSI Prediction Using Autoregressive Conditional Diffusion Models.
abstract: Acquiring accurate channel state information (CSI) is critical for reliable and efficient wireless communication, but challenges such as high pilot overhead and channel aging hinder timely and accurate CSI acquisition. CSI prediction, which forecasts future CSI from historical observations, offers a promising solution. Recent deep learning approaches, including recurrent neural networks and Transformers, have achieved notable success but typically learn deterministic mappings, limiting their ability to capture the stochastic and multimodal nature of wireless channels. In this paper, we propose a novel CSI prediction scheme based on diffusion models. We decompose the CSI prediction task into two components: a temporal encoder, which extracts channel dynamics, and a diffusion-based generator, which produces future CSI samples autoregressively. Extensive simulations demonstrate that our diffusion-based models significantly outperform state-of-the-art baselines.

title: Radio Channel Measurements of D2X Communication in a Running Industrial Factory.
abstract: The trends associated with Industry 4.0 are fundamentally dependent on wireless communication technologies to facilitate a mobile and flexible factory floor. Consequently, comprehensive radio channel measurements are necessary for understanding the challenges and characteristics of the propagation environment. This paper presents a channel measurement campaign conducted within an operational industrial factory utilizing both static and mobile nodes to emulate device-to-everything (D2X) communications. An analysis is performed by first computing the distribution of node distance, followed by a conditional characterization of received power. Moreover, the spatial correlation properties of both device-to-infrastructure (D2I) and device-to-device (D2D) links are evaluated, revealing shorter decorrelation distances for D2D links, which highlight their deployment challenges in industrial environments.

title: Forward-Forward Autoencoder Architectures for Energy-Efficient Wireless Communications.
abstract: The application of deep learning to the area of communications systems has been a growing field of interest in recent years. Forward-forward (FF) learning is an efficient alternative to the backpropagation (BP) algorithm, which is typically used as the training procedure for neural networks. Among its several advantages, FF learning does not require the communication channel to be differentiable and does not rely on the global availability of partial derivatives, allowing for an energy-efficient implementation. In this work, we design end-to-end learned autoencoders using the FF algorithm and numerically evaluate their performance for the additive white Gaussian noise and Rayleigh block fading channels. We demonstrate their competitiveness with BP-trained systems in the case of joint coding and modulation, and in a scenario where a fixed, non-differentiable modulation stage is applied. Moreover, we provide further insights into the design principles of the FF network, its training convergence behavior, and significant memory and processing time savings compared to BP-based approaches.

title: QSFL-ID: Quantum-Split Federated Learning for Intrusion Detection in IIoT Networks.
abstract: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) is reshaping industrial automation through interconnected, intelligent systems. However, this evolution increases exposure to sophisticated cyber threats, especially given the constraints of IIoT devices such as limited processing power, bandwidth, and heterogeneous protocols. Traditional machine learning methods often fail to meet these security demands due to their computational intensity and centralized data requirements. To address this, we propose a hybrid quantum-classical Split Federated Learning (SFL) framework for intrusion detection in IIoT networks. Our method integrates Variational Quantum Circuits (VQCs) to model complex, non-linear data relationships, enhancing detection accuracy while preserving data privacy through decentralized learning. The architecture assigns lightweight preprocessing to edge devices and complex analysis to a quantum backend, ensuring efficiency and scalability. To evaluate the proposed framework, we conduct extensive experiments on the real-world EDGE-IIoT dataset; the experimental results demonstrate that the model attains 95.5% training accuracy, significantly surpassing classical SFL (85.7%). In addition, the quantum model’s enhanced entanglement properties and expressibility strengthen its generalization performance. This approach offers an efficient and privacy-preserving solution for securing IIoT systems.

title: PACDiff: Protocol-Aware Diffusion-Based Anomaly Detection for Next-Generation Vehicular Networks.
abstract: In-vehicle Controller Area Network (CAN) security in next-generation vehicular networks requires anomaly detection mechanisms that achieve high detection fidelity under normal-only training while preserving sensitivity to protocol-level deviations. This paper proposes PACDiff, a generative AI–driven, protocol-aware diffusion-based anomaly detection framework for in-vehicle networks that explicitly incorporates CAN identifier (CAN-ID) conditioning into the generative modeling process. By conditioning both the encoder and the diffusion denoiser on CAN identifiers, PACDiff learns ECU-specific normal traffic distributions rather than a single homogeneous representation of CAN traffic, enabling protocol-aware modeling for intelligent and next-generation in-vehicle network monitoring. Anomalous CAN messages are identified using multi-timestep diffusion-based reconstruction errors computed under a normal-only training regime. In addition, a model-driven attribution mechanism enables localization of anomalous behavior at both the CAN-ID and payload-byte levels without requiring signal decoding or labeled attack data. Experimental evaluation on CAN datasets demonstrates high anomaly detection performance, achieving an F1-score of 0.99 with zero false positives. Beyond binary detection, the framework provides interpretable localization by ranking anomalous CAN identifiers and attributing deviations to specific payload bytes.

title: Doppler-Precoded OTFS with Frequency-Domain Shaping and Extension.
abstract: Orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation has emerged as a promising waveform for high-mobility wireless communications due to its inherent robustness against severe Doppler effects. However, the multicarrier structure of OTFS leads to a high peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR), which degrades power amplifier efficiency and poses challenges for practical deployment. To mitigate the high-PAPR issue, this paper proposes a low-PAPR OTFS waveform design by jointly exploiting Doppler-domain Zadoff–Chu (ZC) precoding and frequency-domain spectral shaping (FDSS) with symmetric spectral extension (SE). By appropriately adjusting the spectral extension ratio while preserving the original spectral efficiency, the proposed scheme is capable of reducing the instantaneous PAPR to approximately 3 dB at the 10−4complementary cumulative distribution function (CCDF) level, with only negligible degradation in block error rate (BLER). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed waveform design method achieves significant PAPR reduction without compromising error-rate performance, rendering it a promising solution for practical high-mobility OTFS systems.

title: Integrated Sensing, Computation and Communications Using Continuous-Aperture Array.
abstract: This paper presents a continuous-aperture array (CAPA)-enabled integrated sensing, computation and communications (ISCC) framework. In this architecture, a CAPA-based base station (BS) performs continuous receive beamforming to collect sensing information from distributed ISCC nodes, while simultaneously supporting communications and over-the-air computation (AirComp) via the waveform superposition property of the wireless multiple access channel (MAC). The computation error minimization (CEM) problem is formulated under sensing performance constraints and subsequently addressed within an alternating optimization (AO) framework. In particular, closed-form minimum mean-squared error (MMSE) CAPA receivers for sensing and computation are derived, and the transmit beamforming subproblem is efficiently tackled using a semidefinite relaxation (SDR)-based method. Extensive numerical results validate the effectiveness of the proposed design. The proposed ISCC algorithm achieves significant reductions in computation error while maintaining reliable sensing performance compared with conventional zero-forcing (ZF) and MMSE schemes; and ii) the CAPA architecture consistently provides substantial performance advantages over the traditional spatially discrete array (SPDA).

title: Federated Learning-Based Beamforming Design Towards CRLB Minimization in RIS-Assisted ISAC.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems jointly utilize wireless resources for high-rate data transmission and accurate environmental sensing. Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) enable dynamic control of propagation, enhancing both communication reliability and sensing precision. This paper proposes a full-duplex (FD) RIS-assisted ISAC framework integrated with federated learning (FL) for distributed, privacy-preserving optimization of beamforming and RIS phase shifts. Using a realistic Rician channel model, the Fisher information matrix and Cramér-Rao lower bound are derived to assess sensing accuracy. The FL-based algorithm jointly maximizes sum rate and minimizes localization error under power and QoS constraints through local training and global aggregation. Simulations show that the proposed method achieves up to 8% higher throughput and 20% lower CRLB than centralized SGD, demonstrating the effectiveness of combining RIS and FL for scalable, privacy-aware ISAC systems.

title: Robust Split Federated Learning Against Multi-Vector Poisoning in Semantic Communication Networks.
abstract: Sixth-generation (6G) semantic communication systems rely on distributed intelligence across edge and cloud layers, but their openness also exposes them to adversarial manipulation. This paper investigates the robustness of split federated learning (SFL) under multi-vector poisoning attacks in a semantic communication environment. Three attack modalities, namely label poisoning, weight poisoning, and representation-space (smash) poisoning, are modeled and evaluated using the MNIST dataset as an image-semantic proxy for edge sensing. A multi-k Krum aggregation scheme with L2-norm clipping is proposed to enhance Byzantine resilience while preserving communication efficiency. Comparative experiments under conservative (30% malicious clients) and strong attack scenarios show that the proposed defense achieves near-clean accuracy (95.52% and 98.19%) and bounds semantic deviation within ±robust aggregation effectively mitigates semantic corruption in1% of the benign baseline. The results demonstrate that distributed learning, offering a secure and resource-efficient foundation for AI-native 6G networks.

title: Variational Bayesian Learning Estimator for NF gMIMO-OTFS with Spatial Non-Stationarity.
abstract: Near-field propagation and spatial non-stationarity in gigantic multiple-input multiple-output (gMIMO) orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) systems introduce unique challenges for channel estimation. We propose a novel channel model, which captures spatial non-stationarity in spatial dimension and fractional Doppler shift in delay Doppler domain. These aspects lead to a structured two-dimensional (2D) sparsity in the delay-Doppler-spatial domain. To exploit this 2D sparsity, we propose a novel 2D Gaussian mixture prior, where each Gaussian component models a different sparsity pattern in the channel. Using this 2D prior, we develop a variational Bayesian learning (2DGVBL) framework to approximate the channel posterior distribution. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed 2DGVBL algorithm achieves superior performance over state-of-the-art algorithms under high-mobility conditions.

title: Electromagnetically Coupled Near-Field Uplink Holographic MIMO Channel and Beamforming.
abstract: This paper investigates uplink near-field holographic MIMO (HMIMO) systems operating in the radiating Fresnel region, where dense apertures and electromagnetic (EM) coupling invalidate conventional far-field models. A hybrid EM-statistical channel model is proposed that jointly captures deterministic mutual coupling and stochastic non-line-of-sight (NLoS) scattering, enabling physically grounded yet tractable near-field analysis. Within this framework, uplink receive beam-forming is studied via a max-min fairness design and an analytical characterization of maximum-ratio combining (MRC). To address the resulting nonlinear signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) expressions, an equivalent-in-distribution SINR model and a mean-equivalent approximation are developed, yielding closed-form SINR and achievable-rate approximations. The analysis is further extended to imperfect channel state information (CSI) through an error-aware SINR formulation. Simulation results validate the analysis and show that MRC provides a robust complexity-performance tradeoff in near-field HMIMO uplinks, remaining stable under EM-coupling and CSI mismatch, while zero-forcing (ZF) and max-min beam-formers are more sensitive to estimation errors.

title: A Hardware-Based Adaptive Power Updating System for Ultraviolet Communication.
abstract: To address varying environmental conditions, this paper proposes a transmitter-side adaptive power updating mechanism for ultraviolet (UV) communication. The receiver performs channel estimation on the forward link and sends back the signal and background radiation components to the transmitter via the feedback link. We begin by generating a bit error rate (BER) performance map via offline simulation for various signal and noise conditions. The transmitter combines real-time channel information from the feedback link with this performance map to dynamically update the number of active transmitting elements (LEDs), ensuring the signal strength required for an ultra-low BER. Furthermore, to reduce power consumption, we have also defined a power-saving threshold, which is intended to proactively limit and decrease the number of active LEDs when the channel conditions are favorable, such as in short-range communication, thereby avoiding unnecessary energy loss. Outdoor experiments are conducted to verify the performance in long-range scenarios where the transceiver distance increases. Experimental results demonstrate the dual advantage of the proposed mechanism: it ensures high power efficiency by operating at low power in favorable channel conditions, while also guaranteeing communication reliability and robustness by increasing power in long-distance, weak-channel scenarios.

title: Task-Driven Semantic Networking Coding for Image Transmission in Low-Altitude Communication Network.
abstract: Semantic communication is considered as a promising solution for low-latency transmission in low-altitude communication networks. Nevertheless, existing methods for semantic image transmission all focus on the link level, while ignoring the image semantic fusion among multiple nodes at the network level, resulting in inefficient bandwidth utilization. This paper introduces an efficient Combined-and-Forward Relaying framework with Task-Driven Semantic Networking Coding (TD-SNC) for real-time object detection from multiple unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) views. By fusing semantic features into a single compact representation, TDSNC significantly enhances transmission efficiency while preserving essential task semantics. Driven by the goal of balancing detection accuracy and transmission efficiency, we implement a task-oriented optimization that combines object detection loss with L1-norm sparsity, allowing the model to discard irrelevant data effectively. A two-stage training strategy—initial pre-training for stable reconstruction followed by end-to-end fine-tuning—ensures reliable convergence in this complex system. Evaluations on the MDMT dataset show that TDSNC achieves superior transmission efficiency and noise resilience compared to existing benchmarks.

title: A Transformer Decoder with Tanner Graph-based Positional Encoding.
abstract: Error correction codes (ECCs) are essential for reliable communication over noisy channels. While Transformer-based decoders surpass traditional methods on short and medium-length codes, they insufficiently exploit the structural information of Tanner graphs. In this paper, we propose a novel Transformer decoder with Tanner Graph-Based Positional Encoding (TGPE) which introduces a dual-level positional encoding mechanism to effectively integrate graph topology into the attention process. The intra-type encoding utilizes a distance matrix to embed shortest-path relationships among nodes of the same type, thereby enhancing the modeling of intra-group dependencies. Meanwhile, the inter-type encoding extends the differential attention mechanism by combining mask-based edge connectivity—derived from the parity-check matrix—with a distance-modulated attention term that captures distance-aware dependencies between variable and check nodes while suppressing background attention noise. This dual encoding enables the decoder to capture both global and local, indirect and direct topological dependencies. Extensive experiments on standard ECC benchmarks demonstrate that TGPE consistently outperforms previous methods including BP, ECCT and CrossMPT. Moreover, interpretability analysis confirms that the learned distance encodings reflect theoretical coding principles, with smaller graph distances corresponding to stronger correlations, highlighting TGPE’s robustness and theoretical soundness.

title: Machine Learning-based Dynamic Spectrum Sharing and Traffic Classification with dApp.
abstract: The growing demand for wireless communication in 5G and Next-Generation (Next-G) is placing significant strain on the commercial spectrum. Spectrum reserved for incumbent users, such as government and military, is often under-utilized and can be shared with commercial/civil users via spectrum sharing as extra spectrum resources. However, existing centralized spectrum sharing schemes suffer from high latency and significant administrative overhead. Within decentralized frameworks like O-RAN, the RAN Intelligent Controller (RIC) cannot directly observe User Plane parameters, such as I/Q samples. While dApps provide the capability to acquire I/Q samples, few studies have focused on intelligent spectrum sharing schemes that leverage dApps. To address this gap, this paper proposes a dApp-based scheme that extracts I/Q samples for machine learning-based signal classification, which in turn informs dynamic spectrum management policies. In the experiment, the proposed scheme achieves a 99.66% recall in incumbent protection, significantly outperforming the baseline (63.80%), thereby reducing interference risk to high-priority users.

title: Parameter-Adaptive Channel Prediction for 6G Upper Mid-Band Communications.
abstract: Upper mid-band (7.125–24.25 GHz) massive MIMO is recognized as a pivotal technology for future 6G communication systems, providing wide bandwidth while maintaining reliable coverage. To fully unlock the beamforming potential of massive MIMO antenna systems, acquiring accurate channel state information (CSI) at the base station (BS) is paramount. However, this task is challenging in the upper mid-band systems, where channels vary rapidly within the uplink sounding reference signal (SRS) interval, causing a significant mismatch between the estimated and actual CSI. To mitigate the performance degradation caused by such channel aging, accurate channel prediction is indispensable. In this paper, we propose parameter-adaptive channel prediction (PACP), which decomposes the uplink SRS into multipath geometric channel parameters (GCPs), such as angle, delay, and path gain, and predicts each parameter according to its own temporal dynamics. Using the predicted multipath GCPs, BS proactively generates a proactive beamforming matrix for downlink data transmission. Numerical results demonstrate that PACP provides an 8 dB channel normalized mean square error (NMSE) gain over the conventional schemes and nearly matches the data rate of perfect CSI.

title: KAN-Pointformer: Hierarchical Learning for Covert ISAC in Pixel Reconfigurable Fluid Antenna Systems.
abstract: Fluid antenna systems (FAS) based on pixel reconfigurable antennas (PRA) provide enhanced spatial degrees of freedom (DoF) to improve physical layer security in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks. However, the inherent coupling between discrete port selection and continuous beamforming under stringent sensing and covertness constraints leads to a challenging mixed-integer non-convex optimization problem. To address this, we propose a hierarchical learning framework that decouples the optimization variables via a constraint-aware collaborative mechanism. Specifically, a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) serves as the inner beamformer to accurately approximate the non-linear mapping from irregular array manifolds to optimal weights, replacing traditional Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLP). Guided by KAN-evaluated rewards, a Pointformer-based reinforcement learning policy is developed to efficiently optimize the large-scale combinatorial port selection by capturing global spatial correlations. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms fixed-position antenna (FPA) and achieves near-optimal covert rates. Moreover, numerical results confirm that the Pointformer policy achieves an order-of-magnitude reduction in training overhead compared to the Pointer Network baseline, demonstrating its superior scalability for practical deployment.

title: Unified Far-Field and Near-Field Cascaded Channel Estimation for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Systems.
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) can significantly enhance wireless coverage, yet their gains rely on accurate cascaded channel state information (CSI). In large-aperture systems, a non-negligible portion of users operate in the radiative near field, where spherical wavefronts invalidate conventional far-field, angle-domain estimation. This paper develops a unified cascaded channel model in the wavenumber domain (WD) using electromagnetic information theory and the Weyl expansion. The model characterizes the physically admissible WD support and reveals a sparse structure applicable to both far-field and near-field users. Based on this representation, cascaded channel estimation is cast as a compressed-sensing problem and solved by two algorithms: wavenumber domain-least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (WD-LASSO) and a greedy wavenumber domain-orthogonal matching pursuit (WD-OMP). Numerical results demonstrate improved normalized mean square error (NMSE) and robustness, with WD-OMP achieving the best performance under short pilots.

title: PHANTOM: PHysical ANamorphic Threats Obstructing Connected Vehicle Mobility.
abstract: Connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs) rely on vision-based deep neural networks (DNNs) and low-latency (Vehicle-to-Everything) V2X communication to navigate safely and efficiently. Despite their advances, these systems remain vulnerable to physical adversarial attacks. In this paper, we introduce PHANTOM (PHysical ANamorphic Threats Obstructing connected vehicle Mobility), a novel framework for crafting and deploying perspective-dependent adversarial examples using anamorphic art. PHANTOM exploits geometric distortions that appear natural to humans but are misclassified with high confidence by state-of-the-art object detectors. Unlike conventional attacks, PHANTOM operates in black-box settings without model access and demonstrates strong transferability across four diverse detector architectures (YOLOv5, SSD, Faster R-CNN, and RetinaNet). Comprehensive evaluation in CARLA across varying speeds, weather conditions, and lighting scenarios shows that PHANTOM achieves over 90% attack success rate under optimal conditions and maintains 60-80% effectiveness even in degraded environments. The attack activates within 6-10 meters of the target, providing insufficient time for safe maneuvering. Beyond individual vehicle deception, PHANTOM triggers network-wide disruption in CAV systems: SUMO-OMNeT++ co-simulation demonstrates that false emergency messages propagate through V2X links, increasing Peak Age of Information by 68-89% and degrading safety-critical communication. These findings expose critical vulnerabilities in both perception and communication layers of CAV ecosystems.

title: Profit Maximization for Service Placement in Multi-Access Edge Computing Considering Locational Marginal Prices of Electricity.
abstract: Multi-access edge computing (MEC) is a promising paradigm for next-generation wireless networks, including emerging 6G networks. It is designed to support services such as virtual and augmented reality, which require low latency, high bandwidth, and fast computation. In MEC, service placement refers to the process of deploying service instances close to the users to meet their demands. Although MEC has been studied extensively from a technical perspective, models that evaluate the economic sustainability of MEC deployments are largely underexplored. Economic sustainability involves the profitability of such deployments, requiring the balancing of operational costs of infrastructure, including electricity expenses, with revenue generation. In this work, we propose a techno-economic model of the service placement problem. The model accounts for region-dependent electricity costs, which can fluctuate significantly over time and location due to factors such as variations in renewable energy generation. Furthermore, the interactions between service providers (SPs) and infrastructure providers (IPs) and their individual costs and revenues are modeled. For the users, we consider service demands such as latency and quality of service (QoS). To solve the formulated service placement problem, we provide an optimization-based algorithm, which is evaluated using real-world data sets from 22 SPs and 5 IPs. Our results show that our proposed approach yields up to 5% more total profit by optimizing the service placement to lower the cost for procuring electricity by 10%, while maintaining the provided QoS in comparison to the state-of-the-art benchmark algorithms.

title: DOA Estimation for Tri-Polarized Continuous Aperture Array.
abstract: This paper addresses direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation using tri-polarized continuous aperture arrays (CA-PAs). By leveraging electromagnetic (EM) information theory, the spatially continuous signals received by the tri-polarized CAPA are modeled to enable accurate DOA estimation. To facilitate subspace decomposition for continuous operators, a continuous-discrete transformation technique is developed. Furthermore, both self- and cross-covariances of the tri-polarized signals are exploited to construct a tri-polarized spectrum, thereby significantly improving DOA estimation performance. In particular, the computationally intensive integral operations involved in the spectrum formulation are efficiently approximated using Gauss-Legendre quadrature, which substantially reduces the computational burden. Numerical results validate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed framework.

title: Threshold-based Wavelet Decomposition for 3D Point Clouds in Digital Environments.
abstract: This paper proposes a compressed sensing method based on threshold-driven multi-level wavelet decomposition to reduce storing and processing of 3-dimensional point cloud data. The approach is evaluated on 3D point clouds of rural and urban terrains and compared to an approach based on the discrete cosine transform. Our results show that mountainous landscapes can be effectively reconstructed from a compressed set of wavelet coefficients, achieving a lower mean absolute error and higher visual fidelity than DCT-based reconstructions while more work needs to be done for urban environment to achieve similar accuracy. The proposed method can be applied to larger, high-resolution point clouds and other higher dimensional datasets, such as hyperspectral images, for digital environments.

title: Movable Antenna-Assisted UAV-to-UAV Communication: Joint Beamforming and Antenna Position Optimization.
abstract: This paper investigates a movable antenna (MA)-assisted uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) swarm communication system. Each UAV is equipped with an MA array deployed on two hemispherical surfaces at the head and tail, significantly expanding the spatial degrees of freedom (DoFs). A far-field line-of-sight (LoS) channel model is adopted to characterize the UAV-to-UAV (U2U) communication links. We formulate a sum rate maximization problem by jointly optimizing the antenna position vectors (APVs) and transmit/receive beamforming vectors, subject to constraints on maximum transmit power, limited antenna moving region, and minimum inter-antenna spacing. To tackle this non-convex and highly coupled problem, we propose a two-loop iterative optimization algorithm that effectively combines the Spider Wasp Optimizer (SWO) for APV optimization and alternative optimization (AO) for beamforming design. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed MA-assisted scheme outperforms traditional fixed position antenna (FPA) systems and other benchmark algorithms under different settings.

title: Energy Efficiency Optimization of STAR-RIS Assisted MIMO-NOMA Networks.
abstract: Simultaneous transmission and reflection reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS) extends coverage beyond conventional RIS by enabling full-space signal manipulation. This paper investigates a STAR-RIS assisted multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) network. We aim to maximize the energy efficiency (EE) of this system, which is modeled to include the direct link between the base station (BS) and the reflection-user (R-user), which mostly exists in practice. We jointly optimize the active and passive beamforming, respectively at the BS and STAR-RIS, by decomposing the original non-convex problem into two tractable subproblems, which are then efficiently solved via an alternating optimization (AO) algorithm. The non-convexity is addressed by integrating the Dinkelbach method, quadratic fractional programming (QFP), semidefinite relaxation (SDR), and successive convex approximation (SCA) to convert each subproblem into a convex form. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed scheme can substantially improve overall EE over existing STAR-RIS assisted MIMO-NOMA networks.

title: Enabling Practical 6G Extreme Massive MIMO: Block Krylov-Nyström Beamspace Processing.
abstract: Extreme massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) in the upper mid-band spectrum (7-20 GHz) is a key enabler for 6G. In orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems, two-stage beamforming is essential for practical deployment, but most existing works rely on simplified channels and do not consider real-time processing constraints. Current methods require full-dimensional covariance computation and/or eigenvalue decomposition (EVD), resulting in prohibitive memory use and computational complexity. We propose a block Krylov-Nyström framework for beamspace beamforming that avoids full covariance storage and reduces complexity compared to EVD counterparts. The proposed scheme reconstructs full beamforming weights from low-rank channel information using the block Krylov-Nyström subspace, ensuring numerical stability and efficiency. To capture real-time constraints, we further introduce two evaluation methodologies: a complexity-to-delay conversion integrated with channel aging, and a spectral efficiency-to-complexity ratio (SECR) metric. Simulations with 3GPP 38.901 channel models demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves benchmark spectral efficiency with significantly lower latency and complexity, offering up to 15-30 higher SECR than baseline methods. These results establish the block Krylov-Nyström framework as a practical and robust solution for real-time massive MIMO-OFDM beamforming in 6G networks.

title: Detection in Bistatic ISAC with Deterministic Sensing and Gaussian Information Signals.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) is a disruptive technology enabling future sixth-generation (6G) networks. This paper investigates target detection in a bistatic ISAC system, in which the base station (BS) transmits superimposed ISAC signals comprising both Gaussian information-bearing and deterministic sensing components to simultaneously provide communication and sensing functionalities. First, we develop a Neyman-Pearson (NP)-based detector that effectively utilizes both the deterministic sensing and random communication signals. Closed-form analysis reveals that both signal components contribute to improving the overall detection performance. Subsequently, we optimize the BS transmit beamforming to maximize the detection probability, subject to a minimum signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraint for the communication user (CU) and a total transmit power budget at the BS. The resulting non-convex beamforming optimization problem is addressed via semi-definite relaxation (SDR) and successive convex approximation (SCA) techniques. Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed NP-based detector, which leverages both types of signals, over benchmark schemes that treat information signals as interference. They also reveal that a higher communication-rate threshold directs more transmit power to Gaussian information-bearing signals, thereby diminishing deterministic-signal power and weakening detection performance.

title: Space-to-Ground Entanglement Downlinks: When to Transmit - and When Not.
abstract: The study considers when a low Earth orbiting (LEO) satellite should transmit or hold entangled photons to a ground station in a rapidly varying free-space optical (FSO) channel. A channel-aware observable scheduler is developed that uses time-tag statistics to develop per-slot transmission decisions. The study compares the performance of the scheduler under six environmental conditions and the algorithm delivers secure-key totals providing similar results to an always-transmit scenario, yet allowing for considerable resource efficiency by reducing activity under harsh channel conditions. The system has higher conditional success among used slots and shows a higher avoidance of infeasible and high-error windows. The controller converges faster under normal conditions while longer convergence times are taken only under harsh environmental conditions. The study proposes a practical, drop-in scheduling layer that allows to achieve resource-efficient key delivery by considering the volatile atmospheric conditions for a LEO-to-ground transmission system.

title: Outdoor Accuracy Evaluation of DecaWave's DWM1002 PDoA Kit Measurements.
abstract: Accurate localization in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) is critical for applications such as emergency response, traffic monitoring, and industrial process control. Range-based methods generally outperform range-free ones, and Ultra Wideband (UWB) technology is particularly promising due to its high bandwidth and robustness against multipath effects. This paper evaluates the DecaWave DWM1002 Phase Difference of Arrival (PDoA) kit, an experimental commercial UWB platform extending the earlier DWM1001 Time Difference of Arrival (TDoA) boards, through a real-world outdoor test-bed spanning multiple distances and angles. Our objective is not to propose a new localization algorithm, but to characterize and correct structured, repeatable PDoA bias that affects outdoor deployments. The raw measurements show systematic errors, with short ranges often underestimated and longer ranges increasingly overestimated, deviating significantly from the centimeter-level accuracy claimed by the manufacturer. The observed bias is highly consistent across repetitions, indicating good precision but poor accuracy and motivating lightweight calibration. To mitigate these biases, we explored regression- and Machine Learning (ML)-based calibration models. The best-performing ML approach reduced the average error to around 12cm, achieving an improvement of roughly 70% over the uncalibrated data. These results indicate that while the kit is unsuitable for safety-critical localization in its raw form, lightweight calibration makes it viable for non-critical tasks such as tracking or crowd monitoring.

title: Precoder Design Using Local CSI for Full-Duplex Integrated Satellite-Terrestrial Networks.
abstract: This article addresses an interference management challenge in an integrated satellite-terrestrial network (ISTN) amidst spectrum sharing and full-duplex (FD) operational drawbacks. In particular, a beamforming optimization problem is formulated to maximize network throughput while minimizing the adverse effects of interference. To address the non-convex and non-smooth nature of the optimization problem, we first relax it into a product of Rayleigh quotients and then reformulate it into a smooth function using the LogSumExp technique. Next, the resulting problem is split into two subproblems to guarantee distributed beamforming for the satellite (SAT) and base station (BS), respectively, without sharing channel state information (CSI). Going forward, each subproblem is solved using the generalized power iteration (GPI) algorithm to obtain solutions for the respective SAT and BS beamforming vectors. The simulation results presented in this article affirm that the proposed strategy performs better than the existing schemes.

title: Hybrid Wireless Network Architectures for Resilient Communication in Seismic Zones.
abstract: Reliable communication is vital during seismic events, yet traditional cellular networks are prone to complete failure. This paper proposes a hybrid architecture integrating conventional cellular systems with cell-free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) to enhance resilience. We model a catastrophic base station failure and leverage the distributed nature of neighboring access points to prioritize the affected zone through fractional power control. Simulation results show that this hybrid approach maintains 70-85% of the pre-disaster per-user rate, preventing the total outage typical of traditional networks. Furthermore, we introduce a proactive disaster identification mechanism using Gradient Boosting Regression to predict network instability. This machine learning component is tightly coupled with the physical layer, triggering recovery actions early to ensure continuous, end-to-end communication in extreme failure scenarios.

title: SLIPT-Enabled Ground-to-UAV FSO Systems with Optical Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces.
abstract: This paper proposes an optical reconfigurable intelligent surface (ORIS)-assisted ground-to-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) free-space optical (FSO) communication system empowered by simultaneous lightwave information and power transfer (SLIPT). To overcome the line-of-sight (LoS) limitation of FSO-based SLIPT systems, we introduce an ORIS that reflects the laser beam towards a non-LoS UAV receiver. We model and analyze the combined channel characteristics, incorporating atmospheric loss, turbulence-induced fading, pointing error, and angle-of-arrival fluctuations due to UAV hovering. We derive closed-form expressions for harvested energy, outage probability, and symbol error rate (SER). Numerical results show that integrating ORIS improves EH efficiency while maintaining manageable outage and SER performance.
