title: An Evaluation of the Remote CX Protocol under Noise in Distributed Quantum Computing.
abstract: Quantum computers connected through classical and quantum communication channels can be combined to function as a single unit to run large quantum circuits that each device is unable to execute on their own. The distributed quantum computing paradigm is therefore often seen as a potential pathway to scaling quantum computing to capacities necessary for practical and large-scale applications. Whether connecting multiple quantum processing units (QPUs) in clusters or over networks, quantum communication requires entanglement to be generated and distributed over distances. Using entanglement, the remote CX protocol can be performed, which allows the application of the CX gate involving qubits located in different QPUs. In this work, we use a specialized simulation framework for a high-level evaluation of the impact of the protocol when executed under noise in various network configurations using different number of QPUs. We compare naive and graph partitioning qubit assignment strategies and how they affect the fidelity in experiments run on Grover, GHZ, VQC, and random circuits. The results provide insights on how QPU and network configurations or naive scheduling can degrade performance.

title: Joint Pilot Muting and 3D U-Net Reconstruction for Inter-Cell Pilot Contamination in 6G UDNs.
abstract: Pilot contamination is a fundamental bottleneck in 6G ultra-dense networks (UDNs), where static pilot reuse cannot adapt to irregular user-centric topologies and spatially non-stationary channels. We propose a joint optimization framework combining binary pilot muting and deep learning-based channel reconstruction. Network layouts are modeled by a Matérn hard-core process (HCP) derived from a Poisson point process (PPP), and small-scale fading is generated using a 3D non-stationary geometry-based stochastic model (GBSM). Pilot muting is formulated as a binary combinatorial optimization that minimizes network-wide pilot-domain normalized mean square error (NMSE) and is solved efficiently via an Estimation of Distribution Algorithm (EDA). To compensate for sparsified observations, a compact 3D U-Net performs channel inpainting to recover full resource blocks from muted pilots. Simulations show faster convergence than greedy heuristics and notable gains in Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio (SINR) and channel estimation accuracy, especially for edge users in dense network environments.

title: Spectral Efficiency Maximization in Pinching-Antenna-Enabled CR Networks.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate a cognitive radio (CR) network underpinned by pinching antennas (PAs), in which both the primary transmitter (PT) and secondary transmitter (ST) employ a single waveguide and multiple PAs to support simultaneous spectrum sharing. A sum spectral efficiency (SE) maximization problem is formulated to jointly optimize the pinching beamforming at both the PT and ST, under constraints on the PA deployment. To solve this non-convex problem, a two-stage optimization algorithm is developed, which sequentially optimizes the PT and ST pinching beamforming. For each pinching beamforming optimization, the coarse positions of the PAs are first determined at the waveguide level, followed by wavelength-level refinements to achieve constructive signal combining at the target user and destructive superposition at the non-intended users. Simulation results demonstrate that PAs yield substantial SE gains compared to conventional fixed-position antennas.

title: Secure Beamforming for Pinching-Antenna Systems.
abstract: Recently, pinching-antenna systems (PASS) have demonstrated pronounced advantages in mitigating large-scale path loss. This paper investigates their performance advantages in downlink secure transmission. We consider a scenario with multiple waveguides, one legitimate user, and one eavesdropper. The goal is to maximize the secrecy rate by jointly designing the baseband beamformer and the positions of pinching antennas (PAs). To handle the coupled optimization problem, we first exploit a generalized Rayleigh quotient structure to derive the optimal baseband beamformer. This step converts the coupled problem into a single-variable optimization over PAs' positions. Then, an efficient gradient-based method is proposed to achieve PA position updates. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm converges rapidly and stably, and that PASS achieve substantial secrecy rate gains over the fixed-antenna baselines.

title: Joint Age of Information and Energy Minimization in Two-hop Status Update Systems.
abstract: We consider a relay-assisted status update system, where each relay is responsible for transmitting updates from a cluster of sources to a base station (BS). The relays harvest energy from the environment to sustain the operations. To avoid collisions, only one relay is scheduled to transmit updates to the BS at a time. To this aim, the relays send update proposals to the BS, and the BS greedily selects the one that minimizes the overall age of information (AoI). Our goal is to design an update proposal policy for the relays that jointly minimizes their average AoI and energy consumption. Considering that each relay can only access its local information, i.e., its own AoI, buffer and battery status, and that the energy harvesting and update arrival processes are stochastic, we first model the update scheduling problem as a partially observable Markov game. Then, we propose a decentralized multi-agent proximal policy optimization (DMAPPO) algorithm at each relay to solve it. Our results show that the proposed DMAPPO algorithm outperforms baseline schemes in terms of AoI and energy consumption.

title: Joint Power Allocation and Positioning Optimization for Multi-Satellite Cooperative Transmission.
abstract: The rapid evolution of multi-satellite cooperative transmission (MSCT) systems has enabled unprecedented improvements in global broadband connectivity. As the deployment density of low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites increases, the short inter-satellite distances allow MSCT systems to exhibit array-like behaviors, where spatial geometry and relative positioning critically affect coherent signal transmission and interference management. This paper studies a downlink MSCT system, where multiple LEO satellites collectively function as a large-scale distributed antenna array. By flexibly adjusting their relative positions, the array geometry can be reconfigured to enhance coherent transmission and mitigate inter-user interference. To fully exploit this geometric flexibility, we develop a joint power allocation and position optimization framework to maximize the weighted sum rate under power, displacement, and collision avoidance constraints. The system is modeled as a multi-user multiple-input multiple-output network with Rician fading. To address the strong coupling between power allocation and spatial configuration, an alternating optimization framework is proposed. Specifically, the transmit power is optimized through a Lagrangian dual-based algorithm that introduces auxiliary variables and employs a bisection search to satisfy power constraints, while the satellite positions are refined using a particle swarm optimization procedure within feasible spatial domains. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed optimization framework.

title: Energy-Efficient Resource Management for MEC-Assisted VR Systems: A D3QN-IL Approach.
abstract: Virtual reality (VR) enables immersive experiences for remote monitoring, guidance, and control, improving operational efficiency across Internet of things-enabled and other cyber-physical applications. However, VR services characterize with ultra-high resolution, ultra-low latency, and frequent computation-intensive viewport rendering, posing stringent requirements on wireless communication and computation. In this paper, we propose a mobile edge computing assisted VR streaming transmission scheme to improve quality of experience (QoE) and alleviate computing burden of VR devices. A joint optimization problem is formulated to minimize the weighted energy consumption under QoE constraints. To solve the high-dimensional mixed integer non-convex problem, we propose a hierarchical optimization framework. The upper layer leverages convex optimization methods, while the lower layer uses dueling double Q network enhanced with imitation learning for binary decisions. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can achieve lower energy consumption and adapts faster to dynamic environments.

title: Quality-Cost-Security Trade-off via Semantic Feature Importance Aware Adaptive Transmission.
abstract: Although semantic communication offers superior transmission efficiency, it simultaneously brings new security vulnerabilities. To address this challenge, we propose a Feature-Importance Guided Selective Masking-Encryption (FISME) scheme to balance the semantic communication tasks quality, transmission cost and security performanc, where an eavesdropper conducts the model inversion attack by exploiting intercepted semantic information. First, we define a composite system cost function that integrates channel decoding iterations and encryption processes. Second, we jointly optimize feature masking, encryption, and channel coding parameters to minimize the composite system cost while ensuring robust and secure transmission. Third, we propose a dynamic Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) coding-rate selection mechanism to adjust coding parameters based on real-time SNR, ensuring a balance between reliability and redundancy. Moreover, we propose a Bayesian optimization of semantic transmission parameters via the Sequential Model-based Algorithm Configuration (BOST-SMAC3) algorithm to dynamically optimize masking feature set, encryption feature set, LDPC coding rate and LDPC decoding iterations. Simulation results show that the proposed FISME scheme achieves a flexible trade-off among cost, quality, and security by dynamically adapting communication, encryption, and channel coding costs to varying SNR.

title: Frequency-Aware Passive Beamforming for Shared IRS-Aided Communications.
abstract: In a system in which a single intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) is shared among multiple communication systems (CSs) operating at different frequency bands with jointly controlled phase shift, optimizing the phase shift for specific frequency may result in limited coverage for certain CSs across the communication area. This is because of the frequency-dependent reflection characteristics of the IRS, which cause variations in performance across different CSs. This study proposes an IRS control scheme that maximizes the minimum signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) in order to prevent unfairness in IRS shared systems. In particular, we designed the phase-shift control of the IRS to maximize the minimum SNR in the coverage area of the IRS, considering the frequency characteristics. The results show that the proposed method improves the SNR and ensures fairness among CSs, compared to the control that considers only a single frequency. The results show that the proposed method maximizes the minimum SNR, thereby ensuring fairness among CSs. This method contributes to optimizing communication performance when multiple CSs operating at different frequencies simultaneously employ an IRS.

title: On the Impact of Densification in Near-Field Downlink mmWave Cellular Networks.
abstract: In this work, we present an analytical framework for a dense mmWave network consisting of base stations (BSs) with extremely large antenna arrays (ELAA) where users may fall within the near-field region of electromagnetic wave propagation. Near-field channels enable BSs to beamform using complete user-location information. We first analyze the location-based beamforming (LBF) to provide a simplified beamforming gain model that can be incorporated in large-scale analysis. We show that near-field beamforming may lead to loss of directivity in some regions. By leveraging stochastic geometry tools, we derive the coverage probability of the typical user while incorporating the near-field effects in the presence of random blockage. Through numerical investigations, we compare near-field LBF and far-field direction-based beamforming (DBF). Our analysis reveals many interesting insights, including the impact of densification and the existence of multiple critical BS densities due to near-field effect, blockages, and noise-interference trade-off. We show that near-field effects may lead to degradation in coverage probability, thus requiring a more careful design.

title: Distributed Model Predictive Control-Based Trajectory and Resource Optimization for Aerial Base Stations.
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) equipped with aerial base stations (ABSs) have gained considerable attention for their ability to enhance coverage and capacity in the beyond 5G era. However, optimizing ABS trajectories is challenging due to limited battery capacity and inter-cell interference in multi-ABS scenarios. Existing ABS trajectory control methods are mostly offline and centralized, relying on the assumption of perfect knowledge about future channel states and user locations, rendering them impractical in real environments. In this paper, we propose an online and distributed ABS trajectory and resource optimization method based on distributed model predictive control (MPC). We formulate a problem that jointly optimizes ABS trajectories, user association, and power control to minimize flight time and power consumption while satisfying users’ data reception requirements. In the proposed method, each ABS solves its own local MPC problem to achieve the overall objective through local computation and communication. Because each local problem is non-convex, we develop an efficient algorithm using successive convex approximation. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Fully-Activated GSSK with LFM Waveform for Integrated Sensing and Communication.
abstract: This paper proposes a fully-activated generalized space shift keying (FA-GSSK) modulation scheme for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems to address the difficulty of simultaneously satisfying communication and sensing requirements. Unlike conventional GSSK, FA-GSSK activates all transmit antennas at the base station (BS) within each symbol period, enabling multi-user communication while achieving high-precision sensing tasks. To further enhance sensing capability, the communication symbols are embedded into a linear frequency modulated (LFM) waveform, enabling the ISAC system to exploit the pulse compression gain of LFM signals for coherent target sensing. Under this framework, a joint transmit–receive beamforming optimization problem is formulated to maximize the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the target echo received at the ISAC BS, subject to the constraints of correct FA-GSSK demodulation at each communication user (CU) and a total transmit power budget. The resulting nonconvex problem is efficiently solved using semidefinite programming (SDP). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed FA-GSSK with LFM waveform achieves a superior communication–sensing trade-off compared to conventional orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) based benchmarks.

title: Concatenated error-correcting codes for the interference channel with multi-antenna reception.
abstract: Error correcting codes (ECCs) such as low-density parity check (LDPC) codes and polar codes can operate close to Shannon capacity, especially in the low-noise regime. However, ECCs are not designed to mitigate high levels of interference – a task usually relegated to signal processing at the physical layer. For channels with strong interference, recent work has shown that packet repetition at the transmitter with dual antenna reception and canonical correlation analysis (CCA) signal alignment at the receiver can significantly improve the bit error rate under strong and unpredictable interference. Inspired by this, this paper proposes the use of concatenated high-rate LDPC - repetition codes with combined CCA and belief propagation (BP) decoding. Our numerical results show that concatenating a high-rate LDPC code and a repetition code can significantly reduce the block error rate (BLER) compared to LDPC codes with the same code rate when interference is present; and, interestingly, even for interference-free channels with multi-antenna reception. Furthermore, adjusting the code rate of the LDPC codes and the repetition codes can further optimize the BLER performance.

title: Doppler-Resilient LEO Satellite OFDM Transmission with Affine Frequency Domain Pilot.
abstract: Orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) based low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communication system suffers from severe Doppler shifts, while the Doppler-resilient affine frequency-division multiplexing (AFDM) transmission suffers from significantly high processing complexity in data detection. In this paper, we explore the channel estimation gain of affine frequency (AF) domain pilot to enhance the OFDM transmission under high mobility. Specifically, we propose a novel AF domain pilot embedding scheme for satellite-ground downlink OFDM systems for capturing the channel characteristics. By exploiting the autoregressive (AR) property of adjacent channels, a long short-term memory (LSTM) based predictor is designed to replace conventional interpolation operation in OFDM channel estimation. Simulation results show that the proposed transmission scheme significantly outperforms conventional OFDM scheme in terms of bit error rate (BER) under high Doppler scenarios, thus paving a new way for the design of next generation non-terrestrial network (NTN) communication systems.

title: Expansion-Aware Design Model for Optical-Circuit-Switched Data Center Networks Suppressing Fiber Link Rewiring.
abstract: The rapid growth of data center traffic has intensified the need for scalable and cost-efficient network architectures. Optical circuit switching (OCS) has emerged as a promising technology for this purpose, offering high bandwidth, low latency, and energy efficiency compared to traditional electrical packet switching. Among OCS-based architectures, the twisted and folded Clos network (TF-Clos) is particularly attractive due to its structural simplicity and modular scalability. However, conventional TF-Clos design models primarily address one-time network construction and do not explicitly consider incremental expansions, during which extensive optical fiber link rewiring may be required. Such reconfiguration increases operational complexity and risks service disruption, underscoring the need for expansion-aware design approaches. This paper proposes an expansion-aware OCS-based TF-Clos design model that incorporates multiple steps of network expansion while balancing two conflicting objectives: maximizing the switching network size and suppressing fiber link rewiring operations. We formulate the design problem as an optimization problem, and we introduce a pruning-based search algorithm to approximately solve it with reduced computation time. Numerical results show that the proposed model can reduce the number of fiber link rewirings at the expense of network size. These results highlight the practical advantages of the proposed model for designing scalable and reliable OCS-based TF-Clos networks in real data center environments.

title: Robust Composite DNA Storage under Sampling Randomness, Substitution, and Insertion-Deletion Errors.
abstract: DNA data storage offers a high-density, long-term alternative to traditional storage systems, addressing the exponential growth of digital data. Composite DNA extends this paradigm by leveraging mixtures of nucleotides to increase storage capacity beyond the four standard bases. In this work, we model composite DNA storage as a multinomial channel and draw an analogy to digital modulation by representing composite letters on the three-dimensional probability simplex. To mitigate errors caused by sampling randomness, we derive transition probabilities and log-likelihood ratios (LLRs) for each constellation point and employ practical channel codes for error correction. We then extend this framework to substitution and insertion-deletion (ID) channels, proposing constellation update rules that account for these additional impairments. Numerical results demonstrate that our approach achieves reliable performance with existing LDPC codes, comparing prior schemes designed for limited-magnitude probability errors, whose performance degrades significantly under sampling randomness.

title: Robust Semantic Transmission for Low-Altitude UAVs: Predictive Channel-Aware Scheduling and Generative Reconstruction.
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) downlink transmission facilitates critical time-sensitive visual applications but is fundamentally constrained by bandwidth scarcity and dynamic channel impairments. The rapid fluctuation of the air-to-ground (A2G) link creates a regime where reliable transmission slots are intermittent and future channel quality can only be predicted with uncertainty. Conventional deep joint source-channel coding (DeepJSCC) methods transmit coupled feature streams, causing global reconstruction failure when specific time slots experience deep fading. Decoupling semantic content into a deterministic structure component and a stochastic texture component enables differentiated error protection strategies aligned with channel reliability. A predictive transmission framework is developed that utilizes a split-stream variational codec and a channel-aware scheduler to prioritize the delivery of structural layout over reliable slots. Experimental evaluations indicate that this approach achieves a 5.6 dB gain in peak signal-to-noise (SNR) ratio over single-stream baselines and maintains structural fidelity under significant prediction mismatch.

title: LUT-GenNet: Target-PSNR- and Input-Guided Neural Lookup Table for Adaptive Rate Control in Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding.
abstract: Deep joint source-channel coding (DeepJSCC) is a promising technology for high efficiency wireless image transmission, but many existing models adopt a fixed compression rate. To address this problem, this paper proposes a DeepJSCC with lookup table generation network (LUT-GenNet), a novel scheme that provides peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) guaranteed adaptive compression rate control. Conventional adaptive rate control approaches determine the compression ratio after encoding, which makes a processing bottleneck. Furthermore, since the encoder requires channel SNR information, if the channel SNR changes after it is obtained and encoding is performed, the image quality can degrade significantly. The proposed LUT-GenNet is a neural network that generates an image-specific LUT directly from the input image. This LUT instantaneously determines the optimal compression rate based on the target PSNR and channel SNR. This approach enables parallel processing of encoding and rate determination and avoids the SNR mismatch problem because the encoder does not rely on SNR feedback. A comparison with the conventional method under SNR mismatch conditions showed that while the conventional performance degrades significantly as the mismatch increases, the proposed method maintains stable.

title: FTA-NTN: Fairness and Throughput Assurance in Non-Terrestrial Networks.
abstract: Designing optimal non-terrestrial network (NTN) constellations is essential for maximizing throughput and ensuring fair resource distribution. This paper presents FTA-NTN (Fairness and Throughput Assurance in Non-Terrestrial Networks), a multi-objective optimization framework that jointly maximizes throughput and fairness under realistic system constraints. The framework integrates multi-layer Walker Delta constellations, a parametric mobility model for user distributions across Canadian land regions, adaptive K-Means clustering for beamforming and user association, and Bayesian optimization for parameter tuning. Simulation results with 500 users show that FTA-NTN achieves over 9.88 Gbps of aggregate throughput with an average fairness of 0.42, corresponding to an optimal configuration of 9 planes with 15 satellites per plane in LEO and 7 planes with 3 satellites per plane in MEO. These values align with 3GPP NTN evaluation scenarios and representative system assumptions, confirming their relevance for realistic deployments. Overall, FTA-NTN demonstrates that throughput and fairness can be jointly optimized under practical constraints, advancing beyond throughput-centric designs in the literature and offering a scalable methodology for next-generation NTN deployments that supports efficient and equitable global connectivity.

title: Deep Learning-Driven Friendly Jamming for Secure ISAC Under Channel Uncertainty.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication enables efficient spectrum sharing by jointly performing radar sensing and wireless transmission. This paper proposes a deep learning–driven framework for secure ISAC under imperfect channel state information (CSI) and unknown eavesdropper (Eve) locations. Unlike conventional friendly jamming (FJ) methods requiring Eve’s CSI or precise angle-of-arrival (AoA), the proposed approach leverages radar echo feedback to guide directional jamming without explicit Eve information. To ensure robustness against sensing uncertainty, we introduce a radar-aware neural network that jointly optimises beamforming and jamming using a nonparametric Fisher Information Matrix (FIM) estimator based on f-divergence. The design satisfies Cramér–Rao lower bound constraints under noisy AoA. A quantised tensor-train encoder reduces model size substantially while maintaining performance. A non-overlapping secure subband scheme further isolates communication channels. Simulations demonstrate higher secrecy rates, reliable BLER, and robustness to CSI and angular errors, confirming the practicality of learning-based secure ISAC.

title: Joint Beamforming and Resource Allocation for ISAC-Enabled UAV Networks in Disaster Response.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is becoming an important approach in modern wireless networks by combining sensing and communication within shared hardware. However, deploying such systems in complex scenarios like disaster environments, where infrastructure is often damaged, remains challenging. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) enhance ISAC capabilities due to their mobility, flexibility, and cost efficiency, making them well-suited for time-critical operations. In this study, an ISAC-enabled UAV framework is proposed for disaster response, where UAVs simultaneously perform environmental sensing, such as survivor detection and debris mapping, while maintaining reliable communication with ground stations. A unified system model is developed to jointly optimize beamforming, power allocation, and resource partitioning between sensing and communication while ensuring a minimum communication quality of service (QoS). Additionally, an orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM)-based dual-functional waveform is introduced to balance sensing accuracy and communication performance. Simulation results demonstrate improved sensing coverage and communication reliability compared to conventional schemes, along with reduced hardware complexity and more efficient spectrum utilization.

title: Propagation and Rate-Aware Cell Switching Optimization in HAPS-Assisted Wireless Networks.
abstract: Cell switching is a promising approach for improving energy efficiency in wireless networks; however, existing studies largely rely on simplified models and energy-centric formulations that overlook key performance-limiting factors. This paper revisits the cell switching concept by redefining its modeling assumptions and mathematical formulation, explicitly incorporating realistic propagation effects such as building entry loss (BEL) and atmospheric losses relevant to non-terrestrial networks (NTN), particularly high-altitude platform station (HAPS). Beyond proposing a new cell switching strategy, the conventional energy-focused problem is reformulated as a multi-objective optimization framework that jointly minimizes power consumption, unconnected users, and data rate degradation. Through this reformulation, the proposed methods ensure that energy-efficient operation is achieved without compromising user connectivity and data rate performance, thereby inherently supporting sustainability objectives for sixth-generation (6G) networks. To solve this reformulated problem, two complementary approaches are employed: the weighted sum method (WSM), which enables a flexible and adaptive weighting mechanism, and the -constraint-inspired method ( CM), which converts connectivity and rate-related objectives into constraints within the conventional energy-focused problem. Moreover, unlike prior work relying only on simulations, this study combines system-level simulations with Sionna–OpenAirInterface (OAI) based emulation on a smaller network to validate the proposed cell switching concept under realistic conditions. The results show that, compared to the conventional approach, WSM reduces rate degradation for up to 70% for high-loss indoor users and eliminates the 44% drop for low-loss indoor users.

title: Neural Beamforming with Doppler-Aware Sparse Attention for High Mobility Environments.
abstract: Beamforming has significance for enhancing spectral efficiency and mitigating interference in multi-antenna wireless systems, facilitating spatial multiplexing and diversity in dense and high mobility scenarios. Traditional beamforming techniques such as zero-forcing beamforming (ZFBF) and minimum mean square error (MMSE) beamforming experience performance deterioration under adverse channel conditions. Deep learning-based beamforming offers an alternative with nonlinear mappings from channel state information (CSI) to beamforming weights by improving robustness against dynamic channel environments. Transformer-based models are particularly effective due to their ability to model long-range dependencies across time and frequency. However, their quadratic attention complexity limits scalability in large OFDM grids. Recent studies address this issue through sparse attention mechanisms that reduce complexity while maintaining expressiveness, yet often employ patterns that disregard channel dynamics, as they are not specifically designed for wireless communication scenarios. In this work, we propose a Doppler-aware Sparse Neural Network Beamforming (Doppler-aware Sparse NNBF) model that incorporates a channel-adaptive sparse attention mechanism in a multi-user single-input multiple-output (MU-SIMO) setting. The proposed sparsity structure is configurable along 2D time-frequency axes based on channel dynamics and is theoretically proven to ensure full connectivity within p hops, where p is the number of attention heads. Simulation results under urban macro (UMa) channel conditions show that Doppler-aware Sparse NNBF significantly outperforms both a fixed-pattern baseline, referred to as Standard Sparse NNBF, and conventional beamforming techniques ZFBF and MMSE beamforming in high mobility scenarios, while maintaining structured sparsity with a controlled number of attended keys per query.

title: Limitations and Enhancements for Network Energy Savings Towards 6G: Time Domain Adaptations.
abstract: Network Energy Saving (NES) techniques are becoming increasingly important for the radio access networks towards 6G, considering the high demand for beamforming due to higher frequency bands in 6G. This indicates even higher energy consumption and motivates further NES enhancements in 6G. Although cell discontinuous transmission (DTX) has been standardized to reduce energy consumption, its effectiveness is constrained by the time-domain occupancy of mandatory common signaling (e.g. SIB1), particularly when multiple beams are used. In this paper, we investigate the impact of beamforming on cell DTX performance and analyze how periodic transmission of common signals limits energy savings. To address this limitation, we evaluate a standalone on-demand System Information Block (SIB1) mechanism, in which system information is transmitted only upon explicit user equipment request. Simulation results show that, while beamforming improves interference, reducing periodic SIB1 transmission is necessary to decrease time-domain occupancy. In a standalone configuration, on-demand SIB1 reduces energy consumption and delay in beamforming deployments particularly for future 6G deployments using frequency bands of FR3 (7.125 GHz to 24.25 GHz).

title: Energy-Efficient Uplink-Downlink Decoupling for 6G TN-NTN Multi-Connectivity.
abstract: In 6G, LEO satellites complement terrestrial networks by extending coverage and offloading downlink services. However, direct satellite access faces a severe uplink energy bottleneck: required transmit power far exceeds handheld device capabilities. We propose decoupling uplink and downlink associations: uplink via short-range infrastructure (TN, UAV, HAPS) and downlink via satellite. Using 3GPP-compliant link budget analysis, we quantify substantial uplink power gaps and demonstrate order-of-magnitude battery lifetime extension with over 90% energy savings versus satellite-only operation. We address protocol feasibility through disaggregated RAN that eliminates inter-BS HARQ coordination overhead, and evaluate adaptive HARQ strategies (HARQ-less, independent, bundled). Results show bundled HARQ achieves substantial power reduction while maintaining high reliability with minimal delay overhead.

title: Digital Twin-Enabled Proactive Resource Management for Connected Robotics.
abstract: Industrial connected robots depend on reliable wireless communication to meet mobility and quality of service requirements. Conventional wireless network management approaches are mostly reactive and become inadequate in dynamic factory environments, particularly when high-frequency technologies such as millimeter wave and LiFi are used. This paper presents digital twin-enabled proactive wireless resource management for connected robotics. A proof-of-concept digital twin of an industrial environment is developed, capturing robot states, trajectories, and line-of-sight link characteristics, and enabling predictive interaction with the network. By exploiting future-aware information from the digital twin, network decisions such as resource allocation and handovers are performed proactively to prevent connectivity degradation. Two representative use cases are investigated. The first considers line-of-sight-aware resource management in heterogeneous LiFi-RF networks, achieving around 16 percentage improvement in the robot’s experienced data rate. The second addresses proactive handover management in 5G mobile networks, significantly reducing service interruption time due to handovers. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of network digital twins in enhancing wireless performance and ensuring seamless connectivity for industrial robots.

title: Coverage Enhancement through Network Controlled Repeaters: An XR perspective.
abstract: eXtended Reality (XR) is expected to be one of the most demanding and socially impactful application categories for future 6G networks. As 6G moves toward supporting immersive experiences with ultra high data rates and low latency, it becomes essential to explore novel radio access network (RAN) enhancements. In this context, this paper investigates the potential of network controlled repeaters (NCRs) as a scalable RAN element to support XR deployments. NCRs differ from conventional repeaters by enabling network driven beamforming and resource management, allowing the base station (gNB) to coordinate beam selection and direct signal relaying for more efficient coverage extension. We evaluate the performance of NCRs in simple (with single gNB and NCR) and complex (multiple gNB’s and NCR’s) urban XR scenarios. Users are placed indoor and outdoor and we investigate for two representative frequency ranges: FR1 (4GHz) and FR2 (28GHz). XR applications are emulated by considering their appropriate traffic models with the traffic parameters set from experimentally collected XR traffic. Key performance indicators such as signal to noise interference ratio (SINR), block error rate (BLER) and throughput heat maps are analyzed. In both simple and complex configurations, NCRs achieve substantially higher throughput and SINR, while reducing BLER for improved reliability. In scenarios with multiple base stations and NCRs, coverage is significantly expanded, making NCRs highly effective for large scale deployments. These improvements in link reliability, coverage, and XR quality of experience demonstrate the practical value of NCR enabled architectures for meeting the growing demands of 6G XR applications.

title: Joint Near-Field/Far-Field Beam split-based Allocation in Multi-User THz Wideband Systems.
abstract: Wideband TeraHertz (THz) networks are anticipated to provide extremely high data rates and massive device connectivity, catering to the needs of 6G applications. While THz systems have demonstrated strong performance in the Far-Field (FF), recent research has highlighted the importance of accounting for Near-Field (NF) conditions. However, NF communications may suffer severe degradations due to the beam split effect. In this work, we address the weighted sum-rate maximization problem with NF-FF multi-user coexistence, for which we propose a two-step beamforming and resource allocation approach. In the first step, we design a low-complexity subarray–group assignment that leverages NF-FF spatial multiplexing. In the second step, given the selected subarray–group matching, we perform a beam split–aware intra-group resource allocation method that exploits multi-user diversity in NF-FF. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms benchmarks in terms of sumrate, while improving user fairness.1

title: Statistics Approximation-Enabled Distributed Beamforming for Cell-Free Massive MIMO.
abstract: We study a distributed beamforming approach for cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output networks, referred to as Global Statistics & Local Instantaneous information-based minimum mean-square error (GSLI-MMSE). The scenario with multi-antenna access points (APs) is considered over three different channel models: correlated Rician fading with fixed or random line-of-sight (LoS) phase-shifts, and correlated Rayleigh fading. With the aid of matrix inversion derivations, we can construct the conventional MMSE combining from the perspective of each AP, where global instantaneous information is involved. Then, for an arbitrary AP, we apply the statistics approximation methodology to approximate instantaneous terms related to other APs by channel statistics to construct the distributed combining scheme at each AP with local instantaneous information and global statistics. With the aid of uplink-downlink duality, we derive the respective GSLI-MMSE precoding schemes. Numerical results showcase that the proposed GSLI-MMSE scheme demonstrates performance comparable to the optimal centralized MMSE scheme, under the stable LoS conditions, e.g., with static users having Rician fading with a fixed LoS path.

title: Synergizing Global Pattern Learning and Time Order Characterization in Mobile Channel Prediction: An RWKV-Based Approach.
abstract: Owing to the potential to reduce pilot overhead and mitigate channel aging, channel prediction is emerging as an important research topic in wireless communications. Meanwhile, deep neural networks are becoming a foundational technology for high-precision prediction thanks to their excellent non-linear representation capabilities. In this paper, we conceive a task-driven prediction network, which aims to deeply synergize the following two functions: learning global patterns for shareable features across adjacent time slots and structurally encoding time order to characterize the inherent causality within the channel dynamics. To implement channel prediction accuracy, we employ RWKV (receptance weighted key value) as network backbone and adapt it to the task’s specific characteristics, utilizing its deep interleaved learning architecture to extract global patterns across multiple channel samples and leveraging its unique exponential decay to characterize temporal order. These task-driven unique designs significantly improve the learning efficiency of prediction network. Comprehensive experimental evaluations demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method over current data-driven methods, such as long short-term memory and Transformer, in the channel prediction task, including 1.84~4.29 dB gains in normalized mean squared error and 2.6~10.5 percentage point gains in cosine correlation.

title: Joint Trajectory and Resource Optimization for Secure UAV Communications Based on Graph Attention Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: UAV communications have been a vital technology for 5G and the forthcoming 6G wireless communications. However, the realization of secure communication remains a critical challenge due to the broadcast nature of UAV links. In this paper, we investigate a UAV-assisted framework, where the UAV is deployed as a flying base station (BS) to serve multiple user equipments (UEs) against eavesdropping threats. We propose a Graph Attention Reinforcement Learning for Secure Communications (GARL-SC) algorithm, where the complex relational features among UAV and UEs are extracted by Graph Attention Network (GAT) for jointly optimizing the UAV trajectory. We further develop Secure Hierarchical Bandwidth Allocation (SHBA) algorithm and Adaptive Hybrid Power Allocation (AHPA) algorithm for optimizing transmission power control and bandwidth allocation, aiming at maximizing the overall throughput and secrecy rate. From the experimental results, the proposed algorithm has considerable performance gains over existing traditional and Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-based baselines in terms of the optimization objective.

title: Bandwidth Enhanced Rydberg Atomic Quantum Receivers for Wireless Communication and Sensing.
abstract: Rydberg atomic quantum receivers (RAQRs) have emerged as highly sensitive receivers for future communication and sensing systems. However, conventional RAQRs are primarily effective for single-carrier and narrowband reception, typically with an operational bandwidth of only a few hundred kilohertz. To enable the reception of multi-carrier signals with larger bandwidth, we propose a multi-carrier Rydberg atomic quantum receiver (MC-RAQR) architecture based on a five-level quantum system model. We analyze the amplitude and phase of the output laser in MC-RAQR and extract the baseband electrical signal for signal processing. Furthermore, we quantify the performance of MC-RAQR in multi-carrier communication and sensing by studying the channel capacity and distance estimation, respectively. Numerical results show that the MC-RAQR is capable of achieving a bandwidth of $7.2$ MHz, which is an order of magnitude larger than conventional RAQRs. Besides, compared to conventional receivers, MC-RAQR can improve the capacity and distance estimation by $18$-fold and $10^3$-fold, respectively. This validates the superiority of MC-RAQR in receiving multi-carrier signal, and demonstrates its compatibility in detecting waveforms such as orthogonal frequency‐division multiplexing.

title: Enhanced Multi-Target Detection and Range-Angle Estimation via RIS Space-Time Beamforming.
abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-enabled multi-target sensing using communication waveforms. We propose to leverage both space-domain and time-domain RIS beamforming gains to further enhance the sensing performance. To this end, we propose a signal processing framework for multi-target sensing under RIS space-time beamforming, which jointly processes echo signals received under multiple time-varying RIS spatial beams. The framework consists of delay-domain signal processing for multi-target detection and range estimation, as well as space-time-domain signal processing for super-resolution angle estimation. We reveal that orthogonal RIS space-time beamforming codebook is optimal for the proposed signal processing method and design the RIS space-time beamforming by using the discrete Fourier transform matrix or the Hadamard matrix as the space-time codebook. The simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed space-time processing method in detection and super-resolution estimation performance compared to the traditional method under RIS spatial beamforming.

title: DRL-Based Mitigation Against Nonreciprocal RIS-Aided Channel Reciprocity Attacks.
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) technology enhances wireless communication performance, but it also introduces new vulnerabilities. This paper investigates channel reciprocity attack (CRACK) threats in multi-antenna wireless systems operating in time-division duplexing mode using a physically consistent nonreciprocal RIS (NR-RIS) model. CRACK can degrade the communication rate by distorting the downlink precoding, without requiring any additional signal transmission or channel state information (CSI). Unlike conventional RIS jamming strategies, the NR-RIS does not need synchronization with the legitimate system and thus can operate with slow or fixed configurations to implement CRACK, complicating corresponding defensive precoding designs. To counter this threat, we develop "SecureCoder," a deep reinforcement learning-based framework that can mitigate NR-RIS CRACK by determining an improved downlink precoder matrix using the estimated uplink CSI. Simulations confirm the severe degradation caused by NR-RIS CRACK and demonstrate the effectiveness of SecureCoder in improving the system throughput.

title: Attention-Aided Boundary Equilibrium GAN for Wideband Power Amplifier Predistortion.
abstract: Digital predistortion (DPD) is an essential technique for linearizing power amplifiers (PAs) in wideband wireless communication systems. Neural networks (NNs) have become a mainstream solution for DPD due to their nonlinear approximation capabilities. However, as escalating signal bandwidths intensify memory effects, the efficacy of conventional models is limited by the point-wise error minimization objective, which tends to learn a deterministic average mapping that cannot fully capture the complex statistical distribution of the PA’s inverse characteristics. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes a novel DPD method that leverages a boundary equilibrium generative adversarial network (BEGAN) for robust distributional learning of the PA’s inverse characteristics. An integrated attention mechanism further identifies and weights critical temporal features to address long-term memory effects. Simulation results demonstrate the proposed method outperforms existing NN-based approaches for a 100 MHz input signal, achieving approximately 2 dB enhancements in both normalized mean square error (NMSE) and adjacent channel power ratio (ACPR).

title: Mutual Coupling Kernel Approximation for Continuous Aperture Beamforming.
abstract: A mutual coupling aware beamforming design is proposed for continuous aperture arrays (CAPAs), a paradigm that features continuous electromagnetic (EM) radiating surfaces. The optimal uni-polarized continuous aperture beamforming is derived as a function of the inverse of the mutual coupling kernel. To address the non-trivial kernel inverse, a kernel approximation method is proposed based on the Fourier transform and Gauss-Legendre quadrature, resulting in a closed-form optimal beamforming solution. Numerical results validate the rapid convergence of the proposed approximation. It also reveals the anisotropic nature of mutual coupling in uni-polarized CAPAs, demonstrating that its effect can be either constructive or destructive depending on the direction of radiation relative to the polarization direction.

title: Joint Optimization of Communication and Sensing Performance for ISAC Systems Under Jamming.
abstract: This paper investigates the communication and sensing performance of integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems under constrained energy consumption and malicious jamming, with imperfect channel state information (CSI). We formulate a problem of maximizing the minimum communication performance (MCP) under the sensing constraint by jointly optimizing base station (BS) beamforming, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) transmit and receive beamforming. To address this coupled non-convex problem, we develop an alternating optimization (AO)-based scheme. Specifically, we first transform the BS beamforming problem into a semidefinite program (SDP) problem and solve it using the semidefinite relaxation (SDR) method. Second, auxiliary variables are introduced to solve the UAV beamforming problem by employing the successive convex approximation (SCA) method. Subsequently, the UAV receive beamforming optimization problem is transformed into a Rayleigh quotient problem, thus yielding a closed-form solution for the receive beamforming vector. Extensive simulation results validate that the proposed scheme exhibits excellent convergence properties and outperforms benchmarks.

title: Channel-Adaptive Generative Semantic Communication with Dynamic Bandwidth Allocation for Future 6G Systems.
abstract: Deep learning-based semantic communication (SemCom) has emerged as a key technology for 6G networks to improve information transmission efficiency. However, existing adaptive-rate frameworks typically operate as black boxes, failing to jointly optimize semantic distortion and bandwidth consumption under dynamic channel conditions. To address this, we propose an Ordered Variational Autoencoder-based Generative SemCom (OVAE-GSemCom) framework guided by semantic rate-distortion (SRD). By enforcing a strict ordering in semantic confidence via nested dropout training, the framework transforms the VAE latent space into an importance-ranked semantic representation, enabling efficient semantic feature selection. Building on this ordered representation, a learnable semantic water-filling mechanism is designed to dynamically allocate bandwidth, jointly optimizing semantic reconstruction and channel resource usage. The simulation results demonstrate that OVAE-GSemCom achieves superior semantic rate-distortion performance, requiring only approximately $\frac{1}{6}$ of the bandwidth required by conventional methods while maintaining high perceptual quality.

title: Learning to Jointly Optimize Antenna Positioning and Beamforming for Movable Antenna-Aided Systems.
abstract: The recently emerged movable antenna (MA) and fluid antenna technologies offer promising solutions to enhance the spatial degrees of freedom in wireless systems by dynamically adjusting the positions of transmit or receive antennas within given regions. In this paper, we aim to address the joint optimization problem of antenna positioning and beamforming in MA-aided multi-user downlink transmission systems. This problem involves mixed discrete antenna position and continuous beamforming weight variables, along with coupled distance constraints on antenna positions, which pose significant challenges for optimization algorithm design. To overcome these challenges, we propose an end-to-end deep learning framework, consisting of a positioning model that handles the discrete variables and the coupled constraints, and a beamforming model that handles the continuous variables. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves superior sum rate performance, yet with much reduced computation time compared to existing methods.

title: Joint Communication and Computation in Optical System with Mach-Zehnder Modulator.
abstract: 6G requires intelligent computations in the communication networks. Conventional scheme is to compute in a standalone processor after receiving the raw data transmitted through the communication system. In this paper, we present a technique of processing image classification tasks during data transmission through optical fiber communication systems instead of processing after transmission in the classical networks, which complies with the joint communication and computation (J2C) scheme. The Mach-Zehnder modulators (MZM) in optical system exhibit behaviors of Bessel functions when the peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) of the transmitted signal is large, which imposes a limitation in modern communication system. In this paper, we demonstrated that this unwanted Bessel-function behavior can be turned useful if the signal is computed during transmission. Simulation results with Cifar-10 datasets show that the proposed MZM-based J2C scheme outperforms the classical scheme in both accuracy and efficiency.

title: A Novel Channel Estimation Scheme for OTFS MIMO Systems Assisted with Double IRSs.
abstract: Intelligent-reflecting-surfaces (IRSs) cooperation is an available way to enhance signal coverage for Internet of Things by dynamically adjusting the phases of the elements on the IRSs. This paper investigates the channel estimation of a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system in orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) assisted by double IRSs to enable reliable communication in high-mobility environments, and a novel channel estimation scheme is developed to overcome the hybrid-channel estimation challenge introduced by double IRSs. Specifically, to reduce computational complexity and improve estimation efficiency, three orthogonal subcarrier subsets are used to implement channel estimation for the three cascaded channels respectively. Furthermore, to induce linearly varying frequency offsets for different links, the phases of the elements on the two IRSs are rotated dynamically, which endows each cascaded channel with unique spectral characteristics and enhances multipath separability. Meanwhile, each individual link is efficiently estimated in the delay-Doppler domain via the orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) algorithm. Simulation results are presented to validate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed scheme in channel estimation for double-IRS assisted MIMO systems.

title: Extended Target Tracking for Contour-Aware Predictive Beamforming in ISAC Systems.
abstract: Recent advances in massive multiple-input multiple-output and millimeter-wave technologies have enabled target sensing with sub-degree angular and decimeter-level range resolution. Consequently, conventional point-target models become inadequate for capturing the detailed spatial characteristics of targets during tracking. In this work, we introduce the concept of target contour, which is modeled by the truncated Fourier series to capture the spatial extent of the target, for extended target tracking within an integrated sensing and communication framework. A predictive beamforming design is developed, where each tracking period is divided into a sensing block and a data block. During the sensing block, the base station (BS) performs beam scanning and applies maximum likelihood estimation to extract scatterer measurements along the target contour. These measurements are then processed by an extended Kalman filter to jointly estimate the target’s kinematic states and contour parameters, which are further used to predict the direction of the target-mounted communication terminal (CT). In the subsequent data block, the BS steers an adjustable narrow beam towards the predicted CT direction to establish reliable communication link. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves robust target tracking performance and high communication rate under complicated target trajectories.

title: Energy-Efficient Resource Management via Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning in O-RAN.
abstract: Sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks are expected to meet all the demands of the next decade, a feasibility that is only possible with advances in network design and management. This paper first proposes a unified resource management framework for a 6G-based network architecture that includes an Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) deployment and then defines a hierarchical network energy control and resource management approach. Leveraging the openness of O-RAN, the proposed novel Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL)-based scheme provides two-level centralized agent policy evaluation and decentralized agent real-time scheduling optimization, thereby minimizing system energy consumption while ensuring Quality of Service (QoS). To validate the performance of this management approach, we propose a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)based algorithm for each level. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of this solution in terms of throughput, user-experienced data rate, and energy consumption.

title: Age of Information Minimization for Buffer-Aided Uplink Systems via Movable Antennas.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate an uplink multiple-access system assisted by movable antennas (MAs), with the objective of minimizing the long-term average weighted Age of Information (LAW-AoI). To tackle the resulting nonconvex mixed-integer programming problem from the joint optimization of MA positioning and user scheduling, we develop an adaptive transmission policy under a Lyapunov optimization framework. An alternating optimization approach incorporating successive convex approximation (SCA) is introduced to efficiently update the MA positions, while a dynamic time-division multiple access (TDMA)-based scheduling strategy is designed to maintain queue stability and information freshness. Simulation results confirm that the proposed scheme achieves a significant reduction in average AoI compared to conventional benchmark methods, demonstrating the effectiveness of MA-assisted optimization in time-sensitive wireless communication systems.

title: Outage Performance of PASS Under Random LoS Blockage.
abstract: Pinching antenna systems (PASS) offer considerable potential for wireless communications due to their unique ability to dynamically reconfigure radiation positions along a waveguide. However, the performance of PASS remains a critical challenge in the presence of random line-of-sight (LoS) blockage, leading to significant attenuation and even communication outages. In this paper, the outage performance of PASS in the presence of LoS blockage is investigated from the perspective of stochastic geometry. Obstacles are modeled as a homogeneous Poisson point process that captures the randomness in their spatial distribution and geometric dimensions. Based on the proposed blockage model, closed-form analytical and asymptotic expressions for the outage probability are obtained. The numerical results reveal that denser obstacle environments or statistically larger obstacles substantially increase the outage probability of PASS.

title: Energy Consumption Modeling and Optimization for Hybrid PLC/WLC Systems.
abstract: Hybrid Power Line Communication (PLC) and Wireless Communication (WLC) technology provides a reliable and cost-effective communication framework for applications such as smart grids and the Industrial Internet of Things (IoT), by synergistically leveraging the complementary strengths of both PLC and WLC. However, most existing energy efficiency studies have focused on a single communication medium, and the energy efficiency of hybrid PLC/WLC systems has not yet been systematically modeled or analyzed. To address this issue, closed-form expressions for the energy consumption per bit (bEC) of PLC and WLC are derived, providing a theoretical foundation for subsequent energy efficiency evaluation. Furthermore, a low-complexity Delay-Constrained Energy Consumption Optimization (DC-ECO) algorithm is proposed to minimize the overall system energy consumption through dynamic allocation between PLC channels and WLC channels. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed DC-ECO algorithm reduces the total energy consumption by more than 50% compared with the conventional single WLC scheme. Under low-load conditions, the performance gap from the theoretical lower bound is <5%, significantly improving the energy efficiency while satisfying the transmission delay requirements, thereby providing an effective and practical solution for future energy-efficient hybrid communication systems.

title: A Physical Layer Security Method Based on Multi-AAV Collaborative Beamforming.
abstract: With the development of the low-altitude economy, a large number of autonomous aerial vehicles (AAVs) will be deployed in low-altitude environments, capable of effectively performing data collection and relay tasks. Unlike non-line-of-sight transmission environments on the ground, the line-of-sight transmission of AAVs offers greater channel gain while facing a higher risk of data interception. Although the traditional encryption method can decrease the risk of data being cracked, it cannot diminish the probability of data being intercepted by eavesdroppers. In this paper, we propose a physical layer security method based on the distributed collaborative beamforming for the multi-AAV networks, in which both scenarios of known and unknown eavesdropper locations are considered. Then, two beamforming algorithms are designed for these scenarios. Besides, the theoretical performance is derived for the case where the location of the eavesdropper is known, while for the unknown-location case, a beamforming scheme based on the generalized Rayleigh quotient is introduced to substantially improve the secure transmission performance. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves a substantial improvement in average secrecy rate without increasing the payload of AAVs compared with the conventional methods.

title: iRadioDiff: Physics-Informed Diffusion Model for Indoor Radio Map Construction and Localization.
abstract: Radio maps (RMs) serve as environment-aware electromagnetic (EM) representations that connect scenario geometry and material properties to the spatial distribution of signal strength, enabling localization without costly in-situ measurements. However, constructing high-fidelity indoor RMs remains challenging due to the prohibitive latency of EM solvers and the limitations of learning-based methods, which often rely on sparse measurements or assumptions of homogeneous material, which are misaligned with the heterogeneous and multipath-rich nature of indoor environments. To overcome these challenges, we propose iRadioDiff, a sampling-free diffusion-based framework for indoor RM construction. iRadioDiff is conditioned on access point (AP) positions, and physics-informed prompt encoded by material reflection and transmission coefficients. It further incorporates multipath-critical priors, including diffraction points, strong transmission boundaries, and line-of-sight (LoS) contours, to guide the generative process via conditional channels and boundary-weighted objectives. This design enables accurate modeling of non-stationary field discontinuities and efficient construction of physically consistent RMs. Experiments demonstrate that iRadioDiff achieves state-of-the-art performance in indoor RM construction and received signal strength based indoor localization, which offers effective generalization across layouts and material configurations. Code is available at https://github.com/UNIC-Lab/iRadioDiff.

title: An Alternating Directional Dual-RBF Approach for Joint Multi-BSs and Multi-RISs Deployment.
abstract: The deployment of sixth-generation (6G) networks must overcome the spatial mismatch between network capacity and traffic demand caused by heterogeneous traffic patterns, all while managing high energy consumption. To achieve sustainable network deployment, this paper investigates the joint deployment of base stations (BSs) and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) to maximize Integrated Relative Energy Efficiency (IREE). We propose an Alternating Directional Dual-Radial Basis Function (ADD-RBF) framework, which models BSs and RISs as two distinct classes of radial basis neurons within a unified architecture. This framework enables the alternating optimization of active beamforming, bandwidth allocation, and node locations for BSs, alongside the passive beamforming and placements for RISs, to enhance capacity while mitigating spatial traffic mismatches. Simulation results demonstrate that the ADD-RBF scheme effectively mitigates the traffic-capacity mismatch while achieving reduced energy consumption, confirming the complementary roles of both components: RISs efficiently resolve localized traffic hotspots, while BSs address systemic capacity shortages. These findings offer practical guidelines for green 6G network design.

title: Pruned Causal Inference Enabled Active Deception for Covert Internet of Things (IoT).
abstract: In this paper, the problem of covert wireless communication in Internet of Things (IoT) systems under passive eavesdropping attacks is investigated. In the considered model, an IoT system intents to transmit a confidential signal from an origin to a destination under time and energy limitations. Meanwhile, a group of eavesdroppers attacks the IoT system by only passively listening to the confidential transmission without transmitting any signals. By detecting the oscillator leakage, the IoT devices can perceive the existence of nearby passive eavesdropping attacks. In this case, we propose an active deception scheme, with which the IoT devices will strategically transmit fake signals to distract and expose the passive eavesdroppers. Then, the passive eavesdroppers have to carefully choose the signal to intercept while avoiding exposure. The complex interaction among IoT devices and passive eavesdroppers is captured using tools from dynamic deception game, within which the conflicting goals of IoT system privacy and eavesdropping attacks are captured in multi-attribute utilities. Considering the challenges on searching the perfect bayesian equilibrium (PBE) in the partially observable, large-scale wireless IoT system, a pruned causal inference based approach is proposed. Simulation results show that the proposed method yields an up to 63.6% improvement in the convergence speed as compared to the traditional Bayesian-inference algorithm, while exhibiting an up to 229% improvement in security performance as compared to a traditional deception strategy that is designed by an open-loop algorithm.

title: Deep Unfolding Supported Cell-free Anti-jamming Coordinated Multipoint Beam Pattern Synthesis.
abstract: Traditional cell-free anti-jamming beamforming faces high complexity, poor adaptability, and limited scalability. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a novel two-stage deep unfolding-assisted coordinated multipoint beam pattern synthesis (DUCoMP-BPS) scheme, which seamlessly integrates model-based optimization with data-driven learning. In the first stage, each access point (AP) independently determines analog beamforming using local angle information with deep unfolding accelerating computation, eliminating the need for real-time central processing unit (CPU) communication. Then, the CPU aggregates analog beamforming weights from multiple APs to perform cooperative digital beamforming. The proposed scheme possesses excellent scalability with complexity increasing linearly with the number of APs. Simulations show that DUCoMP-BPS shows strong anti-jamming communication robustness and reduces single-AP analog beamforming runtime by about 67% compared to model-driven methods and outperforms the data-driven approach in beam pattern performance. For example, under the configuration of 10 APs and 64 antennas per AP, < 1 dB mainlobe ripple can be achieved while maintaining ≤ -15 dB sidelobe and two 8°/-30 dB nulls.

title: Unified Channel Estimation Framework for Flexible Sparse DMRS Patterns via Transformer-based Point Cloud Neural Operator.
abstract: In current mobile communication systems up to 5G, orthogonal demodulation reference signals (DMRS) are inserted per resource block (RB) and for each layer of spatial multiplexing. However, as we move to increase the number of layers in 6G, DMRS overhead potentially limits the expected benefits of capacity growth. While CNN channel estimation methods under sparse DMRS allocation (such as ReEsNet and ChannelNet) have been proposed, these existing models are trained for specific DMRS patterns and cannot handle practical systems with resource schedulers, where RB allocation patterns vary dynamically over time slots. This configuration fragmentation requires massive dedicated model libraries, limiting scheduling flexibility. To address these fundamental issues, this paper proposes a unified channel estimation framework based on Transformer architecture inheriting the concept of point cloud neural operator, enabling a single model to handle arbitrary DMRS patterns and densities flexibly. Extensive simulations across 5 distinct configurations demonstrate that the proposed unified model achieves 5.0 to 5.5 dB improvement over dedicated ReEsNets and up to 11.0 dB improvement over classical LS estimation at 50% DMRS density, while enabling 50 to 75% overhead reduction. The unified approach eliminates the need for massive model libraries and does not limit the potential gains of scheduling operations, providing a practical solution for next generation wireless systems.

title: The Asymptotic Vector Witsenhausen Counterexample: When Optimal Transport Meets the Hypersphere.
abstract: Implicit communication has attracted considerable recent attention because it holds the promise of enabling decentralized decision-making or control with nonclassical information in next-generation industrial internet-of-things and other cyberphysical systems. The Witsenhausen counterexample plays a vital role in understanding implicit communication based decentralized control. Unfortunately, computing the optimal solution of the scalar Witsenhausen counterexample has been shown to be NP-complete. In this paper, we are interested in an asymptotic vector Witsenhausen counterexample with sufficiently large dimension, which also sheds light on the performance upper bound of its scalar version. In this context, the sphere hardening effect allows us to build a unified framework based on optimal transport from the surface of a high-dimensional sphere to a target domain in Euclidean space. Both the target domain and transport plan are judiciously conceived in order to minimize the mean-square error (MSE) in estimating variables distributed in the target domain, given a constraint on the transport cost. By leveraging the sphere packing and covering theorems in high-dimensional geometry, we obtain the closed-form MSE. Numerical results not only validate our theoretical analysis, but also demonstrate the performance gain of the optimal transport-based policy over the information theory-based policy inspired by dirty-paper coding and joint source-channel coding.

title: When Guidance Turns Poisonous: Backdooring the SAR-guided Cloud Removal Model.
abstract: Models for optical-image cloud removal guided by Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) have made remarkable progress in addressing cloud occlusion in remote sensing. However, the vulnerability of such models to backdoor attacks remains unexplored. To fill this gap, we present the first backdoor attack on SAR-guided optical-image cloud removal models. Unlike previous approaches that embed triggers into optical images, we embed triggers into SAR images. By exploiting the inherent speckle-like texture of SAR imagery, we design a frequency-aware speckle trigger that is both stealthy and robust against common data augmentations. After training on poisoned data, the backdoored model generates manipulated cloud-free outputs that faithfully reconstruct an attacker-specified target scene when the trigger is present, while preserving high-quality restoration performance on clean inputs. We evaluate three commonly used SAR-guided optical-image cloud removal models on public datasets, and the experimental results demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms other triggers designed for optical images.
