title: Rotatable Antenna Array-Enhanced Null Steering: Performance Analysis and Optimization.
abstract: Conventional fixed-orientation antenna (FOA) arrays offer limited degrees of freedom (DoF) for flexible beamforming such as null steering. To address this limitation, we propose a new rotatable antenna array (RAA) architecture in this paper, which enables three-dimensional (3D) rotational control of an antenna array to provide enhanced spatial flexibility for null steering. To characterize its performance, we aim to jointly optimize the 3D rotational angles of the RAA, to maximize the beam gain over a given desired direction, while nulling those over multiple interference directions under zero-forcing (ZF) beamforming. However, this problem is non-convex and challenging to tackle due to the highly nonlinear expression of the beam gain in terms of the rotational angles. To gain insights, we first examine several special cases including both isotropic and directional antenna radiation patterns, deriving the conditions under which full beam gain can be achieved over the desired direction while meeting the nulling constraints for interference directions. These conditions clearly indicate that compared with FOA arrays, RAAs can significantly relax the angular separation requirement for achieving effective null steering. For other general cases, we propose a sequential update algorithm, that iteratively refines the 3D rotational angles by discretizing the 3D angular search space. To avoid undesired local optimum, a Gibbs sampling (GS) procedure is also employed between two consecutive rounds of sequential update for solution exploration. Simulation results verify our analytical results and show superior null-steering performance of RAAs to FOA arrays.

title: Digital Twin-Assisted Measurement Design and Channel Statistics Prediction.
abstract: Prediction of wireless channels and their statistics is a fundamental procedure for ensuring performance guarantees in wireless systems. Statistical radio maps powered by Gaussian processes (GPs) offer flexible, non-parametric frameworks, but their performance depends critically on the choice of mean and covariance functions. These are typically learned from dense measurements without exploiting environmental geometry. Digital twins (DTs) of wireless environments leverage computational power to incorporate geometric information; however, they require costly calibration to accurately capture material and propagation characteristics. This work introduces a hybrid channel prediction framework that leverages uncalibrated DTs derived from open-source maps to extract geometry-induced prior information for GP prediction. These structural priors are fused with a small number of channel measurements, enabling data-efficient prediction of channel statistics across the entire environment. By exploiting the uncertainty quantification inherent to GPs, the framework supports principled measurement selection by identifying informative probing locations under resource constraints. Through this integration of imperfect DTs with statistical learning, the proposed method reduces measurement overhead, improves prediction accuracy, and establishes a practical approach for resource-efficient wireless channel prediction.

title: RIS-assisted Maximum-SNR mmWave Communications via Stochastic Approximation.
abstract: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) have emerged as a solution to enhance the performance of millimeter wave (mmWave) wireless links by dynamically tuning the phase shift of a large number of reflecting elements. In this paper, we propose a practical framework to maximize signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for RIS-assisted mmWave Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) links. We first optimize the RIS phase shifts to maximize the received signal strength (RSS) by adopting Kiefer-Wolfowitz Stochastic Approximation (KWSA) where the gradient is approximated through RSS measurements. Upon optimizing the RIS configuration, we design the transmit and receive beamforming vectors based on the estimated channel and noise covariance matrices at the receiver. We implement the proposed method in a RIS-assisted mmWave software-defined radio (SDR) testbed based on USRP® and TMYTEK® platforms in an indoor laboratory environment. We demonstrate that the proposed RIS optimization approach achieves the highest RSS with almost half of the amount of RSS measurements required by the exhaustive grid search approach. Upon RIS optimization, we show that Tx/Rx beamformer optimization offers an additional 7 dB gain in SNR. Given an RSS-optimized RIS configuration, the proposed optimization of Tx/Rx beamformers to maximize SNR requires 51x less computations than exhaustive search.

title: Harnessing LLMs with Graph Representation Learning for Anomaly Detection in Microservices.
abstract: Large-scale microservice systems, characterized by distributed and complex architecture, pose substantial challenges for anomaly detection. Existing approaches operating at the trace or service level often fail to capture intricate and fine-grained dependencies between services, leading to suboptimal detection performance. To address these limitations, we propose a novel graph-based anomaly detection framework MAD-LLM, which takes advantage of the rich knowledge of Large Language Models (LLMs). Our approach consists of three key steps. First, we design a unified data model that integrates heterogeneous observability data, including traces, logs, and metrics, into a structured representation. Second, inspired by graph neural networks, we introduce a self-supervised neighbor aggregation module to fine-tune LLMs by incorporating local topological context from service dependency graph. Finally, we employ a fine-tuned LLM to generate node embeddings that encode the semantic and structural properties of a metric-aware events graph, which are leveraged for anomaly detection. Extensive experiments on five real-world datasets demonstrate the superiority of our approach. MAD-LLM achieves an average F1-score improvement of 9.1% over the best-performed baseline, with a maximum gain of 22.9% on the TraceBench dataset. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of our design and highlight its necessity for achieving optimal performance. The source code can be available at https://github.com/wz-01/MAD-LLM.

title: Joint Communication and Sensing Beamforming for Secure Transmission in 6G SAGINs.
abstract: In 6G space-air-ground integrated networks (SAGINs), integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables terrestrial devices to support secure computation offloading via simultaneous uplink transmission and eavesdropper detection using shared spectrum resources. However, non-orthogonal access induces severe multi-terminal interference (MTI), while limited angular resolution leads to uncertainty in eavesdropper localization—posing significant challenges to physical-layer security. To address this, we propose a joint ISAC beamforming design that maximizes communication performance while guaranteeing robust secrecy against directional eavesdroppers despite angular estimation uncertainty. To solve this non-convex, dynamic problem, we propose a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based deep reinforcement learning framework under the centralized-training-decentralized-execution (CTDE) paradigm, which learns adaptive beamforming policies in a model-free manner while enabling low-overhead online execution. Simulations show the method significantly improves communication performance and effectively resists worst-case eavesdropping, demonstrating its potential for securing future 6G ISAC-enabled SAGINs.

title: Movable-Antenna Position Optimization with Partial CSI via RACOS.
abstract: Movable antennas (MAs) are recognized as a promising technology for enhancing the performance of wireless communication by enabling local antenna movement. However, optimizing MA positions requires full channel knowledge within a continuous movement region, which incurs excessively high training overhead. To tackle this problem, this paper proposes a new antenna position optimization framework for MA systems without explicit channel state information (CSI). Unlike existing partial-CSI-based MA position optimization algorithms limited to point-to-point scenarios, the proposed framework can be applied to a broader range of problems involving more constraints and design variables. Its basic idea is to transform the constrained position optimization problem into a black-box problem with an unknown objective function. This problem is then solved by combining a penalty-based method and the randomized coordinate shrinking classification (RACOS) method. As a case study, we investigate a joint power control and antenna position optimization problem for an MA-enhanced cognitive radio system by applying the proposed framework. Numerical results demonstrate that our proposed framework can significantly outperform the conventional fixed-position antennas (FPAs) and other baseline schemes with or without explicit CSI.

title: Movable Antenna Position Optimization for Energy Efficient Secure Communications.
abstract: Movable antenna (MA) can be employed to enhance physical-layer security by reconfiguring wireless channel conditions for both legitimate users and eavesdroppers via local antenna movement. However, to achieve accurate and fast antenna movement, MA drivers entail non-negligible power consumption, rendering secure energy efficiency (SEE) optimization more critical compared to conventional fixed-position antenna (FPA) systems. To tackle this problem, this paper develops a new mechanical power model for two-dimensional (2D) MA arrays. Based on this model, we formulate a new SEE maximization problem, aiming to jointly optimize the MAs’ 2D moving velocities, 2D positions, and their transmit beamforming vector. Due to the complex mechanical power consumption model, this SEE maximization problem is difficult to solve optimally. To overcome this difficulty, we first uncover that the SEE always monotonically increases with the velocity of each MA in each dimension. For the remaining joint position and beamforming optimization, we develop a two-layer optimization framework. In the inner layer, the Dinkelbach algorithm is employed to derive the optimal beamforming solution in a generalized Rayleigh quotient form for any given MA positions. In the outer layer, a sequential update algorithm is proposed to iteratively refine the MA positions based on the optimal values obtained from the inner layer, jointly with Gibbs sampling to avoid local optimality. Numerical results show that the SEE of the considered system can be significantly improved compared with FPAs and other baseline schemes.

title: Optimizing Security Performance of LEO Satellite Communications with IRS against Mobile Diverse Eavesdroppers.
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite communication can complement to terrestrial networks by providing extended Internet access to remote regions, especially those in harsh environments. However, some operational satellites may work as Eavesdroppers (Eves), referred to as ESats, intercepting confidential signals during communication between the Ground Station (GS) and the Serving Satellite (SSat). Besides, Eavesdropping Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (EUAV) also poses a potential threat to satellite-ground communication along the extended propagation paths. In view of this, this paper deploys an Intelligent Reflecting Surface (IRS) near the GS within the satellite system, where several ESats and EUAV coexist and the satellite follows a predictable trajectory. We discuss the optimal transmit beamforming vector and IRS configuration to maximize the Ergodic Secrecy Rate (ESR) and minimize the Secrecy Outage Probability (SOP). Besides, to mitigate the multipath effect induced by the satellite mobility, the Doppler spread is taken into consideration, which is to be minimized. A Genetic Algorithm (GA) is introduced to solve this intractable non-convex multi-objective problem. To evaluate the efficiency of IRS deployment and IRS phase shift optimization, we compare our proposed scheme against benchmark strategies, including systems without IRS, with random IRS, and with Artificial Noise (AN). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed system achieves enhanced security and communication performance and outperforms baselines.

title: Efficient Privacy-Preserving Genetic Analysis via Distributed Function Secret Sharing.
abstract: Genetic research is pivotal for personalized medicine and understanding disease mechanisms, yet this field faces a critical privacy challenge due to the inherent sensitivity of genomic data. General Secure Multi-Party Computation protocols offer confidentiality but suffer from prohibitive communication and computational overheads, hindering their practical deployment. Function Secret Sharing (FSS) provides exceptional online efficiency, but its practicality is limited by reliance on trusted dealers or high offline costs in dealer-less constructions. To address these bottlenecks, this paper proposes an efficient privacy-preserving genetic analysis framework centered on distributed FSS. The core of our framework is a novel Dealer-less Compressed Full Domain Key Evaluation protocol. This protocol successfully adapts the early termination optimization to the dealer-less setting, reducing GGM tree traversal depth and PRG invocations without requiring a trusted dealer, which may be of independent interest. Furthermore, we leverage FSS-based primitive to construct efficient lookup tables and a secure division protocol. These building blocks are then applied to implement secure protocols for three crucial genetic analysis tasks including Secure Genomic Predicate Analysis, Secure Hamming Distance Evaluation, and Secure Bayesian Classification. Experimental results show our compressed full domain evaluation achieves up to a 3.99× latency reduction over prior FSS work. Compared to a SOTA general MPC framework, our full framework provides up to 31.03× less communication and 263.71× lower latency in both LAN and WAN environments.

title: Resource Allocation Strategy for AUVs-Assisted UWSN with MI Communication in Multi-Layer Ocean Current Environments.
abstract: Aiming at the challenges of low network coverage and limited battery power in underwater wireless sensor network (UWSN) operating within ocean currents, resource allocation strategy for autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs)-assisted UWSN with magnetic induction (MI) communication in multi-layer ocean current environments is investigated in this paper. Specifically, the target monitoring area is divided into multiple ocean current layers at unequal intervals. First, sensor nodes (SNs) are deployed in these ocean current layers. The effect of ocean currents on SNs is analyzed. An improved virtual force algorithm (I-VFA) is employed to enhance the network coverage of the UWSN. Then, AUVs navigate to specific ocean current layers and collect data from SNs via MI communication. A genetic algorithm (GA) is adopted to optimize the navigation trajectories of AUVs. The transmitting power of SNs and the distance between SNs and AUVs are jointly optimized to minimize the energy consumption of SNs under the constraints of energy causality, transmitting power, distance, and transmission time. The suboptimal solution to the formulated optimization problem is obtained by adopting the global search whale optimization algorithm (GSWOA). Simulation results show that the GSWOA has a faster convergence speed and better global search capability than other benchmark methods.

title: Robust Vision-Aided mmWave TDMA Hybrid Beamforming With Low-Resolution Phase Shifters.
abstract: Vision-aided beamforming is emerging as a key enabler for Next-Generation Multiple Access (NGMA), where multi-modal sensing and intelligent signal processing jointly enhance communication efficiency. However, extending vision-aided techniques to hybrid millimeter-wave (mmWave) architectures with limited-resolution phase shifters and ensuring robustness under dynamic environments remain challenging. This paper proposes a Vision-aided Hybrid Beamforming Network (VHBN) that explicitly embeds hardware constraints into a neural network trained with a physics-informed loss function. To enhance robustness, a Hierarchical Visual–Wireless Beamforming (HVWB) framework is further developed, where coarse visual predictions guide refined channel estimation through dictionary-based sparse reconstruction. Numerical results based on the DeepSense6G dataset demonstrate that: (i) the proposed approach achieves spectral efficiency nearly identical to that of conventional CSI-based schemes; (ii) VHBN offers greater hardware compliance for low-resolution phase shifters than existing CSI-free approaches; and (iii) HVWB exhibits superior robustness compared with existing vision-aided techniques in previously unseen environments. These results demonstrate the potential of vision-aided hybrid beamforming as a practical and intelligent solution toward NGMA realization.

title: Distributed Covert Communication Under Imperfect Synchronization.
abstract: Covert communication offers a highly undetectable framework for wireless transmission in scenarios demanding secrecy and resilience by concealing the communication existence. However, centralized covert communication systems may achieve a heightened detectability when the eavesdropper and intended receiver are geographically co-located. Distributed multi-antenna systems provide a promising solution, upon leveraging spatial diversity to enhance coverage flexibility. Nevertheless, synchronization imperfections among distributed antennas critically degrade system performance, posing a fundamental challenge to covertness. To address this problem, we investigate joint beamforming and transmit power control for distributed covert communication, aiming at maximizing the covert capacity with the consideration of frequency-phase synchronization offsets. By employing Lagrange decomposition, we derive an analytical upper bound of asymptotic covert capacity and obtain a near-optimal beamforming solution. Simulation results validate our theoretical findings.

title: Topology Reconfiguration for Vulnerability Optimization in Damaged LEO Satellite Networks.
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks, as a key component of the next-generation (6G) mobile communications infrastructure, hold great promise to provide global connectivity and massive throughput. However, it is susceptible to the complex and dynamic space environment. For instance, sun outages induce transient link disruptions, and geomagnetic storms together with space-weather perturbations can lead to node failures and connectivity degradation, which in turn heightens network fragility and jeopardizes the reliability of the constellation. To enhance the resilience and robustness of LEO satellite networks, a vulnerability optimization framework based on topology reconfiguration is proposed, which dynamically rebuilds inter-satellite links (ISLs) to alleviate topological vulnerabilities and preserve connectivity under damaged conditions. To quantify vulnerability and guide reconfiguration, an improved hop–plane–node (IHPN) method is developed, and the feasible reconfiguration space is explored using a soft actor-critic–augmented hyperplane-assisted evolutionary algorithm (SAC-hpaEA). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively reduces network vulnerability across diverse impairment scenarios and lowers communication cost, achieving superior robustness compared with conventional multi-objective optimization (MOP) algorithms.

title: Resilient Hierarchical Split Federated Learning over Resource-Limited Wireless Communication Systems.
abstract: As machine learning models escalate in size and wireless networks expand, deploying federated learning (FL) in edge environments encounters challenges, including increased transmission failures and constrained wireless resources. Although split federated learning (SFL) framework is proposed to mitigate these challenges by shifting workload from clients to a central server, the single-server suffers from limited capability to manage extensive communication workloads. To tackle these challenges, we design a Resilient Hierarchical Split Federated Learning (RHSFL) framework that ensures reliable, resource-efficient communication across a three-tier system by adopting a novel sub-model gradient recycle technique. Based on our analysis, we reformulate the joint optimization problem as minimizing the squared Age of Information (AoI) to indirectly reduce global training loss, and subsequently derive an equivalent linear programming formulation. To efficiently address this optimization, we propose an adaptive algorithm for client orchestration and resource block (RB) allocation. Simulation experiments conducted on the MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets demonstrate that the proposed RHSFL framework outperforms baselines in terms of accuracy and convergence speed.

title: SemAID: Zero-Shot Semantic-Aware Image Communication with Adaptive Sampling and Diffusion-based Signal Recovery.
abstract: The paradigm of semantic communication prioritizes the recovery of semantically meaningful information over pixel-level fidelity, which is crucial for bandwidth-constrained and extreme environments such as deep-space exploration and disaster response. However, existing deep learning-based approaches often rely on task-specific training and struggle with the compound distortion of aggressive compression and severe channel noise. In this paper, we formulate semantic-aware image transmission as a signal recovery problem from incomplete and noisy measurements, guided by semantic importance. We propose SemAID, a novel framework that integrates an adaptive, semantic-driven non-uniform sampler at the transmitter and a generative diffusion-based Bayesian estimator at the receiver. The transmitter dynamically masks pixels based on saliency and edge information, effectively implementing content-aware compression. The receiver, leveraging a pre-trained diffusion model as a strong generative prior, solves the corresponding inverse problem via posterior sampling without any retraining. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SemAID achieves superior performance in both perceptual quality and reconstruction fidelity under low-SNR conditions, showcasing remarkable generalization across varying channel states and unseen data distributions. This work validates the potent efficacy of generative priors for semantic signal recovery under the compound challenge of non-uniform sampling and channel noise, offering a practical zero-shot solution for extreme communication environments.

title: Joint Discriminative Generative Semantic Communications via MLLMs.
abstract: Deep learning-based joint source-channel coding has recently demonstrated strong potential for semantic communication (SemComm). However, most existing approaches focus on optimizing visual-fidelity metrics, which can lead to reduced perceptual quality. Generative model-based SemComm leverages rich prior knowledge from large-scale pre-training to enhance perceptual quality, but often at the cost of increased distortion and unreliability. This paper addresses above issues by proposing a two-stage semantic image transmission framework, integrating a multimodal large language model (MLLM) for generative editing. In the first stage, a JSCC-based discriminative transmission selectively prioritizes semantically important regions, preserving scene layout and object integrity under limited bandwidth. In the second phase, MLLM-driven generative editing refines missing details based on the textual descriptions, enhancing semantic fidelity and perceptual quality. Extensive experiments show that the proposed framework achieves state-of-the-art performance in semantic preserving, perceptual quality, and visual fidelity across a wide range of channel conditions, specially in low-SNR regimes.

title: SMART: A Sparse MoE-Transformer Framework for Environment-aware Channel Prediction.
abstract: Accurate channel prediction is essential for addressing the channel aging issue without introducing additional signaling overhead in wireless communication systems. Most existing works rely on a general, static model to handle highly diverse wireless environments, suffering from poor generalization, limited adaptability, and suboptimal performance in real-world deployments. Although large language models (LLMs) have recently demonstrated promising sequence modeling capabilities for channel prediction, their massive computational costs hinder real-time deployment, especially for latency-sensitive communication scenarios. To address these limitations, we propose SMART, a novel Sparse MoE-trAnsformer framework for enviRonment-aware channel predicTion, which achieves both personalized prediction and computational efficiency. SMART replaces the standard feed-forward networks in each Transformer sub-layer with a sparse mixture of experts (MoE) module, consisting of one shared expert capturing environment-invariant features and multiple specialized experts, each tailored to distinct environmental conditions. A lightweight routing network is trained to dynamically activate only the most relevant experts for each input, enabling adaptive inference pathways for different channel characteristics of different environments. Our proposed SMART only activates a small subset of experts during each forward process, thereby significantly improving computational efficiency while preserving high model capacity. Extensive experiments have been conducted to compare the performance of SMART with state-of-the-art solutions. Our experimental results suggest that SMART provides up to 14.02% and 41.77% improvement in multi-environment channel prediction accuracy, compared to Transformer and LLM-based solutions, respectively.

title: BMPrune: Bidirectional Magnitude-based Backdoor Pruning with Clean Preservation and Malicious Penalization.
abstract: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are vulnerable to backdoor attacks, posing serious risks to their secure deployment. Recent research reveals that backdoors can be erased from infected DNNs by pruning a specific group of neurons, while how to effectively identify and remove these backdoor neurons remains an open challenge.In this paper, we found that backdoor neurons exhibit abnormal magnitude-saliency correlations distinct from benign neurons. Building on this observation, we propose BMPrune, a bidirectional pruning framework that includes: (1) exposing backdoor behavior by amplifying malicious neurons’ abnormal magnitude patterns, (2) eliminating backdoor triggers through deviation-aware pruning, and (3) preserving model functionality by stabilizing clean neurons’ magnitude-saliency alignment. This bidirectional strategy enables BMPrune to achieve state-of-the-art defense performance across diverse attacks using minimal clean data, conclusively demonstrating neuron magnitude’s pivotal role in trustworthy model repair.

title: Multi-hop Parallel Image Semantic Communication for Distortion Accumulation Mitigation.
abstract: Existing semantic communication schemes primarily focus on single-hop scenarios, overlooking the challenges of multi-hop wireless image transmission. As semantic communication is inherently lossy, distortion accumulates over multiple hops, leading to significant performance degradation. To address this, we propose the multi-hop parallel image semantic communication (MHPSC) framework, which introduces a parallel residual compensation link at each hop against distortion accumulation. To minimize the associated transmission bandwidth overhead, a coarse-to-fine residual compression scheme is designed. A deep learning-based residual compressor first condenses the residuals, followed by the adaptive arithmetic coding (AAC) for further compression. A residual distribution estimation module predicts the prior distribution for the AAC to achieve fine compression performances. This approach ensures robust multi-hop image transmission with only a minor increase in transmission bandwidth. Experimental results confirm that MHPSC outperforms both existing semantic communication and traditional separated coding schemes.

title: Joint Transceiver Beamforming and IRS Phase Shift Design for mmWave MIMO with Modulo ADCs.
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) has accelerated the efficiency of modern wireless systems, yet its performance is constrained by the propagation blocking effect and the receiver analog-to-digital converters (ADC) saturation. Motivated by these, this paper first attempted to study an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS)-aided downlink mmWave MIMO system equipped with a modulo ADC front end at the receiver and explicitly models receiver-side quantization error. We propose spectral efficiency (SE) maximization under total-power and constant-modulus constraints and develop a real-valued genetic algorithm-based scheme that, in each generation, (i) explores the IRS reflection matrix and (ii) updates the transceiver beamformers by performing singular value decomposition on the cascaded channel, updated with the IRS reflection matrix. Experimental results demonstrate that the modulo ADC achieves higher SE and lower bit error rates with fewer bit resolution, effectively mitigating saturation-induced clipping and outperforming conventional ADCs.

title: Function-Aligned Nonuniform Quantization Graph Coloring for Distributed Functional Compression.
abstract: We study distributed functional compression for computing a target Z = f (X,Y) from separated sources and found that strict graph coloring wastes bits in nearly homogeneous regions when rare contexts along the other source create conflicts; a single conflicting context blocks merging globally. We propose a function-aligned design that (i) places nonuniform axis cuts via grid-guided one-dimensional dynamic programming (DP) in a coordinate-descent loop and (ii) applies τ-tolerant characteristic-graph coloring with a lookup-table decoder. Rates are accounted for by length-weighted color entropy, which is sampling-invariant and matches separate entropy coding. On Temperature–Humidity Index (THI) classification, the proposed scheme shifts the bits– accuracy Pareto frontier: the method we propose saves about 15% bits above the same accuracy where there are more levels to classify. On the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI) task, nonuniform quantization with τ-tolerant coloring achieves up to 37% fewer bits at accuracies above 95%. The design is distribution-free and function-aware, scales by per-axis DP with majority votes of grid cells. Results indicate that once the task surpasses a binary label or moves to higher dimensions, grid-guided nonuniform partitioning with strict or τ-tolerant coloring is a strictly better operating point for graph coloring.

title: Sensing-Assisted Low-Complexity Beamforming for Dual-RIS ISAC Systems.
abstract: This paper investigates a multi-user integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system that leverages semi-passive reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) equipped with sensing elements to enhance both communication and sensing performance. To ensure the quality of service and fairness for all users, a max-min signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) optimization problem is formulated, involving the joint design of base station (BS) transmit beamforming and RIS discrete phase shifts. However, for large-scale RIS, conventional optimization methods typically suffer from high computational complexity. To this end, we first utilize the RISs to perform user angle estimation, thereby simplifying the solution process of the formulated problem. Building on this, an efficient alternating optimization algorithm is subsequently proposed. Specifically, semi-definite relaxation and the bisection method are employed to solve the BS beamforming optimization subproblem. For optimizing the RIS phase shift matrices in multi-user scenarios, a low-complexity algorithm is developed that leverages a sensing-assisted approach to constrain the discrete search space. Numerical simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves performance that closely approaches that of the ideal continuous phase shift configuration.

title: Spot Pilot Scheme for AFDM under Fractional Delay-Doppler Channel.
abstract: Affine Frequency Division Multiplexing (AFDM) has recently attracted considerable attention owing to its strong resilience against multipath delay and Doppler dispersion, making it a promising candidate for next generation wireless communication systems. However, accurate channel estimation under multipath channels with fractional delay–Doppler shifts remains a major challenge that limits the performance of AFDM. In this paper, a novel spot pilot scheme is proposed for AFDM. By exploiting the banded and quasi-static structure of the affine domain channel matrix, multiple sparsely distributed pilots are inserted within a single frame to capture the channel responses at selected positions. The complete channel matrix is then reconstructed at the receiver through interpolation. Furthermore, a neural network is developed to mitigate the pilot interference caused by fractional delay–Doppler effects and to refine the estimated channel matrix. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed spot pilot scheme achieves significantly improved estimation accuracy compared with single embedded scheme pilot under fractional delay–Doppler conditions.

title: Network Slicing in Integrated Sensing and Communication: A Flexible Multi-Domain Resource Allocation Scheme.
abstract: Performing network slicing in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is an essential task to enhance the performance of dual functionalities. However, the existing works merely consider a single resource domain and neglect the sensing capabilities. Motivated by this, we propose a flexible network slicing framework that leverages resources in multiple domains. We formulate a joint optimization problem for beamforming and frequency allocation to maximize the sum communication rate, subject to constraints on the sensing beam pattern, transmit power, and total bandwidth. To solve this problem, we formulate it as a Markov decision process (MDP) and apply the Twin Delayed DDPG (TD3) algorithm. To further improve convergence, we propose a Lagrangian duality-based TD3 algorithm. Experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms, and they outperform baseline methods in terms of sensing accuracy and computational efficiency. Furthermore, we analyze the trade-off between the two functions (sensing and communication) and examine the impact of key system parameters.

title: A Federated Trust Modeling Framework for Anomaly Detection in Zero Trust Edge Networks.
abstract: Edge networks are increasingly vulnerable to sophisticated cyber-attacks, yet conventional security approaches struggle to balance robust threat detection with user privacy preservation. In this paper, we propose a Federated Trust Modeling framework, a solution for secure anomaly detection in Zero Trust edge networks. By integrating multi-modal anomaly detection, Byzantine-resilient federated learning, and context-aware trust scoring, the framework addresses critical gaps in existing IoT security approaches. The framework employs a three-layer architecture: Device-Level Trust Learning for local anomaly detection using ensemble methods (Enhanced VAE, Isolation Forest, LSTM, and Statistical Process Control), Federated Aggregation Layer for Byzantine-resilient model aggregation with differential privacy, and Trust Scoring & Decision Layer for context-aware access control using Subjective Logic. Comprehensive evaluation on synthetic IoT data demonstrates high precision, near-linear scalability, and privacy preservation with high accuracy even under strict differential privacy. The multi-modal anomaly detection achieves high accuracy while generating zero false alarms. Statistical validation confirms sub-linear time complexity and significant trust score differentiation across security contexts. The framework provides a practical, deployable solution for edge networks requiring strong security with privacy guarantees.

title: Diffusion Posterior Sampling with Channel Feedback for Adaptive Semantic Communication.
abstract: Diffusion-aided deep joint source–channel coding (DeepJSCC) has shown strong potential for semantic communication (SemCom) under challenging wireless conditions. However, existing diffusion-based JSCC schemes lack adaptivity in three key aspects: (i) task-specific fine-tuning, (ii) channel and rate adaptation, and (iii) instance-level generalization. We propose FPS-SemCom, a feedback-guided diffusion posterior sampling framework that unifies posterior-based decoding and feedback-driven progressive encoding. FPS-SemCom achieves instance-, channel-, and rate-adaptive image transmission via a training-free sampler and a lightweight feedback-guided linear encoder. Built entirely on frozen pre-trained diffusion models, FPS-SemCom refines the posterior toward high-fidelity reconstructions while preserving semantic consistency across varying channel conditions. Remarkably, our results reveal that under strong generative priors, even a simple linear encoder can achieve competitive performance, underscoring the representational power of diffusion priors for SemCom. Extensive experiments based on a pre-trained diffusion model show that FPS-SemCom outperforms the existing diffusion-based JSCC baseline, achieving up to a 33.3% improvement in LPIPS and a 1.56 dB gain in MS-SSIM.Project page: https://eedavidwu.github.io/FPS-SemCom/

title: Orthogonal Additive Inverse EP Codes over GF(5m) for Overloaded FFMA Systems.
abstract: The finite-field multiple-access (FFMA) framework effectively addresses the multiuser finite blocklength problem by inverting the conventional processing order of channel coding and multiplexing. In this architecture, element-pairs (EPs) function as virtual resources to separate users directly in the finite-field domain. The algebraic structure of EPs, which can be constructed over different finite fields, plays a crucial role in determining system characteristics and performance advantages. This paper focuses on orthogonal additive inverse EP (AI-EP) codes constructed over GF(5m), enabling an overloaded FFMA scheme that achieves both enhanced spectral efficiency and reliable error performance. The superimposed signals from J users collectively form a structured channel codeword, for which we develop a dynamic programming q-ary sum-product algorithm (DP-QSPA) that ensures effective multiuser signal separation while maintaining tractable decoding complexity. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed GF(5m)-based FFMA system achieves superior error performance compared to conventional power-domain NOMA and SCMA systems.

title: Dual Time-Constrained UAV Routing for Reward Maximization Under Joint Multi-PoI Capture.
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are widely used in various applications, such as surveillance and disaster response. These missions often involve video recording of multiple spatially distributed points-of-interest (PoIs). However, limited battery capacity imposes a strict dual time constraint, making efficient route planning essential. A green effective strategy is to capture multiple PoIs simultaneously from a single capture point, where the required capture time at that point is determined by the longest duration among the captured PoIs. Moreover, PoIs may carry different reward values that reflect their priority or importance in the mission. Therefore, it is critical to jointly select the PoIs to be captured and their associated capture points, such that the UAV visits each selected point within the tour and capture time budget while maximizing the total collected reward. The paper formulates an optimization problem and proposes an approximation algorithm. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that our algorithm outperforms other baselines by up to 67%.

title: Latency Minimization toward Communication-Sensing-Computing Integration for C-AEB in Internet of Vehicles.
abstract: Connected Autonomous Emergency Braking (C-AEB) must complete collision detection and issue a braking command within one second. Traditional Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) architectures, however, often fail to satisfy collision-protection requirements in complex traffic scenarios. In this paper, we propose a trace-driven Integrated Communication-Sensing-Computing (ICSC) joint optimization framework for vehicular networks. First, we establish a high-fidelity system model grounded in the real-world pNEUMA dataset and 3GPP TR 38.901 channel models, explicitly formulating the trade-off between sensing beamforming gain and transmission delay. Based on Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3), we propose TD3-ICSC, a robust joint optimization framework to solve this non-convex problem. Unlike standard Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) approaches, we leverage the Twin Critic mechanism to explicitly mitigate the Q-value overestimation caused by high-mobility channel stochasticity, ensuring that the agent learns a stable policy that simultaneously optimizes active sensing duration and computation offloading ratios. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TD3-ICSC achieves the lowest average latency of 113.8 ms, reducing latency by 61.0%, 38.7%, 37.0%, and 31.7% compared to Random, Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) baselines, respectively. Furthermore, ablation studies verify that the proposed joint optimization of sensing duration and offloading ratio is essential for enhancing the reliability of C-AEB services.

title: OTFS-based Integrated Positioning and Communication Systems with Low-Resolution ADCs.
abstract: This paper proposes a two-phase orthogonal time–frequency space (OTFS)-based integrated positioning and communication (IPAC) framework under realistic low-resolution analog-to-digital converters (ADCs). In the uplink phase, the positioning signal is used to estimate channel parameters, which are subsequently used to determine the user’s position. The spatial smoothing-multiple signal classification algorithm is introduced to estimate the angle-of-arrival, whereas an iterative interference cancellation scheme is conceived for the remaining parameters’ estimation. The corresponding Cramer–Rao lower bounds of channel parameters and user position are also derived. During the downlink communication phase, the estimated parameters are exploited to improve beamforming at the base station. Simulation results evaluate the impact of ADC quantizer resolutions. Specifically, it is shown that enhanced downlink bit error rate performance can be achieved with improved uplink positioning, while the use of low-resolution ADCs induces noticeable performance degradation in the OTFS-IPAC system.

title: An Immersive Image Transmission System with Mutual Information based Feature Separation.
abstract: The emergence of immersive 360-degree image applications in 6G networks presents new challenges for multi-user semantic communication. Existing multi-user approaches, such as those incorporating multiple access or broadcast technologies, have successfully enhanced transmission efficiency from unicast approaches. However, they still fail to address the inherent redundancy of overlapping field-of-view regions among various users. To address this issue, we investigate a multi-user wireless communication system for immersive 360-degree image transmission, respectively extracting both shared and personalized semantic feature from overlapping and non-overlapping regions. Specifically, we propose a mutual information based feature separation regularization (MI-FSR) to formulate an optimization objective that achieves complementarity between personalized and shared semantic features while eliminating redundancy. Furthermore, we design a personalized semantic extractor integrated with a joint importance-redundancy attention module to efficiently extract semantic information from non-overlapping regions. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed system achieves significant performance gains over both the modern broadcast semantic communication and conventional unicast joint source-channel coding baseline.

title: PCF: Proactive Communication Framework for Edge Collaborative Perception.
abstract: Collaborative video perception leverages pervasively deployed cameras to expand coverage, reduce occlusions, and enhance perception in domains such as transportation, community safety, and robotics. However, analyzing large-scale video streams is data-intensive and strains network and computation resources, especially when only a small region of interest (ROI) is relevant. To address this challenge, we propose PCF (Proactive Communication Framework), with a task-oriented method that incorporates ROI awareness into the detection task objective during training and inference, and an ROI-aware efficient camera selection policy at run time. Evaluations on a public dataset demonstrate up to a 7.5-percentage-point improvement in detection accuracy, while reducing communication cost by 56% without sacrificing performance. These results highlight PCF’s potential to enable efficient, ROI-aware perception for battery-powered mobile robots and other resource-constrained edge systems.

title: Deep Graph Unfolding for QoS-Aware Distributed Beamforming in Cell-Free Massive MIMO.
abstract: This paper investigates low-latency downlink beamforming design for cell-free massive multi-input multi-output (CF-mMIMO) systems with user quality of service (QoS) requirements. To address the high computational complexity and slow convergence of conventional distributed weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) algorithms, we propose a graph-based deep unfolding architecture, termed GUPD-WMMSE, which integrates parallel distributed WMMSE updates with graph neural networks (GNNs). By unfolding the iterative WMMSE procedure into a multi-layer GNN and introducing a gated recurrent unit (GRU) to exploit historical state information, the proposed approach avoids explicit matrix inversion and step-size search in each iteration. Simulation results demonstrate that GUPD-WMMSE achieves near-optimal sum rate performance with significantly reduced computational complexity and fast convergence. Moreover, the proposed architecture generalizes well to different network scales without retraining, making it suitable for real-time distributed beamforming in large-scale cell-free networks.

title: LEO-DPSL: An Efficient Split Learning Framework for AI Tasks over LEO Satellite Networks.
abstract: The increasing deployment of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites has enabled seamless global coverage, positioning satellite networks as critical infrastructure for intelligent applications such as remote sensing and disaster monitoring. To empower these applications, Artificial Intelligence (AI) models are widely deployed to process massive sensing data. However, conventional centralized training paradigms, which require transmitting raw data to a central server, face severe communication bandwidth and energy consumption bottlenecks over resource-constrained links. To address this, we propose a Low Earth Orbit Dual-Partitioning Split Learning framework (LEO-DPSL), a novel framework designed to overcome these limitations. By implementing a dual partitioning strategy across both model and data dimensions, LEO-DPSL enables the parallel execution of computation and transmission, significantly improving the overall pipeline efficiency. Furthermore, we formulate a joint total latency and energy consumption minimization problem and utilize an Enhanced Simulated Annealing algorithm to efficiently explore the complex solution space and determine the optimal model splitting strategy and collaborative satellites. Experimental results demonstrate that compared with the federated learning baseline, LEO-DPSL reduces training time by approximately 75.3% and energy consumption by 38.7% while maintaining model accuracy.

title: Reading Radio from Camera: Visually-Grounded, Lightweight, and Interpretable RSSI Prediction.
abstract: Accurate, real-time wireless signal prediction is essential for next-generation networks. However, existing vision-based frameworks often rely on computationally intensive models and are also sensitive to environmental interference. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel, physics-guided and light-weighted framework that predicts the received signal strength indicator (RSSI) from camera images. By decomposing RSSI into its physically interpretable components, path loss and shadow fading, we significantly reduce the model’s learning difficulty and exhibit interpretability. Our approach establishes a new state-of-the-art by demonstrating exceptional robustness to environmental interference, a critical flaw in prior work. Quantitatively, our model reduces the prediction root mean squared error (RMSE) by 50.3% under conventional conditions and still achieves an 11.5% lower RMSE than the previous benchmark’s interference-eliminated results. This superior performance is achieved with a remarkably lightweight framework, utilizing a MobileNet-based model up to 19 times smaller than competing solutions. The combination of high accuracy, robustness to interference, and computational efficiency makes our framework highly suitable for real-time, on-device deployment in edge devices, paving the way for more intelligent and reliable wireless communication systems.

title: System Design and Convergence Analysis for Decentralized Federated Fine-Tuning on LEO Satellite Networks.
abstract: With low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellites emerging as edge nodes for Federated Learning (FL), their high deployment cost and limited onboard resources make efficient model training crucial. This paper addresses the challenge of global weather forecasting using a network of LEO satellites, where individual satellites have limited regional coverage and insufficient access to global data. To overcome this, we propose a Decentralized FL (DFL) framework that incorporates both observed and self-generated data for training. Each satellite locally fine-tunes its weather forecasting model using its own observations and synthetic data generated from its model, and then collaboratively updates model parameters across the network using DFL to achieve global knowledge sharing without transmitting raw data. Furthermore, we provide a theoretical convergence bound for the proposed framework, and simulation results demonstrate that it achieves accurate forecasting while ensuring robust convergence.

title: A Low-Complexity Unified Error Correction Transformer.
abstract: Channel coding is vital for reliable sixth-generation (6G) data transmission, employing diverse error correction codes for various application scenarios. Traditional decoders require dedicated hardware for each code, leading to high hardware costs. Recently, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven approaches, such as the error correction code Transformer and its enhanced version, the foundation error correction code Transformer, have been proposed to reduce the hardware cost by leveraging the Transformer to decode multiple codes. However, their excessively high computational complexity of $\mathcal{O}\left( {{N^2}} \right)$ due to the self-attention mechanism in the Transformer limits scalability, where N represents the sequence length. To reduce computational complexity, we propose a unified Transformer-based decoder that handles multiple linear block codes within a single framework. Specifically, a standardized unit is employed to align code length across different code types, while a redesigned low-rank unified attention module, with computational complexity of $\mathcal{O}\left( N \right)$, is shared across various heads in the Transformer. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that the proposed unified Transformer-based decoder outperforms existing methods and provides a high-performance, low-complexity solution for next-generation wireless communication systems.

title: Unlocking High-Fidelity Analog Joint Source-Channel Coding on Standard Digital Transceivers.
abstract: Analog joint source-channel coding (JSCC) has demonstrated superior performance for semantic communications through graceful degradation across channel conditions. However, a fundamental hardware-software mismatch prevents deployment on modern digital physical layers (PHYs): analog JSCC generates continuous-valued symbols requiring infinite waveform diversity, while digital PHYs produce a finite set of discrete waveforms and employ non-differentiable operations that break end-to-end gradient flow. Existing solutions either fundamentally limit representation granularity or require impractical white-box PHY access. We introduce D2AJSCC, a novel framework enabling high-fidelity analog JSCC deployment on standard digital PHYs. Our approach exploits orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing’s parallel subcarrier structure as a waveform synthesizer: computational PHY inversion determines input bitstreams that orchestrate subcarrier amplitudes and phases to emulate ideal analog waveforms. To enable end-to-end training despite non-differentiable PHY operations, we develop ProxyNet—a differentiable neural surrogate of the communication link that provides uninterrupted gradient flow while preventing JSCC degeneration. Simulation results for image transmission over WiFi PHY demonstrate that our system achieves near-ideal analog JSCC performance with graceful degradation across SNR conditions, while baselines exhibit cliff effects or catastrophic failures. By enabling next-generation semantic transmission on legacy infrastructure without hardware modification, our framework promotes sustainable network evolution and bridges the critical gap between analog JSCC’s theoretical promise and practical deployment on ubiquitous digital hardware.

title: Capacity Maximization for FAS-Enhanced MIMO Systems: A Low Complexity Approach.
abstract: In this paper, the problem of fluid antenna system (FAS)-enhanced multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) capacity maximization is studied. Different from conventional MIMO systems equipped with fixed-position antennas (FPAs), we consider fluid antennas (FAs) can be flexibly repositioned in a fixed region, such that the MIMO channel between them is reconfigured to achieve higher capacity. We aim to jointly optimize the beamforming matrix and FA positions of the transmitter to maximize the MIMO capacity. First, we develop an alternating optimization (AO) algorithm to find a locally optimal solution by iteratively optimizing the transmit beamforming matrix and the positions of each FA with the other variable being fixed. For the beamforming matrix optimization, we adopt the conventional eigenmode transmission scheme, and the optimal power allocation is calculated by water-filling method. For the FA positions optimization, we identify a small set of promising candidates that can be exhaustively searched efficiently. Next, we analyze two special cases in which the MIMO-capacity maximization reduces to maximizing the sum of eigenvalues with respect to the FA positions. The proposed candidate set can then be directly applied to these cases as well. Numerical results show that the performance of the proposed method is close to that of the successive convex approximation (SCA)-based method, while consistently outperforming other benchmarks up to 30% in achievable rate. Most importantly, the proposed algorithm requires only 16.9% of the simulation time compared to the SCA-based method. This highlights its potential for practical and efficient position optimization of FAs, paving the way for real-world applications in 6G.

title: Practical RIS Gain without the Pain: Randomization and Opportunistic Scheduling in 5G NR.
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate the performance gains achieved by an in-house built reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) integrated with a real-time 5G new radio (NR) system implemented using the OpenAirInterface (OAI) framework. We first quantify the gain in throughput achievable by integrating an RIS with a 5G system. Next, we show that randomly setting the RIS phase configuration and leveraging the inherent proportional fair (PF) scheduling mechanism of 5G NR can yield near-optimal throughput, provided the throughput averaging window of the PF scheduler is chosen judiciously. This occurs because, in each time slot, the PF scheduler naturally prioritizes data transmission to the user equipment (UE) that experiences the best channel conditions, namely, the UE to which the randomly configured RIS is aligned. Subsequently, we experimentally evaluate key performance metrics, including the reference signal received power (RSRP), block error rate (BLER), modulation and coding scheme (MCS) index, and throughput, under random RIS configurations. These results confirm that even a randomly configured RIS with negligible overhead can deliver performance comparable to optimized RIS designs, in real-world 5G NR wireless communication systems.

title: SmartIA: Context-Aware Feedback-Free Beam Discovery for Efficient Initial Access.
abstract: Future wireless networks leveraging millimeter-wave and sub-Terahertz spectra rely on highly directional beamforming to counter severe path loss. However, identifying the optimal beam, specially during the Initial Access (IA) procedure, remains challenging due to the lack of feedback between the Base Station (BS) and User Equipment (UE). In this paper, we present SmartIA a context-aware feedback-free hierarchical beam scanning framework for efficient IA. We design an optimized sequence of transmitted beam patterns that uniquely encode spatial directions, enabling all UEs to identify the best beam by aggregating multi-stage information. This achieves logarithmic-complexity beam discovery with reduced acquisition time while preserving high spatial resolution. We further introduce a novel analog antenna weight vector design that achieves the required spatial coding with full power amplifier utilization. We develop an adaptive Synchronization Signal Block (SSB) transmission strategy that leverages contextual information on link conditions across the user distribution to minimize BS radio resource utilization, while preserving cell coverage under power-constrained multi-directional transmissions. Simulation results show 50% lower IA acquisition time and BS energy consumption, with 3 dB gains in both coverage and link quality compared to standard approaches, validating SmartIA as an scalable solution for beam discovery and IA in future high-frequency networks.

title: Trajectory-Adaptive Beam Shaping: Towards Beam-Management-Free Near-field Communications.
abstract: The quest for higher wireless carrier frequencies spanning the millimeter-wave (mmWave) and Terahertz (THz) bands heralds substantial enhancements in data throughput and spectral efficiency for next-generation wireless networks. However, these gains come at the cost of severe path loss and a heightened risk of beam misalignment due to user mobility, especially pronounced in near-field communication. Traditional solutions rely on extremely directional beamforming and frequent beam updates via beam management, but such techniques impose formidable computational and signaling overhead. In response, we propose a novel approach termed trajectory-adaptive beam shaping (TABS) that eliminates the need for real-time beam management by shaping the electromagnetic wavefront to follow the user's predefined trajectory. Drawing inspiration from self-accelerating beams in optics, TABS concentrates energy along pre-defined curved paths corresponding to the user's motion without requiring real-time beam reconfiguration. We further introduce a dedicated quantitative metric to characterize performance under the TABS framework. Comprehensive simulations substantiate the superiority of TABS in terms of link performance, overhead reduction, and implementation complexity.

title: Three-Stage Channel Estimation for Active RIS-FAS-Assisted Millimeter-Wave Systems.
abstract: This paper investigates the channel estimation problem in millimeter-wave systems assisted by an active reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) and fluid antenna system (FAS). A three-stage estimation scheme is proposed by strategically controlling the RIS on/off states and the FAS position switching. Stage I deactivates the RIS to enable channel estimation for the user equipment (UE)-base station (BS) link. Stage II activates the RIS while fixing the FAS position, thereby avoiding strong channel coupling to enable RIS cascaded channel estimation. Stage III activates the RIS while allowing the FAS to switch positions; despite the resulting strong coupling between cascaded angles and UE-RIS link angles of departure (AoDs), an alternating iterative projection method, leveraging prior-stage estimates, is proposed to achieve accurate UE-RIS link AoD estimation. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

title: TwinPot-Gen: A Generative Semantic Digital-Twin Honeypot Framework for Adaptive and Explainable Defence in 6G Networks.
abstract: The security of emerging 6G small-cell networks increasingly depends on intelligent deception mechanisms, where honeypots serve as proactive defence components. However, conventional honeypots lack semantic and behavioural realism and often risk leaking sensitive data when emulating complex network states. Existing systems remain limited by static personas, weak sanitisation, and unexplainable reactions, making them ineffective against adaptive attackers. To address this challenge, we propose TwinPot-Gen, a digital-twin-assisted honeypot framework that integrates semantic communication , graph-based knowledge modelling, and generative AI to achieve realistic and privacy-preserving deception. The framework establishes two isolated domains-the Digital-Twin Network and the Honeypot Network-connected through two secure gateways: the Generative Knowledge Gateway (GKG) and the Defence-Orchestration Gateway (DOG). GKG performs semantic sanitisation and persona generation using a large language model, while DOG enforces adaptive, policy-driven responses. Experimental results on a Kubernetes-based 6G testbed show that TwinPot-Gen improves persona realism by 35-50%, achieves a 0.94 F1-score in attack detection, and maintains sub-100 ms orchestration latency, confirming its efficiency and trustworthiness in dynamic 6G environments.

title: Conditional Generative AoA/AoD Estimation: A Pilot-Free and System-Agnostic Approach.
abstract: Accurate angle of arrival (AoA) and angle of departure (AoD) estimation underpins spatial precision, efficient beamforming, and the overall Quality of Service (QoS) and Quality of Experience (QoE) of integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). This paper introduces a generative AI (GenAI) framework that synthesizes the complete set of multipath 2D AoA/AoD parameters directly from transmitter (TX) and receiver (RX) locations, overcoming the limitations of traditional model-based and current data-driven learning methods. The proposed classifiers-guided conditional generative adversarial network (CG-CGAN) offers a system-agnostic approach that removes the need for pilot signals and operates effectively under challenging coherent multipath conditions. Its three-stage architecture integrates classification and conditional generative modeling to jointly infer line-of-sight (LoS) status, number of propagation paths, and angular parameters. Simulations on the DeepMIMO dataset demonstrate over 99.5% classification accuracy and 92% angle generation accuracy, significantly outperforming classical techniques while reducing computational complexity and enhancing the QoS/QoE of ISAC-enabled systems.

title: Priority Assignment of Packets in Sensor Nodes for Goal-Oriented Semantic Communications.
abstract: The power and bandwidth demands of massive machine-type communications (mMTC) are expected to notably grow in beyond 5G (B5G) networks, thereby straining network resources and operators [1]. In response, semantic communication frameworks are proposed to reduce communication overhead in B5G. Transmission of resulting semantic information over prioritized random access channels (RACH) thus emerged. In this work, we propose a content-centric priority assignment procedure at the sensor level for this paradigm. We define an information gain metric using reinforcement learning nomenclature that relates sensor observations to a goal. We propose a novel objective function that maximizes information retrieval at the base station while adhering to the given RACH configuration. It is shown that state sequences reconstructed at the BS follow actual sequences more accurately, measured using the proposed metric. We further demonstrate the feasibility of our proposal in a case study of distributed control in heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC), and show that it achieves a smaller tracking error compared to non-prioritized RACH.

title: Task Offloading for Stacked Intelligent Metasurface enabled MEC in Millimeter-Wave Communications.
abstract: Millimeter-Wave (mmWave) communications enable ultra-high data rates but suffer from severe path loss and blockage, which significantly limits reliability and coverage. Mobile edge computing (MEC) has been recognized as a promising paradigm to reduce latency and enable computation-intensive applications by bringing cloud capabilities closer to end users. However, the performance of MEC systems is still constrained by unfavorable propagation conditions. Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) offer a cost and energy-efficient technology to enhance link quality; however, conventional single-layer RISs provide limited capabilities in interference suppression and beamforming flexibility. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a novel stacked intelligent metasurface (SIM) architecture integrated with MEC in mmWave communications. By jointly leveraging multilayer wave-domain processing and edge computing resources, the proposed SIM-MEC framework enables efficient task offloading in multi-user mmWave systems, effectively increasing the total computing task size under strict latency constraints. We formulate a joint optimization problem of SIM phase shifts and time allocation for transmission and computing, which is solved using a combination of projected gradient ascent and active-set algorithms. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed SIM-enabled MEC framework significantly outperforms benchmark schemes, including direct transmission without SIM, single-layer RIS, and equal-phase configurations, in terms of maximization of the computing task size.

title: Conditional Diffusion Model-Driven Massive MIMO Iterative Detection.
abstract: To ensure future high-quality and reliable massive communication during 6G uplink transmissions, we propose a conditional diffusion model-driven massive MIMO detector, which can iteratively estimate channels and detect data for the uplink multiuser access. This approach utilizes a generative diffusion model to learn the score function of the joint posterior by integrating the prior distribution with the likelihood derived from the transmission model. The prior distribution is obtained either by learning from channel statistics or through analytical derivation from the symbol constellation. By employing noise matching initialization and an asynchronous annealed Langevin dynamics (ALD) sampling scheme, the receiver alternates efficiently between score-based channel estimation and data detection, thus avoiding traps of local minima. Simulation results demonstrate that this iterative diffusion process outperforms Bayesian-based and existing synchronous ALD channel estimation and data detection schemes in multiuser uplink scenarios.

title: HoRAMA: Holistic Reconstruction with Automated Material Assignment for Ray Tracing using NYURay.
abstract: Next-generation wireless networks at upper mid-band and millimeter-wave frequencies require accurate site-specific deterministic channel propagation prediction. Wireless ray tracing (RT) provides site-specific predictions but demands high-fidelity three-dimensional (3D) environment models with material properties. Manual 3D model reconstruction achieves high accuracy but requires weeks of expert effort, creating scalability bottlenecks for large environment reconstruction. Traditional vision-based 3D reconstruction methods lack RT compatibility due to geometrically defective meshes and missing material properties. This paper presents Holistic Reconstruction with Automated Material Assignment (HoRAMA) for wireless propagation prediction using NYURay. HoRAMA generates RT-compatible 3D models from RGB video readily captured using a smartphone or low-cost portable camera, by integrating MASt3R-SLAM dense point cloud generation with vision language model-assisted material assignment. The HoRAMA 3D reconstruction method is verified by comparing NYURay RT predictions, using both manually created and HoRAMA-generated 3D models, against field measurements at 6.75 GHz and 16.95 GHz across 12 TX-RX locations in a 700 square meter factory. HoRAMA ray tracing predictions achieve a 2.28 dB RMSE for matched multipath component (MPC) power predictions, comparable to the manually created 3D model baseline (2.18 dB), while reducing 3D reconstruction time from two months to 16 hours. HoRAMA enables scalable wireless digital twin creation for RT network planning, infrastructure deployment, and beam management in 5G/6G systems, as well as eventual real-time implementation at the edge [1].

title: Impact of UAV 3D Posture and Wobbles on the Non-Stationary Air-to-Ground Channels.
abstract: Accurate modeling of UAV-to-ground (U2G) channels is essential for the design and evolution of future wireless systems. This paper introduces a three-dimensional (3D) non-stationary multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channel model that accounts for both UAV posture variations and wobbling dynamics. The model characterizes fuselage posture changes, represents internal UAV vibrations as a sinusoidal random process, and describes wobbling induced by random airflow using a Gaussian distribution. By integrating these 3D posture and wobbling effects within the air-to-ground (A2G) channel framework, this study examines how the temporal auto-correlation function (ACF) varies with different postures,wobble angle amplitudes, and carrier frequencies. The findings indicate that even minor UAV posture adjustments and wobbles can substantially influence the channel’s temporal correlation. Numerical analysis further demonstrates a rapid decline in the ACF as wobble angle amplitudes and carrier frequency increase.

title: Multi-User Semantic and Data Communications with Adaptive Source-Channel Coding.
abstract: This paper considers a multi-user semantic and data communication (MU-SemDaCom) system, where a base station (BS) simultaneously serves users with different semantic and data tasks through a downlink multi-user multiple-input single-output (MU-MISO) channel. We propose a multi-user adaptive source-channel coding (MU-ASCC) framework that adaptively optimizes deep neural network (DNN)-based source coding, digital channel coding, and superposition broadcasting according to the channel conditions. First, we employ a data-regression method to approximate the end-to-end (E2E) semantic and data distortions. Then, based on the derived formulas, we formulate a weighted-sum E2E distortion minimization problem that jointly optimizes the source-channel coding rates, power allocation, and beamforming vectors for both the data and semantic users. Finally, an alternating optimization (AO) framework is developed, where the adaptive rate optimization is solved using the subgradient descent method, while the joint power and beamforming is addressed via the uplink-downlink duality (UDD) technique. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed MU-ASCC scheme achieves simultaneous improvements in both the data recovery and semantic task performance compared with conventional schemes.

title: A Future-Aware Cognitive Semantic Communication System via Knowledge Graphs and Large Language Models.
abstract: Cognitive semantic communication (SemCom) system is envisioned as a promising paradigm for enhancing traditional semantic communication by incorporating semantic inference and error correction enabled by knowledge graphs (KGs). However, existing KG embedding models are typically static or rely solely on historical data, limiting their ability to capture the temporal evolution of entities and relationships. To address this challenge, we propose a future-aware cognitive SemCom system named FAC-SemCom. In this system, large language models (LLMs) are first employed to generate enhanced quadruple datasets incorporating a time stability index, extending conventional KG datasets that consist of triples like (head, relation, tail) with future-oriented semantic information. A novel loss function is then defined by taking into account the temporal stability with future awareness during model training. In addition, a relation-sensitive classification transmission strategy is introduced to improve communication energy efficiency. To mitigate the errors introduced by this classification-based approach, an LLM-driven triple correction module is further designed to reduce transmission error rates and enhance semantic accuracy. Simulation results demonstrate that FAC-SemCom achieves approximately 45.2% higher transmission accuracy than baseline methods under low signal-to-noise ratio while significantly lowering total energy costs for large-scale triple transmission.

title: Beamwidth-Adaptive Reconfigurable Holographic Surfaces Enabled ISAC Systems.
abstract: The performance of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO)-based integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems is often constrained by the high power consumption of phase shifters and the complexity of spatial-domain waveform design. To address these challenges, we employ reconfigurable holographic surfaces (RHS), a type of metamaterial surface, as the transceiver antenna for MIMO-ISAC, eliminating the need for phase shifters. By leveraging the element-wise amplitude-tuning feature of RHS, we present a low-complexity RHS spatial-domain waveform design that directly generates multi-lobe beam patterns via a linear superposition of closed-form single-beam holographic beamformers. Moreover, the element-wise amplitude-tuning feature is also utilized to realize effective aperture tuning, yielding beam patterns with adaptive beamwidth and flat gain, which outperforms antenna arrays with a fixed aperture size. Based on this design, we develop a two-stage ISAC scheme enabled by a beamwidth-adaptive RHS, where the holographic and digital beamforming is jointly optimized for improved ISAC performance. Simulation results show that the proposed beamwidth-adaptive ISAC scheme achieves a higher weighted sum rate than schemes based on RHSs with a fixed beamwidth or phased arrays, given the same power consumption and sensing signal-to-noise ratio constraint.

title: OECaaS: Towards Serverless Computing for LEO Multi-Satellite On-Orbit Processing.
abstract: Fresh and high-quality satellite imagery is critical for applications such as disaster response, agricultural monitoring, and environmental observation. However, Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites face a severe downlink bottleneck, with only about 2% of acquired data typically transmitted to the ground, leading to significant resource waste. Existing onboard processing schemes often rely on static strategies that cannot adapt to dynamic fluctuations in computational capacity, energy availability, and image content. To address this limitation, this paper introduces OECaaS, a serverless computing-based scheduling system for multi-satellite on-orbit image processing. OECaaS decomposes tasks into fine-grained functions and employs an intelligent scheduler that dynamically selects suitable satellites, constructs optimized processing pipelines, and performs energy-adaptive task priority scheduling based on real-time resource states and task requirements. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that OECaaS achieves an average 61.2% improvement in task completion rate and reduces average task completion latency by 36.1% under the same energy constraints compared to existing baselines
