title: A Queuing Theory-based Dynamic Adaptive Energy Sustainability Algorithm in Battery-free Sensor Networks.
abstract: Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer (SWIPT) technology enables the realization of Battery-free SWIPT-enabled Sensor Networks (BSSN). However, existing SWIPT energy efficiency optimization schemes typically rely on static traffic models, making them ill-suited for dynamic and large-scale network conditions. To this end, a Queuing Theory-based Dynamic Adaptive Energy Sustainability Algorithm (QT-DAES) is proposed. Specifically, the data transmission process of BSSN was modeled as an M/M/1/K queuing model based on queuing theory to capture its dynamic characteristics. Based on these characteristics, an energy efficiency optimization problem is formulated, which is proven to be a non-convex optimization problem. Finally, by adopting QT-DAES to address this optimization problem, the adaptability and scalability of BSSN in dynamic scenarios were significantly enhanced. Experimental results demonstrate that QT-DAES achieves rapid convergence, requiring only 5 iterations on average. Moreover, in high-load scenarios, QT-DAES achieves network throughput improvements of 37%, 57.1%, and 80.6% over DSNRA, MRMEE, and MTE-EHWSN respectively.

title: SemCast: One Representation Semantic Communication for Multi-task Receivers.
abstract: Traditional wireless transmission prioritizes bit-perfect transmission, wasting bandwidth on details irrelevant to downstream tasks. Existing semantic communication methods train task-specific encoders from scratch for each application or channel condition, limiting scalability and requiring extensive retraining. To overcome these limitations, we present SemCast, a semantic communication system that leverages frozen pretrained encoders to enable multi-task visual transmission over diverse wireless channels without task-specific encoding or retraining. A unified transmitted representation, extracted by a frozen Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) encoder via joint source–channel coding (JSCC), supports concurrent decoding for multiple tasks, including classification, object counting, attribute recognition, depth estimation, and segmentation. The transmitter employs a learned mapper with unequal error protection (UEP) to automatically prioritize task-critical feature dimensions. At the receiver, PRISM-Rx introduces a mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture with low-rank adaptation (LoRA) and pilotless vector-quantized channel tokenization for blind adaptation to diverse channels without Channel State Information (CSI). JEPA’s masked prediction pretraining provides superior spatial and compositional representations for multi-task semantic communication compared to contrastive and pixel-reconstruction baselines. PRISM-Rx achieves near CSI-known performance without CSI, while achieving significantly lower latency than CSI-based approaches.

title: A Low-Complexity Receiver Design for Uplink ISAC.
abstract: Uplink integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems have recently emerged as a promising research direction, enabling simultaneous uplink signal detection and target sensing. In this paper, we propose the flexible projection (FP)-type receiver that unify the projection-type receiver and the successive interference cancellation (SIC)-type receiver by using a flexible tradeoff factor to adapt to dynamically changing uplink ISAC scenarios. With adjustable tradeoff factors, the FP-type receiver can balance the enhancement of the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) with the reduction of correlation in the reconstructed signal for communication signal detection. A homotopy optimization framework is first applied for the FP-type receiver with a fixed trade-off factor. This framework is then extended to develop the dynamic FP (DFP)-type receiver, which iteratively adjust the trade-off factor for improved algorithm performance. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed receiver designs is verified via simulations.

title: Experimental Integration of Quantum Key Distribution for Secure 5G Networks.
abstract: The rapid advancement of quantum computing fundamentally threatens 5G network security by undermining conventional public-key cryptography. This paper presents an experimental integration of quantum key distribution (QKD) into operational 5G environments. Through three representative use cases spanning midhaul, backhaul, and backbone segments, we deploy commercial QKD systems with ETSI-compliant key management interfaces to evaluate performance impacts on latency and throughput. Experimental results demonstrate that QKD-based encryption maintains the stringent low-latency and high-throughput requirements of 5G applications. The proposed quantum cryptography function further enables flexible application of QKD-generated keys to selective data flows, providing fine-grained security control. These findings validate the technical feasibility and operational practicality of QKD in realistic 5G settings, highlighting its crucial role in building future-proof, quantum-resistant communication infrastructures.

title: Joint Delay, Doppler, and Phase Noise Tracking for Distributed Inter-Satellite Synchronization.
abstract: Inter-satellite networks require tight synchronization to support coherent links, cooperative processing, and distributed beamforming.In low Earth orbit, fast relative motion causes perlink delay and Doppler to drift over a synchronization burst, while independent oscillators introduce relative phase noise.Limited link budgets further lead to sparse connectivity, so each receiver observes only a subset of neighboring links.We develop an OFDM pilot-based, motion-aware synchronization approach that jointly models propagation and oscillator impairments and links them to an SINR-type reliability metric.A unified frequency-domain observation model is derived in which delay, Doppler, and phase noise appear explicitly, and intra-symbol phase-noise leakage contributes a self-interference term in the despread pilot statistic.Coupled delay-Doppler dynamics yield an EKF-ready state-space model, and a two-stage tracker combining EKF updates, RTS smoothing, and Doppler compensation refines delay and phase estimates.Simulations show that the proposed processing improves delay and phase tracking across SINR, providing a consistent basis for synchronization under stochastic drift and sparse connectivity.

title: Unseen Cost of Space Computing: Quantifying LEO Battery Aging via Physics-Driven Modeling.
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations in the 6G era are evolving into intelligent in-orbit computational platforms, forming Space Computing Power Networks (SCPNs) to deliver global-scale computing services. However, the intensive computation within SCPN incurs a significant ``unseen cost'': the frequent charge-discharge cycles accelerate the physical degradation of satellites' life-limiting and high-cost batteries, thereby threatening the long-term operational viability of such a system. Existing approaches, often relying on indirect metrics like Depth of Discharge (DoD) and neglecting the complex, nonlinear degradation process of battery aging, fail to accurately quantify this cost. To address this, we introduce a high-fidelity, physics-driven model that quantitatively links computational workload parameters to the nonlinear battery degradation. Building on this model, we formulate a degradation-aware scheduling problem and analyze heuristic policies across different energy regimes. Simulations reveal that the optimal strategy should be adaptive: in solar-rich conditions, a myopic policy maximizing instantaneous solar utilization is superior, whereas under energy scarcity, a reactive policy leveraging real-time battery state significantly extends lifetime.

title: An Architectural Framework for Open and Interoperable Web 4.0 and Virtual Worlds.
abstract: Web 4.0 and virtual worlds represent a new stage in the evolution of the Internet toward open, interoperable, and user-centered digital ecosystems. This paper presents a structured architectural framework for Web 4.0, based on open standards, open source, and digital commons, and aligned with regulatory requirements. We present a layered reference architecture that unifies immersive applications, identity and trust services, interoperability middleware, open hardware infrastructures, and governance mechanisms into a single ecosystem. This framework systematically maps the five priority areas of the Virtual Worlds Partnership, identity management, software supply chain security, open hardware, decentralized alternatives to centralized platforms, and Virtual Worlds demonstrations, highlighting their cross-layer interactions. In addition, we define evaluation criteria and key performance indicators that connect architectural design choices to measurable technical, socio-economic, and regulatory outcomes. The proposed architecture offers a common baseline for early Web 4.0 demonstrations and interoperability-driven virtual worlds, supporting scalable, secure, and sustainable deployment.

title: Security Evaluations of Post-Quantum Cryptographic Primitives Against Quantum and AI-Based Attacks.
abstract: The emergence of quantum computing poses an existential threat to conventional cryptographic systems, prompting the development of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) based on quantum-resistant mathematical problems. However, the long-term security of these primitives remains uncertain, especially under realistic quantum and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven attack scenarios. This paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of the security of PQC primitives with a dual focus: (i) analyzing advances in quantum algorithms that target the underlying hardness assumptions of lattice-based, code-based, and other post-quantum schemes; and (ii) leveraging AI-based methodologies for identifying cryptographic vulnerabilities. We survey the current state of quantum cryptanalysis, propose a unified insights for evaluations. Our findings offer updated parameter recommendations and highlight both strengths and potential fragilities in leading PQC candidates. The results contribute actionable insights toward the design and standardization of resilient cryptographic systems for the post-quantum era.

title: OAM Shift Keying in LDPC-Coded Free-Space Optical Communication via Vision Mamba.
abstract: Orbital angular momentum shift keying (OAM-SK) encodes symbols as discrete vortex charges in free-space optical (FSO) links. However, atmospheric turbulence (AT) distorts ring structure and vortex cores, inducing inter-mode crosstalk and decoding errors. In this work, we address OAM-SK demodulation in a low-density parity-check (LDPC)-coded FSO link under turbulence with a Vision Mamba (Vim)-based decoder. The proposed Vim-based decoder adopts a selective state-space model architecture and performs bidirectional scans to aggregate context over long ranges without the ${\mathcal{O}}\left({{N^2}}\right)$ cost of attention. It uses input-gated state updates to adapt the effective kernel to local evidence. We identify that these mechanisms are well matched to AT-induced ring warping, core wandering, and orientation jitter. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed Vim-based decoder outperforms the Swin Transformer and a convolutional neural network baseline in symbol-decoding accuracy across the training, validation, and test sets, with the advantage becoming more pronounced as turbulence increases. When the predicted symbols feed the LDPC chain, the proposed Vim-based decoder can bring significant link-level performance gains in terms of lower bit error rate and higher peak signal-to-noise ratio across turbulence. Furthermore, the proposed Vim-based decoder improves accuracy and stability under turbulence while retaining linear time complexity.

title: Joint Resource Allocation and Beamforming for STAR-RIS-aided Multicast OAM systems.
abstract: This paper investigates orbital angular momentum (OAM) multicast transmissions aided by a simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS). In dense networks, OAM mode orthogonality is easily compromised by transceiver misalignment, leading to severe inter-mode interference. To address this, we leverage STAR-RIS to provide full-space wavefront control, effectively compensating for misalignment and suppressing crosstalk. We formulate a weighted sum capacity (WSC) maximization problem and propose a joint resource allocation and beamforming algorithm. By applying Lagrange-dual and quadratic transform methods combined with semidefinite relaxation (SDR), the algorithm effectively coordinates active base station resources and passive STAR-RIS phase shifts. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed system significantly outperforms conventional MIMO and reflective RIS-aided benchmarks, particularly by restoring mode orthogonality in misaligned scenarios. Furthermore, the system achieves superior network energy efficiency, supporting next-generation green communication objectives.

title: Ghost-LSNet: See Large, Focus Small for WLANs.
abstract: The Wi-Fi Alliance (WFA) has incorporated 4096-QAM into the 802.11be protocol, enabling Wi-Fi 7 to achieve a 20% increase in peak throughput over its predecessor. However, due to cost constraints, most chip vendors rely on Wiener-based channel estimators even as rising Modulation and Coding Scheme (MCS) indices demand far greater precision. Such methods are prone to channel estimation distortion caused by over-smoothing from fixed receptive fields, which is especially severe in deeply faded subcarriers. To address this, we propose Ghost-LSNet (GLSNet), a channel estimation algorithm tailored for Wi-Fi 7 receivers supporting 4096-QAM demodulation. Particularly, inspired by the "See Large, Focus Small" strategy of LSNet, which captures wide-context features using large kernels and refines local details via small-kernel aggregation, and Ghost-Net’s efficient convolution mechanism, we design a novel 1D convolutional architecture. Additionally, it adopts a separate training strategy for edge/central band to address edge band accuracy loss, another key cause of high-order MCS performance degradation. Simulation results under standard channel models show GLSNet outperforming Wiener-filter estimators and even state-of-the-art neural network-based methods, with substantially lower computational overhead.

title: LLM-Aided UAV Anti-jamming Communications Based on Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL)-based unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) anti-jamming communication schemes optimize transmit power and channel, but have communication reliability degradation due to delayed feedback under dynamic environment. In this paper, we propose a large language model (LLM)-aided RL-based UAV anti-jamming communication scheme to optimize transmit power and channel based on the environmental features extracted by LLM including terrain layout and weather conditions that cause channel fading, as well as jamming features including the received jamming power and jammed channel. The risk function formulated based on the bit error rate (BER) and inference latency to avoid communication outage or even task failure. In addition, a long-short-term memory network is employed to predict channel variation based on the historical channel gain sequences to mitigate feedback delay in channel estimation. The proposed scheme is implemented based on a UAV and a control center running the 7-billion-parameter LLM, LLaVA, for detecting nets and kites on power lines. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme reduces BER and energy consumption and improves inference accuracy compared with the benchmarks.

title: TTD3-Enhanced Reliable Downlink Communication in Multi-UAV Networks Supported by 6DMA-Assisted Symbiotic Radio.
abstract: Reliable communication in multi-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks faces challenges due to link gain fluctuations caused by UAV mobility and limited spectrum resources. To address these issues, we propose a multi-UAV network supported by six-dimensional movable antennas (6DMA)-assisted symbiotic radio (SR), in which a 6DMA-assisted UAV serves as an aerial auxiliary node. By flexibly adjusting their three-dimensional (3D) positions and orientations, 6DMA enables precise beam alignment and controllable signal reflection, thereby enhancing link stability and communication reliability. Meanwhile, SR technology facilitates efficient spectrum sharing and energy reuse, effectively alleviating spectrum scarcity and improving overall spectral efficiency. Based on this framework, a spectral efficiency maximization problem is formulated by jointly optimizing active/passive beamforming and 6DMA posture. To efficiently solve the resulting high-dimensional problem, a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based twin-twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TTD3) algorithm is developed, which decomposes the task into beamforming and six-dimensional posture control subproblems. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms conventional baseline schemes in terms of spectral efficiency.

title: Movable-Antenna Array-Enhanced Energy-Efficient RSMA Communication Networks.
abstract: Movable antennas (MAs) are increasingly recognized as a promising technology for emerging next-generation communications due to their unique capability to dynamically adapt their positions and satisfy service demands. In this paper, we investigate an MA-enhanced rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) network, aiming to maximize overall energy efficiency through joint optimization of antenna positioning, data transmission, and repositioning durations, beamforming, and common-rate allocation under a shared-energy source and non-linear motor power model. Since the formulated problem is highly non-convex, we develop an alternating optimization-based framework to decouple the original design problem into three subproblems, which are addressed iteratively. Simulation results unveil that the proposed MA-enhanced RSMA system achieves significant energy efficiency gains over conventional fixed-position antenna networks and consistently outperforms all benchmarks.

title: Toward Interference Mitigation for Wi-Fi 8 Coordinated Beamforming in Multi-AP network.
abstract: Next-generation Wi-Fi 8 (IEEE 802.11bn) targets Ultra-High Reliability (UHR) by introducing Coordinated Beamforming (CoBF). In dense networks with many access points (APs), simultaneous downlink multi-user MIMO (MU-MIMO) transmissions from multiple APs can cause severe interference, both within a basic service set (intra-BSS) and between BSSs (inter-BSS). CoBF is envisioned to allow multiple APs to transmit concurrently without mitigated interference. This paper proposes a coordinated beamforming nulling strategy that completely cancels all intra-AP and inter-AP interference when sufficient spatial degrees of freedom are available. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed CoBF approach significantly mitigates interference and achieves substantial throughput gains in dense AP scenarios.

title: DRL-MCR: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Multi-Modal Communication Routing Scheme for Multi-Domain Integrated Networks.
abstract: Next-generation networks envision ubiquitous multi-domain integrated networks, extending into challenging environments like remote ocean and deep-sea regions. To overcome the limitations of single-modal communication, the multi-modal communication emerges as a promising solution by leveraging the complementary strengths of diverse modalities such as radio frequency (RF), underwater acoustic communication (UAC), and optical wireless communication (OWC). However, conventional routing approaches designed for single-modal or homogeneous networks are inadequate to manage the network complexity. To address these challenges, we propose a deep reinforcement learning-based multi-modal communication routing (DRL-MCR) scheme for multi-domain integrated networks (MDINs). The DRL-MCR enables decentralized network nodes with decision-making capability through the trial-and-error learning process, to exploit multi-modal communication cooperation and learn the optimal routing policies for path and modality selections. Moreover, we design an algorithm that employs double deep Q-network, dueling network structure, and prioritized experience replay mechanism, to efficiently evaluate the value of routing actions, thereby improving decision-making effectiveness and learning convergence. The simulation results demonstrate the superiority of our proposed scheme compared with benchmarks in both latency and packet delivery ratio in various scenarios.

title: Fractional Doppler Shifts Channel Estimation for OTFS Systems Based on the Novel CBAM Network.
abstract: Orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation is a promising waveform for sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks, offering robustness to severe Doppler effects through its operation in the sparse delay-Doppler (DD) domain. However, fractional Doppler shifts inevitably arise in practical systems with finite bandwidth and signaling duration, causing channel energy leakage that fundamentally impairs DD domain sparsity. The resulting inter-Doppler interference (IDI) renders accurate channel estimation challenging, as the channel response fails to be directly resolved from received pilot symbols. To address the issue, this paper proposes a novel convolutional block attention module (CBAM) network that directly learns the DD domain channel response from pilot signals. By leveraging channel and spatial attention mechanisms, the proposed network enhances discriminative feature learning, improves sensitivity to fractional Doppler components, and effectively mitigates IDI. Furthermore, a post-estimation thresholding strategy is employed to extract delay and Doppler indices along with corresponding channel gains for signal detection. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed CBAM network significantly outperforms both the CNN and ResNet-CNN machine learning-based approaches, achieving approximately 1.5–3.8 dB normalized mean square error (NMSE) improvement at 30 dB signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).

title: Channel Estimation in MIMO Systems Using Flow Matching Models.
abstract: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems require efficient and accurate channel estimation with low pilot overhead to unlock their full potential for high spectral and energy efficiency. While deep generative models have emerged as a powerful foundation for the channel estimation task, the existing approaches using diffusion-based and score-based models suffer from high computational runtime due to their stochastic and many-step iterative sampling. In this paper, we introduce a flow matching-based channel estimator to overcome this limitation. The proposed channel estimator is based on a deep neural network trained to learn the velocity field of wireless channels, which we then integrate into a plug-and-play proximal gradient descent (PnP-PGD) framework. Simulation results reveal that our formulated approach consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art (SOTA) generative model-based estimators, achieves up to 49 times faster inference at test time, and reduces up to 20 times peak graphics processing unit (GPU) memory usage. Our code and models are publicly available to support reproducible research.

title: Beamforming for Multiuser LEO Satellite Communications with Irregular Tiled Array.
abstract: Due to the large aperture and low grating lobe of irregular tiled array (ITA), we consider the beamforming design for multiuser low earth orbit satellite communications (SatComs) with ITA. We partition the entire ITA into multiple identical super arrays, where each super array is composed of a few subarrays. To maximize the total sum-rate of Sat-Coms, we propose an ITA and beamforming alternating optimization (IBAO) scheme. Specifically, we transform the sumrate maximization problem into a weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) problem, thereby obtaining a closed-form solution for the beamforming design. Subsequently, the binary conversion matrix is introduced to model the subarray layout. For each super array, we relax the binary conversion matrix into continuous variables, which are then optimized within the WMMSE problem. The alternating optimization is iteratively performed between the continuous conversion matrix and beamforming matrix until the convergence. Finally, the binary conversion matrix is recovered via integer programming, which approximates the continuous solution by selecting feasible subarrays from a predefined set. Simulation results show that the IBAO scheme can significantly reduce hardware costs while maintaining competitive SatComs performance.

title: AFDM Channel Estimation with Chirped FMCW.
abstract: Affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) is a promising waveform for doubly selective channels because it can efficiently handle Doppler effects and achieve full diversity. Reliable AFDM, however, requires accurate channel estimation. Existing AFDM estimators typically employ guard-banded pilots or superimposed pilots in the affine domain, which either reduce spectral efficiency or incur high receiver complexity. This paper proposes a novel frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW)-assisted channel estimation framework for AFDM. An FMCW pilot is superimposed on the time-domain signal prior to the AFDM post-chirp operation in the inverse discrete affine Fourier transform, eliminating guard intervals and improving spectral efficiency. At the receiver, after the standard AFDM post-chirp dechirping step, FMCW dechirping and reshaping produce a radar-like delay–Doppler response (DDR). A one-dimensional DFT across slow time localizes each path in a unique column, from which delay, Doppler, and complex gain are estimated using low-complexity processing. Analysis characterizes the effective affine-domain pilot structure, the resulting complexity reduction, and the data-to-pilot interference statistics. Also, our simulation results show that the proposed method achieves comparable normalized mean square error (NMSE) and bit-error-rate (BER) performance relative to conventional MMSE estimators while reducing complexity significantly.

title: Performance Optimization of Semantic Communication for Users with Dynamically Evolving Knowledge.
abstract: This paper develops a dynamically evolving knowledge-based semantic communication framework, where the base station (BS) and users possess continuously updating multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) to keep up with the evolving knowledge. In the investigated framework, a BS extracts semantic information based on its own MLLM, and transmits it to the users, who process the received semantic information according to their own MLLMs. Here, the MLLM of the BS is constantly updated to keep up with the newest knowledge. In each transmission period, the BS uses the adaptive low rank method (AdaLoRA) to decompose the updated parameters of MLLM and transmits important parameters to the users. Due to the limited wireless resources, the BS must transmit an appropriate size of semantic information and parameters for each user. We formulate this problem as an optimization problem aimed at maximizing the MLLM synchronization metric (MSM). To solve this problem, we introduce a hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) algorithm to allocate resource blocks (RBs) for the users and subsequently transmit semantic information along with updated parameters to the users. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework can improve the MSM by up to 1.36x compared to the framework without parameter transmission.

title: Spatially Non-Stationary Channel Estimation for XL-RIS-Aided MIMO Systems.
Reflections over the Sea: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface for Maritime Self-Powered Communications.
abstract: Maritime communication is becoming a vital component of 6G networks, driven by the rapid expansion of the maritime economy. However, existing technologies face critical challenges in signal coverage, availability, and robustness, especially under harsh sea conditions. This paper proposes a novel framework for the maritime Internet-of-Things (IoT) communications that leverages the reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) mounted on offshore infrastructures, such as wind turbines, to enhance coverage and reliability. To capture dynamic maritime environment, a near-ocean-surface channel model is developed considering the impact of sea waves. In addition, a wave energy harvesting (EH) system is designed to self-power IoT sensors for data acquisition, processing, and transmission. To support real-time adaptation, channel state information is continuously measured to optimize RIS reflection parameters and maximize multi-user communication rates. Simulation results show that the proposed system significantly improves IoT communication performance by over 20%, under harsh sea conditions.

title: Joint Resource Allocation and Active/Passive Beamforming Optimizations Over Integrated Sensing and Symbiotic Radio Networks Using RIS-MIMO.
abstract: This paper proposes a novel joint resource allocation and active/passive beamforming optimization scheme over integrated sensing and symbiotic radio (ISASR) networks equipped with reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) and MIMO techniques. For our considered ISASR networks, a full-duplex (FD) base station (BS) communicates with a multi-antenna user and simultaneously senses multiple internet-of-things devices (IoTDs) with the aid of IoTDs’ equipped RISs. Moreover, each IoTD modulates its own data on the incident signals sent by the BS and passively backscatters its own data to the user with the aid of its RIS. Hence, in our proposed ISASR networks, RISs can not only enhance the performance of target sensing, but also improve the performance of passive backscatter communication. First, we formulate a system throughput maximization problem that jointly optimizes the BS’s throughput and all IoTDs’ throughput, subject to the sensing signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and communication constraints. Second, leveraging deep reinforcement learning (DRL), we develop a joint optimization scheme for BS’s active beamforming, RISs’ phase shifts (i.e., passive beamforming), power allocation, and time scheduling to balance the performance of communication and sensing. Finally, simulation results demonstrate the superior convergence, stability, and communication and sensing performance of our developed scheme over the existing baseline schemes.

title: MA-Aided Hierarchical Hybrid Beamforming for Multi-User Wideband Beam Squint Mitigation.
abstract: In wideband near-field arrays, frequency-dependent array responses cause wavefronts at different frequencies to deviate from that at the center frequency, producing beam squint and degrading multi-user performance. True-time-delay (TTD) circuits can realign the frequency dependence but require large delay ranges and intricate calibration, limiting scalability. Another line of work explores one- and two-dimensional array geometries, including linear, circular, and concentric circular, that exhibit distinct broadband behaviors such as different beam-squint sensitivities and focusing characteristics. These observations motivate adapting the array layout to enable wideband-friendly focusing and enhance multi-user performance without TTD networks. We propose a movable antenna (MA) aided architecture based on hierarchical sub-connected hybrid beamforming (HSC-HBF) in which antennas are grouped into tiles and only the tile centers are repositioned, providing slow geometric degrees of freedom that emulate TTD-like broadband focusing while keeping hardware and optimization complexity low. We show that the steering vector is inherently frequency dependent and that reconfiguring tile locations improves broadband focusing. Simulations across wideband near-field scenarios demonstrate robust squint suppression and consistent gains over fixed-layout arrays, achieving up to 5\% higher sum rate, with the maximum improvement exceeding 140\%.

title: Active Channel Sparsification for FDD Massive MIMO: A Graph Reinforcement Learning Approach.
abstract: While massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) promises high data rates and link reliability, the massive number of antennas introduces critical challenges in downlink (DL) channel estimation and precoding, especially in frequency-division duplex (FDD) systems, due to the lack of instantaneous channel reciprocity. Going beyond compressed sensing-aided approaches, active channel sparsification (ACS) has emerged as a promising candidate to realize joint DL channel estimation and precoding with limited pilot budget, relaxing the reliance of the level of channel sparsity. However, the complex combinatorial optimization problem inherent in the ACS methodology incurs prohibitive computational costs, hindering itself from potential practical deployment. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a novel ACS-GRL framework to produce sparsified channel representation via a bipartite graph neural network (GNN) architecture together with deep reinforcement learning (DRL). As such, leveraging second-order channel statistics, the proposed ACS-GRL framework generates a sparsifying pre-beamforming matrix that maps the multiuser channels to a sparsified one, which can be estimated effectively with a limited DL pilot budget, and at the same time yields sparsifying DL precoding vectors to maximize the effective multiplexing gain. Preliminary experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed scheme over the existing ACS methods in improving the sum rate performance.

title: Semantic-Aware Co-Design of Spatio-Temporal Focusing and Adaptive Modulation for Wearable Brain-Body Neuro-Interfaces.
abstract: This paper presents a communication-theoretic, semantic-aware co-design for a wearable brain-body neuro-interface that addresses the dynamic somatic dysregulation in Major Depressive Disorder. At the physical layer, we derive an analytical spatio-temporal focusing model for temporal interference (TI) stimulation using a multilayer spherical head formulation. Closed-form envelope metrics enable efficient optimization of focusing gain and mainlobe-to-sidelobe ratio (MSR) under scalp-current safety constraints, yielding a library of high-precision stimulation actions. At the MAC layer, wearable biosignals are abstracted into semantic channel state information, and adaptive modulation is cast as a Markov decision process with energy/safety-aware rewards; the optimal policy is obtained by value iteration. Analytical and simulation results show that the proposed co-design sustains high MSR at deep targets with phase-locked steering, improves long-term therapeutic reward versus static or myopic baselines, and shortens the time to a desired "Calm" state, with multiplicative benefits over isolated layer designs.

title: Joint Optimization of Role Switching and Trajectory Planning for Multi-UAV Assisted Uplink Secure Communications.
abstract: As an aerial base station, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) offer significant potential to enhance terrestrial communications due to their flexible on-demand deployment, enabling rapid and reliable line-of-sight (LoS) wireless connectivity. This paper investigates a multi-UAV-assisted uplink wireless communication network under eavesdropping threats with location uncertainty. The proposed system enhances operational sustainability through energy replenishment stations while introducing multi-role UAVs capable of dynamic role-switching among three functions: communication reception, friendly jamming, and energy replenishment. To maximize worst-case secrecy capacity, we formulate a joint optimization problem encompassing UAV role-switching decisions, power allocation, and trajectory planning. By decomposing this multi-variable optimization problem into tractable subproblems, we derive a globally optimal solution through an iterative framework based on block coordinate descent (BCD) and successive convex approximation (SCA). Simulation results confirm that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing benchmarks in improving secrecy capacity.

title: Low-Complexity Frequency-Domain Successive-Interference-Cancellation Equalization for OTFS.
abstract: Frequency-domain (FD) pilot-based channel estimation and equalization are widely adopted due to their implementation efficiency, but their performance degrades in doubly selective channels. In this paper, we propose an FD-based pilot insertion and successive-interference-cancellation equalization framework with an adaptive-length equalizer that dynamically adjusts its effective span according to the channel delay-Doppler characteristics. By exploiting the banded (localized) structure of the FD channel matrix, the proposed method avoids unnecessary equalizer expansion in benign conditions while retaining sufficient degrees of freedom in severe time-frequency dispersion. A low-complexity criterion is developed to determine the equalizer length without requiring full channel knowledge. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed adaptive equalizer achieves near-optimal error-rate performance with significantly reduced computational complexity compared to conventional FD equalizers, making it particularly suitable for high-mobility and real-time communication scenarios.

title: Generative AI Based Secrecy Throughput Improvement in IRS-NOMA-Aided FANETs.
abstract: Intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) is a promising technology, which can significantly improve channel propagation quality. However, the openness of wireless channels exposes information security risks such as malicious eavesdropping, especially in flying ad hoc networks (FANETs). This paper presents a generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) scheme to optimize the secrecy throughput in the non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-aided FANETs, where the IRS is strategically configured to establish supplementary communication links. Specifically, to prevent eavesdroppers from intercepting signals using serial interference cancellation (SIC), the secrecy throughput maximization is formulated under the constraints on IRS phase control, drone beamforming, and mobility. Then, we utilize the deep retrieval-augmented generation (DRAG)-based GenAI to translate complex security scenarios into rigorous Markov decision process (MDP) formulations, thereby achieving domain knowledge enhancement. Further, a mixture-of-experts (MoE)-based dual-agent proximal policy optimization (DA-PPO) algorithm is proposed to jointly optimize IRS phase shift, drone beamforming and trajectory. Especially, MoE facilitates robust policy learning under diverse channels, and the shared critic mechanism is deployed to guide the dual agents, effectively maximizing the benefits of the joint optimization. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed MoE-based DA-PPO algorithm achieves at least a 6.2% secrecy throughput improvement over traditional baselines.

title: Minimizing Task Delay for Mobile Edge Generation in D2D Underlaying Cellular Network.
abstract: A mobile edge generation (MEG) framework is proposed for latency-sensitive tasks in social-aware D2D underlaying cellular networks. User devices (UDs) are organized into socially cohesive communities for cooperative generation via cellular and D2D links. A joint seed-and-content-based (JSCB) protocol is proposed to enable adaptive switching UD association between seed acquisition with local generation and direct content sharing, while a spillover mechanism is incorporated to handle overdue transmissions. An average task delay minimization problem is formulated to jointly optimize UD association, transmission mode, D2D pairing, and beamforming. To address the hybrid, temporally coupled problem, a joint matching and proximal policy optimization (JMPPO) algorithm is developed, in which discrete and continuous actions are decoupled through hierarchical deep reinforcement learning and matching. Numerical results demonstrate that JSCB achieves reduced delay via adaptive scheduling, while JMPPO outperforms learning-based and traditional baselines under diverse conditions.

title: 6DMA-aided Multiple Access Point Coordination: Two-timescale Decentralized Beamforming and Antenna Movement Optimization.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate six-dimensional movable antenna (6DMA)-aided multi-access point (AP) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communication systems. To address practical implementation constraints and improve scalability, we propose a two-timescale decentralized optimization framework that jointly designs beamforming, antenna position, and array orientation. In the short timescale, each distributed AP designs its receive beamformer locally based on instantaneous channel state information (CSI). In the long timescale, the central processing unit optimizes the antenna positions and array orientations for all APs to maximize the ergodic sum rate of all users. The reconfiguration of antenna positions and array orientations is based on the statistical CSI, rendering the optimization problem interesting but also challenging to solve. To address this problem efficiently, a constrained random successive convex approximation algorithm is developed. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed 6DMA-aided multi-AP system outperforms the conventional fixed-position antenna and other flexible-antenna schemes.

title: Learning-Based Joint Channel Acquisition and Communication Optimization for Movable Antennas.
abstract: This paper presents an end-to-end deep learning framework for movable-antenna (MA)-enabled multiuser communications. Unlike conventional methods that presume perfect channel state information (CSI), our design explicitly addresses practical CSI acquisition via tailored pilot signals and quantized feedback, while jointly optimizing channel estimation, MA placement, and precoding. An end-to-end framework with a corresponding training paradigm is designed to integrate these key phases of MA systems. The proposed pipeline learns transmission strategies directly from imperfect channel data, overcoming the mismatch of separately performing channel estimation and MAs’ position optimization. Simulation results show consistent gains in achievable sum rate over traditional benchmarks, particularly under limited feedback. Notably, the proposed method obtains performance comparable to widely used gradient-based schemes, yet requires substantially lower feedback overhead. These results underscore the effectiveness and adaptability of learning-based MA system design for future wireless networks.

title: Constructing Knowledge Map for MIMO-OFDM Clustered Channel Estimation.
abstract: Channel knowledge map (CKM) exploits environment information to assist channel estimation during communication. For clustered channels, which represent a typical type of wireless propagation environment, there has been no research devoted to designing an appropriate CKM to enhance their estimation. To exploit environment information for clustered channel, improve channel estimation accuracy and reduce pilot overhead, we propose ClusterCKM, a CKM providing the range of clustered multipath parameters for any pair of transmitter-receiver links in the region of interest. Firstly, we construct ClusterCKM through estimating the spatial range of scatterer clusters from historical channel information. From these spatial range of scatterer clusters, ClusterCKM infers the range of multipath parameters for the target link. Furthermore, a ClusterCKM-based channel estimation algorithm is developed to utilize the parameter range provided by ClusterCKM. Simulation results show that, more accurate channel estimation can be achieved and pilot overhead can also be reduced by ClusterCKM and the ClusterCKM-based estimation algorithm.

title: Predictive Beamforming in Low-Altitude Wireless Networks: A Cross-Attention Approach.
abstract: Accurate beam prediction is essential for maintaining reliable links and high spectral efficiency in dynamic low-altitude wireless networks. However, existing approaches often fail to capture the deep correlations across heterogeneous sensing modalities, limiting their adaptability in complex three-dimensional environments. To overcome these challenges, we propose a multi-modal predictive beamforming method based on a cross-attention fusion mechanism that jointly leverages visual and structured sensor data. The proposed model utilizes a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to learn multi-scale spatial feature hierarchies from visual images and a Transformer encoder to capture cross-dimensional dependencies within sensor data. Then, a cross-attention fusion module is introduced to integrate complementary information between the two modalities, generating a unified and discriminative representation for accurate beam prediction. Through experimental evaluations conducted on a real-world dataset, our method reaches 79.7% Top-1 accuracy and 99.3% Top-3 accuracy, surpassing the 3D ResNet-Transformer baseline by 4.4%-23.2% across Top-1 to Top-5 metrics. These results verify that multi-modal cross-attention fusion is effective for intelligent beam selection in dynamic low-altitude wireless networks.

title: Big-Data-Driven ISAR RF Digital Twin for UAV Channel Modeling in 6G Non-Terrestrial Networks.
abstract: This paper extends an ISAR based RF digital twin framework by incorporating big data technologies to model unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communication channels in sixth generation non terrestrial networks (6G NTNs). High resolution inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) echoes, vehicle trajectories, network telemetry and environmental context are collected via an edge–cloud data pipeline. Lightweight preprocessing at the edge performs motion and Doppler compensation and compresses radar echoes into compact spectral–temporal descriptors, while distributed storage and processing in the cloud facilitate large scale training and real time decision making. A Transformer backbone fuses ISAR features with trajectory and context signals, and a reinforcement learning engine adapts beamforming, power allocation and scheduling. Novel freshness aware state variables ensure the digital twin remains synchronized with rapid UAV attitude changes and blockage conditions, and anomaly detection triggers recalibration when sensor drift is detected. Simulations across urban, suburban and open environments show that the big data enhanced twin achieves lower outage probability, reduced end to end latency and higher throughput than statistical, CNN based or ray tracing baselines, illustrating the value of combining ISAR detail, big data pipelines and edge intelligence in 6G NTN scenarios.

title: Minimum Required Power for Continuous-Aperture Array Based Secure Transmission.
abstract: A continuous-aperture array (CAPA)-based secure transmission framework is proposed, where continuous current distribution, or beamformer, is designed to minimize the required transmission power for achieving a specific target secrecy rate. On this basis, closed-form expressions for the minimum required power (MRP) and the associate optimal current distribution are derived. These results are further compared with conventional maximal ratio transmission (MRT) and zero-forcing (ZF) beamforming schemes to provide deeper insights. The analytical findings are then specialized to the typical array structures, e.g., planar CAPAs and planar spatially discrete arrays (SPDAs), followed by asymptotic analyses under the assumption of an infinitely large aperture. Numerical results demonstrate that: i) the proposed secure continuous beamforming design outperforms MRT and ZF beamforming; ii) CAPAs achieve superior secrecy performance compared to conventional SPDAs.

title: Distributed MoE-based Uplink Detection for Cell-Free Communication Systems.
abstract: Cell-free Massive multiple input and multiple output (MIMO) is recognized as a key technology for beyond-5G networks, where distributed access points (APs) jointly serve user equipments (UEs) to address the inherent inter-cell interference issue inherent in cellular systems. While conventional distributed signal detection methods offer a practical balance between performance and fronthaul load, they are fundamentally limited by linear processing constraints. In this paper, we propose a novel deep learning based uplink detection framework by introducing the distributed mixture of experts detection network (DMoE-DetNet). In this architecture, each AP acts as a local expert employing convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for non-linear feature extraction, and transmits the local minimum mean square error (MMSE) detection results and statistical channel information to the central processing unit (CPU). In the CPU, an attention-based encoder module captures complex spatio-temporal dependencies among users for global feature fusion, with a gating network at the central processor dynamically weighting the contributions from different APs. At last, a linear detector outputs the symbol probability. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed DMoE-DetNet significantly outperforms conventional linear processing based cell-free signal detection methods in terms of symbol error rate, showcasing the potential of artificial intelligence-enabled communication systems.

title: A Joint Target Sensing and Data Detection Scheme for Multistatic ISAC Networks via Broadcast Transmission.
abstract: The integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) technology leverages full-dimensional resources for simultaneous sensing and communication (S&C), serving as a key enabler of beyond-5G networks. However, most existing monostatic ISAC systems employ separate S&C receivers and primarily focus on transmitter design, which limits the potential of joint processing and cooperative gains. In this paper, we propose a joint target-sensing and data-detection (JTD) scheme for multistatic ISAC under broadcast (BC) transmission, employing superposition coding and successive interference cancellation to exploit the mutual benefits of S&C. Locally, each receiver refines channel estimation or target localization by reusing detected data symbols as virtual pilots, while at the network level, receivers further enhance performance by reusing symbols decoded from others via BC transmission. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme significantly enhances JTD performance and outperforms the time-division multiple access protocol.

title: Phase Error Resilient Practical Channel Estimation by Special Orthogonal Group Equivariant AI/ML.
abstract: Channel estimation (CE) is an essential part at the receiver impacting the performance of the whole network. It also attracts tremendous study on using artificial intelligence / machine learning (AI/ML) to optimize CE. Despite the focus of these studies is on building the ability to handle additive-noise reduction, interpolation, and generalization, one impact from the multiplicative phase noise has been underestimated. For example, there may be linear phase rotation caused by timing offset or common phase rotation caused by frequency offset or phase noise of oscillators. In the conventional CE process, there is often estimation on that rotation and offset in order to (re-) compensate their impacts. However, such compensation involves estimation or/and interpolation error(s) which may propagate and seriously degrade the CE performance of both AI and non-AI methods. Therefore, an upgraded multi-layer perceptron (MLP) model is proposed with the trainable weights and biases in each layer being projected onto certain subspaces, which is special orthogonal group equivariant (SOGe). Such design facilitates the joint handling of phase rotation, additive-noise, and channel interpolation. Carefully designed algorithms for the projector also exploit the sparsity feature thus leading to low computational complexity. The simulation results show that the proposed AI/ML model achieves more than 10dB gain on NMSE over other AI/ML models, with more than 99% reduction on both computational complexity and model parameter numbers. Compared with conventional CE methods, the proposed method has comparable complexity and achieves up to 5dB gain in terms of BLER and 8 times throughput performance.

title: Comparisons on Ξ-, Λ- and V-Type Atomic Receivers in Wireless Communication and Sensing.
abstract: Atomic receiver based on the Electromagnetically Induced Transparency (EIT) demonstrates its potential in high sensitivity, miniaturization and wide frequency range wireless communication and sensing. Existing experiments have confirmed that EIT can be realized in Ladder(Ξ)-, Lambda(Λ)- and Vee(V)-type, each corresponding to distinct atomic excitation pathways. However, existing research on atomic receiver mainly focuses on the Ξ-type, overlooking the other two types. In this paper, we analyze the four-level configuration of Λ- and V-type atomic receivers under signal field for the first time. In particular, by using the rotating-wave transformation, we extend the three-level Hamiltonian to four-level system under the influence of the external signal field, and analyze how this interaction alters the EIT spectrum. Then, based on the master equation, we analyze and compare the performance of three systems for wireless communication and sensing. Under typical settings in currently reported experiments, result shows that Ξ-type system performs better in sensitivity and available frequency, while V-type system performs better in instantaneous bandwidth and Λ-type exhibits an exceptionally stable EIT window in complex electromagnetic environments.

title: A Novel Channel Estimation Method for Stem-connected Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface.
abstract: Stem-connected reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) has been recognized as a promising beyond-diagonal RIS (BD-RIS) that achieves the optimal tradeoff between performance and circuit complexity but poses a significant challenge for channel estimation. In this work, we introduce a novel two-stage channel estimation approach that uses on-off switches on the RIS stems to address this issue. In the first stage, with switches off, the stem-connected RIS reduces to a simple diagonal structure with parameters estimated based on parallel factor (PARAFAC) decomposition. In the second stage, with switches on, we efficiently estimate the remaining with parameters based on alternating least square. Simulation results demonstrate that our approach achieves superior channel estimation accuracy with lower computational cost than existing methods. Furthermore, it is applicable to most beyond-diagonal RIS architectures, enabling the first comprehensive comparison of channel estimation performance across single-, fully-, tree-, and stem-connected RIS architectures.

title: Weighted Sum-Rate Maximization for Fully-Connected Pinching Antenna Systems.
abstract: A fully-connected architecture for pinching antenna systems (PASS) is investigated. In contrast to the conventional sub-connected architecture, where each waveguide is fed by a single radio frequency (RF) chain, the proposed fully-connected design distributes the signal from each RF chain to all waveguides. This approach fully use the overall spatial degrees of freedoms and also enables scalability in the number of RF chains. A phase shifter (PS)-based network is utilized to realize the full connection between the RF chains and waveguides, a configuration that also facilitates a tri-hybrid beamforming architecture. To exploit the reconfigurability of the system, a sum-rate-driven optimization algorithm is proposed. To handle the coupling among design variables in the objective and constraints, the algorithm iteratively updates each variable while keeping the others fixed, with tailored update rules ensuring optimality and convergence. Simulation results verify that the proposed design allows flexible trade-offs between performance and hardware complexity, achieving comparable spectral efficiency to sub-connected PASS systems with fewer RF chains.

title: Model-Free Channel Estimation for Massive MIMO: A Channel Charting-Inspired Approach.
abstract: Channel estimation is fundamental to wireless communications, yet it becomes increasingly challenging in massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems where base stations employ hundreds of antennas. Traditional least-squares methods require prohibitive pilot overhead that scales with antenna count, while sparse estimation methods depend on precise channel models that may not always be practical. This paper proposes a model-free approach combining deep autoencoders and LSTM networks. The method first learns low-dimensional channel representations preserving temporal correlation through augmenting a channel charting-inspired loss function, then tracks these features to recover full channel information from limited pilots. Simulation results using ray-tracing datasets show that the proposed approach achieves up to 9 dB improvement in normalized mean square error compared to the least-squares methods under ill-conditioned scenarios, while maintaining scalability across MIMO configurations.

title: Reconfigurable Holographic Surface-Aided SWIPT: Holographic Beamforming and Waveform Design.
abstract: Massive multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) is widely used for high spatial gain and interference mitigation in simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT). However, the high hardware cost and power consumption of conventional phased arrays (PAs) employed in massive MIMO hinder their scalable deployment in massive IoT networks. In this paper, we propose a reconfigurable holographic surface (RHS)-assisted SWIPT system. Implemented with low-cost components, RHSs offer a cost-effective alternative to PAs. By dynamically adjusting the amplitude response of serially connected elements under wave excitation, RHSs enable directional beamforming for SWIPT. Due to power coupling in serially connected elements, the amplitude response of the RHS cannot be explicitly characterized, and conventional deterministic beamforming and waveform design are inapplicable; thus, we construct a statistical characterization of the serially-coupled RHS and further propose beamforming and waveform designs for multicarrier signals under an inherent coupling mechanism. Simulations show that, under equal hardware cost, the proposed scheme achieves a larger rate–energy (R–E) region than PA-based systems, high-lighting the potential of RHSs for cost-effective SWIPT.

title: System Modeling of Microfluidic Molecular Communication: A Markov Approach.
abstract: This paper presents a Markov-based system model for microfluidic molecular communication (MC) channels. By discretizing the advection-diffusion dynamics, the proposed model establishes a physically consistent state-space formulation. The transition matrix explicitly captures diffusion, advective flow, reversible binding, and flow-out effects. The resulting discrete-time formulation enables analytical characterization of both transient and equilibrium responses through a linear system representation. Numerical results verify that the proposed framework accurately reproduces channel behaviors across a wide range of flow conditions, providing a tractable basis for the design and analysis of MC systems in microfluidic environments.

title: Dynamic Cooperative Cell-Free ISAC: A Secure Design.
abstract: This paper focuses on the security issue in the cell-free (CF) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, where multiple targets act as potential communication eavesdroppers. Artificial noise (AN) is transmitted to not only jam the confidential information but also sense the targets so as to achieve the dual-functional role. Different from previous security studies that assume fixed AP operation modes, a dynamic cooperative CF (DC-CF) ISAC network is proposed where different APs are dynamically adjusted as ISAC transmitters or sensing receivers according to different channel conditions and system priorities for sensing and communication (S&C). Therefore, an optimization problem is formulated by jointly designing AP operation modes, transmit beamforming, and receive combining to achieve the tradeoff between S&C, where the minimal sensing signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio and minimal secrecy rate are utilized as performance metrics for S&C separately to achieve fairness. The integer variables and their strong coupling are addressed utilizing the penalty-based method, and an alternative optimization-based algorithm is proposed to find a sub-optimal solution. Numerical results validate the superiority of the proposed DC-CF ISAC network in security and sensing performance enhancement over some existing schemes.

title: Near-Field Wideband Channel Estimation for Extremely Large-Scale RIS-Aided Communication Systems.
abstract: This paper studies wideband channel estimation for OFDM systems assisted by extremely large RIS (XL-RIS). Due to the large aperture of XL-RISs, the user equipment may operate in the near-field region, while the base station–XL-RIS link remains in the far field, leading to a cascaded channel with hybrid near-field and far-field characteristics. Moreover, wideband effects further complicate channel estimation in mmWave/THz systems. To address these challenges, we propose a frequency-independent orthogonal dictionary by augmenting the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) matrix with additional parameters, which enables an efficient representation of the wideband cascaded channel using a two-dimensional block-sparse structure. Based on this property, the considered channel estimation problem is effectively solved within a tailored compressed sensing framework. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms conventional polar-domain channel estimation approaches in terms of estimation accuracy.

title: Joint Design of Positioning and Beamforming for Wideband Multi-User Movable Antenna Systems.
abstract: While Movable Antenna (MA) systems have demonstrated significant performance gains in narrowband scenarios, their application in wideband regimes is less developed. Existing wideband MA studies reveal a performance gap compared to narrowband counterparts and lack a unified optimization framework that concurrently delivers high performance, low complexity, and extensibility. This work identifies a critical bottleneck: in wideband Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM), the requirement for all subcarriers to share the same antenna position intrinsically limits the available degrees of freedom. To overcome this, we introduce a joint MA positioning and beamforming optimization method. Our key innovation lies in reformulating the challenging sumrate maximization problem using a sparse optimization framework. This transforms the problem into one of joint position matching and coefficient calculation, enabling all subcarriers to collectively determine the optimal antenna positions within a matching pursuit algorithm, which ensures convergence within few iterations. Simulations confirm the method’s effectiveness, showing substantial improvements over fixed-antenna systems and providing insights into the performance boundaries of wideband MA configurations.

title: 3DCKM: A Large-Scale Multiband 3D Channel Knowledge Map Dataset for Low-Altitude Corridors.
abstract: The emergence of Low-Altitude Corridors (LACs) for unmanned aerial vehicle operations introduces unique challenges for wireless communication, where three-dimensional (3D) air–ground links exhibit strong altitude-dependent channel variations. Accurate modeling of these effects requires 3D channel information that captures the spatial relationship between wireless propagation and the environment. Existing channel datasets remain limited to terrestrial scenarios and lack comprehensive 3D spatial and multiband channel information. To bridge this gap, we propose 3DCKM, a large-scale multiband 3D Channel Knowledge Map dataset designed for LACs. 3DCKM provides extensive coverage across multiple frequency bands from sub-6 GHz to millimeter-wave, capturing detailed channel characteristics at varying altitudes to model altitude-dependent propagation effects. 3DCKM dataset integrates spatially aligned environmental data, including building map, terrain features, and material properties, with rich channel knowledge encompassing path loss, propagation delay, angle of arrival/departure (AoA/AoD), zenith angles (ZoA/ZoD), and multipath interactions. By offering large-scale multiband 3D channel knowledge, 3DCKM enables critical applications such as CKM construction, AI-based channel prediction, and LAC network optimization. The dataset is available at https://github.com/zcy2002zcy/3DCKM-datasets.git.

title: Experimental Study of Delay-Jitter Determinism and Robustness in Visible-Laser Links.
abstract: Delay jitter is a fundamental metric of communication link determinism and stability. This work introduces a path-ablation and timestamp-embedding feedback methodology, supported by a purpose-built static visible light communication (VLC) testbed, to systematically evaluate delay jitter. Two transmission paths are compared: a direct physical-layer connection and a protocol stack-based transmission. Real transmission results show that the direct connection constrains end-to-end average jitter tightly within 0.565–0.789 µs, achieving two-to-three orders of magnitude improvement over the stack-based transmission, where jitter ranges from 22.057 to 200.589 µs. Under diverse environmental perturbations and incidence angles, the direct connection jitter remains stable between 0.588–0.663 µs, confirming robustness and angular insensitivity. Furthermore, optical power sweeps at the receiver reveal a usable-power regime, within which valid-packet jitter converges consistently to 0.594–0.611 µs. Collectively, these results establish the deterministic and robust nature of the direct-connection-based visible-light links, providing experimental evidence for their application in high-reliability optical communications.

title: Semantic Communication Performance Optimization with Channel and Content Preference Feedbacks.
abstract: In this paper, a novel channel and content preference feedbacks enabled semantic communication framework that enables a transmitter to use limited channel and content for efficient and accurate image data transmission is developed. In the proposed framework, a base station (BS) divides an image into several sub-images according to the image content and extracts the semantic information from sub-images. Then the BS allocates the semantic information to different sub-channels and transmits them to a user. After receiving the semantic information, the user regenerates the image and selects to transmit a feedback (i.e., channel state information (CSI) feedback or content preference feedback) to the BS. The BS will use this feedback information to optimize sub-channel allocation and feedback selection. Meanwhile, since the number of feedback that the receiver can transmit is limited, the BS must determine when to receive a feedback as well as which type of the feedback should be transmitted according to the dynamic wireless environment. We formulate this problem as an optimization problem whose goal is to minimize the mean square error (MSE) between the original image and the regenerated image via optimizing sub-channel allocation and feedback selection. To address this problem, an actor-critic based reinforcement learning (RL) with dynamic neighborhood construction (AC-DNC) scheme is proposed. Compared to the current RL methods, the proposed method is more effective in finding better actions in huge discrete action spaces since the designed method approximates the discrete neighboring action space using a continuous action and selects an action with the maximum Q value from the neighboring action space. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme can improve the performance by up to 27.14% and 26.87% compared to the proposed scheme without CSI and content preference feedback information and the regular Q actor-critic (QAC) method.

title: Learnable Constellation Mapping and Attention-based Channel Adaptation for Digital Semantic Communication System.
abstract: Aiming at the problems of semantic distortion caused by multipath fading channels and compatibility between digital communication and semantic communication systems, we propose a learnable constellation mapping and attention-based channel adaptation mechanism for digital semantic communication system. By constructing a semantic encoder-modulator, the mapping probability from the source to discrete constellation symbols is learned, and the non-differentiable problem of digital modulation is avoided. Neural networks are designed to combine non-trainable but differentiable multipath channels and orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) to achieve end-to-end cross-layer joint optimization of the system. A dual attention-based channel state information (CSI) feedback mechanism is used to adjust the semantic coding process to ensure dynamic matching between features and subcarriers. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system enhances robustness against channel variations while ensuring compatibility with conventional digital communication systems, consequently improving image transmission quality.

title: Movable XL-array Enabled Mixed Near-field and Far-field Covert Communications.
abstract: In this paper, we propose to deploy a modular-based movable extremely large-scale array (XL-array) at Alice for enhancing covert communication performance. Compared with existing work that mostly considered either far-field or near-field covert communications, we consider in this paper a more general and practical mixed-field scenario, where multiple Bobs are located in either the near-field or far-field of Alice, in the presence of multiple near-field Willies. Specifically, we first formulate an optimization problem to maximize the achievable sum-rate under covertness constraint. To solve this non-convex optimization problem, we first decompose it into two subproblems, corresponding to an inner problem for beamforming optimization given positions of subarrays and an outer problem for subarray movement optimization. Although these two subproblems are still non-convex, we obtain their high-quality solutions by using the successive convex approximation technique and devising a customized differential evolution algorithm, respectively. Last, numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of proposed movable XL-array in balancing sum-rate and covert communication requirements, as compared to various benchmark schemes.

title: Robust Beamforming for Near-Field Physical Layer Security under Location Uncertainty.
abstract: In this paper, we study robust beamforming design for near-field physical-layer-security (PLS) systems, where a base station (BS) equipped with an extremely large-scale array (XL-array) serves near-field legitimate user (Bob) in the presence of near-field eavesdropper (Eve). Unlike existing works mostly assuming perfect channel state information (CSI) or location information of Eve, we consider the scenario where the location of Bob is perfectly known, while only imperfect location information of Eve is available at the BS. Specifically, we formulate a robust optimization problem to maximize the achievable rate of Bob while guaranteeing a worst-case limit on the eavesdropping rate under location uncertainty. To overcome the limitations of conventional methods, we first establish the conditions for which the first-order Taylor approximation of the near-field channel steering vector under location uncertainty is largely accurate. Then, we propose a two-stage robust beamforming method, which first partitions the uncertainty region into multiple sub-regions, followed by the second stage to formulate and solve a refined linear-matrix-inequality (LMI)-based robust beamforming optimization problem. Finally, numerical results validate that the proposed method achieves a superior trade-off between rate performance and secrecy robustness, hence significantly outperforming existing benchmarks under Eve location uncertainty.

title: Enhancing Physical Layer Security for SIM-aided Cell-free mMIMO Systems.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the physical layer security of cell-free (CF) massive multiple-input multiple-output (mMIMO) systems enhanced by stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIM), which offer promising wave-domain beamforming capabilities. We propose a joint optimization framework that simultaneously designs the AP digital precoding and SIM wave-based beamforming to maximize the weighted sum secrecy rate (WSSR). To address the inherent non-convexity caused by the coupling of power and phase design, we decouple the original problem into two sub-problems and solve them using alternating optimization, where AP precoding is optimized via convex reformulation and SIM phase shifts are updated using an efficient ADMM-based algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves a 50% improvement in secrecy performance compared to MMSE baseline methods.

title: Spectral and Energy Efficiency Trade-off: A Pinching Antenna Perspective.
abstract: The trade-off between spectral efficiency (SE) and energy efficiency (EE) for pinching antenna systems (PASS) is investigated. First, the optimization problem is formulated to maximize the weighted product of SE and EE by jointly optimizing the transmit and pinching beamforming. Under the maximum ratio transmission (MRT) strategy, the optimization of transmit beamforming reduces to the design of the scalar transmit power. It is then proved that the design of the pinching antenna (PA) placement is independent of the transmit power, but not vice versa. Based on this insight, a two-stage joint optimization framework is developed: 1) In the first stage, a general multi-waveguide PA placement framework is proposed; 2) In the second stage, a closed-form solution for the optimal transmit power is derived with the given optimized PA positions. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of our approach. Code is available at https://github.com/Zihao-Felix-Zhou/SE-EE-Tradeoff-Pinching-Antenna-Systems.

title: Semantic-Driven Continual Learning for Weather-Adaptive Vision-Aided mmWave Beam Selection.
abstract: Vision-aided millimeter-wave (mmWave) beam selection is pivotal for 6G networks but struggles in non-stationary environments where channel distributions shift with dynamic weather. Existing deep learning models suffer from catastrophic forgetting when adapting to such changes, rapidly losing previously acquired alignment capabilities. To address this, we propose a semantic-driven continual learning framework tailored for weather-adaptive beam selection. We introduce the Experience Replay with Synaptic Intelligence (ERSI) algorithm, which leverages asynchronously and sparsely triggered visual semantic cues to detect environmental drifts and trigger adaptive model updates. ERSI synergizes semanticgated experience replay with importance-weighted parameter regularization to consolidate historical channel knowledge while maintaining plasticity for new domains. Extensive evaluations on the multimodal M3SC dataset demonstrate that ERSI effectively mitigates forgetting during sunny-to-rainy/snowy transitions. The method maintains a Top-5 accuracy of over 81% on previous tasks and restricts the forgetting rate to approximately 11%, significantly outperforming conventional baselines and enabling robust lifelong learning in dynamic wireless networks.
