title: Collaborative Edge Inference for Large Language Models with Speculative Decoding.
abstract: Existing edge-based large language model (LLM) serving systems primarily rely on autoregressive decoding (AD) to generate inference results, generating only one output token per forward pass. The AD process underutilizes GPUs’ parallel processing capabilities and inherently introduces high serving latency, thereby hindering efficient LLM serving in resource-constrained edge networks. To address this challenge, we propose a speculative decoding (SD)-based LLM serving framework that coordinates small and large models deployed on heterogeneous edge nodes to accelerate output token generation and thus reduce serving latency. To improve resource utilization of edge nodes, we introduce pipeline parallelism that groups multiple inference tasks into batches and processes them in a pipelined manner. Building on this framework, we derive the total serving latency that jointly considers communication and inference latencies. We then formulate a joint task batching and wireless communication resource allocation problem to minimize the total serving latency under computing and communication resource constraints. To solve this problem, we derive closed-form solutions for wireless communication resource allocation, and develop an efficient algorithm to obtain optimal task batching strategies. Simulation results show that the proposed LLM serving framework outperforms benchmarks, achieving up to 23.1% latency reduction.

title: ScreenAnt: Transparent On-Screen Antennas for 6G.
abstract: 6G will require on-device antenna systems to operate at ultra-high frequency bands, achieve robust beamforming on the compact user devices, and be blockage-robust. Conventional edge-mounted antennas on devices have limited apertures, suffer from the 'death grip' caused by user-induced blockage, and have poor scalability at mmWave and sub-THz bands. To address these issues, motivated by the rapid evolution of transparent materials and antennas, we propose ScreenAnt in this work--which integrates a transparent antenna array onto the screens of future mobile devices. Specifically, we propose using a transparent on-screen uniform planar array and develop a framework to model its electromagnetic property, spatial configuration, and blockage robustness under realistic user-induced blockage. We also design a gradient-ascent-based algorithm to efficiently optimize power and phase control of on-screen antennas to maximize ScreenAnt's spectral efficiency. Our thorough simulations show that the proposed ScreenAnt can increase the uplink spectral efficiency by over 50% compared to edge-mounted antennas at 28 GHz, and by more than 150% at 300 GHz. ScreenAnt also demonstrates strong robustness against user-induced blockage, paving the way for practical and high-capacity 6G user device designs.

title: Towed Movable Antenna Array for Airborne Secure Communications.
abstract: This paper proposes a novel towed movable antenna (ToMA) array architecture to enhance the physical layer security of airborne communication systems. Unlike conventional onboard arrays with fixed-position antennas (FPAs), the ToMA array employs multiple subarrays mounted on flexible cables and towed by distributed drones, enabling agile deployment in three-dimensional (3D) space surrounding the central aircraft. This design significantly enlarges the effective array aperture and allows dynamic geometry reconfiguration, offering superior spatial resolution and beamforming flexibility. We consider a secure transmission scenario where an airborne transmitter communicates with multiple legitimate users in the presence of potential eavesdroppers. Based on the statistical distributions of locations of users and eavesdroppers, the antenna position vector (APV) of the ToMA array is optimized to maximize the users’ ergodic achievable rate. Analytical results for the case of a single user and a single eavesdropper reveal the optimal APV structure that minimizes their channel correlation. For the general multiuser scenario, we develop a low-complexity algorithm by leveraging Riemannian manifold optimization. Simulation results confirm that the proposed ToMA array achieves significant performance gains over conventional onboard FPA arrays.

title: A Closed-Loop Hybrid Beamforming Scheme Using Dynamic Arrays for ISAC.
abstract: Hybrid beamforming (HBF) is a crucial technology in wireless communication networks. To enable persistent communication and sensing of users in mobility scenarios, a HBF scheme with dynamic antenna structures is proposed. Specifically, a HBF structure with overlapped subarrays is designed using orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) algorithm for the downlink transmission. A sparse array is constructed to receive the echo signals from users, and a single-snapshot angle estimation algorithm to estimate the directions of the users is employed. The estimated directions are utilized for the next downlink transmission to achieve a reliable communication link and a fine tracking of the users. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed HBF scheme is capable of achieving both effective communication and accurate sensing.

title: SwinCE-DM: A Big Data-Driven Diffusion-Transformer Framework for Robust Channel Estimation in LEO Satellite Communications.
abstract: Accurate channel estimation remains a key challenge for low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communications, where rapid orbital motion and low SNR environments severely degrade traditional estimators. To address this, we propose SwinCE-DM, a big data–driven framework that tightly couples a hierarchical Swin Transformer encoder with diffusion-based refinement through a task-oriented co-design of the encoder–denoiser interface for LEO time-varying channels. A large-scale big data channel modeling platform, fully compliant with 3GPP TR 38.811, is developed to simulate massive orbital dynamics, multipath fading, and atmospheric effects, generating terabyte-level datasets across SISO and MIMO Ka-band scenarios. Leveraging these data-rich simulations, swinCE-DM learns high-dimensional temporal–spatial correlations via multi-scale windowed attention and iterative noise inversion. SwinCE-DM achieves consistent gains over Transformer- and diffusion-based baselines, e.g., reaching an NMSE of –11.7 dB at 0 dB SNR in MIMO settings. Comprehensive ablation studies further confirm the effectiveness of the Swin backbone, diffusion refinement, and big data–enhanced multi-stage training. These results highlight the promise of combining hierarchical vision transformers, generative diffusion models, and big data channel simulations to advance robust and scalable channel estimation for next-generation LEO satellite communications.

title: A Data-Friendly Deep Learning Architecture for High-Resolution Radio Map Construction.
abstract: High-resolution radio maps provide rich information about the radio landscape that is useful to a myriad of wireless applications. Although deep learning (DL) methods have shown their effectiveness in radio map construction, existing approaches require massive high-resolution radio maps in the dataset, the acquisition of which is labor-intensive and time-consuming in practice. In this paper, our goal is to devise a data-friendly high-resolution radio map estimation solution via training over a hybrid dataset, under which radio maps associated with a small fraction of the environment maps are of high-resolution, while those corresponding to most environment maps are of low-resolution. To exploit this heterogeneous data structure, we propose a novel two-stage DL framework. Specifically, in the first stage, we predict the low-resolution radio map corresponding to any given environment map via a neural network trained on the the abundant low-resolution radio maps in the dataset; while in the second stage, we refine the obtained low-resolution radio map into a high-resolution one via employing an image super-resolution network trained over the limited high-resolution radio maps in the dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework can achieve almost the same performance as the existing DL methods, but with about 80% reduction in the number of high-resolution radio maps in the dataset.

title: Cooperative Beamforming for Multi-BS ISAC in the Presence of Time and Phase Asynchrony.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is pivotal for 5G-Advanced. However, existing multi-base station (BS) cooperative frameworks often rely on idealized synchronization and the limited flexibility of non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA), rendering them impractical for real-world deployments. Consequently, modeling the impact of imperfect synchronization and exploring more flexible multiple access (MA) strategies, such as rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA), remain critical yet insufficiently investigated challenges. To address this issue, this paper investigates cooperative ISAC under realistic synchronization imperfections by modeling both the initial phase of BS transmit antennas and the time synchronization (TS) errors among BSs. Based on this model, we further derive the Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB) to establish the fundamental performance limits of sensing. Moreover, we develop a cooperative beamforming strategy that maximizes sensing accuracy while ensuring the required communication rate. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme enhances the cooperative ISAC performance and exhibits robustness to synchronization imperfections.

title: PIMV-GNN: A Physics-Informed Multi-View Graph Neural Network for Robust Channel Knowledge Map Construction.
abstract: Channel knowledge map (CKM) is a key enabler for environmental awareness in future wireless systems. However, reconstructing high-fidelity CKM from sparse and noisy measurements poses a significant challenge. While Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have emerged as a potent tool for this task, existing methods often lack physical consistency and generalization due to reliance on single graph structures and purely data-driven approaches. To tackle this challenge, in this paper, we propose a physics-informed multi-view graph neural network (PIMV-GNN) framework. This framework innovatively integrates two mechanisms within a unified GNN backbone: a multi-view learning (MVL) module that builds a rich spatial representation of the complex environment by fusing two complementary graph structures, namely a "spatial line-of-sight" graph and a "physical proximity" graph; and a physics-informed neural network (PINN) module that enforces physical consistency by imposing constraints derived from the Helmholtz equation in the graph domain. Extensive simulations demonstrate that our proposed PIMV-GNN framework significantly outperforms baseline models under various levels of data sparsity and measurement noise. Furthermore, the results reveal a profound synergistic effect between the MVL and PINN modules, where high-quality multi-view features significantly improve the regularization efficiency of the physics-based constraints.

title: Hybrid Offline-Online Robust Beamforming for MU-MIMO with Unknown Channel Statistics.
abstract: Robust beamforming design under imperfect channel state information (CSI) is a fundamental challenge in multiuser multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) systems, particularly when the statistics of channel estimation errors are unknown. To address this difficulty, this paper proposes a hybrid offline–online robust beamforming framework that jointly integrates data-driven covariance learning with meta-learning for robust beamforming, thus bypass the need for prior error statistics. In the offline phase, a shared deep neural network (DNN) is proposed to infer the channel error covariance matrix from observed channel samples, and a sparse augmented low-rank (SALR) approximation method is presented to reduce model complexity with minimal performance loss. In the online phase, the model is efficiently fine-tuned with a few gradient steps for rapid adaptation. In particular, a multiple-basis model-agnostic meta-learning (MB-MAML) strategy is proposed to enhance the generalization capability of the proposed framework under non-stationary channel conditions. Simulation results show that the proposed framework achieves superior robustness and sum-rate performance compared to existing methods, while maintaining low online computational complexity.
